supermanbin/study-game.desc: 小学课堂知识使用游戏提升学习
supermanbin/study-game.readme:
# 九九乘法闯关

给二年级小朋友练习九九乘法表的网页小游戏，基于 Phaser 3 + TypeScript + Vite。

数字或算式从天上落下来，点击正确答案；答对有连击、道具和爆炸特效，还有语音鼓励。游戏包含：

- 看题目点得数、看得数点算式（反向）两种玩法
- 按顺序解锁的关卡，第 3 关和第 6 关是 Boss 关，按表现评星
- 错题回流：做错的口诀会更常出现
- 口诀卡收集，以及可以调整的设置
- 进度保存在浏览器本地（localStorage）

## 开发

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # 本地开发服务器
npm run build      # 类型检查并构建到 dist/
npm test           # 单元测试 (vitest)
npm run test:e2e   # 端到端测试 (Playwright，自动启动 5199 端口)
```

首次运行 e2e 可能需要先执行 `npx playwright install chromium`。

## 重新生成语音

语音文件在 `public/audio/voice/`，由 `content/voice-lines.json` 中的文案用 edge-tts 生成。

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv-tts && .venv-tts/bin/pip install edge-tts   # 只需一次
# 修改 content/voice-lines.json 后：
node scripts/tts/generate.mjs           # 只生成缺少的
node scripts/tts/generate.mjs --force   # 全部重新生成
```

也可以用环境变量 `EDGE_TTS_BIN` 指定 edge-tts 可执行文件。每条语音 id 都必须有对应的 mp3，单元测试会检查。

## 调试模式

在地址后加 `?debug`（例如 `http://localhost:5173/?debug`），页面上会出现 `window.__funyDebug`，可以直接答对/答错、开始指定关卡、解锁全部关卡、读取当前状态。端到端测试就是通过它来操作游戏的。带 `?debug` 时页面底部还会出现物理调参面板（重力、弹性、空气阻力、弹珠钉、出场方式、恢复默认），参数存在本机，下一题生效。

## 文档

需求与设计：`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-multiplication-game-design.md`

jupixels/game-sounds.readme:
# game-sounds

A ready-to-use library of **636 real game sound effects, jingles and music tracks**, organized and described so Claude (or anyone) can pick the right sound without hearing it. 606 are **CC0 / public domain** from [Kenney.nl](https://kenney.nl), free for personal and commercial games with no credit required (credit is appreciated). The `ww2` and `music` folders hold real recordings from Freesound and OpenGameArt; some of those are CC-BY and need a credit line (see `LICENSE.md`).

## What's inside

| Folder | Count | What |
|---|---|---|
| `sounds/ui` | 151 | clicks, hovers, confirm, error, open/close, toggles, ticks |
| `sounds/impacts` | 105 | punches, thuds, wood, metal, glass, armor, bells, mining |
| `sounds/jingles` | 85 | short music stingers: 8-bit, orchestral hits, pizzicato, sax, steel drum |
| `sounds/scifi` | 73 | lasers, explosions, shields, thrusters, engines, sci-fi doors |
| `sounds/arcade` | 62 | retro synth jumps, power-ups, zaps, coins, blips |
| `sounds/tabletop` | 54 | cards, chips, dice |
| `sounds/rpg` | 41 | doors, coins, blades, books, cloth, leather |
| `sounds/footsteps` | 35 | grass, concrete, wood, snow, carpet, dirt |
| `sounds/ww2` | 28 | real recordings: rifle shots, machine guns, distant battle, artillery, howitzer, air-raid siren, warplane flyby, Sherman tank, ship horn, morse radio |
| `sounds/music` | 2 | orchestral loops: a somber war lament (3:48) and a battle theme (1:16) |

All files are MP3 (plays in every browser), mono for effects and stereo for jingles, music and the two flyby/machine-gun recordings. Most families come with several variants so repeated sounds don't feel robotic.

## Files

- **`CATALOG.md`**: the human- and Claude-readable list. It starts with quick picks (game event → sound), then every family with a description of each file.
- **`sounds.json`**: the same data in machine-readable form: what each sound is, what it sounds like (length, brightness, attack, pitch direction, all measured from the audio), what to use it for, and a suggested volume so sounds mix evenly.
- **`preview.html`**: open it in a browser to listen to everything. Star your favorites and copy the list to tell Claude which ones you like.
- **`lib/sfx.js`**: a small audio manager (no dependencies) that preloads, plays random variants, varies pitch slightly, loops engines and music, and handles the browser's "audio needs a click first" rule.
- **`tools/find.py`**: search from the command line: `python3 tools/find.py laser`.
- **`tools/embed.py`**: packs chosen sounds into a JS file of data URIs for single-file HTML games.
- **`tools/build/`**: the scripts that built this library, for adding more packs later. `add_recorded.py` cuts long field recordings into clips (the `ww2` and `music` sets), and `envelope.py` prints a loudness timeline so cut points can be chosen without listening.

## Using it in a game

```html
<script src="lib/sfx.js"></script>
<script>
  const sfx = new SFX({ base: "sounds/" });
  sfx.load({
    jump: { src: ["arcade/jump_02.mp3", "arcade/jump_03.mp3"], volume: 0.4 },
    coin: { src: "rpg/coins_01.mp3", volume: 1 },
    step: ["footsteps/footstep_grass_01.mp3", "footsteps/footstep_grass_02.mp3", "footsteps/footstep_grass_03.mp3"],
  });
  // later, in game code:
  sfx.play("jump");
  sfx.play("step", { vary: 0.08, volume: 0.6 });
</script>
```

**From GitHub without copying files:** once this repo is on GitHub, any game can load sounds through jsDelivr's free CDN:
`new SFX({ base: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/<your-username>/game-sounds@main/sounds/" })`

**Single-file HTML game:** `python3 tools/embed.py jump=arcade/jump_02.mp3 coin=rpg/coins_01.mp3 > sounds-embedded.js`, then paste that output and `sfx.js` into the page and call `sfx.load(window.SFX_DATA)`.

## Adding more sounds

Drop new files into a category folder and add entries to `sounds.json`, or extend `tools/build/families.py` and re-run the build. Other good CC0 sources include more Kenney packs, OpenGameArt (filter by CC0), and Freesound (filter by CC0).

## License

The Kenney.nl audio is CC0 1.0. The `ww2` and `music` recordings are CC0 or CC-BY 3.0/4.0, listed per file in `LICENSE.md` and `sounds.json`. The code in `lib/` and `tools/` is released as CC0.

# IsoRim Waylith - VE Framework Pack

[Vanilla Expanded Framework](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2023507013) pipe networks across the floors of [IsoRimZ](https://github.com/peren717/IsoRim-ProjectZ), for [IsoRim Waylith](https://github.com/peren717/IsoRim-1.7) (RimWorld 1.7).

- A pipe connects to a pipe of the same network directly above or below it, like power conduits.

- In the 3D view a vertical pipe piece links the floors, also in the pipe overlay.
- VEF beam weapons (the VWE flamethrower and others) come out of the muzzle in the 3D view, and burn only on the target's floor between floors.

Requires IsoRim Waylith, Vanilla Expanded Framework and IsoRimZ with Api 3 (without IsoRimZ the pack does nothing). Load after all three.

Vanilla Expanded Framework is made by the Vanilla Expanded team (Oskar Potocki and others). This pack contains no files of the original mod.

MIT License.

lopezlav/biplanes.readme:
# Bluetooth Biplanes (web port)

A port of the J2ME phone game **Bluetooth Biplanes** (Morpheme Ltd., 2004) to JavaScript. It runs in the browser.

Play it: **https://biplanes.chope.dev**

The game logic is a line-by-line translation of the original Java bytecode. The physics, the computer pilots, the menus, the taunts, the scores, the records and the two-player packets work as in the original. It is not an emulator: there is no Java VM.

## Controls

| Desktop | Phone | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W A S D / arrow keys | joystick (left side) | fly, move in menus |
| Space | FIRE | fire, select in menus |
| E | EJECT | eject; press again to open the parachute |
| Enter | the left menu button, or tap the "Select" / "Next" / "Help" label | left soft key |
| Esc | ❚❚, the "Back" menu button, or tap the "Back" / "Close" label | right soft key (Back, pause, Close) |
| E | tap your pilot | online: say a taunt on the airfield |
| F | | full screen |

On a phone the game uses the whole screen and the controls show over it. The joystick is always there. While you fly, FIRE, EJECT and ❚❚ show on the right. In menus, two small buttons show there instead. They have the same labels as the game's soft keys (Select, Back, Next, Close, ...) and do the same thing.

In menus you can tap or click an item to choose it. On desktop the mouse also highlights the item under it. A tap on a message, a help page, a result page or the score board goes on.

## Online

The original game has a two-player mode over Bluetooth. Here it is online, in the main menu under *Online*:

1. Type your name.
2. Choose your pilot (all 8 pilots of the game are free online) and your colour. Your plane and your little pilot get that colour.
3. You are on the airfield with everybody who is online. Walk with A / D, the arrow keys or the joystick, or tap a place to walk there. Tap your pilot (or press E) to say one of your pilot's taunts.
4. Walk up to another player and press *Fight {name}* (left soft key, Space, or the button). They get 15 seconds to accept.
5. When they accept, you both go to a private match: the original two-player game, first to 10. After it you are both back on the airfield, and *Rematch* asks again.

How it works:

- `worker/index.js` is a Cloudflare Worker with two Durable Objects:
  - `Lobby` (one for everybody) keeps the players on the airfield, their positions and the invites. It uses WebSocket hibernation, so it costs almost nothing when nobody moves.
  - `Match` (one per fight) is a private room for two players.
- In a match, the two browsers first try a direct WebRTC data channel (STUN only). If it does not open in 4 seconds, the packets go through the `Match` room.
- The game packets are the original ones (an int and 18 bytes, 20 times per second). The original game waits when it is 2 packets ahead of the other player, which is right for Bluetooth. Online, both players measure the delay before the start and set this window from it, so a slow link does not make the game slow. With 130 ms between the players the window is 5 and the game runs at full speed; with the original window of 2 it ran at about a third of the speed.
- There are no accounts. Your name, pilot and colour are kept in the browser.

## How it is built

- `web/res/` holds the original resource files from the JAR: `r` (packed images, menu data and music), `f`/`fzr`/`fzb` (bitmap fonts) and `tg`/`tt`/`tm` (text).
  - The game rebuilds its PNG images from `r` at start, the same way the original does.
- `web/res/music.wav` is the game's own MIDI file, rendered to audio with the GeneralUser GS soundfont. Browsers cannot play MIDI. The game plays clips of it at the original times.
- `web/js/` is the port, one file per original class:
  - `game.js` = `b` (game, screens, input, packets)
  - `entities.js` = `e` (plane and pilot), `f` (bullet), `d` (debris)
  - `font.js` = `c` (bitmap font), `menu.js` = `g` (menus), `sound.js` = `h`, `input.js` = `i`, `link.js` = `j` (the two-player link, here over the internet)
  - Field names are the original ones; methods have readable names, with the original signature in a comment above each one.
- `web/js/online.js` is new: the online screens (name, pilot, airfield) and the start and end of a match. It draws with the game's own graphics, font and sprites.
- `web/js/midp.js` is a small copy of the phone APIs the game uses: Graphics, Image, data streams, `java.util.Random` and RecordStore (here it saves to `localStorage`).
- `web/js/render.js` is a display layer. It changes how the game looks, not how it plays:
  - **Screen shape:** the game's screen size follows the window. In landscape it is 128 px tall and up to 255 px wide, which is the whole arena. In portrait it is 128 px wide and up to 208 px tall. The game already reads its screen size from the phone, so the logic does not change.
  - **Sharp pixels:** the game draws at full device resolution, in whole steps, so the pixel art stays sharp.
  - **Smooth motion:** the game still runs at 20 ticks per second. Each tick is kept as a list of draw commands, and the screen draws it again at 60 fps. The camera and the moving sprites slide smoothly between ticks.
  - **Parallax:** the original sky and ground strips are split by colour into far clouds, trees and ground. These scroll at different speeds over a sky gradient.
  - **Side bars:** a blurred copy of the picture fills the space beside the screen.
  - `?w=128&h=128` in the address gives the original square screen.

### Changes for the web

- The main menu has no "Quit" item.
- "Two Player Game" (Bluetooth) is now "Online" (see above).
- The 128×128 title and advert pictures are centered over a blurred copy of themselves.
- Keyboard, joystick and touch buttons replace the phone keypad.
- The two-player link goes over the internet (see above).

## Run it locally

```sh
npx wrangler dev
```

Then open http://localhost:8787. This runs the game files, the lobby and the match rooms on your computer. To play online

Dickybima/vozz.readme: # VOZZ — GPU Mining Game Waitlist Waitlist landing page for VOZZ, a GPU-themed mining simulation game built on **Robinhood Chain**, with an animated GPU mining simulation running in the background (canvas). ## Files - `index.html` — page structure (hero + waitlist form, features, roadmap, FAQ) - `style.css` — neon/cyberpunk theme, responsive - `background.js` — canvas mining simulation: a wall of GPUs with spinning fans & RGB lighting, hash rain, *share* particles flying to the block being mined, and a blockchain that slides along every time a block is found - `app.js` — live stats, beta countdown, waitlist form & "Miner License" ticket - `assets/logo.svg` — full logo (mark + wordmark) - `assets/logo-mark.svg` — logo mark only (hex GPU chip with a V and a mined block) - `favicon.svg` — simplified mark for small sizes - `assets/brand/` — logo exports: SVG + PNG mark (512/1024, transparent), full logo (transparent and on dark), 1000×1000 avatar and 1500×500 X banner - `assets/beta-mining.mp4` / `.webm` + `beta-mining-poster.jpg` — 38s "Beta Mining Gameplay" video, opened from the **Beta Gameplay** item in the top menu - `video/beta-demo.html` — source of that video (a scripted canvas mock of the beta UI; open it in a browser to preview in real time) - `video/render.js` — renders the video frame by frame and encodes it - `assets/how-to-join.mp4` (+ poster) — 56s "How to join the VOZZ waitlist" tutorial recorded from the real site. Re-record it with `node video/record-join.js` after changing the waitlist flow. - `play/` — the playable beta game (`index.html`, `game.css`, `game.js`) - `config.js` — network settings (Robinhood Chain mainnet/testnet) and the Mining Pass contract address - `wallet.js` — wallet picker (EIP-6963: MetaMask, Rabby, Coinbase, OKX, … plus open-in-app links on mobile), network switching (used by the waitlist's Connect wallet button; the Mining Pass helpers are unused for now) - `contracts/` — a VOZZ Mining Pass NFT contract (0.001 ETH mint), with tests and a deploy script. It is **not used yet**: the game doesn't require it and it isn't deployed. See `contracts/README.md`. ## Playable beta (`play/`) `play/index.html` is a playable closed-beta prototype, linked from **Play Beta** in the nav and the hero. It's an idle GPU-mining game: - **Rig:** buy GPUs (6 models) into slots; sell for 50% back. Each card shows live hashrate, temperature, wattage and spinning fans. - **Overclock:** core / memory / power limit / fan sliders trade hashrate against heat and power bill. Cards throttle at 88°C and crash for 8s at 100°C. - **Upgrades:** rig slots (4 → 12), PSU wattage (cards beyond PSU capacity get no power), cooling. - **Mining:** the simulated network finds a block about every 10s (50 VOZZ reward). Pool mining (NEON-FORGE steady, HashLords variable) pays your share of every block; solo mining wins whole blocks by chance. Network hashrate and difficulty grow over time. - **Missions** with VOZZ rewards, a leaderboard against simulated miners, an event log and a Robinhood Chain block lane (simulated). - Progress autosaves to `localStorage`; offline earnings are credited at 50% for up to 2 hours. A wallet linked through the waitlist shows in the top bar. The beta is free to play: no wallet or NFT is needed. Nothing in the beta is on-chain yet. Balancing constants are at the top of `play/game.js`. ## Running No build step — open `index.html` in a browser, or: ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 ``` ## Re-rendering the beta video Requires Node with Playwright and ffmpeg (libx264 + libvpx-vp9): ```bash node video/render.js # writes assets/beta-mining.mp4 + poster ffmpeg -i assets/beta-mining.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 36 -b:v 0 assets/beta-mining.webm node video/render.js 6 16 22 # just save PNG stills at those seconds ``` ## Waitlist flow Clicking **Join Waitlist** opens a modal with 4 missions that unlock in order: 1. Follow on X 2. Like the post 3. Repost the post 4. Comment on the post Each mission button opens the matching X intent link in a new tab, then marks the mission done after a short "verifying" delay. X actions can't be verified from the browser alone, so this only confirms that the link was opened. Once all 4 are done, the Robinhood Chain wallet address step appears, with a **Paste** button. Only EVM addresses (`0x` + 40 hex characters) are accepted. There is also an optional **Connect wallet & add Robinhood Chain** button that reads the address from an injected wallet (e.g. MetaMask) and switches it to — or adds — Robinhood Chain. Set the X account and post in `app.js`: ```js const X_HANDLE = "vozzGPU"; const X_POST_ID = "2113652208571228400"; ``` ## Robinhood Chain Network settings live in the `CHAIN` constant in `app.js` (mainnet, chain ID 4663 / `0x1237`, gas in ETH, RPC `https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com`, explorer `https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com`). Check them against [docs.robinhood.com/chain](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain) before launch; for the testnet use chain ID 46630 and `https://rpc.testnet.chain.robinhood.com`. ## Storing waitlist signups By default signups are only saved in the visitor's browser (`localStorage`). To collect real signups, set `WAITLIST_ENDPOINT` in `app.js` to a URL that accepts a JSON `POST` of `{ wallet, chainId, ref, tasks }` (e.g. Formspree, Supabase, or your own API). The beta date is set via `BETA_DATE` in `app.js`.

Adnan78623/kytyps5-demons-souls-linux-la.desc: Unofficial Linux launcher for Demon's Souls on the KytyPS5 emulator (chenxiao07): AppImage, FSR 3, shader precompile, one-click updates
Adnan78623/kytyps5-demons-souls-linux-la.readme:
# KytyPS5 Demon's Souls Linux Launcher (unofficial)

> [!NOTE]
> **Vibe-coded with Claude.** 🤖⚔️ This launcher was written by Anthropic's Claude (in Claude Code), with a human
> pointing at things and saying "make it do that". It was played and tested on one Linux PC, which is more testing
> than most Souls bosses get before shipping.
>
> If you die, that's the game. If the launcher dies, that's on us: [open an issue](../../issues).
> *Try praising the AI.* (This paragraph was also written by AI.)

A settings window for playing **Demon's Souls (PS5)** on Linux with
[KytyPS5 by chenxiao07](https://github.com/chenxiao07/KytyPS5), an experimental PS5 emulator made for this game.

The emulator itself is **chenxiao07's work**. This project only adds a launcher around their official Linux release:
the installer and the updater download it from their GitHub releases, so you always run their latest build. Bugs in
the emulator belong in [their issues](https://github.com/chenxiao07/KytyPS5/issues); bugs in the launcher, here.

This project is not affiliated with Sony, Bluepoint Games, FromSoftware or the KytyPS5 developers. It contains no
game files: you need your own copy of Demon's Souls (PPSA01340/01341/01342), version 01.007.000 or 01.005.000.

## Install

1. Download **`DemonsSouls-KytyPS5-Launcher-x86_64.AppImage`** from the
   [latest release](../../releases/latest).
2. Make it executable: right-click → Properties → *Is executable*, or `chmod +x DemonsSouls-KytyPS5-Launcher-x86_64.AppImage`.
3. Double-click it. On first start it offers to add itself to your application menu, then press **⬇ Install KytyPS5**:
   it downloads the emulator (about 100 MB) from chenxiao07's GitHub into `~/Games/KytyPS5-DeS`.

Then choose your Demon's Souls folder, press **⚙ Precompile shaders** once, and **▶ Launch**.

The AppImage brings its own Python and Qt: nothing else to install. If it does not start, your system may lack FUSE 2
(`sudo apt install libfuse2` on Ubuntu 22.04+; on most other distributions it is already there), or run it with
`--appimage-extract-and-run`.

## What it does

- **One-click install** of the latest KytyPS5 Linux release, checked against GitHub's checksum.
- **Game check:** tells you whether the folder you chose is Demon's Souls, and a version KytyPS5 runs.
- **Display:** window size, render resolution (the 3D world, 720p to 2160p, in performance mode), frame rate
  (30/60/120 Hz), present mode, fullscreen, HDR.
- **AMD FSR 3**, built into KytyPS5 and working on any GPU: upscaling on the game's PS5 Pro path, frame generation
  (2x), low latency.
- **Shader precompile** in one click (upstream's `precompile-linux.sh`), so new areas do not stutter on their first
  shaders. Progress shows in the launcher.
- **Updates** in one click: shows what changed, keeps the previous version for `./des-update.py --rollback`.
- GPU choice (for PCs with an integrated GPU too), console language, MangoHud, gamescope window scaling, and an
  experimental *Skip intro logos*.

## Requirements

- Linux x86-64 with a CPU that has AVX2, a Vulkan 1.3 GPU with current drivers (Mesa for AMD/Intel), glibc 2.35+
- Optional: `vulkan-tools` (GPU list), `mangohud`, `gamescope`

### Without the AppImage

With Python 3 and PyQt6 installed (`sudo pacman -S python-pyqt6`, `sudo apt install python3-pyqt6`,
`sudo dnf install python3-pyqt6`):

```
git clone https://github.com/Adnan78623/kytyps5-demons-souls-linux-launcher
cd kytyps5-demons-souls-linux-launcher
./install.sh
```

This puts KytyPS5 and the launcher in `~/Games/KytyPS5-DeS` (or `./install.sh <folder>`; an existing KytyPS5 Linux
folder gets the launcher added) and adds **Demon's Souls (KytyPS5)** to the application menu.

The precompile takes minutes to an hour the first time, can be stopped, and resumes. Run it again after a GPU driver
update. Your settings, saves, logs and the shader cache are in `~/Games/KytyPS5-DeS` (`DES_HOME` changes it).

## Tips

- **Performance mode, not Cinematic**, in the game's settings: the render resolution and FSR 3 apply to the
  performance mode only, and Cinematic renders native 4K at 30 fps.
- **Faster:** lower *Render resolution* and turn on *FSR 3 upscaling* (1080p or higher, or 720p). Keep the window at
  your monitor's size; gamescope scaling is not needed then.
- **Smoother:** *FSR 3 frame generation* with *Frame rate 60 Hz* shows 120 fps on a 120 Hz monitor (a little more input
  lag; *Low latency* helps).
- The log under the buttons shows what the emulator does; `logs/last-run.log` keeps it.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `des-launcher.py` | the launcher (PyQt6) |
| `des-update.py` | installs and updates KytyPS5 from chenxiao07's releases; `--rollback` goes back one version |
| `install.sh` | installs both without the AppImage and adds the menu entry |
| `packaging/` | the AppImage build (`build-appimage.sh`), run by `.github/workflows/appimage.yml` for each `v*` tag |

The launcher sets the emulator's own switches (`KYTY_RENDER_HEIGHT`, `KYTY_UPSCALER`, `KYTY_FRAMEGEN`, …) and starts
upstream's `run_ds.sh`, with one line of it changed so that the window size and language can be set.

## License

GPL-2.0, as KytyPS5. See `LICENSE`.

gabrielamidon8-sys/RiversOfRust.readme:
# RiversOfRust

A post-apocalyptic vehicle-combat game by **DeclAIre Studios**: build a war machine from scrap in the garage, then take it out on the sand. Plays on PC (keyboard and mouse), with a controller, and on phones and tablets (touch, and an Android app).

**Play the prototype:** https://gabrielamidon8-sys.github.io/RiversOfRust/
**Website:** https://riversofrust.wordpress.com

## What's new in 0.2.0

- **Three ways to play, picked automatically.** The game uses whatever you touched last and switches on the spot: a key or the mouse means keyboard and mouse, a finger on the screen means touch, a button or stick on a controller means controller. Every hint and button label changes to match, and controllers show their own buttons (Xbox A B X Y, or PlayStation ✕ ○ □ △).
- **Touch.** Garage: tap a part, then tap a glowing spot to bolt it on; tap a part on the car to take it off; drag to look, pinch to zoom. Drive: a stick that appears under your left thumb (up for gas, down to brake and reverse, sideways to steer); drag anywhere on the right to look and aim; **Fire** (keep your thumb on it and slide to aim while firing), **Handbrake** and **Flip** buttons. Phones get a layout of their own, sideways and upright, lighter graphics, and a governor that lowers the resolution when the frame rate drops.
- **Controller.** Garage: D-pad ↑↓ choose a part, A pick it up / bolt it on, LB/RB (or D-pad ←→) move it to the next spot, B put it back, LB/RB with empty hands choose a part on the car and X takes it off, Y build mode, right stick look, LT/RT zoom, Menu test drive. Drive: RT gas, LT brake and reverse, left stick steer, right stick aim, RB fire, A handbrake, Y flip, B camera behind, View back to the garage. It rumbles when parts go on and when you fire.
- **Android app** (`android/`): the game runs offline from inside the app, full screen and sideways, with controllers passed straight through and the back button doing the game's back (put the part down, leave build mode, leave the drive, then leave the app).
- Driving is analog now: half a trigger is half the gas, a light touch on the stick is a light turn.

## What's in 0.1.0

- **The garage.** A rusted workshop with a scissor lift in the middle and an orbit camera on the bay. Drag to look around, scroll to zoom.
- **Build mode.** Press **Build** (or pick a part on the right). Every spot the part can bolt onto glows; move near one and the part snaps there in green; click to bolt it on. Click a part on the car to take it off again (anything bolted to it goes back on the shelf). Right-click or Esc puts the part you're holding back. In build mode the lift raises the car so the wheels hang clear of the floor.
- **The parts** (one grid unit is 0.35 m):
  | Part | Size | Bolts to |
  |---|---|---|
  | Frame | 4 × 12 × 2 ladder frame | the lift; everything else bolts to it |
  | Half body | 4 × 6 cabin, no hood, 1.05 m tall | the frame's deck (three positions); its 4 × 2 roof takes parts on top only |
  | Engine | supercharged V8, 420 hp | the engine well at the front of the frame |
  | Steering wheel × 2 | 0.84 m tyre | a 1 × 2 mount; steers (at the back they steer the other way) and is driven |
  | Drive wheel × 2 | 0.84 m tyre | a 1 × 2 mount; accelerates |
  | Turret | machine gun on a 2 × 2 base | the roof |
- **Test drive.** Unlocks when every part is on. A desert course with ramps, a barrier chicane, containers, crates, drums and a tyre wall. 4WD with steering on the steering wheels, raycast-vehicle physics (cannon-es), 0-100 km/h in about 7 s, about 115 km/h flat out. The turret follows your aim and fires.
  - `W`/`S` drive and brake (hold `S` when stopped to reverse) · `A`/`D` steer · `Space` handbrake · mouse aims (click to lock the mouse, `Esc` to let it go) · click fires · `R` flips you back upright · `Tab` back to the garage.
- Your car is saved in the browser and comes back next time.
- Everything is made in code: models, textures, sounds. No asset files apart from the fonts.

## Shared with Zombie City

- **Engines.** RiversOfRust is built from engines on the same CORE hub contract as Zombie City (`coreAdd`, `coreOn`/`coreEmit`, `coreCost`, `coreHurt`, `coreTick`, the watchdog), so an engine can move between the games. See `js/core.js`. Engines so far: GARAGE, BUILDER, DRIVE, TEXEL, SFX.
- **Accounts.** One DeclAIre account for every game, run from the DeclAIre Studios account hub on Wix. When you're signed in to Zombie City in the same browser (GitHub Pages), the garage shows your name. Signing in from inside RiversOfRust comes next.
- **Fonts.** Chakra Petch, Saira Stencil One and Share Tech Mono, as in Zombie City (SIL Open Font License, in `fonts/`).

## Layout

```
index.html        the page, the HUD and the import map
css/style.css     the HUD
js/config.js      sizes, masses and the parts list
js/parts.js       the parts, modelled in code
js/assembly.js    which part bolts where (pure logic, tested on its own)
js/builder.js     build mode: picking, snapping, placing, taking off
js/garage.js      the workshop
js/vehicle.js     the physics vehicle (pure logic, tested on its own)
js/drive.js       the test drive
js/materials.js   procedural textures
js/audio.js       synthesised sound
js/core.js        the CORE engine hub
js/input.js       keyboard/mouse, touch or controller: detection, the controller, button names
js/touchdrive.js  the on-screen stick and buttons for the drive
js/quality.js     lighter settings for phones
android/          the Android app: manifest, the WebView wrapper, icons, build_apk.py
vendor/           three.js r186 and cannon-es 0.20.0 (MIT)
tests/            physics.test.mjs (node); browser_check.py, input_check.py, app_bundle_check.py (Playwright)
tools/            the tile render and the icon drawing
```

## Run it locally

Any static server works: `python3 -m http.server` in this folder, then open http://localhost:8000.

Tests: `node tests/physics.test.mjs` (driving behaviour, no screen), `python3 tests

pusam/nolja.readme:
# 놀자 🎮

거실 TV에서 조이콘 들고 같이 노는 게임 모음. 브라우저(PC 크롬·엣지)에서 돌아가고, 조이콘은 WebHID로 직접 읽음.

- 바로 하기: https://pusam.github.io/nolja/
- 게임: 🎾 테니스 (조이콘을 라켓처럼 휘둘러서 치는 2인 대결 · 몬스터 캐릭터 16종 · 3D)

## 하는 법

1. 노트북(그램 등) 블루투스에서 조이콘 L·R 각각 페어링 (레일 옆 동그란 버튼 길게)
2. 크롬으로 위 주소 열기 → 게임 메뉴에서 **조이콘 연결** (두 개면 두 번)
3. 노트북을 TV에 HDMI 연결 → `윈도우키 + P` → 두 번째 화면만 → TV 해상도 1920×1080 · 60Hz
4. `F` 전체화면, TV는 게임 모드

인터넷 없이 하려면 `start-game.bat` 더블클릭 (이 폴더를 http://localhost:8765 로 열어줌. 그 포트를 다른 프로그램이 쓰고 있으면 8766~8775 중 빈 포트를 씀. 창은 켜둘 것).
포트가 바뀌면 브라우저가 다른 사이트로 봐서 저장된 설정(캐릭터·감도 등)이 처음 상태로 보일 수 있음.
파일을 직접 열면(file://) 크롬이 조이콘 연결을 막아서 키보드만 됨.

## 테니스 조작

이동은 자동. 공이 오면 휘두르기만 하면 됨.

- **타이밍**: 포핸드는 일찍 치면 왼쪽, 늦게 치면 오른쪽으로 감. 백핸드는 반대. 너무 늦으면 네트, 너무 이르면 길게 나가기 쉬움
- **세기**: 살살 = 로브, 세게 = 빠른 공. 세고 평평하게 칠수록 길게 나가기 쉬움
- **휘두르는 방향** (조이콘): 아래→위로 올려 치면 탑스핀(뚝 떨어지고 높게 튐), 위→아래로 깎으면 슬라이스(낮게 깔림), 수평이면 플랫
- **포핸드·백핸드** (조이콘): 공이 라켓 쪽으로 오면 포핸드, 반대쪽이면 백핸드로 휘둘러야 제대로 맞음. 반대로 치면 "반대쪽!"과 함께 약하게 넘어감
- **서브**: 한 번 휘둘러 토스 → 공이 제일 높을 때 한 번 더. 일찍 치면 길게, 늦게 치면 네트. 실수하면 폴트, 두 번 연속이면 더블 폴트
- **키보드**: P1 `A` 살살 · `S` 보통 · `D` 세게 · `X` 슬라이스 / P2 `J` · `K` · `L` · `,` — `Enter` 시작 · `Esc` 일시정지 · `F` 전체화면
- **게임패드**: `A` 보통 · `X` 살살 · `Y`/`RB`/`RT` 세게 · `B` 슬라이스

메뉴의 **그래픽 · 플레이 설정**: 그래픽 단계, 스윙 감도, 타이밍 보정, 타이밍 가이드(칠 자리·포핸드/백핸드 표시), 왼손잡이(P1·P2), 포핸드·백핸드 판정 끄기(아이들과 할 때), 심판 목소리, 소리 크기(음악·효과음·관중).

**소리**: 파일 없이 브라우저에서 즉석 합성. 메뉴·캐릭터 선택에선 배경 음악, 경기 중엔 실제 중계처럼 음악 없이 관중 웅성거림. 타구음은 세기·구질(탑스핀 "슥", 슬라이스 "턱")·나이스 타이밍("깡")에 따라 다르고, 바운드·네트·운동화 끽 소리, 박수·"오~"·아쉬운 탄성, 이겼을 때 축하 음악이 나옴.

## 구조

```
index.html          홈 화면 (게임 고르기)
games/
  tennis/           테니스
    index.html        메뉴·캐릭터 선택·가이드 화면
    tennis.js         경기 규칙 · 공 물리(공기저항·스핀·바운드) · 2D/3D 그리기
    tennis-ui.js      메뉴 배치 · 접근성 (규칙은 tennis.js)
    tennis.css        테니스 화면 스타일
    assets/           메인 그림 (monster-team.png 원본, 화면에는 .webp)
shared/
  store.js          설정 저장 (게임끼리 공유: 캐릭터·감도·그래픽)
  joycon.js         조이콘 연결·스윙 감지(세기·스핀·포핸드/백핸드)·버튼·진동·기울기
  characters.js     몬스터 캐릭터 16종 (얼굴 그림 + 3D 모델 + 자세)
  audio.js          소리 합성 (효과음·관중·음악, 볼륨)
  nolja.css         공용 스타일
  home.css          홈 화면 스타일
  vendor/three.min.js  three.js r149 (MIT, THREE_LICENSE)
tools/test_tennis.js  테니스 로직 시뮬레이션 테스트 (node tools/test_tennis.js)
start-game.bat      오프라인 실행기
```

## 새 게임 추가

1. `games/게임이름/index.html` 만들고 `shared/*.js`를 불러와서 사용 (`window.Nolja.joycon`, `.characters`, `.audio`, `.store`)
2. 루트 `index.html`의 `GAMES` 목록에 한 줄 추가

## 고친 걸 올릴 때

js·css를 고쳤으면 `index.html`·`games/tennis/index.html`에서 파일 주소 끝의 `?v=날짜`를 새 값으로 바꿔서 올림. 안 바꾸면 전에 접속했던 브라우저가 옛 파일과 새 파일을 섞어 써서(GitHub Pages는 10분 동안 캐시) 게임이 멈출 수 있음.

## 그래픽

2018년형 노트북 내장그래픽(인텔 UHD 620)에서도 돌아가게 가볍게 만듦. 렌더 해상도는 최대 1080p, 메뉴의 그래픽 설정에서 자동/높음/보통/낮음/2D 선택 (자동은 느리면 알아서 낮춤).

Gridyq/homebase.desc: Personal iPhone app with bundled mini-apps (Jellyfin first), built for SideStore
Gridyq/homebase.readme:
# Homebase

A personal iPhone app that contains several mini-apps in one install, so it only uses one of
SideStore's three free app slots. The first mini-app is a Jellyfin client.

Built with Expo (React Native). No Mac needed: GitHub Actions builds an unsigned `.ipa`, and
SideStore signs it with a free Apple ID.

## Installing on your iPhone

1. Set up SideStore on the phone (https://docs.sidestore.io).
2. On GitHub, open **Actions → Build iOS → Run workflow**, choose **Release**, and wait for it
   to finish (about 15–25 minutes).
3. On the iPhone, open the repo's **Releases** page in Safari, download `Homebase-Release.ipa`
   from **latest-release**, then share it to SideStore (or use **+** in SideStore's My Apps tab).
4. Refresh it in SideStore at least once every 7 days.

## Developing from Linux

Build and install the **Debug** configuration once the same way. It's a development build: it
loads JavaScript from your computer instead of having it built in.

```sh
npm install
npx expo start
```

With the phone on the same Wi-Fi, open Homebase and pick your computer from the list (or enter
the URL `npx expo start` prints). Edits reload on the phone as you save. You only need a new
build when native packages or `app.json` change.

Before committing:

```sh
npx tsc --noEmit
npx expo lint
```

## Over-the-air updates

JavaScript changes don't need a new build. The app checks a self-hosted update server
(`update-server/`, running on the Jellyfin PC) when it starts and when it comes back to the
foreground, then shows "Update ready. Tap to restart" on the launcher.

```sh
npm run publish-update
```

- The status server (below) serves `update-server/` on a port of its own, 8787, which is the
  address built into the app (`fedora.tail27f991.ts.net`, over Tailscale). The code is
  `status-server-rs/src/updates.rs`; until 2026-10-23 it was a server of its own.
  Without Tailscale the app keeps running the last update it downloaded.
- Updates are signed with `update-server/keys/private-key.pem`, which is git-ignored. The app
  rejects anything not signed with it. Back that key up: if it's lost, you need a new build
  with a new certificate.
- Updates only reach builds with the same `version` in `app.json`. When you change native code
  (packages with native code, `app.json` plugins or iOS settings), bump `version` and make a
  new build.

## Adding a mini-app

1. Create its screens in `src/app/<id>/`, with a `_layout.tsx` for its own navigation stack.
2. Put its non-screen code in `src/miniapps/<id>/`.
3. Add an entry to `src/miniapps/registry.ts` so it shows on the launcher.
4. Register its stack in `src/app/_layout.tsx` with `headerShown: false`.

## Server mini-app

Shows CPU, memory, GPU, network, temperatures, disks, what Jellyfin is playing (and whether it's
transcoding, and why), and the Podman containers and systemd units on the home server, and can
start, stop and restart them. The data comes from the status server, a Rust program in
`status-server-rs/` that keeps its files in `status-server/`. It also serves the Requests, Drop,
Videos and Assistant mini-apps and the over-the-air updates, and sends an ntfy message when a disk
passes 90%, a sensor passes 90°C, a service fails, crashes or is killed for memory, or a drive's
SMART health turns bad (and again when it recovers).

The dashboard, service pages and Conversions screen keep a WebSocket open (`/api/live`) and update
as things change, falling back to polling when it can't connect. Service changes come from
systemd's D-Bus signals and drive changes from udisks', so they show within a couple of seconds;
new files in the libraries are noticed through inotify. Conversions pause while Jellyfin transcodes
video for someone, and the app warns before game mode while someone is watching.

Analytics: Memory breaks RAM into programs, kernel and cache and lists every service and app by
memory, CPU or disk traffic (from their cgroups, so cache is counted apart from what programs
hold); Processes lists the top programs; CPU shows each thread's load and clock and how long
programs waited on CPU, memory and drives (pressure stall info); Graphics card (tap the GPU tile)
shows engine load including video encode/decode, video memory, temperatures, power, fan, clocks
and which programs have the card open (from DRM fdinfo); Drives shows SMART health, wear and
temperature from udisks, and who's reading and writing each drive (cgroup `io.stat`); Network
splits traffic by container (each container's own network namespace) and by Tailscale device;
Power adds up the CPU's and graphics card's measured draw into kWh and cost; Reliability counts
crashes, memory kills (kernel OOM killer and systemd-oomd, from the journal) and reboots per
service, with a timeline. Trends and each service, drive and device page chart up to a year, with
reboots, crashes and game mode marked.

History is a reading every 15 seconds, kept a day, with averages kept longer: every 10 minutes for a
week, hourly for a month and every 6 hours for a year. All of it is in `status-server/history.db`
(SQLite, one row per series per entry), so a chart reads only the series and range it shows. Events
are `status-server/events.jsonl` (all git-ignored), appended as they come and trimmed every few
hours.

- CPU power comes from the CPU's energy counter (RAPL), which only root can read. A udev rule
  lets the server's user read it, and only that user, since the counter is a known side channel
  (CVE-2020-8694). In `/etc/udev/rules.d/99-homebase-rapl.rules`:
  `SUBSYSTEM=="powercap", KERNEL=="intel-rapl:0", RUN+="/bin/sh -c 'chgrp leonidas /sys%p/energy_uj && chmod 0440 /sys%p/energy_uj'"`
  (it takes effect at the next boot, or run the `chgrp` and `chmod` once by hand).
- It runs as a systemd user service: `systemctl --user status homebase-status`, running
  `~/.local/bin/homebase-status`. To deploy a change: `cargo build --release` in
  `status-server-rs/` (its build output goes to `~/.cache/homebase

blocklist from /api/cleanup, which now also reports strike limits, the
lapse time and whether the queue check is failing. The app calls
/api/conversions (the server keeps /api/tdarr for older updates), and
Seerr's old /api/arr/seerr route is gone.

- /api/live WebSocket pushes status, conversions, Jellyfin sessions and events;
  the dashboard, service pages and Conversions screen use it (useLive), falling
  back to polling
- systemd and udisks changes arrive over D-Bus (zbus), so service starts, stops
  and crashes are logged within ~2 s; SMART reads no longer shell out to busctl
- Libraries are watched with inotify; scans follow changes, every 30 min besides
- History moves to SQLite (history.db), imported once from the JSON-lines tiers
- Jellyfin sessions on the dashboard; conversions pause while Jellyfin
  transcodes video; the app warns before game mode while someone is watching

# Rock Paper Scissors

A Rock Paper Scissors game with a Spring Boot 3 (Java 17) REST API and a Vue 3 frontend.

## Running locally

```bash
mvn spring-boot:run
```

Open http://localhost:8080. The API is under `/api/games`.

Run the tests with `mvn test`.

## Deployment

The Java backend (which also serves the frontend) runs on **Render** using the `Dockerfile`.
If you want, you can also serve the static frontend from **Netlify**, which forwards `/api` calls to Render.

### Render (backend + frontend)

1. In the Render dashboard, click **New → Web Service**.
2. Connect this GitHub repository.
3. Render detects the `Dockerfile` and picks the **Docker** runtime.
4. Choose the **Free** plan.
5. Click **Deploy Web Service** and wait for the build to finish.
6. Open `https://<name>.onrender.com`, where `<name>` is your service name.

You don't need to set a port. The container reads the `PORT` variable that Render provides.

### Netlify (optional, frontend only)

1. In Netlify, click **Add new site → Import an existing project** and choose this repository.
2. Leave the **build command** empty.
3. Check that the **publish directory** is `src/main/resources/static`. Netlify reads it from `netlify.toml`.
4. In `netlify.toml`, replace `RENDER_APP_NAME` with your Render service name (for example, `https://my-rps.onrender.com/api/:splat`), then commit and push.
5. Deploy. The frontend calls relative `/api/games` URLs, and Netlify forwards them to Render, so you don't need to set up CORS.

### Notes

- Render's free plan puts the service to sleep after about 15 minutes without traffic. The first request after that can take 30 to 60 seconds while it wakes up.
- Games are stored in memory, so they are lost whenever the service restarts or goes to sleep.

congp/wordsearch.readme:
# Word Search

A mobile-first word search game. Tap a letter and swipe across a word to find it. Found words get a neon highlight, and the highlight colours follow a set of rules so that crossing words stay easy to tell apart. The page is plain static HTML with no build step or dependencies, Live at **<https://congph.com/wordsearch/>**, hosted on GitHub Pages from [github.com/congp/wordsearch](https://github.com/congp/wordsearch).

## Features at a glance

- **40 puzzles in 8 categories:** Pop Culture, Food & Drink, Art & Lifestyle, Science & Discovery, Nature, Travel, Play & Adventure, and Mind & Language. Most come from a theme library of ideas. Each board is a fresh 10×10 grid with 20 words drawn from that puzzle's word list.
- **Puzzles list:** grouped by category, with a row of filter chips at the top, completion progress for each category, and the current puzzle highlighted.
- **Lots of crossings:** the generator deliberately packs words so they overlap, like a printed puzzle book. Words can even hide inside other words (SKI inside SKIING).
- **Neon highlights:** six colours in a fixed order (yellow, green, orange, blue, purple, pink). The colour switches by rule, and overlapping highlights mix into new shades.
- **Game modes:**
  - **In order:** words must be found alphabetically.
  - **Crazy:** a countdown (10–60 s) that refills each time you find a word. If it runs out, the board resets.
- **Word cards:** tap any word to read a short paragraph about it.
- **Records:** completion count and personal best time per puzzle, kept separately for each mode combination.
- **Generative music:** an ambient soundtrack created live in the browser, which reacts to progress and the crazy-mode clock. It is off by default.

## Run it locally

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Run that from the repository root, then open <http://localhost:8000/>. The same server is set up in `.claude/launch.json` as "Word Search (local)", for tools that start previews from that file.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | The whole game: styles, markup and one script inside an IIFE (a function that runs immediately). |
| `words-info.js` | The paragraph shown for every word, grouped by puzzle, as `window.WORD_INFO`. |
| `docs/how-it-works.md` | Developer guide: architecture, rules, algorithms, saved data, testing. |
| `docs/design.md` | Design guide: tokens, layout, components, states, motion, sound, copy. |
| `docs/analytics.md` | Analytics: what is tracked (Umami, cookie-free), the events, and the questions they answer. |
| `AGENTS.md` | Brief for AI coding agents: product decisions to keep, how to check changes. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Points Claude Code at `AGENTS.md`. |
| `.claude/launch.json` | Local preview server config. |

## Privacy

The game uses [Umami](https://umami.is), a cookie-free analytics service, to count visits (with approximate location: country, region and city) and gameplay events such as which puzzles are started and finished. It doesn't use cookies or collect names, emails or other personal data, and it doesn't send players' saved best times. Details are in `docs/analytics.md`. A footnote at the bottom of the game says the same.

To stop your own visits being counted, open `congph.com/wordsearch/?analytics=off` once in each browser you use (`?analytics=on` undoes it).

## Hosting and deploying

- **Host:** GitHub Pages, deploying from the `main` branch, repository root. There's no build step: the files are served as they are.
- **Address:** the repo is named `wordsearch`, and the owner's GitHub Pages site uses the custom domain `congph.com`, so this project is served at `congph.com/wordsearch/`. Renaming the repo changes the address.
- **Deploying:** **every push to `main` goes live** within a minute or two. Check changes locally before pushing.
- **Everything is public,** these docs included. GitHub Pages serves Markdown files as pages, for example `/wordsearch/docs/design.html`.
- **Players' saved data** (settings and best times) is stored per web address. Moving the game to a different domain or path starts every player fresh.

# Portal Clone

A small first-person puzzle game for the browser, inspired by Valve's *Portal*. You carry a device that fires two linked portals, and you use them to get a weighted cube onto a button to open the exit.

There are three levels, joined by elevator rides:

- **Level 01:** the basics. The cube is up on a ledge and the button is up on a platform; portals only stick to white panels.
- **Level 02:** moving things with gravity. The cube sits at the bottom of a pit you can't reach, and the button is in an alcove you can't climb into. Whatever falls into one portal falls out of the other.
- **Level 03:** the fling. A chasm separates you from the button, and nothing on the far side holds a portal. Fall far enough into one portal and you come flying out of the other. The cube has to make the trip too.

Pick any level from **Select level** on the start or pause menu. Levels you've finished are ticked (remembered in this browser). The pause menu also has **Restart level**.

The game plays in **third person** by default, with an over-the-shoulder camera that slides in when a wall is behind you and looks through a portal when you stand in front of one. **View** on the menu (or **V**) switches to first person.

When the exit door opens, step into the glass elevator. It closes, rides up its shaft as the screen fades, shows the next level's card, and brings you down into the next level.

**Play:** https://matthewcastellano99-creator.github.io/portal_clone/

It runs in a desktop browser with a mouse and keyboard, or on a phone or tablet with on-screen controls. Phones work best held sideways. It needs WebGL 2 (iOS 16.4 or later, or a recent Chrome, Firefox or Edge).

## Controls

On a phone or tablet:

| Touch | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left half of the screen | Move (the stick appears under your thumb) |
| Drag anywhere else | Look |
| Blue / orange buttons | Fire a portal (keep dragging to aim) |
| Grab | Pick up / drop the cube (it lights up when the cube is in reach) |
| Jump | Jump |
| Pause button (top left) | Pause |

With a mouse and keyboard:

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Mouse | Look |
| W A S D / arrow keys | Move |
| Space | Jump |
| Left click | Fire blue portal |
| Right click | Fire orange portal |
| E (or F) | Pick up / drop the cube |
| R | Restart the level |
| V | Switch between third and first person |
| Esc | Pause |

If the browser won't lock the mouse pointer (some embedded views), drag to look and click without dragging to fire.

Portals only stick to the **white panels**. Dark metal, the door and the cube stop a shot.

## Features

- See-through portals with recursive views (a portal can show itself inside itself).
- Momentum is kept through portals, so falling into a floor portal flings you out of a wall portal. Fast exits come out straight along the portal, and a falling body that's roughly over a floor portal is steered into it, so flings are predictable.
- Carry the cube through portals, or grab it through one. Portal shots pass through the cube, so aiming at it puts a portal under it.
- Elevator transitions between levels, with a level card while the next one loads.
- Floor button, sliding exit door and indicator lights.
- Third-person camera that collides with walls and passes through portals, or classic first person.
- A simple geometric test robot as the player, with a bouncy walk cycle and squash-and-stretch on jumps and landings.
- Ceiling lamps that light the room, drifting dust, haze, ambient occlusion (desktop) and a final colour grade.
- Everything is generated in code: textures, models, sound effects and the ambient music. There are no asset files.

## Running locally

There is no build step. Serve the folder over HTTP (ES modules don't load from `file://`):

```sh
npx http-server -c-1 .        # or: python3 -m http.server
```

Then open `http://localhost:8080` (or whichever port the server prints).

URL options:

- `?quality=low`: lower resolution, no multisampling and 2 levels of portal recursion, for weaker GPUs.
- `?quality=mobile` / `?quality=high`: force the phone or desktop settings. Phones and tablets pick `mobile` automatically, and the render resolution also adjusts itself while you play to keep the frame rate up.
- `?debug`: show an FPS and portal-render counter.

## Publishing

GitHub Pages serves the `gh-pages` branch. To update the live game after changing `main`:

```sh
git push origin main:gh-pages
```

## Tests

`tests/playthrough.mjs` loads the game in headless Chromium and plays both levels through the game's own simulation. It places portals, walks through them, carries the cube, rides the elevator to Level 02, drops the cube out of the pit and onto the alcove button, and finishes. It then throws the player and the cube through randomly placed portals in both levels and fails if anything ends up stuck inside geometry. It also fails on any page error.

```sh
npm install
npx playwright install chromium   # first time only
npm test
```

## How it works

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main.js` | Game setup, quality presets, fixed-step loop, input, cube carrying, UI |
| `src/touch.js` | On-screen touch controls |
| `src/levels.js` | The level layouts (axis-aligned boxes), their elevators, signs and lines |
| `src/level.js` | Builds a level's geometry from boxes, plus shared decoration (lamps, signs, windows) |
| `src/physics.js` | Box-vs-box collision, portal-aware collision and raycasts |
| `src/portals.js` | Portal placement and fitting, portal surface shader, teleporting |
| `src/portalRenderer.js` | Renders the view through each portal, with recursion |
| `src/player.js` | First-person movement (Source-style acceleration and friction) |
| `src/cube.js`, `src/entities.js` | Weighted cube, floor button, door, indicator lights, elevators |
| `src/gun.js`, `src/avatar.js` | The portal device and the player's robot body |
| `src/sculpt.js` | Swept-surface modelling, a panel-line texture and mesh merging for the models |
| `

Firex2200/fighter.readme:
# Fighter

A Smash-style 2D fighting game that runs in a browser — so the same game works on
a laptop, an iPhone, and an Xbox without being rebuilt for each one.

**Play it online:** https://firex2200.github.io/fighter/ — on an iPhone, open it in
Safari, tap Share → **Add to Home Screen**, and it installs like an app.

## The fighter

**Rook Ashvane — "The Wandering Storm."** A drifter from the old highway towns,
born in a thunderstorm to a village swordsmith and a storm spirit. Straw hat, long
blade, short temper. Push him far enough and the blade's edge splits open to let
the storm out — which is why it only lights up when he attacks.

Both players are Rook, told apart by costume: **Indigo**, **Ember** (red
kimono, brown hakama), **Frost** (white kimono, pale blue sash) or **Moss**
(green kimono, cream sash), picked on the costume-select screen before each
fight. His look follows the concept sheet: spiky swept-back hair with a gold
headband, wide sleeves with a cloud pattern, striped shin wraps and straw
sandals, a woven hat on his back, and his sword **Raimei** (black scabbard with a
teal stripe, cyan gem guard, lightning along the blade in storm form).

His 3D model was built in Blender from the front, side and back concept art;
costumes recolour its kimono, sleeve pattern, sash and hakama. His
stats come straight off the concept sheet (Weight 5, Ground 8, Air 7, Power 7,
Range 8, Recovery 6) — the mapping to game values is documented at the top of
`src/characters.js`.

## Play it

Double-click **Fighter** in `~/Desktop/Games`. It starts the game and opens your
browser. Double-click **Stop Fighter** in the same folder when you're done.

That's it — no Terminal needed.

<details>
<summary>Starting it manually instead</summary>

```bash
cd ~/fighter
python3 -m http.server 8010
```

Then open <http://localhost:8010>. Press `Ctrl+C` in Terminal to stop.
</details>

### Why the project lives at `~/fighter` and not in `ai-work`

macOS blocks double-clickable apps from reading files under `~/Desktop`,
`~/Documents` and `~/Downloads`, so the launcher could not start the server from
there. Sideline sits outside those folders for the same reason.

**The game uses port 8010. Sideline uses 8000.** Keep it that way — a second
service on Sideline's port makes its launcher open the wrong thing.

### Rebuilding the launcher apps

Only needed if you move or rename the project folder:

```bash
bash ~/fighter/scripts/make_launcher.sh
```

## Controls

|            | Move       | Jump | Attack | Strong | Special | Shield |
| ---------- | ---------- | ---- | ------ | ------ | ------- | ------ |
| Player 1   | `W A S D`  | `W`  | `J`    | `K`    | `L`     | `I`    |
| Player 2   | arrows     | `↑`  | `,`    | `.`    | `/`     | Right Shift |
| Controller | stick/dpad | `A`  | `X`    | `Y`    | `B`     | any bumper or trigger |

Plug in or pair any Xbox controller and it works — player 1 takes the first pad,
player 2 the second. Keyboard always keeps working alongside.

**On a phone:** with the game running, scan the QR code in the corner of the
laptop screen with your iPhone camera (same wifi). Hold the phone sideways.
Left thumb anywhere on the left half is a joystick; the right side has Jump,
Atk, Strong, Spec and Shield. Pair a controller and the buttons disappear.

**Playing alone:** player 2 is the CPU. The moment anyone presses a player-2
key or picks up a second controller, they take over for the rest of that match.

**Tapping jump gives a short hop; holding it gives a full hop.** That distinction
is the core of the movement game.

Press `H` during a match to see hitboxes (red) and hurtboxes (blue).

### Rook's moves

Hold a direction while pressing a button, like Smash.

| | On the ground | In the air |
|---|---|---|
| **Attack** | jab · up = anti-air swat · down = low sweep | nair spin · forward · back (strongest) · up · down = meteor spike |
| **Strong** | forward smash, his main kill move | same as Attack |
| **Special** | **Storm Draw** — lit-blade dash forward | same; once per jump |
| **Up + Special** | **Rising Storm** — his recovery, climbs high, then helpless until he lands or grabs the ledge | same |
| **Down + Special** | **Thunder Guard** — catch an attack and strike back harder | same |

On keyboard, `W` is both up and jump. Press `W` and an attack key together and
you get the up-move rather than a jump — Smash lets you cancel a jump's first
3 frames into an up-move, and so does this.

### Defense

- **Shield** — hold it. Blocks everything but wears down, and shrinks as it
  does. Let it run out and it breaks: you're stunned and wide open.
- **Spot dodge** — shield + down. **Roll** — shield + left/right.
- **Air dodge** — shield in the air. One per jump. Hold a direction to dash, but
  that leaves you helpless until you land.
- **Ledge** — falling past the stage edge grabs it automatically. Then press
  toward the stage to climb up, jump to leap up, or down to let go. Hang too long
  and you'll drop.

## How a match works

You don't have a health bar. Every hit raises your **damage percent**, and the
higher that number goes the further the next hit launches you. You lose a stock by
being knocked past the edge of the screen. Three stocks each, last one standing wins.

## Running the tests

```bash
cd ~/fighter
node --test test/*.test.js
```

95 tests, no installation needed, all run headlessly without a browser:
`combat` (the Ultimate formulas), `sim` (movement and physics), `moves` (every
attack connects once and launches the right way), `defense` (shield, dodges,
ledge) and `cpu` (the AI recovers, blocks, and can finish a whole match).

## How it's built

No build step, no `node_modules`, no installation. The browser loads the source
files directly. The one dependency is **Three.js** (3D graphics, MIT license) in
`vendor/three/`, committed to the repo so the game works offline.

| File                | Does                                                        |
| ------------------

# ธรรมะ ⚔ อธรรม Online

เกม 2D MMORPG บนเบราว์เซอร์ แนวยุทธภพจีน (Yulgang / Ragnarok) สองฝ่าย **ธรรมะ** (โทนขาว-ฟ้า-ทอง) และ **อธรรม** (โทนดำ-แดง)
เซิร์ฟเวอร์เป็นตัวตัดสินทุกอย่าง (authoritative) ฝั่งผู้เล่นวาดภาพด้วย Canvas

- Node.js + Express + Socket.IO · ฐานข้อมูล PostgreSQL (หรือ Supabase)
- 5 อาชีพ · เลเวล 1–130 · 7 แผนที่ล่ามอนสเตอร์ + สนามรบ PvP
- แผนที่ล่ามอนใช้ร่วมกันทั้งสองฝ่าย ฝ่ายมีผลเต็มที่ในสนามรบธรรมะ-อธรรม

---

## เริ่มใช้งาน

### รันในเครื่อง

ต้องใช้ Node.js **20.12 ขึ้นไป** (เซิร์ฟเวอร์อ่าน `.env` ด้วย `process.loadEnvFile`) และ PostgreSQL

```bash
npm install
copy .env.example .env      # แล้วใส่ DATABASE_URL
npm start                   # http://localhost:3900
npm run dev                 # รันแบบรีสตาร์ตเองเมื่อแก้โค้ด
```

### รันด้วย Docker (ใช้กับเซิร์ฟเวอร์จริง)

```bash
docker compose up -d --build   # http://localhost:3900
```

- มีสองบริการ: `db` (postgres:16-alpine) และ `game` (node:24-alpine)
- image รวมเฉพาะ `server/` `shared/` `public/` ไฟล์ภาพต้นฉบับและเครื่องมือไม่ถูกใส่ (ดู `.dockerignore`)
- **แก้โค้ดแล้วต้อง `docker compose up -d --build` ใหม่ทุกครั้ง** เกมจะรีสตาร์ต ผู้เล่นที่ออนไลน์หลุดชั่วครู่ แล้วผู้เล่นรีเฟรชหน้าเว็บหนึ่งครั้ง

### ค่าใน `.env`

| ค่า | ใช้ทำอะไร |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | ฐานข้อมูล PostgreSQL (สร้างตารางให้เองตอนเปิดครั้งแรก) |
| `SUPABASE_DB_URL` | ถ้าตั้งไว้จะใช้ฐานข้อมูลบน Supabase แทน `DATABASE_URL` (Docker ใช้ Session pooler เพราะใช้ IPv6 ไม่ได้) |
| `SUPABASE_URL` · `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` · `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` · `SUPABASE_JWKS_URL` | เชื่อม Supabase API (ห้ามใส่ secret key ในโค้ดฝั่งเบราว์เซอร์) |
| `PORT` | พอร์ตเซิร์ฟเวอร์ (ค่าเริ่มต้น 3900) |
| `GM` | ไม่ใส่ = เฉพาะบัญชี GM · `all` = ทุกคนใช้คำสั่ง GM ได้ · `0` = ปิด |
| `GM_CODE` | รหัสปลดล็อกคำสั่ง GM ในเกม (`/gmcode <รหัส>`) ไม่ตั้ง = ใช้คำสั่ง GM ไม่ได้ |
| `MAX_CHARS` | จำนวนตัวละครต่อบัญชี (ค่าเริ่มต้น 6) |

> ⚠ **ก่อนเปิดให้คนอื่นเล่นจริง อย่าใช้ `GM=all`** เพราะทุกคนจะเสกไอเทม ทอง และเลเวลได้

### บัญชีและการบันทึก

- หน้าแรก: เข้าสู่ระบบ / สมัครบัญชี → เลือกตัวละคร → สร้างตัวละครใหม่ (เลือกฝ่าย อาชีพ ชื่อ) · ช่องรหัสผ่านมีปุ่มแสดงรหัส · รีเฟรชแล้วไม่ต้องล็อกอินใหม่ (โทเคน 30 วัน)
- เปลี่ยนรหัสผ่านได้ในหน้าเลือกตัวละคร (อุปกรณ์อื่นจะถูกออกจากระบบ) · ในเกมมีปุ่มสลับตัวละครโดยไม่ต้องล็อกอินใหม่
- ตาราง: `accounts` (รหัสผ่านแบบ scrypt · `is_gm`) · `sessions` (เก็บเฉพาะ sha256 ของโทเคน) · `characters` (เซฟทั้งก้อนใน `data` JSONB) · `meta`
- ตัวละครอยู่ในหน่วยความจำ เขียนลงฐานข้อมูลทุก 20 วินาที ตอนผู้เล่นออก และตอนปิดเซิร์ฟเวอร์ (`server/store.js`)
- ตัวละครเก่าจาก `data/players.json` ถูกนำเข้าครั้งเดียว ผูกเข้าบัญชีได้ในหน้าเลือกตัวละคร (ใครผูกก่อนได้ก่อน)

---

## อาชีพ

| อาชีพ | อาวุธ | บทบาท | รายละเอียด |
|---|---|---|---|
| ดาบคู่ | ดาบคู่ | ประชิด ฟันรัว คริติคอล ตีหมู่บางสกิล | [docs/dualblade-design.md](docs/dualblade-design.md) |
| นักพรต | แส้ | เวทระยะไกล ฮีลหมู่ บัพ (ยืนร่ายบนพื้น บัพเป็นแสงรอบตัว) | [docs/taoist-v2.md](docs/taoist-v2.md) |
| นักธนู | ธนู | ยิงไกล บัพคริ/ตีไว | [docs/archer-design.md](docs/archer-design.md) |
| ทวน | ทวน | ประชิด คอมโบ ATK สูง มีท่ากวาดหมู่ | [docs/spearman.md](docs/spearman.md) |
| นักรบแนวหน้า | ดาบและโล่ | แทงค์ HP/เกราะสูง ยั่วยุ ลดดาเมจ คุ้มกันปาร์ตี้ | [docs/warrior-v3.md](docs/warrior-v3.md) |

- อาชีพละ 11 สกิล: สกิลปกติ 9 ช่อง (ปุ่ม 1–9) + มหาวิชา Lv.120/130 อีก 2 ช่อง (ปุ่ม 0 / −) · ทุก 10 เลเวลได้สกิลใหม่หรือพัฒนาสกิลเดิม (แรงขึ้น 30% ต่อขั้น) · ตารางเต็มใน [docs/class-skills.md](docs/class-skills.md)
- ไอเทมช่องอาวุธใช้ร่วมกันทุกอาชีพ (ค่าพลังเท่ากัน) แต่แต่ละอาชีพเห็นชื่อ ไอคอน และรูปทรงอาวุธของตัวเอง (`C.setViewClass`)
- **นักรบแนวหน้า:** สกิลยั่วยุ "คำรามท้าศึก" (คูลดาวน์ 6 วินาที ดึงมอนทุกตัวรอบตัวระยะ 300/340/380 ตามขั้น) มอนตีเราต่อหลังหมดผล ไม่ให้ EXP หรือดาเมจปลอม · พาสซีฟ "โล่หนาม" สะท้อนดาเมจ 8% (25% ตอนตั้งโล่เหล็ก · PvP ครึ่งเดียว) · พาสซีฟ "โล่รับแทน" เพื่อนในปาร์ตี้ระยะ 300 โดนตี นักรบรับแทน 30% (PvP 15% · บัพโล่ของนักรบลดส่วนที่รับ · หยุดรับแทนเมื่อ HP นักรบต่ำกว่า 30%) · ท่าไม้ตาย 0 / - "โล่พิทักษ์ทลายแนว" 700% และ "ป้อมปราการถล่มฟ้า" 1100% · "สัตย์พิทักษ์" และ "ดาบมหาปราการ" ย้ายเป็นสกิลเสริม (ไม่มีปุ่มประจำ ตั้งปุ่มเองในคัมภีร์วิชา)
- เอฟเฟกต์สกิลอลังการขึ้นตามแต้มสกิล ขั้นวิวัฒนาการ และเลเวล ดู [docs/skill-redesign.md](docs/skill-redesign.md) · [docs/skill-performance.md](docs/skill-performance.md)

### รูปลักษณ์ตามเลเวล

ทุกอาชีพเปลี่ยนรูปลักษณ์ที่เลเวลเดียวกัน (`ModelTiers.LEVELS`) ผู้เล่นคนอื่นเห็นเหมือนกัน

| เลเวล | สิ่งที่เปลี่ยน |
|---|---|
| 15 | สีผมเปลี่ยน |
| 30 | ผมยาวขึ้น (ทรงผมยาวของอาชีพ) |
| 50 | สีผมขั้นสูง + มงกุฎ / พู่หมวก |
| 60 | ปีกคู่แรก |
| 80 | ปีกใหญ่ขอบทอง |
| 100 | ปีกสองคู่ + รัศมี (ธรรมะ) / เขาเทพมาร (อธรรม) + ออร่าอาชีพ |
| 130 | ร่างสุดท้าย: เทพเซียน (จานสุริยะ ปีกสามคู่) / เทพมาร (เปลวมาร ปีกพังผืด) |

ชุดเกราะบนตัวละครเปลี่ยนสีและลายตามชุดที่สวมจริงทีละชิ้น อาวุธในมือเปลี่ยนตามขั้นอาวุธ เกรดไอเทมเป็นเส้นแสงขอบตัวและออร่า ค่าตีบวกเป็นแสงและสายฟ้าบนอาวุธ ดู [docs/class-aura.md](docs/class-aura.md) · [docs/equipment-aura.md](docs/equipment-aura.md)

| ปุ่ม | การกระทำ |
|---|---|
| คลิกพื้น | เดินไปจุดนั้น (หาทางเลี่ยงสิ่งกีดขวางเอง) · กดค้าง = เดินตามเมาส์ |

| 1 หรือ Space | โจมตีปกติ: เดินเข้าไปตีเป้าจนตาย (ไม่มีเป้า = เลือกตัวใกล้สุด) |
| 2–9 · 0 · − | สกิลตามที่วางในคัมภีร์วิชา |

| F | เปิดร้าน / ศิลาเคลื่อนย้ายที่ยืนอยู่ใกล้ |
| I หรือ B | กระเป๋าและอุปกรณ์ |
| C | แต้มสถานะ |
| K | คัมภีร์วิชา (เรียน/พัฒนาสกิล) |
| O | กล่องบอทล่าอัตโนมัติ |
| M | แผนที่ใหญ่ + คู่มือดรอป |
| P | ผู้เล่นออนไลน์ |
| R | อันดับผู้เล่น |
| G | ระดมทุนทั้งเซิร์ฟ |
| U | เปิด/ปิด PvP นอกสนามรบ (Lv.20+) |
| L | ซ่อน/แสดงแชท |
| Enter | แชท (`/f` ฝ่าย · `/p` ปาร์ตี้) |
| H | วิธีเล่น |

# حديقة الأسرار

تطبيق قصة تعليمية بصوت الأسرة. ملف واحد `web/index.html` يحوي كل شيء.

## كيف تحصل على التطبيقات
بعد رفع المستودع إلى GitHub، يبني GitHub تلقائيًا عند كل تعديل:
- **Android APK**: Actions → آخر تشغيل → Artifacts → `Hadeeqa-android-apk`. ثبّته على الهاتف (فعّل «مصادر غير معروفة»).
- **Windows**: Artifacts → `Hadeeqa-windows` → ملف `.exe` محمول لا يحتاج تثبيتًا، وملف تثبيت.
- **نسخة ويب قابلة للتثبيت (PWA)**: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions. الرابط يعمل على أي جهاز بما فيه iPhone، ويُثبَّت من «إضافة إلى الشاشة الرئيسية».

## تحديث التطبيق
استبدل `web/index.html` بالنسخة الجديدة وارفع التغيير؛ تُبنى النسخ كلها من جديد.

## ملاحظة
الـ APK موقّع بمفتاح تطوير (debug)؛ يصلح للأسرة ولا يصلح لمتجر Google Play. للنشر في المتجر يلزم مفتاح توقيع خاص.

ngfamclam-cpu/kings-cup.readme:
# King's Cup

King's Cup without a deck of cards. Pass one phone around the table, or mirror it to the TV.

- **Play in the browser:** https://ngfamclam-cpu.github.io/kings-cup/
- **Android app (APK):** https://github.com/ngfamclam-cpu/kings-cup/releases/latest/download/kings-cup.apk

## Features

- Shuffled 52-card deck, rule shown for every card, King counter (4th King ends the game)
- Optional player names with turn reminders
- Question Master and Jack rules stay on screen
- House rules editor: change any card, saved on the device
- Landscape / TV layout with big text, fullscreen, and a screen that stays on
- Works offline once loaded, and resumes the game after an accidental refresh
- Age gate on first launch

## Playing on a TV

Mirror the phone (Android Quick Settings → *Cast* / *Smart View*; iPhone Control Center → *Screen Mirroring*), then turn it sideways. On a laptop, use Chrome's *Cast…* menu and press **F** for fullscreen. **Space** or **Enter** draws a card.

## Installing the APK

Download it on the phone, open it, and allow "install unknown apps" for your browser when Android asks.

The APK is signed with a throwaway debug key that changes on every build, so to install a newer version you have to **uninstall the old one first**. Fixing that needs a permanent signing key (a good next step).

## Project layout

```
www/            the whole game: plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step
  index.html    screens and dialogs
  app.js        game logic
  rules.js      default card rules
  styles.css    phone + TV layouts
  sw.js         offline cache (bump VERSION when files change)
.github/workflows/
  pages.yml     publishes www/ to GitHub Pages on every push to main
  android.yml   wraps www/ with Capacitor and builds the APK
```

## Making changes

Edit files in `www/`, then test locally with any static server, for example:

```bash
py -m http.server 8080 --directory www
```

Push to `main` and the web version updates in a minute or two. To publish a new APK release:

```bash
git tag v0.1.1
git push origin v0.1.1
```

## Credits

Card faces are drawn with CSS and Unicode suit symbols, so there are no third-party art licenses to worry about.

luisboch/palheta-e-baqueta.readme:
# Palheta & Baqueta

Jogo de ritmo para até 2 jogadores, com Cordas (violão e guitarra), baixo e bateria, feito para o Steam
Deck. Você traz os seus MP3s num pendrive. O backend separa os instrumentos com IA e gera as
notas em 4 dificuldades (Fácil, Médio, Difícil e Muito difícil). O jogo, em Godot 4, toca a
música com uma pista 3D por jogador.

> Em construção: o andamento por fase está em [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md).

## Arquitetura

```
pendrive/palheta/*.mp3 ─(menu do jogo)─► data/input ─► worker (Python) ─► data/library/<id>/ ─► jogo (Godot)
                                                          │ data/events.jsonl (fila, progresso)      ▲
                                                          └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Backend** (`pbq/`, Python): importação, separação de stems, transcrição, charts e cache.
  Roda como um worker em segundo plano, em prioridade baixa.
- **Jogo** (`godot/`, Godot 4): só lê a biblioteca e os eventos, e roda o jogo.
- Os dois conversam **só por arquivos**. Detalhes em [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)
  e decisões em [docs/adr/](docs/adr/README.md).

## Instalar o jogo (Debian, Ubuntu)

Baixe o `.deb` da [página de releases](https://github.com/luisboch/palheta-e-baqueta/releases)
e instale com `sudo apt install ./palheta-e-baqueta_<versão>_amd64.deb`. Na primeira vez que o
jogo abre, ele instala a IA do backend (alguns GB, precisa de internet) em
`~/.local/share/palheta-e-baqueta`, onde também ficam as músicas. Só Linux por enquanto
([ADR 0018](docs/adr/0018-pacote-deb.md)). Para montar o pacote localmente:
`scripts/package_deb.sh` (precisa dos templates de exportação do Godot e do `dpkg-deb`).

## Instalação (desenvolvimento)

Requisitos:
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`);
- `ffmpeg` com libvorbis;
- git;
- Godot na versão de `scripts/versions.env`. O script procura em `$GODOT_BIN`, em
  `~/Applications/Godot_v<versão>-stable_linux.x86_64` e no `PATH`.

```bash
scripts/setup.sh     # .venv com Python fixado, GdUnit4, importação do projeto Godot, pre-commit
```

O `uv` baixa sozinho o Python de `.python-version` (3.12), sem depender do Python do sistema.

## Uso

```bash
cp config.example.toml config.toml   # opcional: só para mudar algum ajuste
uv run pbq process                   # processa agora o que estiver em data/input
uv run pbq status                    # estado de cada música, por etapa
uv run pbq watch                     # worker em segundo plano (o jogo inicia sozinho)
uv run pbq drive list                # pendrives montados (o menu do jogo usa os comandos drive)
```

Todos os comandos e o que o jogo lê estão em [docs/backend-protocol.md](docs/backend-protocol.md).

### Jogar

Abra `godot/project.godot` no editor e aperte **F5** (ou rode `$(scripts/godot.sh) --path godot`).
O jogo abre no menu:

- **Jogar**: lista de músicas prontas → instrumento (os que não tocam na música ficam
  desabilitados) → dificuldade → Jogar. "Editar nome" corrige título e artista.
- **Pendrive**: escolha o pendrive e a ação: trazer os MP3s novos de `palheta/` (eles são
  processados sozinhos, com o andamento embaixo do menu), importar músicas prontas ou salvar a
  biblioteca no pendrive. Nada é lido antes de você escolher ([ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-pendrive-pelo-menu.md)).
- Menus: setas/direcional e `Enter`/A; `Esc`/B volta.
- Partida: trastes `1`–`5` (ou `A S D F G`); a nota toca ao apertar o traste, sem palhetada
  ([ADR 0015](docs/adr/0015-tocar-no-traste-sem-palhetada.md)). Bateria: bumbo `Espaço`, pads
  `H J K L`. Controle: trastes A B Y X LB. `Esc`/Start pausa (Continuar, Recomeçar, Sair da
  música); apertar o botão Steam também pausa.
- No modo desktop do Deck, o Steam converte os controles em teclado e mouse e o jogo não vê o
  controle: use um teclado ou rode pelo Steam.
- A música toca do começo ao fim; o instrumento escolhido baixa 18 dB a cada erro e volta no
  acerto. Numa música só de Cordas (como uma de violão e voz), errar deixa quase só a voz.

### No Steam Deck, modo jogo

```bash
scripts/steamdeck/install.sh   # confere o que falta e cria o atalho (pode rodar de novo)
```

Depois, no modo desktop: Steam → Jogos → "Adicionar jogo não-Steam à biblioteca" → marque
"Palheta & Baqueta". No modo jogo o controle funciona direto (A B Y X LB tocam, Start pausa).
O lançador (`scripts/steamdeck/palheta.sh`) acerta o PATH, que no modo jogo não tem o Homebrew
(o worker precisa do ffmpeg dele), e grava a saída em `data/game.log`. O ícone é desenhado por
`scripts/steamdeck/make_icon.gd`.

Para depurar uma partida sem o menu (F6 em `godot/game/play.tscn`, ou pela linha de comando):

```bash
$(scripts/godot.sh) --path godot res://game/play.tscn -- --song data/library/<id> \
    --instrument strings --difficulty Hard --autoplay 1
```

`--autoplay 1` toca sozinho; sem `--song`, abre a música com mais instrumentos.

As etapas de IA precisam dos extras: `uv sync --extra dev --extra ai` (torch CPU e Demucs;
~1,5 GB). O modelo baixa no primeiro uso (~80 MB).

## Testes

```bash
scripts/test.sh                     # tudo que é rápido: Python (cobertura ≥ 80%) + GDScript
scripts/test.sh python -k config    # só Python, com argumentos do pytest
scripts/test.sh godot               # só GDScript (GdUnit4, headless)
scripts/test.sh coverage            # cobertura do GDScript (≥ 80%)
uv run pytest -m slow --no-cov      # modelos de IA reais (minutos)
uv run pre-commit run --all-files   # ruff, mypy, gdformat, gdlint, documentação viva
```

Estratégia de testes e cobertura: [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md).

## Estrutura

```
pbq/            backend Python (CLI `pbq`)
tools/          ferramentas de desenvolvimento (documentação viva)
tests/          testes Python
godot/core/     lógica do jogo em classes puras (testáveis)
godot/tests/    testes GdUnit4
scripts/        setup, testes, versões fixadas
docs/           arquitetura, ADRs, roadmap, testes, armadilhas
```

# Rink Rat Mayhem

A 3-on-3 mutant hockey brawler that runs in your browser. Lead the Rink Rats through seven cursed arenas, win one-period challenges to earn XP, and unlock stranger power-ups along the way.

**Play it:** https://ennywnad.github.io/rink-rat-mayhem/

![Rink Rat Mayhem gameplay](assets/screenshot.jpg)

## Features

- **Seven challenges**, each one period with its own arena, hazards and objective: Opening Night, Hot Hands, Body Count, Brick Wall, Gravity Well, Shorthanded and the Mayhem Cup Final. Bonus objectives earn up to three stars each.
- **Progression:** XP unlocks 12 power-ups and more loadout slots. The power-ups are Rocket Skates, Oil Slick, Fireball Puck, Land Mine, Magnet Stick, Shrink Ray, Ice Wall, Heat-Seeker, Kaiju Mode, Split Shot, Thunderstrike and Deep Freeze.
- **Skill stick:** move your stick with the right stick to stickhandle and poke-check. Pull it back and flick it forward to shoot.
- **Face the net:** hold LT (F on the keyboard) and your skater keeps their body square to the goal they're attacking, whichever way they skate: circle the net, drift sideways or skate backwards (a little slower) and stay ready to shoot.
- **One-timers and dekes:** press shoot while a pass is on its way to fire it straight off the pass. The deke button does a toe drag toward wherever the right stick points, or a between-the-legs move with the stick centred; defenders in front get fooled for a moment.
- **Versus mode:** full exhibition games from the locker room. P1 vs P2, P1 + P2 vs the CPU, or P1 alone vs the CPU. Pick the opponent team, arena, 2 or 3 skaters a side, 1–3 periods of 2, 3 or 5 minutes, CPU skill and the rules. Ties go to sudden-death overtime.
- **Game stats:** goals, shots, saves, hits, knockouts, possession, passing, takeaways, one-timers, dekes and power-ups for both teams, with goals by period. Shown at every intermission, at the final horn, on challenge results and from the pause menu.
- **Ice resurfacers:** every arena has its own machine that drives out of the ice crew tunnel mid-game, laps the rink and goes home, without waiting for an intermission: The Grave Digger (a hearse hauling a coffin), The Slag Hauler, The Ore Crawler, The Muck Sucker, The Moon Buggy, The Log Skidder and The Angler. Pucks carom off it, the front end flattens anyone it catches, and it honks at skaters in its way. Behind it is a strip of fresh ice that's faster for skaters and pucks for about 24 seconds. It also freezes over open water, scrubs sludge puddles and sets off mines. Turn it off with the **Ice resurfacer** rule.
- **Arena organ:** the only music is a ballpark-style organ: a charge before the opening faceoff, rallies when the Rats press, a fanfare for goals, a sad slide when the other team scores, noodles at stoppages and a loop under the menus and intermissions.
- **Two players on one screen:** co-op (both on the Rats) or versus (P1 Rats vs P2) in Versus mode or practice, and co-op in any challenge. Play with two controllers, a keyboard and a controller, or both on one keyboard.
- **Power-up badges:** an icon over whoever holds the team's power-up, and a timer ring around players with an active effect.
- **Instant replays:** after each goal, the last few seconds replay with a slow-motion moment at the goal and a low camera by the net. Shoot or pass to skip; turn them off under Accessibility.
- **Practice rink:** choose 0–3 opponents, 0–2 teammates, the goalies, the opponents' effort and the clock. Drill opponents carry the puck, lob it up ice, then back off or loop behind their net.
- **Rules and sliders:** turn icing, faceoffs after goals, checking, knockouts, hazards, the ice resurfacer and power-ups on or off. Tune speed, acceleration, shot power, checking, puck control and goalie for each team from 50% to 150%. These work in practice and in the regular challenges.
- **Live stoppages:** players skate to the faceoff dot after goals and icings instead of teleporting, and coasting skaters sometimes lift a skate.
- **Comic-book 3D arena:** cel shading and ink outlines, a crowd of mutant fans in team colors that cheers when its team scores, WebGPU by default with a WebGL2 fallback, plus a classic top-down 2D view.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Controller | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skate | WASD / arrow keys | Left stick / D-pad | Drag on the left side |
| Stickhandle, poke-check | I J K L | Right stick | — |
| Skill shot | Hold K (back), then tap I | Pull the right stick back, then flick it forward | — |
| Shoot (hold to wind up) / body-check | Space | A / RT | Shoot button |
| Pass / switch player | Shift | X / LB | Pass button |
| Face the net (hold) | F | LT | Face button |
| Deke | Q | Y / R3 | — |
| Power-up | E | B / RB | Power button |
| Pause | P / Esc | Start / Menu | Pause button |
| Feel tuning panel | ` (backtick) | Pause menu | Pause menu |
| Mute / unmute | M | Pause menu | Speaker button |

Controllers use the standard browser gamepad mapping (Xbox, PlayStation and Switch Pro all work). The on-screen controls strip shows the buttons for whatever you're using. The right stick follows the camera.

Every key and controller button can be changed under **Controls** in the locker room or the pause menu.

### Two players

Open **Versus** in the locker room for full games, pick **2P co-op** or **2P versus** in practice, or **2P co-op** on a challenge screen. Devices are assigned automatically:

| Connected | Player 1 | Player 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two controllers | Controller 1 (+ keyboard) | Controller 2 |
| One controller | Keyboard | Controller |
| None | Left side of the keyboard: WASD skate, F shoot, G pass, R power-up, Q deke, E face the net | Right side: arrows skate, / shoot, . pass, , power-up, ; deke, ' face the net |

P1 is marked amber and P2 cyan.

## Accessibility

The **Accessibility** card in the locker room has a color-blind friendly team palette (Rats in amber and black, every opponent in blue and white, health bars blue
