999novanity4life-glitch/OmegaDev.readme:
# OmegaDev

An AI game studio for Roblox, run by a team of Claude Code agents, with a local
control room to watch them and approve their work.

- **14 agents** in `.claude/agents/`: Lead, Pulse, Architect, Builder, Scenic,
  Frame, Librarian, Balance, Splash, Playtest, Kid Tester, Producer, LiveOps,
  Code Reviewer.
- **Control room** (`control-room/`), organised for beginners: **Start here** (Today, Guide),
  **Make games** (Game ideas with a Build-this-one button, My games), **The team** (Who's working,
  Work queue), **Check work** (Review) and **Learn** (Library: the vault playbook, `docs/rulebooks/`,
  `docs/research/` and `kits/`, searchable, with NEW tags). Plus Ask the Lead and Pause all.
- **Kits** (`kits/`): playtested building blocks to reuse (themed skills + VFX, 3D tilt menu).
- **Vault** (`vault/`): the studio's design rules, chapters 00–13. Open the
  folder in Obsidian if you like; it's plain Markdown.
- **Template** (`template/`): Rojo + strict Luau game skeleton with tests.
  Every game in `games/` starts as a copy of it.
- **CI**: format, lint, strict types, Lune tests and a Rojo build for the
  template and every game, plus a control-room smoke test.

## One-time setup (Windows or macOS)
1. Install Roblox Studio, Node 18+, and Claude Code (`npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, then `claude` to log in).
2. Install Rokit: https://github.com/rojo-rbx/rokit, then in this folder run `rokit install`.
3. `rojo plugin install` to add the Rojo plugin to Studio.
4. Download Roblox types for the type checker:
   `curl -sSfLo globalTypes.d.luau https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JohnnyMorganz/luau-lsp/main/scripts/globalTypes.d.luau`
5. Turn on Studio's MCP server: Assistant → … → Manage MCP Servers → "Enable Studio as MCP server",
   then Quick connect → Claude Code. The agents expect the server to be named `Roblox_Studio`;
   if Quick connect names it differently, copy `.mcp.json.example` to `.mcp.json` instead
   (Windows command: `cmd.exe /c %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat`).

## Daily use
```
node scripts/omega.mjs room                  # control room at http://localhost:4321
node scripts/omega.mjs lead                  # one Lead cycle
node scripts/omega.mjs lead --cycles 20      # keep going (e.g. overnight), 2 min apart
node scripts/omega.mjs pause                 # or the Pause all button
```
For a game in progress, keep Studio open on its place with `rojo serve` running
in `games/<slug>/` so Playtest can test it.

`.claude/settings.json` pre-approves the safe commands the agents need
(omega, rojo, selene, stylua, luau-lsp, lune, git status/diff/add/commit, the
Studio MCP), so cycles can run without you clicking "allow". Review it before
running overnight. Pushing to GitHub and publishing to Roblox stay manual.

## Publishing
Run the **Publish** workflow by hand with the game folder name. Put
`universeId` and `placeId` in `games/<slug>/game.json` and the repo secret
`ROBLOX_API_KEY` (scope `universe-places:write`). Publish `Saved` first.

## Honest limits
- Agents can't make painted art; Splash captures real gameplay and writes
  prompts for your image tool.
- Studio's device emulator and Roblox uploads need your Studio session.
- "Builds games while you sleep" depends on Studio staying open and the MCP
  connected; check the Review and Home tabs in the morning, not just the log.

See `docs/RESEARCH.md` (sources), `docs/VIDEO_ANALYSIS.md` (the TikTok setup
this matches) and `docs/QUALITY_CHECKLIST.md` (shipping gate).

# Lesson 7. Is This Your Jacket? — 말하기 연습 웹 앱

초등 4학년 정보 차(Information Gap) 활동지 「물건의 주인이 누구인지 친구에게 물어보기」를
혼자서도 연습할 수 있게 만든 웹 앱입니다. 활동지의 6개 물건과 색깔을 그대로 사용합니다.

| 물건 | coat | dress | jacket | T-shirt | bag | belt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 내 물건 색깔 (활동지 색 막대) | red | yellow | blue | green | black | orange |

## 기능
1. **내 물건 고르기** – 학생마다 활동지의 Me 위치가 달라서, 내 활동지에서 Me라고 적힌 물건 2개를 고릅니다.
   나머지 4개는 자동으로 "내 물건이 아닌 것"이 됩니다. (선택은 브라우저에 저장됩니다)
   핵심 표현 세 가지를 원어민 음성(TTS)으로 들을 수 있습니다.
2. **Me 물건 연습** – 내 물건 2개로 연습합니다.
   - 질문: *Is this your coat?*
   - 대답: *Yes, it's mine.*
3. **내 물건 아닌 것 연습** – 나머지 4개로 연습합니다.
   - 질문: *Is this your dress?*
   - 대답: *No, it's not. My dress is yellow.*

②·③ 공통: 물건을 누르면 **질문과 대답이 한 화면에 함께** 나오고, 대화 전체를 원어민 음성으로 들려줍니다.
질문 줄과 대답 줄마다 🔊 듣기와 🎙️ 말하기가 있어서, 녹음하면 음성 인식으로 **정확도 점수(0~100)** 와
단어별 결과(초록·노랑·빨강)를 보여 줍니다. 내 녹음 다시 듣기, 물건별 최고 점수 표시(★ 70점 이상).

## 사용 방법
- 별도 설치 없이 정적 파일(`index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`, `images/`)만으로 동작합니다.
- 마이크는 **https** 주소(또는 `localhost`)에서만 쓸 수 있습니다. GitHub Pages로 배포하면 바로 사용할 수 있어요.
  (저장소 Settings → Pages → Branch 선택 → 저장)
- 로컬에서 실행: `python3 -m http.server` 후 `http://localhost:8000` 접속.
- 음성 인식(정확도 측정)은 **Chrome / Edge / Safari** 에서 지원됩니다. 인식에 인터넷 연결이 필요합니다.
  지원하지 않는 브라우저에서는 녹음·듣기만 가능합니다.

## 채점 방식
음성 인식 결과(후보 최대 5개)와 목표 문장을 단어 단위로 맞춰 보고(it's = it is, T-shirt 표기 차이 등 정규화),
맞은 단어 비율로 점수를 매깁니다. 비슷하지만 다른 단어는 반 점, 불필요하게 많은 단어는 약간 감점됩니다.
90점↑ Excellent, 70점↑ Great, 50점↑ Good try.

dj-qwik/ether-road.readme:
# Ether Road

A neon survival race for 2–4 players in the browser, somewhere between Tempest and S.T.U.N. Runner. Every racer
rolls a glowing sphere down the inside of their own see-through pipe; the pipes braid round each other in a 3D
void, so you always see where the others are. Slide left and right round the pipe wall to dodge the spikes, grab a
weapon from the pickup caches, and use it. **Last sphere alive wins 90% of the pot**, escrowed in ETH on **Robinhood Chain** (testnet `46630` now, mainnet `4663` later). Wallets via
**Privy** (Google or email sign-in only), multiplayer on **Render**. A race lasts **at most 60 seconds**.

Built on the Hot Shots stack: the same escrow, co-signers, Privy bridge and server-authoritative netcode, with a
new deterministic race simulation and a three.js renderer.

## Running it live (Render)

`render.yaml` is a Render Blueprint (testnet, branch `main`; every push redeploys).

1. Render → **New → Blueprint** → this repo. It creates `ether-road-game` (web service) and `ether-road-db`
   (Postgres). Render generates every secret; nobody ever sees a private key.
2. `OWNER_ADDRESS` is already set to `0x9944…1a1D` in `render.yaml`: it receives the 10% house fee and is the
   escrow's guardian (can pause or veto a result).
3. Open **`/status`** on the deployed site. Send ~0.05 testnet ETH to the server wallet shown there
   ([Robinhood faucet](https://faucet.testnet.chain.robinhood.com/)). The server deploys the escrow, registers its
   two result co-signers, and opens paid races.
4. Privy dashboard (app `cmvjh7ag7002t0gidfxh6eq57`): production app, **Allowed origins** = the Render URL,
   login methods **Google + email** only.

### Switching to mainnet after testing
Set `CHAIN_ID=4663` and add `ALLOW_RAW_KEYS_ON_MAINNET=i-understand` (the "lean launch" Hot Shots runs: the server
deploys the instant-payout escrow, makes `OWNER_ADDRESS` guardian + treasury and starts handing it the admin role;
accept with `acceptDefaultAdminTransfer()` after 2 days). The server wallet has the same address on both chains;
fund it with ~0.005 ETH. After the first boot pin `ESCROW_ADDRESS` + `ESCROW_DEPLOY_BLOCK`, and move Postgres to a
paid plan. With this setup whoever controls the Render account controls results of races in progress; the hardened
path (Safe admin, KMS keys, co-signers on separate infrastructure, an audit) is described in `contracts/README.md`.

## The race

| | |
|---|---|
| Control | Your ball rides the inside wall of a pipe with 16 positions round it. **← / → or A / D** step one position (67 ms per step; hold for 110 ms and it keeps sliding all the way round). **Space** fires the cannon or uses whatever you are holding. Controller: d-pad, left stick or L1/R1 step, **✕ (PlayStation) / A (Xbox)** uses. Touch: hold the left or right half of the screen, USE button for items. |
| Speed | The game's, never the player's: 20 u/s at the start, +0.25 u/s per second, 35 u/s at the cap. Only strips you choose and items change it. |
| Course | Built from the race seed (two committed random draws). One hazard: **red spikes** on the pipe wall: rings with one opening, twin rings with two, rows of spike clusters to weave through, and long spiral sleeves with a glowing channel that twists round the pipe. Openings tighten and jump further as the race goes on. **Electrified plates** (from 8 s until the final collapse, about six a race): a yellow arc of the wall (4–6 positions in the first half, 5–8 after) that pulses on a steady rhythm, live for 2 beats and dead for 2 (0.83 s each), flickering for 0.3 s before it goes live. Live, it kills like spikes. Half are *bluffs* (lying across the safe line but dead the whole time a racer on the game's pace is on them) and half are *live* (covering where you are, live the whole time you'd pass: get off). They run on the race clock, so everyone on the game's pace meets them in the same state; a strip, a hit or ether boost puts you off the beat, so read the pulse. Every racer gets the same course in their own pipe. A flawless driver must be able to finish every course or it is rebuilt. |
| Pacing | The first half is a warm-up: wide openings, slow twists, small plates (about 7% of good players are out before 30 s). From 30 s the squeeze is on, and the **final collapse** at 48 s narrows the openings to one or two positions. First elimination typically around 42 s; most races are decided before the cap. Every trap leaves a way through: a flawless driver must be able to finish every course or it is rebuilt, a plate never covers more than half the pipe, and a live plate always leaves time to get off it. |
| Tracks | Six, dealt from a shuffled deck: **Nebula Run**, **Ion Helix**, **Solar Canyon**, **Prism Cathedral**, **Vector Storm**, **Signal Ghost**. Each has its own pipe shapes, look and mix of spike patterns; the difficulty schedule is the same on all of them. |
| Equal pipes | Every racer's pipe has its own curves, but all pipes are exactly as long as each other: a pipe that comes out shorter gets long, low swells (about one per 240 u), solved to match, and every pipe is spaced evenly by length, so equal track distance means equal pipe length everywhere and every ball moves at the same speed along its pipe. The pipes never touch (closest 5.9 u between centre lines; pipes are 4.4 u wide), and they're smooth: no pipe turns more than 15° in 4 u (actual worst 8.5°). The camera rides a smoothed line through your pipe on top of that. `tools/tracks.mjs` checks all of it. |
| Pickups | Come in **caches**: 2–3 different items side by side round the pipe, about six caches a race. Roll over the one you want; the rest of that cache vanishes for you, so racers end up carrying different things by choice. What's in each cache and when caches come up are drawn at random from the race seed, and every racer meets the same caches at the same spots. |
| Items | **Cannon** (2 shots: blows away the next spike group on your position, for you) · **Burst** (an e

# Jungle Tag

A Gorilla Tag–inspired jungle tag game for **Windows PC with keyboard and mouse**, made in **Godot 4.3** (free and open source).
Run, knuckle-sprint, climb giant trees, swing from vines, camouflage into the leaves, and tag your friends.

Everything in the game (the map, the gorilla characters, animations, sounds and music) is generated by the project's own code, so there are no third-party assets to license.

---

## 1. Running the game on Windows

1. Download **Godot 4.3 (Standard, not .NET)** for Windows from <https://godotengine.org/download/archive/4.3-stable/>.
   It is a single `.exe` with no installer. Unzip it anywhere.
2. Unzip `jungle-tag.zip` to a folder, for example `C:\Games\jungle-tag`.
3. Start `Godot_v4.3-stable_win64.exe`. In the Project Manager click **Import**, browse to the folder and pick `project.godot`, then click **Import & Edit**.
4. The first time it opens, Godot imports the sounds (a few seconds). Then press **F5** (or the ▶ Play button, top right) to play.

> Newer Godot 4.x versions (4.4, 4.5) also open the project. Godot may offer to upgrade the project; click OK.

### Quick test checklist

| Feature | How to test |
|---|---|
| Movement | `W A S D`, mouse look, `Shift` sprint, `Space` jump, `Ctrl` crouch. Sprint then jump to see momentum carry. |
| Climbing | Walk up to a big tree, look at the trunk and **hold Left or Right mouse**. `W/S` climb up/down, `A/D` circle the trunk. **Alternate left and right clicks** to pull yourself up faster. `Space` = wall-jump off toward where you look. Let go of both buttons (or `Ctrl`) to drop. |
| Branches | Look up at a branch from underneath and hold a mouse button to **hang**. Move along it with `WASD`, press `Space` to pull up on top. You can also simply land on branches and walk along them. |
| Vines | Jump toward a hanging vine and press **E**. Use `W/A/S/D` to pump the swing and build speed. Press **E** or **Space** to let go and launch (Space adds a hop). Chain from vine to vine. |
| Camouflage | Press **G**. Your gorilla fades into a green/brown leaf pattern (with a leaf burst and sound). The bottom-right meter shows time left (15 s max) and then the 20 s cooldown. Moving fast lowers the “% hidden” number. Press G again to end it early. |
| Hiding | Bushes, tree canopies, the cave (west side), the secret tunnel out of the back of the cave, the hollow log, treehouses, and the ledge **behind the waterfall** at the north cliff. |
| HUD | Name, mode, gorilla count (top-left), round timer (top), role badge (top-right), camo meter (bottom-right). Hold **Tab** for the scoreboard. |
| Bananas | Eat 10, then press **F** for 30 seconds of double sprint speed. |
| Camera | **V** switches between third person and first person. Hold **B** for **binoculars** and scroll the mouse wheel to zoom in or out. |
| Pause | **Esc** (solo games actually pause). Settings are in the pause menu too. |

---

## 2. Main menu

* **Play** starts a solo match immediately. AI gorillas fill the empty slots so you can play alone.
* **Host Game** opens an online lobby (optionally a **private room** with a password).
* **Join Game** joins a friend with their **room code** (or an IP address).
* **Player Count** cycles 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 players.
* **Settings**: graphics preset (Low/Medium/High/Ultra), fullscreen, V-Sync, FPS cap, render scale, view distance, vegetation density, shadows, ambient occlusion, glow, FPS counter, mouse sensitivity, invert Y, FOV and four volume sliders.
* **Quit**.

The right side of the menu is the **Match Setup**: your username, your gorilla colour (with a 3D preview), game mode, round time, player count, number of AI gorillas or “fill empty slots with AI”.

## 3. Game modes

* **Classic Tag**: one random gorilla starts as IT (or more, see **Taggers** below). Touching someone makes them IT (they're stunned for 2 s). **No tag-backs**: the new IT can't tag the gorilla who just tagged them, they have to get someone else. When time runs out, whoever spent the **least time as IT** wins.
* **Infection**: one gorilla (two with 10+ players) starts infected and turns lava-orange. Everyone they tag is infected too. The **last uninfected gorilla wins**. If time runs out, all survivors win.
* **Jungle Hide and Seek**: about one seeker per six players. Seekers are blindfolded for 25 s while hiders hide. Found hiders become seekers. Hiders win if anyone is still hidden when time runs out.

### Black holes, the maze and other surprises

* **Black holes** burst out of the ground 60 seconds into a round and then every 15 to 25 seconds, right in front of every player. Look for the tall purple beam and the "BLACK HOLE" marker with its distance. Get within about 11 m and they start sucking you in. Fall in and you land in a **dark underground maze**.
* Find the glowing **green EXIT** to climb back up into the jungle. **The Shadow**, a tagger who lives in the maze, hunts you down there. If it catches you, you go back to the start of the maze. It walks, so sprinting gets you away.
* **Power-ups** float around the jungle: gold **SPEED**, blue **SUPER JUMP**, green **CAMO REFILL**. Run through one to grab it.
* **FRENZY**: in the last 30 seconds of every round everyone moves faster.
* **Bananas**: 45 bananas are scattered around the jungle (a few are hidden deep in the waterfall cave). Walk into one to eat it, and it grows back somewhere else. The counter sits above the camo meter. When you've eaten **10**, press **F** for **2x sprint speed for 30 seconds**. A big countdown appears at the bottom of the screen.
* **Waterfall cave**: walk along the ledge behind the waterfall and through the doorway in the rock. Inside there's a glowing crystal grotto, a big crystal chamber and a maze of torch-lit tunnels with dead ends. Two hidden tunnels come out of the plateau's cliff sides (behind bushes), and a ladder shaft climbs up to the plateau top.

W1nOfGood/burgurgame.readme:
# After Hours Burger

A first-person cooperative burger restaurant for the web. One to four cooks share a late-night
kitchen: customers walk in and order at the counter, and the cooks grab ingredients, turn the
grill knobs, flip patties with a spatula, melt cheese, squeeze the right sauces and serve each
customer the burger on their ticket, built from memory. Works with mouse and keyboard and
with iPad touch controls, in the same room.

> **Status:** Stage 1 (real multiplayer interaction slice) is playable, with Stage 2
> (persistence and recovery) foundations and a Blender-authored art pass: a modelled restaurant
> with Cycles-baked global illumination and reflection probes, food whose cooking state drives
> its shader, stocked props, skin-textured first-person hands, and rigged teammates and walk-in
customers. All art is generated by code
> in `assets/source/blender` (see [docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md](docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md)). See
> [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) and [docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md](docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md).

## Install on your VPS

**Full guide: [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).** The short version, on Ubuntu/Debian
with two DNS records (`game.` and `realtime.`) pointing at the VPS:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
git clone https://github.com/w1nofgood/burgurgame.git /opt/after-hours && cd /opt/after-hours
cp deploy/.env.example deploy/.env      # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, GUEST_TOKEN_SECRET, ALLOWED_ORIGINS, VITE_REALTIME_URL
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d --build
scripts/build-client.sh https://realtime.example.com /var/www/after-hours/client
# then Nginx + Let's Encrypt (deploy/nginx/after-hours.conf), or your DirectAdmin panel
scripts/smoke.sh https://realtime.example.com https://game.example.com
```

**Windows Server VPS?** Follow [docs/DEPLOYMENT_WINDOWS.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT_WINDOWS.md): copy-paste
PowerShell that installs Node.js, PostgreSQL and Caddy (automatic HTTPS) as Windows services, plus
`scripts/windows/update.ps1`, `backup.ps1`, `restore.ps1` and `smoke.ps1`.

**Do you need DirectAdmin or a separate static host?** No. The same VPS serves the static
website (via Nginx) and runs the game service and database in Docker. If your VPS already uses
DirectAdmin, the guide shows how to use its web server instead. A static-only/shared host can't
run the game service, which needs a long-running process with WebSockets.

## Play locally (development)

Requirements: Node.js 22.12+ (24 LTS recommended) and npm.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev:server     # game service on http://localhost:2567 (in-memory saves)
npm run dev:client     # client on http://localhost:5173
```

Open http://localhost:5173 in two browser windows (or a second device on your network using
`http://<your-ip>:5173/?realtime=http://<your-ip>:2567` — add that origin to `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`),
open a kitchen in one and join with the room code in the other.

To develop against PostgreSQL instead of the in-memory store:

```bash
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/afterhours
npm run migrate && npm run dev:server
```

## How to play

- Flip the **OPEN sign** switch by the counter passage to start taking orders.
- Tickets show only the burger's **name**. Learn the builds — the **recipe book** (R, the touch
  *Recipes* button, or the menu) has every recipe; *Settings → Show recipe builds on tickets*
  turns on hints while you learn.
- Patties brown on the side touching the grill: **flip** them (spatula, or E/Use for a quick
  flip). Cheese melts on a hot patty. Some burgers want **grilled** onions, others raw.
- Build on a tray from the bottom bun up, add exactly the sauces the recipe calls for, close it
  with the top bun and put the tray on the **pickup shelf** under the heat lamp.
- More recipes unlock as the night goes on: 3 at first, 8 after a few minutes, then all 16.

Controls are in [docs/CONTROLS.md](docs/CONTROLS.md).

## Tests

```bash
npm test                                   # rules, protocol, server room and store tests
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://… npm test     # also runs the store contract against PostgreSQL
npm run test:e2e                           # desktop + iPad-emulated browsers in one kitchen
npm run typecheck
```

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/client` | Vite + Babylon.js client: menus, rendering, input (mouse/keyboard and touch), audio, networking |
| `apps/server` | Colyseus room, authoritative kitchen simulation, HTTP routes, persistence, migrations runner |
| `packages/simulation` | Engine-independent cooking, recipe scoring, stacking, interaction rules, shared Rapier physics |
| `packages/protocol` | Replicated state schema, message validators, protocol version |
| `packages/data` | Layout, items, recipes, prices, tuning |
| `database/migrations` | PostgreSQL schema |
| `deploy/` | Dockerfile, Compose, Nginx example, environment template; `deploy/windows` Caddy and IIS configs |
| `assets/source` | Blender (bpy) scripts that model, texture, light, bake and export all art; fonts |
| `scripts/` | Client build, backup, restore, smoke test, asset build, probe conversion; `scripts/windows` PowerShell equivalents |
| `tests/e2e` | Playwright multi-browser tests |
| `docs/` | Plan, deployment, architecture, controls, recipes, assets, limitations |

## Documentation

- [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) — VPS install, DirectAdmin, updates, backups
- [docs/DEPLOYMENT_WINDOWS.md](docs/DEPLOYMENT_WINDOWS.md) — Windows Server VPS install (PowerShell, IIS/Plesk)
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — authority, networking, persistence, security
- [docs/CONTROLS.md](docs/CONTROLS.md) — desktop and touch controls
- [docs/RECIPES.md](docs/RECIPES.md) — the menu
- [docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md](docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md) — how the art is built, baked and lit
- [docs/ASSET_MANIFEST.md](docs/ASSET_MANIFEST.md) — asset sources and licences
- [docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md](docs/KNOWN_

Windows service stops cleanly: explicit exit after shutdown, robust stop in scripts

On a Windows Server install the AfterHoursGame service hung in Stop pending:
the graceful shutdown finished ("shutdown complete") but node.exe never
exited, so Restart-Service and update.ps1 could not stop it.

Server (shutdown.ts, used by index.ts instead of Colyseus' handlers):
- SIGINT (NSSM's Ctrl+C), SIGTERM and SIGBREAK run the graceful shutdown
  once, wait for stdout/stderr to drain, then call process.exit.
- An 8 s safety timer exits anyway if the shutdown hangs (inside NSSM's
  10 s console-stop wait); a second signal during shutdown exits at once;
  an uncaught exception shuts down and exits 1.
- After shutdown only the stdio pipes remain open (measured): the HTTP and
  WebSocket servers, room clocks and the store are closed; the explicit
  exit no longer depends on the loop draining.
- Tests: unit tests for every path, and the real service process exits 0
  on SIGINT/SIGTERM within the timeout while a proxy-style keep-alive
  connection is held open.

Scripts (common.ps1 Stop-ServiceRobust, used by update.ps1, restore.ps1):
ask the service to stop, wait up to 15 s; if it is still Stop pending or
paused, end its process tree (taskkill /F /T /FI "SERVICES eq <name>") and
any node.exe running apps\server\dist\index.js, then continue. Warnings
report the service's real state instead of always saying "stopped".

Docs: AppStopMethodConsole 10000; troubleshooting row and a "Stuck in Stop
pending" section with the recovery commands.

Apexal/photo-dojo-revival.readme:
# Photo Dojo: Revival

A browser-only 2D fighting game. Pick a fighting style and pose for sixteen photos on a phone, the phone turns them into a sprite fighter locally, sends it to a laptop over WebRTC, and two people fight with controllers or a shared keyboard. No accounts, no backend storage: fighters live in each browser's IndexedDB. See [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the design.

## Run it

```sh
npm install
npm install --prefix worker
npm run worker:dev      # signaling Worker (wrangler dev) on :8787
npm run dev             # Vite; open http://localhost:5173
```

The Vite dev server proxies `/room/*` and `/turn-credentials` to the Worker, so the pages talk to signaling on their own origin.

**Phones need HTTPS for the camera.** Use `npm run dev:https` (self-signed certificate), open the Network URL Vite prints on the laptop, and scan the QR code. The phone has to accept the certificate once.

Without a phone, open `/capture` on the laptop to capture with its webcam (it saves locally, then download the `.photodojo` file and use **Import fighter file**), or just pick the two built-in stick figures.

### Controls

The game opens on a title screen with a demo fight between fighters from your library; press any button to start (a controller's press joins it as P1).

| | Move | Punch | Kick | Pause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 keyboard | WASD | J | K | Esc |
| P2 keyboard | Arrows | `,` (or numpad 1) | `.` (or numpad 2) | Esc |
| Gamepad | D-pad / left stick | A / Cross | B / Circle | Start |

Keyboard keys can be remapped in **Settings** (Tab or a pad's Select button on fighter select, or from the pause menu).

- **Up** jumps after a 3-frame wind-up (holding back or down during it still blocks). You can jump over the opponent.
- Hold **back** to block standing, or hold **down** to crouch-block. Punches pass right over a crouch; kicks and uppercuts can be blocked either way. The **low kick** has to be blocked crouching, and the **jump kick** (kick in the air, once per jump) has to be blocked standing.
- The **kick** lunges forward, so it reaches further than a punch but is slower. Hold **back** while kicking to kick in place instead (shorter, keeps your distance).
- **Down + punch** is an uppercut: the anti-air. Jumping attacks can't hit you while it comes out, so it beats a jump-in timed right, but it's very punishable if blocked. **Down + kick** is a quick low kick.
- **Punch + kick** together throws when you're close (it beats blocking) and knocks them down, and taunts when you're far away. Press punch + kick while grabbed to break free.
- **Down + punch + kick** is your fighter's **signature move**, set by the fighting style picked during capture:
  - **Brawler: Shoulder Charge.** A slow lean, then a charge most of the way across the stage that knocks them down. Blocked, it's a free punish.
  - **Grappler: Bear Hug.** A grab that reaches almost three times as far as a throw and can't be broken. It loses to any attack, and a miss leaves you open.
  - **Guardian: Parry.** Catches any strike for a moment: no damage, and the attacker staggers long enough for a free hit. Throws go straight through it, and a mistimed one leaves you open.
  - **Acrobat: Flying Knee.** An overhead from the ground: it hits a crouching guard, so block it standing.
- **Knockdowns:** a throw, a bear hug, a shoulder charge, or an uppercut that catches someone in the air knocks them down. Nobody can touch them while they're down; get ready for when they stand up.
- A press up to 5 frames early still counts, and a block still works if you let go of back within the last 3 frames. Blocked hits can't KO.
- Players swap sides every round.
- Gamepads rumble when you get hit (heavier for kicks and throws, a light tick when blocking, a long one on a KO) and buzz once when they join. Turn it off in Settings (or press R in the pause menu). Rumble uses the browser's Gamepad haptics (Chrome/Edge dual-rumble, Firefox pulse), and pads without it just don't rumble.
- **Pause menu** (Esc / Start): Resume, Controls (each player's moves for their device), Settings, Restart round, Quit to fighter select. Any controller can drive it; kick, Esc or Start resumes.
- **Settings:** game volume (hits, blocks, the clock) voice volume (the fighters' clips) and announcer volume separately, screen shake on/off, dynamic camera on/off (zooms in when the fighters are close), rumble on/off, smooth motion on/off (moves, walking, guarding, jumps, hit recoveries and the idle sway morph between photos instead of cutting; with it off you get Photo Dojo hard cuts and motion streaks instead; visual only), and keyboard remapping for each keyboard half. Everything is remembered. Throws need punch + kick at once, and some keyboards can't register that while a direction is held, so remap to keys further apart if throws don't come out.
- If a gamepad disconnects mid-fight, the game pauses and says whose it was. Pressing any button on a pad (or keyboard half) the other player isn't using takes over.
- Each health bar has a P1 / P2 tag (CPU for the computer) and the fighter's name in that player's colour, so it's clear whose bar is whose even when the fighters look alike. A health bar pulses when it's low, and the clock flashes and ticks in the last 10 seconds.
- F1 toggles the hitbox overlay.
- **Fullscreen:** F on fighter select, or the toolbar's ⛶ Fullscreen button. In Chrome and Edge, Esc still pauses while fullscreen (hold Esc to leave); in other browsers Esc leaves fullscreen.
- Before each match, a "How to fight" screen shows each player's controls with slow-motion previews of their fighter's moves.
- **Playing alone:** join with one controller, pick a fighter, and press punch again to choose your opponent: your controller moves a CPU cursor over the grid, and punch picks. Then choose **Match** (◀ ▶ sets the CPU to easy, normal or hard) or **Practice** with up / down, and punch to go; kick steps back. A match against the CPU is a full best-of-three with the cloc

# 2048

The sliding-tile puzzle 2048 for the browser, built with React, TypeScript and MUI.

Combine equal tiles to reach the 2048 tile.

## Features

- Tiles slide with animation, and new and merged tiles pop
- Undo any number of moves, including after game over
- Board sizes 3x3, 4x4, 5x5 and 6x6
- A separate best score for each board size, saved in the browser
- Light and dark themes; follows your system setting until you choose one
- Option to keep playing after reaching 2048
- Keyboard and touch controls
- Animations turn off when your system asks for reduced motion

## Getting started

Requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open the URL that Vite prints (usually http://localhost:5173).

## Controls

| Action | Input |
|---|---|
| Move | Arrow keys, `W` `A` `S` `D`, or swipe on the board |
| Undo | **Undo** button |
| Restart | **New game** button |
| Change board size | `3×3` / `4×4` / `5×5` / `6×6` buttons (starts a new game) |
| Toggle theme | Sun/moon icon |

Reloading the page starts a new 4x4 game. The browser keeps only your best scores and your theme choice.

## Scripts

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start the dev server with hot reload |
| `npm test` | Run the unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm run build` | Type-check and build into `dist/` |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally |
| `npm run lint` | Lint with oxlint |

## Project structure

```
src/
  game/engine.ts       Game rules: move, merge, spawn, score, win/over, undo
  game/engine.test.ts  Tests for the rules
  storage.ts           Saves best scores and theme (falls back safely if storage is blocked)
  Board.tsx            Board, tiles, animations, swipe input
  App.tsx              Game state, keyboard input, controls, dialogs, theme
openspec/
  specs/               Behavior specs: game-rules, game-interface
  changes/archive/     Past change proposals, designs and task lists
```

The rules in `engine.ts` are pure functions that don't depend on React, so you can test them without a browser.

## Specs and workflow

Changes to this project are planned with [OpenSpec](https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec). The current behavior is described in `openspec/specs/`. In Claude Code, the `/opsx:explore`, `/opsx:propose`, `/opsx:apply` and `/opsx:archive` commands (stored in `.claude/`) take a change from idea to archived spec.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

blham/chegal-minecraft-launcher.readme:
# Chegal Minecraft Launcher (KoreaWar Launcher)

A small, free, open-source **Minecraft: Java Edition** launcher for one private community server (*Korea War*, a nation-war server on a Korean-peninsula map).
Not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft. No ads, no payments, no data collection.

![screenshot](docs/screenshot.png)

## What it does (1.3.0+)
Sign-in and game launch are handled by the **official Minecraft Launcher**. This app only prepares things:
1. **Install Fabric Loader** — writes the Fabric version JSON (`meta.fabricmc.net`) into the official launcher's `.minecraft/versions`; the official launcher downloads the game, libraries and Java itself.
2. **Keep the server's companion mods up to date** in a separate game folder (signed list, SHA-256 checked), so they never mix with the player's own `.minecraft/mods`.
3. **Create a "Korea War" installation** in the official launcher (`launcher_profiles.json`: game directory, memory) and open the official launcher.
4. **Auto-connect** — leaves a one-time note in the game folder that the companion mod reads on the title screen.

The app never sees Microsoft or Minecraft credentials. (Before 1.3.0 it signed in directly; that code has been removed.)

## Network endpoints used
| Host | Purpose |
|---|---|
| meta.fabricmc.net | Fabric Loader version JSON |
| our game server (port 8163) | signed mod list, mod files, launcher updates |

## Build
Go 1.24+, standard library only: `./build.sh 1.0.0` (Windows / macOS / Linux, x64 and arm64).
The UI is a local web page served on `127.0.0.1:25585` and opened in the default browser.

---

## 한국어
Korea War 서버 전용 마인크래프트 자바 에디션 런처예요. Fabric·보조 모드를 받고 업데이트한 뒤, 공식 마인크래프트 런처에 "Korea War" 설치 프로필을 만들어 열어 줘요.
로그인과 게임 실행은 공식 런처가 해서, 이 런처는 계정 정보를 전혀 다루지 않아요. 무료·광고 없음·오픈 소스 (MIT).

## License

vonduzenstudios-create/Pixel-Fighter.readme:
# Pixel Fighter

A browser fighting game tech demo in the style of 16-bit console fighters. Every pixel of art,
every sound effect and every note of music is generated in code at load time. The only files
are the spoken voice lines in `public/voices/`, rendered from text by a script (see below).

- **1 stage:** The Thorn Gorge, a plank bridge over a pit of spikes under a blood moon
- **4 fighters:** Abe Lincoln, Nikola Tesla, Joan of Arc and Blackbeard
- **CPU opponent** with Easy, Normal and Hard
- Best of three rounds, a finishing move per fighter, and a stage finish into the spike pit

## Running it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
npm run build    # static build in dist/
npm test         # checks CHANGELOG.md, every fighter/stage, online determinism
```

Pushing to `main` deploys to GitHub Pages through `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
(set **Settings → Pages → Source** to **GitHub Actions** once).

## What's new

`CHANGELOG.md` lists the notable changes, one section per day. The game bundles it into the
**What's new** screen on the title menu, and the build also makes a standalone `whats-new.html`
page. A nightly task adds new days by itself, so you don't need to edit it by hand.

## Controls

| Action      | Gamepad          | Keyboard (P1) | Keyboard (P2)          |
|-------------|------------------|---------------|------------------------|
| Move        | D-pad / stick    | W A S D       | Arrow keys             |
| Low punch   | A                | U             | `[` or Numpad 4        |
| High punch  | X                | I             | `]` or Numpad 5        |
| Low kick    | B                | J             | `;` or Numpad 1        |
| High kick   | Y                | K             | `'` or Numpad 2        |
| Block       | LB, RB, LT, RT   | L or Space    | `/` or Numpad 0        |
| Start/pause | Start            | Enter         | `\`                    |

Holding back also blocks. In menus, A or Start confirms and B (or Esc) goes back. Commands below are written for a fighter facing right
(F = toward the opponent, B = away, D = down).

### Everyone

| Move                    | Command                            |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Uppercut (launches up)  | D + HP                             |
| Roundhouse (launches)   | B + HK                             |
| Sweep (knockdown)       | B + LK                             |
| Crouching attacks       | D + LP, D + LK, D + HK             |
| Judo throw (close, swaps sides) | F + LP                     |
| Pit drop (stage finish) | D + HP while the opponent is dazed |

### Specials and finishers

| Fighter     | Move                   | Command                  |
|-------------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| Lincoln     | Stovepipe Boomerang    | D, DF, F + P             |
|             | Rail Splitter          | B, B + HP                |
|             | Log Roll               | B, F + LK                |
|             | *Emancipation Cleave*  | F, B, F + HP (close)     |
| Tesla       | Coil Bolt              | D, DF, F + P             |
|             | Wireless Step          | D, DB, B + K             |
|             | Alternating Field      | Mash LP (or B, B + LP)   |
|             | *Grand Discharge*      | D, F, D + LP             |
| Joan of Arc | Holy Flame             | D, DF, F + P             |
|             | Banner Charge          | B, F + HK                |
|             | Ascension Blade        | F, D, DF + HP            |
|             | *Purifying Pyre*       | F, D, F + HK (mid range) |
| Blackbeard  | Cannon Volley          | D, DF, F + P             |
|             | Powder Keg             | D, DB, B + LK            |
|             | Cutlass Cyclone        | Mash HK (or D, D + HK)   |
|             | *Powder Keg Surprise*  | B, B, F + LP (close)     |

Finishers (in italics) work in the deciding round when "END THEM!" appears.

"Mash" moves fire when you tap the button four times within half a second; the first taps
come out as normal attacks and the flurry cancels them. Chuck Norris, Bruce Lee, Ali, Bob Ross,
Tesla and Blackbeard each have one. Motion commands are forgiving: a diagonal counts for the
direction beside it, and the steps can be spread over about half a second.

Combos work like the 16-bit classics. A ground normal that connects (hit or block) can be
cancelled into a special by finishing the command over the hit, and the quick attacks (both
standing punches, LK, and the crouching LP and LK) chain straight into each other. The uppercut
(down + HP) comes up under a standing guard, so only a crouching block stops it. Button presses are buffered for 6
frames, so a press made a moment before your fighter recovers still comes out on the first frame
they can act. Frame data for the shared normals lives in `tests/anims.test.ts`.

## How it's built

TypeScript + Vite + plain Canvas 2D at a native 256×224 resolution, scaled up with crisp pixels.

- `src/gfx/painter.ts` paints pixel sprites with shape primitives, auto-shading and outlines.
- `src/chars/build.ts` paints each fighter as separate jointed parts (head, torso, upper arm,
  forearm, thigh, shin, foot) from a `Look`. `src/gfx/rig.ts` poses them with forward
  kinematics, so every animation is a list of joint-angle keyframes (`src/game/anims.ts` and
  each fighter's own file). Hitboxes come from the posed fist or foot, so they always match
  what you see.
- `src/fighters/<id>/` holds everything about one fighter and `src/stages/<id>/` everything
  about one stage. Both are found automatically (`src/fighters/registry.ts`,
  `src/stages/registry.ts`, using Vite's `import.meta.glob`), so adding one never edits a
  shared file. See [Adding a fighter](#adding-a-fighter) and [Adding a stage](#adding-a-stage).
- `src/game/` is the engine: fight rules, fighters, projectiles, particles, the AI
  (`ai.ts` drives the CPU with the same inputs a player would pre

- The knockout blow now freezes briefly, then plays out at a third of normal
  speed; a loser left standing is knocked down, and the round is only called
  once they hit the floor (with a crash and dust).

  the pair before the scene runs.

  online, so lockstep stays deterministic), then shows and calls the victory,
  then OBLITERATION. Announcer calls queue behind any line still playing.

WlnJBrn09/WayCiv.desc: A Civilization VI-style 4X game in Rust and egui: Earth map with historical starts, loyalty, and an AI tech tree. Needs your own Civ VI install.
WlnJBrn09/WayCiv.readme:
# WayCiv

A Civilization VI-style 4X game written in Rust, with egui. WayCiv follows
Civ VI's turn flow and uses its leaders, civilizations, units, buildings,
districts, wonders, technologies, civics, governments, policies, beliefs, and
great people. The rules are WayCiv's own, simpler versions.

WayCiv reads that content from **your installed copy of Civilization VI**
(Steam, Linux) at startup. Nothing from the game is stored in this repository.
If the game isn't in the default Steam library, set `CIV6_DIR` to its install
folder.

```bash
cargo run --release -p wayciv
```

## How a game flows

1. **Create Game**: pick a leader from the portrait grid. Their leader ability,
   civ ability, and agenda are shown. Choose the map (Earth or Random), map size,
   rivals, city-states, and seed.
2. **Turn 1**: found your capital with the Settler (`B`, or the Found City button).
3. Each turn, as in Civ VI, the End Turn button shows what's blocking it: "Choose
   Research", "Choose Civic", "Choose Production", "Unit Needs Orders", "Choose
   Pantheon". Clicking it takes you to the blocker. `Enter` presses it.
4. AI civilizations and city-states take their turns. Then cities grow and build,
   and science, culture, faith, and gold accumulate.
5. Meeting leaders, wars, denouncements, and friendship offers open a leader
   screen with their portrait and their own lines from Civ VI.
6. Win by Science (space projects), Culture (tourism), Domination (all original
   capitals), Religion, or Score at the turn limit.

Controls: left-click selects, right-click moves or attacks, drag or the arrow
keys scroll, the mouse wheel zooms. The minimap (bottom right) recenters the view.

| Key | Action | Key | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | Notifications | `L` | Leaders and relationships |
| `S` | Research (tech tree) | `C` | Civics tree |
| `R` | Religion | `A` | AI tree (once unlocked) |
| `G` | Government | `P` | Great people |
| `E` | City-states | `V` | Victory progress |
| `K` | Map key | `Enter` | Next turn, or the next thing that needs a decision |
| `.` | Next unit | `Space` | Skip unit |
| `F` | Fortify | `Z` | Sleep |
| `B` | Found city | `Esc` | Cancel, then close windows, then deselect |

Pressing a window's key again closes it. Notifications stay off screen until
you press `N`; new ones appear briefly as toasts at the right edge.

The layout follows Civ VI on the Nintendo Switch: research and civic trackers
top left, leaders top right, the unit or city panel at the bottom left and
right, and the big Next Turn button with the minimap at the bottom right.

## The map

- **Earth** (the default) is the real world: continents, mountain ranges,
  rivers, and biomes come from NOAA's ETOPO1 elevation and ocean depth and
  WorldClim 2.1 temperature and rainfall (`tools/earth/build_earth.py`). Rivers
  follow real drainage. Every leader starts at their historical capital
  (Reagan at Washington, Victoria at London, Qin at Xi'an...), city-states sit
  at their real cities, and natural wonders are where they are on Earth (Everest,
  Kilimanjaro, the Great Barrier Reef...). Sizes: Small 104x72, Standard
  128x88, Giant 160x110 (the default).
- **Random** generates a fractal world with the same biomes.
- Hex outlines are always drawn.
- Biomes: grassland, plains, desert, tundra, snow, coast, sea, and deep sea,
  with forest, taiga, rainforest, marsh, floodplains, desert floodplains, oasis,
  dunes, glacier, and sea ice on top, plus hills, mountains, cliffs, rivers, and
  natural wonders. Taiga is like forest and grows in the cold north. Dunes cost
  an extra move. Glaciers (Greenland, Antarctica) are impassable. Cliffs line
  steep coasts and give +3 defense. Deep sea is open ocean, crossed with Cartography.
- Units and resources are drawn with their icons when you zoom in.
- Each civilization's territory is tinted with its color and outlined with a thick
  border in its primary and secondary colors. Cities have banners in the owner's colors.
- "Map key" (bottom left) shows the legend. Hovering a tile shows its biome,
  features, resource, yields, and owner.

## What's simplified

- **Combat** uses Civ VI's damage formula and wall rules, which were recovered
  from the game's binary in `~/Projects/civ6-decompile`. Promotions are simplified
  to levels (+3 strength each).
- **Policies, beliefs, and leader abilities** apply Civ VI's most common effects
  straight from the game data. Examples: production bonuses for unit classes and
  eras, city and building yields, and district and building production. Other
  effects show their description with a "(description only)" tag. Reagan's
  ability is implemented directly.
- **Great people** use one simplified effect per class, plus WayCiv's modern
  great people: Elon Musk (minor boosts to AI, rockets, and solar), Gwynne
  Shotwell (a big boost to a space race project), Palmer Luckey (a flight of
  Anduril Strike Drones), and Ilya Sutskever (a big AI breakthrough) as
  engineers and scientists; Yanni and NF as musicians; and Michael Crichton,
  Iain M. Banks, and Douglas Adams as writers.
- **Religion** uses pantheons, founding at a Holy Site with a Great Prophet,
  missionaries, and passive pressure. There is no theological combat.
- **City-states** give envoy and suzerain bonuses by category. There are no
  quests, and no one can declare war on a city-state.
- **Loyalty**: every city within 9 tiles pulls on a city, harder when bigger and
  closer. Your cities hold it; foreign cities pull it away. Capitals (+5),
  garrisons (+2), Monuments (+1), and happy citizens add loyalty; occupation (-3)
  and unhappiness take it away. A city at 0 loyalty joins the civilization
  pulling on it hardest. The city panel shows the breakdown, and banners show a
  loyalty bar when it drops.
- **Civilians** (settlers, builders, traders, great people...) have no health.
  One attack from a combat unit kills them.
- **Artificial Intelligence** (a new Information Era tech after
  Telecommunic

bheppe/gpsp-3d.readme:
# gpSP 3D

**Game Boy Advance games in stereoscopic 3D on the Nintendo 3DS, at full speed on an Old 3DS.**

gpSP 3D is a standalone 3DS app built on [gpSP](https://github.com/libretro/gpsp)
(the libretro version). It puts each GBA background layer and sprite group at
its own depth, so maps, characters, HUDs and backgrounds separate when you
raise the 3D slider. No RetroArch needed.

**Discord** (help, game reports, test builds): https://discord.gg/pBWY3fRgnU

> This repository is a fork of [libretro/gpsp](https://github.com/libretro/gpsp).
> The original gpSP readme is in [README.gpsp.md](README.gpsp.md).

## Features

- **Per-layer 3D.** Each GBA layer (BG0-BG3, sprites by priority) gets its own
  depth. Presets: Classic, Pop-out, Deep, Gentle, Flat map, or Custom with a
  slider per layer.
- **Smart layers.** Layers that scroll together and share tile graphics (one
  picture split over several layers, as in Pokemon maps) are kept at one depth,
  so hidden filler tiles never show through.
- **Floor tilt.** Brings the bottom of the screen nearer and pushes the top
  further away, so roads in racing games (and floors in general) recede.
- **Per-game 3D profiles.** Settings can be saved for one game. Pokemon games
  start on Deep with Smart layers automatically.
- **Full speed on an Old 3DS.** gpSP's ARM dynarec runs on the main core.
  Picture drawing runs on the second CPU core, so emulation and sound stay at
  60 fps. In 3D, the picture refreshes at about 30 per second on an Old 3DS.
- **GPU display** with three scaling modes: Sharp, Crisp (sharp bilinear) and
  Smooth. Screen sizes: Original (1:1), Fit (1.5x) and Stretch.
- **Color styles**: Original, GBA soft, GBA screen, plus Saturation and
  Brightness.
- **Touch menu** on the bottom screen with a live preview, save states with
  slots, auto frame skip, audio stretch when the game runs slow, and a stats
  panel.
- **Gyro sensor** for WarioWare: Twisted, using the 3DS gyroscope.
- **Forwarder support.** Started with a ROM path as its first argument, the
  app plays that game directly and closes when you quit.
- **Screen effects**: Scanlines and LCD grid (Display -> Screen effect).
- **HOME Menu icons per game** (forwarders), see below.
- **Saves are shared with RetroArch.** Saves go to RetroArch's save folder if
  it exists, so you can switch between the two.

## Requirements

- A Nintendo 3DS / 2DS family console (Old or New) with custom firmware
  ([Luma3DS](https://github.com/LumaTeam/Luma3DS)). The 3D effect needs a model
  with a 3D screen.
- `sdmc:/3ds/dspfirm.cdc` for sound. Dump it with
  [DSP1](https://github.com/zoogie/DSP1). Without it the app runs silently.
- Your own legally dumped GBA games. None are included or linked here.
- No GBA BIOS file is needed. gpSP has a built-in open-source BIOS.

## Install

1. Download `gpsp3d.cia` (or `gpsp3d.3dsx`) from the
   [Releases](../../releases) page.
2. **CIA:** copy it to the SD card and install it with FBI or another CIA
   installer. It appears on the HOME Menu as **gpSP 3D**.
   **3DSX:** copy it to `sdmc:/3ds/` and start it from the Homebrew Launcher.
3. Start gpSP 3D, browse to your games on the bottom screen and tap one.

## Using it

- **GBA controls:** A, B, L, R, Start, Select, D-pad / Circle Pad.
- **Menu:** tap the bottom screen while playing. Tabs:
  **Game** (save/load state, slot, reset, quit), **Display** (screen size,
  scaling, color), **3D** (effect, strength, layer style, per-layer depths,
  sprite pop, focus, floor tilt, smart layers), **Speed** (frame skip, audio when slow,
  stats) and **System** (core 2 drawing, GPU display, core 2 priority).
- **3D:** raise the 3DS 3D slider. **3D tab -> Strength** scales the effect.
  **3D tab -> Layer style** picks a preset. **3D tab -> Settings for** chooses
  whether changes apply to all games or only this one.
- **Files** on the SD card:
  - `sdmc:/3ds/gpsp3d/gpsp3d.cfg`: settings
  - `sdmc:/3ds/gpsp3d/games/<game>.cfg`: per-game 3D profiles
  - Game saves (`.srm`) and states (`.state1` ...): RetroArch's save folder
    if present, otherwise next to the ROM

If the app ever freezes while starting the GPU display, the next launch shows
a message and turns **System -> GPU display** off, so you can always get back
in.

## HOME Menu icons for your games

You can give each game its own HOME Menu icon that starts gpSP 3D straight
into it (a "forwarder"). gpSP 3D must be installed as a CIA.

1. Put the SD card in your PC (or copy the games folder over).
2. In the devkitPro shell, run, with your own folders:
   ```
   bash gpsp3ds/make-forwarders.sh /e/roms/gba /roms/gba
   ```
   The first folder is where the games are on the PC, the second is the same
   folder on the 3DS SD card.
3. Install the CIAs from `gpsp3ds/out/forwarders/` with FBI.

For a custom icon, put a 48x48 PNG with the game's name next to it
(`Pokemon Emerald.gba` -> `Pokemon Emerald.png`). Other forwarder tools that
start `gpsp3d.3dsx` with the game's path as its argument also work.

## Building

You need [devkitPro](https://devkitpro.org/wiki/Getting_Started) with the 3DS
packages (`3ds-dev`, which includes libctru, citro3d and picasso), plus
`makerom` and `bannertool` in your PATH.

```
git clone https://github.com/bheppe/gpsp-3d
bash gpsp-3d/gpsp3ds/build-gpsp3ds.sh
```

The script builds the gpSP core (`make platform=ctr`), then the app, then the
CIA. Results go to `gpsp3ds/out/` (`gpsp3d.cia`, `gpsp3d.3dsx`).

### What changed in the core

- `video_thread.cc` / `video_thread_sys.c`: a threaded renderer. The main core
  records each scanline's registers, palette, OAM and changed VRAM blocks, and
  the second core draws the lines. It is also where stereo 3D happens: each eye
  is drawn with every layer shifted by its depth, with Smart grouping and gap
  filling.
- `video.cc`: hooks for per-eye sprite shifts and layer tracking. The normal
  renderer is unchanged when these aren't used.
- `gba_memory.c`, `arm/arm_stub.S`, `x86/x86_stub.S`, `cpu.h`: VRAM

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the PSG status bits readable in SOUNDCNT_X

Bits 0-3 of SOUNDCNT_X are the read-only channel active flags, which
sound.c keeps up to date in the backing store. The new read mask of
0x0080 hid them, so a game polling for a channel to finish would always
read zero. Use 0x008F.

arm64: send I/O reads at 0x400 and above to the slow reader

The stub only tested bits 8-9 of the offset, so addresses such as
0x04000530 were still read as mirrors of the 1 KiB register block, while
the C reader, the interpreter and the ARM32/x86 stubs all treat them as
open bus. Check the upper offset bits first.

Tested under qemu-aarch64: a dynarec read of 0x04000530 returned the
KEYINPUT mirror (0x03ff) before and now matches the interpreter.

arm: preserve guest flags in the I/O load stub

On the ARM32 backend the guest NZCV flags live in the host CPSR while a
block runs. The new range checks in ld_ioram use cmp without saving the
flags first, so every I/O read from translated code trashed the guest
flags, on both the direct and the slow path (ld_slow saved the already
clobbered value).

Save the flags before the compares, restore them on the direct path and
enter the slow path after its own save_flags, the same way ld_bios and
ld_rdmap_slow already do it.

Tested under qemu-arm with a ROM doing movs/ldr KEYINPUT/addne in a
loop: 183193 of 183193 iterations saw corrupted flags before, 0 after.
Fix GBA I/O read semantics

Fix dynarec execution from VRAM (#289)

* Fix dynarec execution from VRAM

Bridge mutable VRAM execution through the interpreter for ARM32, ARM64, x86 and MIPS, then invalidate RAM translations before resuming the dynarec. Cache only per-entry dispatch stubs so mutable VRAM instructions are never translated.

* x86: fix host stack handling in the VRAM interpreter bridge

The generated VRAM stub reaches execute_vram_arm/thumb with a jmp, so no
host return address is pushed. Both lookup_pc and return_to_main assume
one is on the stack and discard it, so every VRAM entry popped a slot the
stub did not own. The next return_to_main then restored garbage callee
saved registers and crashed. The call into execute_arm_vram was also
made with the stack 8 bytes off the 16 byte ABI alignment on x86_64.

Reserve the missing slot on entry so the stack matches what every other
path into lookup_pc/return_to_main looks like.

Tested on x86_64 Linux with a ROM that writes a routine into VRAM and
calls it in a loop: segfault before, 600 frames clean after.

* mips: emit the block prologue for VRAM interpreter stubs

MIPS has block_prologue_size 16, so block_lookup_translate returns
(block start + 16) as the entry point. The VRAM stub was emitted at
offset 0 with no prologue and is only 12 bytes long, so the entry point
landed past the end of the stub.

The stub also used generate_load_pc, which emits an addiu relative to
reg_pc. reg_pc is loaded by the prologue, so without it a0 carried the
previous block's PC instead of the VRAM address.

Emit the normal block prologue first. That puts the stub body at the
expected entry offset and makes reg_pc valid for generate_load_pc.

Build tested with mipsel-linux-gnu-gcc; not runtime tested.

Co-authored-by: LibretroAdmin <libretroadmin@users.noreply.github.com>

change default value of sound output rate from 65536 to 32768 (#288)

some platforms have noticeable slowdown because of this setting being set too high by default. Change its default value to 32768, low-end platforms will perform well.

Don't let a scanned EEPROM signature override real SRAM/flash access (#287)

The whole-ROM signature sweep added in #281 runs over the entire
cartridge, so it also matches EEPROM_V strings that are left over in
games that actually ship SRAM or flash. When that happens backup_type is
set to BACKUP_EEPROM and read_backup()/write_backup() bail out
immediately, so every access to the 0x0E region is discarded and the
game silently loses its saves.

Mark an EEPROM type that came from the sweep as a guess. If the game
then drives the SRAM/flash region, drop back to BACKUP_UNKN and let the
usual autodetection classify the cart. A guess that is confirmed by a
real EEPROM access, and a type that came from the header scan or from
gba_over.h, are unaffected.

memmap: survive JIT cache mapping failure and support Apple silicon W^X

map_jit_block tested mmap results against NULL, but mmap signals
failure with MAP_FAILED. On a platform where every RWX attempt fails
(hardened runtimes without a JIT entitlement, and Apple silicon
unconditionally for non-MAP_JIT mappings) the mapper burned all
candidate iterations validating and munmapping (void*)-1, returned no
block, retro_init stored the NULL unchecked, and the first translation
wrote through it. Failed attempts now compare against MAP_FAILED, a
NULL cache is logged and pins dynarec_enable to the interpreter (the
core option cannot re-enable it), dynarec init and teardown are
skipped when no cache exists, and the core keeps running frames on the
interpreter instead of crashing.

On Apple platforms the cache is now mapped with MAP_JIT, and on Apple
silicon writes to it are gated with pthread_jit_write_protect_np.
block_lookup_address_arm/thumb is the sole gateway through which block
headers, RAM tag entries, emitted code and branch patches reach the
cache - translation, deferred-exit patching and init_bios_hooks all
funnel through it - so the per-thread write window opens on entry and
closes again before any translated code can run, with no assumptions
about which thread calls in. The helpers are no-ops everywhere else.

Refuse to load a ROM when no gamepak buffer could be allocated

init_gamepak_buffer() takes what it can get, stopping at the first 1MB
malloc that fails, so a memory-starved device can come out of retro_init
with no ROM buffers at all. retro_load_game() now checks for that
alongside the existing frame buffer check and declines the load, since
load_gamepak() reads the cartridge header directly out of
gamepak_buffers[0].

load_gamepak_raw() reports failure when it has no buffer to read a chunk
into, rather than returning success after loading nothing.

dynarec: avoid undefined signed left shift decoding ARM branch offsets

arm_decode_branch and arm_branch_target sign-extend the 24-bit branch
immediate by left-shifting it as a signed int, which is undefined once
the sign bit is reached, i.e. for any backward branch. Perform the left
shift in unsigned arithmetic and only then convert for the arithmetic
right shift, matching the form the interpreter and the Thumb offset
decoding already use. The 0xFFFFFF mask is dropped since the shift
discards the top byte anyway. Generated code is unchanged.

dynarec: resolve external branch exits iteratively to bound host stack use

Translating a block resolves its external branch targets by invoking
block_lookup_translate on each of them, which in turn translates those
blocks and their exits. Every not-yet-translated block in a branch chain
nests another translate_block/block_lookup_translate frame pair (roughly
850 bytes on AArch64), so a long enough chain of first-visit blocks
overflows the host thread stack. Android is the primary victim since
cores run on the native activity thread with about 1MiB of stack, partly
consumed by content loading before the first lookup: both a runtime
lookup and the init_bios_hooks pre-translation of the SWI entrypoint at
retro_load_game can crash this way.

Queue external exits on a growable worklist instead and drain it from
the outermost lookup once translation returns. Nested lookups performed
while draining only translate their block and queue its exits, so the
host stack depth stays constant regardless of the guest branch graph.
The bios_swi_entrypoint short-circuit and the flush-abort contract are
unchanged: any failure discards pending entries, which reference the
flushed cache, and block_lookup_address retries from scratch as before.
Removing the per-frame external_block_exits array also trims 512 bytes
from every translate_block frame.
libretro: add selectable system-clock RTC source (#286)

common: avoid undefined 32-bit shift in ror() for zero rotate counts

ror() computed value << (32 - shift), which for a rotate count of zero
is a shift by 32 - undefined behavior in C, flagged by UBSan on every
aligned read_memory32() call. Mask the left shift count to the 0..31
range; for all rotate counts used (0..31) the masked form is
equivalent, and a zero rotate now reduces to the identity through
well-defined shifts.

No functional change.

memory: fix stack overflow reading open bus while executing from open bus

Open bus reads are emulated by re-reading the opcode at the current
prefetch address (PC + 8 in ARM state, PC + 4 in Thumb state). When the
CPU itself is executing from open or unmapped memory - for example after
a wild jump into the BIOS mirror region past 0x4000 - that PC-relative
read resolves straight back into the open bus handler with the same
address, so read_memory32() recursed without bound until it ran into the
host thread's stack guard page and crashed with SIGSEGV.

Guard the prefetch address before recursing: if it would itself land on
open bus (region 0x01, any region above 0x0F, or region 0x00 past the
16KB BIOS), return the latched bus value instead, using the same byte
selection convention as the existing BIOS read protection. One level of
guarding is sufficient since every other region returns without
recursing.

Reproduced with PC = 0x00780020 and a data read at 0x00780028, matching
the register state in the macOS crash report.

libretro: add Sound Output Rate core option (65536 / 32768 Hz)

sound: parameterize output rate, derive all frequency steps from one source

The PSG frequency-step formulas hardcode the output sample rate as baked
powers of two in five places: the four SOUNDxCNT write handlers in
gba_memory.c and the sweep recompute in sound.c. The direct sound timer
step (sound_update_frequency_step) and the tick conversion in
render_gbc_sound() already reference the rate symbolically.

Introduce a runtime rate restricted to powers of two (sound_frequency ==
1u << sound_freq_bits) so every step formula remains an exact
shift-and-divide against the 2^24 Hz master clock, and express all five
formulas through shared inlines in sound.h:

  tone (ch 0/1):  2^(36-b) / (2048-rate)
  wave (ch 2):    2^(37-b) / (2048-rate)
  noise (ch 3):   2^(35-b) / (r << (s+1)), r==0 as 2^(36-b) >> (s+1)

At b=16 these reproduce the removed literals (1048576, 2097152, 524288,
1048576>>(s+1)) exactly, so this patch is a pure refactor at the default
rate.

Add sound_frequency_changed() (in gba_memory.c, after prescale_table),
which recomputes every derived step from primary state: gs->rate for
tone/wave (required, since the sweep unit mutates rate without an ioreg
write), REG_SOUND4CNT_H for noise (bits 0-2 and 4-7 survive the 0x40FF
write mask), and reload << prescale for the audio timers. Calling it
after savestate load makes frequency_step fully derived state and, as a
side effect, makes savestates portable across rate settings.

Also add sound_flush_ring() for the rate-change path: drops pending ring
contents (rendered at the old rate) and realigns all producer indices and
the consumer base, costing at most the 512-sample readout holdback of
silence, deterministically.

GBA_SOUND_FREQUENCY remains the compile-time maximum, for buffer sizing.

sound: round direct sound interpolation to nearest instead of floor

The linear interpolation term for FIFO samples was truncated by a bare
arithmetic >> 16 (via the misleadingly named fp16_16_to_u32 previously,
now explicit), which floors: negative-slope interpolation segments were
biased by up to -1 LSB, an average -0.5 LSB error whose sign flips with
waveform slope.

Add the half-LSB before the shift in all three render cases. The product
is already computed in 64 bits, so no overflow concern; verified against
the exact real-valued interpolant over all byte pairs, both volume-halve
settings, and ~9400 fraction values each (every rounded result within
0.5 LSB of exact).

sound: round PSG volume scaling to nearest instead of floor

The per-sample PSG term (sample * volume) >> N is an arithmetic shift,
i.e. floor. Since the volume tables attenuate, almost every active PSG
channel carried a systematic negative bias -- measured at -0.40 LSB mean
per channel at 16-bit output scale over the reachable volume range -- and
because truncation error tracks the waveform, low-level envelope-decayed
tones picked up signal-correlated harmonic error rather than benign
noise. The per-channel DC component also steps whenever a channel gates
on or off.

Add the half-LSB before the shift. The product spans [-2^31, 7 * 2^28],
so adding 2^17 can neither overflow INT32_MAX nor wrap at INT32_MIN;
verified over all 6144 reachable sample/volume combinations, with every
rounded term within 0.5 LSB of the exact real-valued product and the
mean error dropping to +0.006 LSB.

sound: mix at full 16-bit scale instead of 12-bit + x16 output shift

The mix bus accumulated all six channels onto an s16 buffer at a nominal
12-bit scale (+/-2048) and the readout path clamped to that range and
multiplied by 16, leaving the bottom 4 bits of every sample handed to the
frontend permanently zero. The 12-bit grid is not a hardware property
being modelled (the BIAS/PWM output stage is not emulated at all); it was
purely an accumulator-width artifact, and it floor-quantized each channel
independently before summation, so quantization noise from up to six
channels added on top of a floor already 24 dB above what the s16 output
format supports.

Widen the buffer to s32 (128KiB -> 256KiB) and accumulate at full 16-bit
scale: PSG terms keep 4 more bits of the already-computed volume product
(>> 18 instead of >> 22; the worst-case product -8 * 2^28 == INT32_MIN
remains representable), and direct sound samples are placed at x256
(exact for 8-bit sources) so the linear interpolator resolves 4 more
fractional bits. The interpolation product now needs a 64-bit multiply
since a 16-bit-scale diff times a 16-bit fraction can reach +/-2^32; this
is a single smull/dmultu on 32-bit targets. Readout clamps at +/-32767
with no upscale.

Floor-shift semantics are unchanged: for every reachable input the new
per-channel term satisfies new >> 4 == old, verified exhaustively for the
PSG path (all 6144 sample/envelope/channel/master combinations) and
near-exhaustively for the DS interpolator (all byte pairs and halve
settings, ~9400 fraction values each plus edge fractions; ~1.2e9 cases).

The ring buffer is not serialized (indices count entries, not bytes) and
all memsets are sizeof-based, so savestate format and semantics are
unaffected.

sound: integer-only fixed-point seeds, remove residual float from audio path

The mixing and output path was already int16 end-to-end (sound_buffer is
s16, sound_read_samples emits s16 straight to audio_batch_cb) -- there was
no float<->int16 sample roundtrip and no vendored float decoder to excise.

What remained were the float computations that seed the fixed-point
timeline: the per-channel frequency_step values, the GBC sample tick step,
the DirectSound timer step, and the tick_delta->buffer rate conversions.
Because sound_frequency == 2^16 and (non-overclock) GBC_BASE_RATE == 2^24,
every one of these collapses to exact integer arithmetic:

  tone1/tone2  freq_step = 2^20 / (2048-rate)
  wave ch3     freq_step = 2^21 / (2048-rate)
  noise dr==0  freq_step = 2^20 >> (shift+1)
  noise dr!=0  freq_step = 2^19 / (ratio << (shift+1))
  retrigger    sample_index -= 65536/12
  ds timer     step(8.24) = (BASE<<24) / (sound_freq * reload)
  tick step    = 256
  buffer_ticks = (tick_delta * sound_freq << 16) / BASE   (= tick_delta*256)
  buffer_adjust= (tick_delta * sound_freq) / BASE * 2

All register-driven cases were swept exhaustively against the old float
form and are bit-identical: tone rate 0..2047, wave rate 0..2047, noise
ratio 0..7 x shift 0..15, ds-timer reload 1..0x40000 -- 266370/266370
match. The two tick_delta conversions are done in u64 so they stay exact
(the float form lost mantissa bits past 2^24 and depended on x87-vs-SSE
rounding / FMA contraction, i.e. it was not reproducible across builds).

GBC_BASE_RATE keeps its float definition for its non-audio consumers
(frontend timing.fps, RTC GBA_FRAME_SECONDS, rumble pct); a GBC_BASE_RATE_INT
companion feeds the audio path.

objdump confirms zero FP instructions remain in render_gbc_sound,
init_sound, trigger_timer and the sound register-write paths. Builds clean
in both default and OVERCLOCK_60FPS configurations.
webOS: set arch params for 64-bit (#284)

libretro: eliminate post-process mix snapshot memcpy via buffer swap

video_post_process_mix and video_post_process_cc_mix each ended with
   memcpy(gba_screen_pixels_prev, gba_screen_pixels, GBA_SCREEN_BUFFER_SIZE)
to stash the just-rendered frame so the *next* frame's mix could read
it as 'prev'.  At 240x160x2 bytes the copy is 75 KB; at 60 fps with
mix enabled that's roughly 4.5 MB/s of memory bandwidth - small on
desktop but visible on embedded ARM where the rest of the renderer is
already memory-bound.

Replace the copy with a pointer swap: after the mix loop, swap
gba_screen_pixels and gba_screen_pixels_prev.  After the swap,
gba_screen_pixels points to the buffer that just held 'prev' (about
to be overwritten by the next frame's scanline-render pass), and
gba_screen_pixels_prev points to this frame's pixels (which become
prev for next time).

Safety:
- The scanline renderer fully overwrites every pixel of
  gba_screen_pixels before any read.  fill_line_background runs
  first per scanline (video.cc), seeding every pixel with the
  backdrop colour; tile/affine/bitmap layers then write over it.
  No read-before-write hazard on the post-swap buffer.
- video_cb gets gba_processed_pixels (the mix output), not the
  swapped buffers.  RetroArch's contract requires the buffer
  valid only during the video_cb call, which is satisfied.
- Both buffer allocations are independent mallocs; the swap just
  exchanges which pointer holds which block, retro_deinit's
  free(gba_screen_pixels) + free(gba_screen_pixels_prev) still
  frees both without leak or double-free.
- Frame-skip: when skip_next_frame fires the renderer doesn't run
  and video_post_process isn't called - no swap, buffers unchanged,
  identical to the prior memcpy version's skip behaviour.
- Toggling mix off mid-session: init_post_processing reassigns
  video_post_process; both buffers stay allocated.  Toggling back
  on later will read whatever stale frame is in *_prev (same as
  before this patch; the existing white-fill at allocation time
  handled the initial-frame case).
- Determinism: the swap doesn't touch any emulator state.  Both
  pre- and post-swap buffers are equally valid render targets;
  the next render fills the screen from scratch regardless of
  which physical buffer it lands in.

The cc-only path (video_post_process_cc, no mix) is unchanged - it
never used the prev buffer.  No memcpy in that path, no swap added.

libretro,cheats: honor retro_cheat_set(enabled=false) by disabling

The libretro contract for retro_cheat_set(index, enabled, code) is
"apply a cheat code if enabled, disable it otherwise."  gpsp
handled the enabled=true side (parse + activate) but the
enabled=false path was just 'if (!enabled) return;' - the cheat
stayed active until the next retro_cheat_reset() or content reload.

A user toggling a cheat off in the frontend had no effect.  The
practical bug surface is small because RetroArch's normal change
flow is retro_cheat_reset() followed by a full reapply with the new
enabled set, which clears everything via cheat_clear() first.  But
direct API callers, alternative frontends, and any future RetroArch
optimization that avoids the full reapply would all expose this
silently.

Added cheat_disable(unsigned index) in cheats.c as a soft-disable:
flips cheat_active=false at that index so process_cheats() skips
it, but leaves the parsed code data in place so a later re-enable
via the same index does not require the frontend to send the code
string again (matters mainly to direct-API callers; RetroArch
itself does send the code each time).  Out-of-range indices are
silently ignored.

cheat_master_hook is deliberately NOT recomputed on disable.  The
hook is "stickiest of any cheat with a master-code (opcode 1)
entry" and process_cheats short-circuits on !cheat_active, so a
stale hook is observationally harmless - it just causes
process_cheats to be called at the hooked PC where it then does
nothing.  Recomputing the hook would require scanning the other
MAX_CHEATS slots on every toggle, which is unnecessary for a
frontend-toggle path.

Declaration added to cheats.h next to cheat_parse / cheat_clear.
retro_cheat_set in libretro.c now calls cheat_disable in the
!enabled branch instead of returning silently.

gbp: persist SIO handshake state across savestates

gbp.c keeps three file-local statics that drive the GBP (Game Boy
Player) SIO handshake protocol:
  - gbp_seq_n      (u32, 0..15) the current step in the handshake
  - gbp_rumble     (bool) the last rumble-active bit from the master
  - gbp_allow_rumble (bool) a safety latch that gates rumble until
                            execution has been observed from ROM space

None of these were captured by the savestate, so a state saved
mid-handshake (the first ~16 SIO transfers after game boot) resumed
at the wrong step in the canned-response table.  The GB Player ROM
verifies those responses, so a mismatch would either stall the
handshake or - in the worst case - drop into an error path.  Once
the handshake completes gbp_seq_n cycles through indices 12..15 and
the practical impact shrinks, but gbp_rumble and especially the
allow-rumble latch matter throughout the session: the latch is set
on first execution from cart-ROM space and stays set; saving before
it fires would defer rumble forever, since loaded state replays the
saved 'pre-ROM' condition.

Added gbp_get_state / gbp_set_state accessors in gbp.c, packed into
a single u32 (low 4 bits = sequence counter, bit 4 = rumble flag,
bit 5 = allow-rumble latch) since all three values are small and
keeping them as one BSON int32 is the lightest schema change.
Declarations in serial.h next to the existing gbp_reset/gbp_transfer
prototypes.  Round-trip in main.c's "emu" subdocument alongside the
existing serial-irq-cycles and rand-state fields.

Read path is optional: missing "gbp-state" in older states leaves
the in-memory values alone, which after gbp_reset on content load
is gbp_seq_n=0, gbp_rumble=false, gbp_allow_rumble=false - safe
boot defaults.

video: fix mosaic skip in rotated-bitmap render path

In render_scanline_bitmap's ROTATED sub-path (mode-3/4/5 bitmap
modes when REG_BG2PC is nonzero, i.e., rotation applied) the loop
counter 'i' was declared but never incremented, so 'i % mosh'
constant-folded to 0 and the mosaic skip never triggered.  The
observable effect: BG2 horizontal mosaic was silently ignored on
rotated-bitmap scanlines, while it worked correctly on the BLIT and
SCALED sibling paths in the same function and on the other affine
renderers (render_affine_background, render_affine_object).

mosaic sites (see the prior 'video: replace i % mosh with a
down-counter' commit for the rationale).  The counter triggers at
i == 0 and every mosh iterations thereafter, matching the semantics
of GBA BG mosaic (re-sample the source every Nth destination
pixel, copy the previous sample to intervening pixels).

Caveat for the reviewer: this changes observable behavior in the
rotated-bitmap-with-mosaic case.  The trigger surface is small
(bitmap mode + rotation + BG2 mosaic enabled + REG_MOSAIC.horiz
nonzero), but if any game's visual output happens to rely on the
prior (incorrect) always-sample behavior, this is a visual
regression for that game.  No reference-hardware A/B was performed;
the fix is justified by analogy to the working SCALED-bitmap and
affine-object paths and by the GBA TRM's description of BG mosaic
semantics.  If a regression is reported, revert this commit and
investigate against mGBA or NanoboyAdvance.

gba_memory: hoist rom_scan_signatures_in_memory loop counter for C89 build

The for-loop in rom_scan_signatures_in_memory declared its counter
in the for-init clause:

    for (u32 i = 0; i < chunk_size - 10; i += 4)

This is C99 syntax; toolchains compiling gpsp in -std=gnu89 mode
(gcc's traditional default for older versions, still in active use
on some libretro target platforms) reject it with:

    error: 'for' loop initial declarations are only allowed in
    C99 or C11 mode

The rest of the codebase uses gnu89-compatible idioms (// comments,
inline, long long, mixed declarations after statements are all
gnu89 extensions; declaration-in-for-init is not).  Hoist the
counter to a separate u32 i; declaration at the block top to match.

No behavior change; the loop body and termination conditions are
identical.
