gba_memory: drive RTC from a load-time baseline + frame_counter

The emulated RTC read paths (RTC_COMMAND_OUTPUT_TIME and
RTC_COMMAND_OUTPUT_TIME_FULL) called time(NULL) and localtime()
directly and fed the result into the bit-stream the game reads. The
game therefore saw a different timestamp on every read, every
session, every machine - which makes record/replay and cross-machine
savestate sharing impossible for any RTC-using title (Pokemon Ruby /
Sapphire / Emerald, Boktai series, Sennen Kazoku, Rockman EXE 4.5).

Replace the wall-clock reads with rtc_current_time(), which returns
rtc_base_time + frame_counter * GBA_FRAME_SECONDS:

  - rtc_base_time is a UNIX timestamp captured once per content load
    via rtc_init_base_time() in load_gamepak.  It is NOT reset by
    init_memory / retro_reset, so the baseline is stable across soft
    resets within a session.
  - frame_counter is the existing global incremented once per vblank
    in main.c::update_gba.  It is already persisted in the 'emu'
    subdocument of the savestate.

Both inputs round-trip through the savestate (rtc_base_time as a new
optional 'rtc-base-time' field in the 'backup' subdocument, stored
as a 2-element u32 array for 64-bit range; falls back to the
load-time capture for forward-compat with older states).  The entire
RTC bit-stream is therefore a pure function of the savestate
contents.  A replay started from a saved state reproduces the same
in-game time on every machine.

frame_counter is used as the time source rather than cpu_ticks
because cpu_ticks is u32 and wraps every ~256 seconds at the native
cycle rate, which would rewind the in-game clock every few minutes.
frame_counter wraps after ~2.27 years of continuous emulation.

GBA_FRAME_SECONDS = 280896 / GBC_BASE_RATE: 280896 is the
cycles-per-frame constant (308 lines * 228 dots * 4 cycles/dot) at
native rate, and the same divisor works at the 60FPS overclock
because GBC_BASE_RATE scales correspondingly.  At native emulation
speed this gives one in-game second per second of wall-clock time;
under fast-forward the in-game clock advances faster, matching real
hardware behaviour where the RTC oscillator is independent of the
CPU clock.

Trade-off: retro_reset zeroes frame_counter without touching
rtc_base_time, so the in-game clock snaps back to the load-time
point on soft reset.  This is the correct semantics for replay
determinism (the post-reset state is fully determined by the inputs
since load) and is what mGBA does as well.

x86: restrict Win64 shadow space allocation to real C-function calls

The earlier commit "x86: allocate Win64 shadow space around JIT-
emitted helper calls" wrapped every generate_function_call site with
'sub $40, %rsp / call / add $40, %rsp'.  That was wrong on two
counts that together produce a crash at startup on Win64 release
builds:

1. Half of the generate_function_call sites do not target real C
   functions - they target hand-written assembly stubs in x86_stub.S:
   x86_update_gba, execute_store_cpsr, and the entire
   execute_load_u8/u16/s8/s16/u32 and
   execute_store_u8/u16/u32/aligned_u32 family.  Asm stubs have no
   compiler-generated argument-spill prologue, so they do not need
   shadow space.  Worse, x86_update_gba has non-local return paths
   ('jne lookup_pc' and 'js return_to_main') that tail-jump out of
   the stub without ever returning to the JIT block's 'add $40, %rsp'
   cleanup, leaking the shadow allocation and corrupting downstream
   stack discipline.  Those stubs also already bracket their own
   internal C calls via CALL_FUNC, which keeps the ABI alignment
   correct from the unwrapped JIT entry point; adding shadow space
   at the JIT->stub boundary throws off the alignment seen by the
   stub's inner CALL_FUNC and faults inside the C helper.

2. generate_branch_no_cycle_update has a hardcoded 'jns +10' that
   skips exactly 'mov $imm32, %eax; call x86_update_gba' (5 + 5

   from 10 to 18 bytes, so the branch then landed inside the call's
   disp32 and the CPU executed garbage on the not-taken path.  The

   first byte of the disp32 with the 'in (%dx), %al' decoding of
   whatever happened to be there.

rel32' (and is used at all 15 asm-stub call sites, unchanged from

and is used at the 6 real C-function call sites: trace_instruction,
execute_spsr_restore, execute_swi (twice), and process_cheats
(twice).  None of those sites sit under a hardcoded byte-offset
jump, so growing them is safe.

This keeps the original fix's intent (real C callees get their
shadow space, runloop_iterate state survives across retro_run on
Win64) while removing the two regressions that the broader wrapping
introduced.

x86: allocate Win64 shadow space around JIT-emitted helper calls

The x86_64 dynarec emits direct 'call rel32' instructions from JIT
blocks into the C helper routines (update_gba, execute_load_*,
execute_store_*, flush_translation_cache_ram, execute_swi,
process_cheats, trace_instruction, ...) via generate_function_call.
On the SysV AMD64 ABI (Linux/macOS) this works because the callee is
free to use the red zone or its own prologue stack adjustment for any
spills it needs.

On the Win64 ABI the caller is required to reserve 32 bytes of
'shadow space' on the stack before any call so the callee can spill
its incoming register arguments (rcx, rdx, r8, r9).  gcc / clang
prologues on Windows routinely emit those spills - 'mov %rcx, 8(%rsp);
mov %rdx, 0x10(%rsp); ...' as the first instructions of any function
that takes register arguments and may need them across an inner call.
Without the caller's shadow allocation those spill stores land on top
of whatever was below the call's pushed return address.

In execute_arm_translate_internal's frame the bytes immediately below
the JIT block's return address are the rbp/rdi/rsi/rbx values pushed
by SAVE_REGISTERS at function entry.  The C helper's prologue clobbers
all four.  When the dynarec eventually returns through return_to_main,
REST_REGISTERS pops the corrupted slots back into rbp/rdi/rsi/rbx, and
control returns to RetroArch's runloop_iterate with rbp holding a stale
rcx value rather than the &runloop_state pointer the host compiler had
pinned there across the retro_run call.  The deref at
'testb , 0x86dc(%rbp)' SIGSEGVs as soon as the next iteration of
runloop_iterate uses that register.

The bug only manifests on Win64 release builds because:
  - SysV builds don't need shadow space.
  - Debug builds run the interpreter, not the JIT.
  - The corruption is masked when the corrupt rbp happens to fall on a
    mapped page (it often does), so crashes look intermittent.
  - Fast-forward executes the JIT ~10x more often per wall-clock second
    and dramatically increases the chance that runloop_iterate touches
    rbp before the next JIT entry overwrites it again.

Win64 only.  40 (not 32) keeps the stack 16-byte aligned at the call
site: execute_arm_translate_internal hands control to the JIT with
%rsp mod 16 == 8; the JIT's 'sub $40' brings that to 0; the 'call'
push lands the callee at mod 16 == 8 as Win64 requires.  32 alone
would leave the cal

dynarec: read GBA opcodes via readaddress* so big-endian hosts work

cpu_threaded.c (the dynarec block scanner and translator) used the
raw address16/address32 macros to read ARM and Thumb opcodes from the
ROM/RAM region, while cpu.cc (the interpreter) used readaddress16/32
which apply eswap. The GBA stores opcodes little-endian in the ROM
image, the file is read into memory byte-for-byte without
byteswapping, so on a big-endian host (PowerPC: PS3, Xbox 360, Wii,
GameCube) the dynarec saw byte-swapped opcodes and produced nonsense
translations, while the interpreter worked correctly.

Five sites need the swap and now use readaddress*:

  - translate_arm_instruction (ARM opcode read at translate time)
  - translate_thumb_instruction (Thumb opcode read at translate time)
  - Thumb PC-relative load const-pool optimization (ROM literal baked
    into the dynarec output)
  - arm_load_opcode (ARM block scanner)
  - thumb_load_opcode (Thumb block scanner)

Four sites in smc_write_arm_yes / smc_write_thumb_yes correctly
remain as raw address* - they compare against zero and write a tag
value, both endian-invariant operations that round-trip through the
same address* macros on read.

dynarec: annotate unused must_swap parameter on x86, MIPS, AArch64

init_emitter(bool must_swap) is called from main.c with
gamepak_must_swap() (true when the ROM is too large to fit in the
resident gamepak buffers and must page in via load_gamepak_page on
read). Only the 32-bit ARM backend specializes its load-handler
dispatch table on this flag; x86, MIPS, and AArch64 simply ignore the
parameter and use the same load handlers either way.

This is by design - on those backends the regular load handlers
already deal with paged reads through the same code path - but a
silently unused parameter looks like a forgotten TODO and trips
-Wunused-parameter on stricter build configurations. Add an explicit
'(void)must_swap;' with a comment in each backend so the intent is
visible.

rfu, savestate: drop wall-clock seeding, persist RNG for replay determinism

The libretro frontend must be able to record an input stream, replay
it later, and get bit-identical output - including over save/load
boundaries. Two sources of non-determinism in the existing RNG path
broke that guarantee:

1. rfu_reset() seeded the global RNG with time(NULL). rfu_reset is
   triggered by a GPIO pulse from the game (and from serial.c when the
   game pokes the right RCNT bit), so the seed varies with wall-clock
   time even though the trigger itself is deterministic. Replaying the
   same input stream produced a different RNG state.

   Drop time(NULL) and keep only cpu_ticks (which is fully determined
   by the GBA program). The rand_seed XOR-fold structure means losing
   one seed source just reduces entropy slightly; for replay use this
   is exactly what we want.

2. new_devid() XORed time(NULL) into every generated device ID. Same
   problem - swap for cpu_ticks.

3. random_state itself (static in main.c) was not persisted in the
   savestate. After load, the next rand_gen() picked up wherever the
   RNG happened to be from this session's execution, not from the
   saved one. Round-trip random_state through the existing 'emu'
   subdocument as an optional field (default = leave alone, so older
   states still load).

For non-replay single-player use the visible effect is nil: the RNG
is only consulted from rfu.c, which is inert outside of RFU netplay.

libretro: guard against NULL info->path in retro_load_game

The core sets need_fullpath = true, so a well-behaved frontend always
provides info->path. But the libretro contract does not strictly
forbid a frontend from calling retro_load_game(info) with info->path
== NULL, and the very first call after this check
(extract_directory(main_path, info->path, ...)) is strcpy on the
NULL pointer. Add the obvious guard.

gba_memory: reject bogus filestream_get_size and fix 1MiB mirror fallback

load_gamepak_raw had two related problems in the ROM-load path:

1. raw_size = (u32)filestream_get_size(...). filestream_get_size
   returns int64_t. A read error yields -1, which casts to 0xFFFFFFFF
   - then raw_size is rounded up to overflow and gamepak_file_blocks
   inherits a wildly wrong value. A file larger than 4 GiB silently
   truncates. Both cases lead to downstream malloc / memset on bogus
   sizes and the wrong number of pages being mapped. Capture the
   int64_t result, reject <= 0 and > 512 MiB (well above any real GBA
   ROM) before casting.

2. The mirror-1MiB fast path materializes a private 4 MiB image that
   contains four copies of the on-disk 1 MiB ROM. If the malloc fails,
   the code silently fell through to the chunked-load branch with
   gamepak_size still set to 4 MiB and gamepak_mirror_1m still true.
   The chunked loader keys rom_blocks off gamepak_size (= 128) but
   only has gamepak_file_blocks (= 32) pages of actual ROM; the upper
   3 MiB of the address range got mapped to garbage. Undo the
   gamepak_size lie and clear the mirror flag in the fallback path so
   that the chunked loader maps a consistent (non-mirrored) 1 MiB
   region instead of a broken 4 MiB one.

cheats: fix OOB pointer construction and stale max_cheat after clear

Two small correctness fixes in cheats.c:

cheat_parse() constructed 'cheat_type *ch = &cheats[index]' before
range-checking 'index'. Forming a pointer beyond a one-past-the-end
position is undefined behavior even if the pointer is never
dereferenced, and the dead bounds check below was unreachable for
out-of-range indices on debug builds that crash on such pointer
arithmetic. Reorder: bounds-check first, then form the pointer.

cheat_clear() reset every slot but left max_cheat at its previous
high-water mark. process_cheats() iterates 'i <= max_cheat' on every
vblank, so after a content swap the scan kept walking inactive slots
from the previous game's cheat set forever. Reset max_cheat to 0
alongside the slot clear.

savestate: close determinism gaps in audio, serial IRQ, input

A libretro frontend should be able to take a savestate, load it back
later, and reproduce the same video/audio/input stream from that frame
forward. Three pieces of state were excluded from the BSON save
document and broke that contract:

1. sound.c::sound_buffer (128 KiB ring) is intentionally not serialized
   to keep the savestate within its GBA_STATE_MEM_SIZE cap, but its
   contents persisted across load. The GBC sound and Direct Sound
   mixers use += into this ring, so stale pre-load samples were mixed
   into the first frame after load. Zero the ring inside
   sound_read_savestate so that any range marked 'in flight' by the
   saved buffer_base / gbc_sound_buffer_index pair decodes as silence
   rather than random data. The cost is at most one frame of silence
   at the load point; the gain is deterministic audio output.

2. serial.c::serial_irq_cycles, the pending serial-IRQ countdown,
   was not saved. A state captured mid-transaction resumed either with
   a permanently stuck SIOCNT busy bit or with a spurious immediate IRQ
   on the next update_serial(). Add small get/set accessors and
   serialize the field through the existing 'emu' subdocument in
   main_*_savestate. The field is read with a sensible default of 0
   when absent, so older savestates load without errors.

3. input.c turbo and GBP-detection state (turbo_a_counter,
   turbo_b_counter, gbp_keypad_frames, gbp_keypad_sent) was not
   saved. Holding a turbo button across save/load desynced the pulse;
   GBP detection rearmed itself on every load. Extend the 'input'
   subdocument with these fields. The new fields are optional on read
   (default to neutral state) so older savestates remain compatible.

savestate: harden BSON parser against malformed/malicious states

Three related defects in the BSON deserialization layer:

1. bson_read_int32_array dereferences a NULL pointer when the requested
   key is missing. After the 'if (p) { ... }' early-return path, the
   function falls through to '*value = bson_read_u32(p);' with p == NULL,
   which is a guaranteed crash. The fall-through line is also pointless
   (the function is about to return false). Remove it.

2. bson_read_int32_array ignored its 'cnt' parameter and trusted the
   array element count encoded in the BSON document. A crafted savestate
   that claims a larger array than the caller allocated will overflow
   the destination buffer (e.g. reg[REG_ARCH_COUNT] in cpu_read_savestate,
   spsr[6], reg_mode[7*7], or rtc_data_array[2] in memory_read_savestate).
   Reject any state whose array size does not match the expected count.

3. bson_read_u32 expanded to '(p[3] << 24) | ...' where p is a u8*.
   Each element undergoes default integer promotion to signed int; for
   bytes >= 0x80, the '<< 24' shift moves the value into the sign bit
   of int, which is undefined behavior per the C standard. Cast to u32
   before shifting.

Standardize endianness detection on MSB_FIRST

common.h previously gated eswap16/eswap32/netorder32 on
__BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__, while arm/arm_codegen.h gated
ARM bitfield layouts on MSB_FIRST. The Makefile already passes
-DMSB_FIRST for PowerPC targets. On gcc/clang the two checks happen to
agree, but a toolchain that defines neither (or only MSB_FIRST via the
build system) silently picked the wrong eswap branch, producing
incorrect reads from palette RAM, OAM, IO registers, tile data and so
on.

Make MSB_FIRST the single source of truth across the codebase:

  - At the top of common.h, auto-define MSB_FIRST when any of the
    common toolchain endianness macros indicate big-endian
    (__BYTE_ORDER__/__ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__, __BIG_ENDIAN__, _BIG_ENDIAN,
    __BYTE_ORDER/__BIG_ENDIAN). The auto-detect only fires when
    MSB_FIRST is not already defined, so -DMSB_FIRST from CFLAGS still
    wins.
  - Switch the netorder32 and eswap16/eswap32 conditionals from
    __BYTE_ORDER__ to MSB_FIRST.

arm/arm_codegen.h already uses MSB_FIRST and is unchanged. The
existing -DMSB_FIRST entries in the Makefile remain (now redundant on
gcc/clang but harmless, and they keep working for any toolchain that
doesn't expose the standard predefined endian macros).

iamboosted/fire-mission-play.readme:
# Fire Mission — play in your browser

A co-op artillery game. This repository only holds the built game that GitHub Pages serves; there is
no server and nothing to install.

**Play:** open the GitHub Pages address of this repository in Chrome, Edge or Firefox.

**Co-op:** one player presses **Host co-op** and sends the invite code to a friend privately. The
friend presses **Join with code**, pastes it and sends back the reply code. Nobody can join a battle
unless the host pastes their reply. Game traffic goes directly between the two browsers, encrypted.

Third-party assets and their licences are listed in [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

ItsDanik/DXXRebirth_MiSTer.readme:
# DXXRebirth for MiSTer

Descent and Descent II on [MiSTer FPGA](https://github.com/MiSTer-devel/Main_MiSTer/wiki) as a hybrid port.

The games themselves are [DXX-Rebirth](https://www.dxx-rebirth.com/) (D1X-Rebirth and D2X-Rebirth), the source port of the Descent and Descent II engines, with its software renderer. They run on the MiSTer's ARM CPU. The DXXRebirth FPGA core provides native 15kHz video (CRT, VGA and HDMI) at 320x200 or 320x240, 44.1kHz audio, the music on its FM chip or MIDI synthesizer, and keyboard, mouse and gamepad input with rumble. The two halves talk through shared DDR3 memory.

> **Beta.** Expect rough edges and please report problems in the issues.

Disclaimer: AI is being used to speed up development of this project.

## Requirements

- **danik_hybrid_ports**, the launcher (`Scripts/danik_hybrid_ports.sh`): run it **once** from the MiSTer's `Scripts` menu. It starts the game whenever its menu entry is loaded, keeps running after a reboot, and serves all our hybrid ports; its screen picks which ports and games to have, and can keep them up to date through `update_all`. It replaces `danik_hybrid_cores`, the launcher before it, and moves ports installed the old way into the new folders by itself. Without it the core says "Game not running".
- **Game data**, which is not included: your own copy of Descent and/or Descent II (the versions sold by GOG and Steam work), or the free shareware and demo versions. One of the two games is enough.

## Installation

With `update_all` (Downloader 2.4 or newer, which update_all keeps up to date):

1. Copy [`downloader_danik_hybrid_ports.ini`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ItsDanik/Hybrid_MiSTer/main/launcher/downloader_danik_hybrid_ports.ini) to the root of your SD card (`/media/fat`).
2. Run `update_all`. That installs the launcher, **danik_hybrid_ports**, in `Scripts`.
3. Run **danik_hybrid_ports** from the `Scripts` menu, tick the games you want and press *X: Apply*. They are installed, and update_all keeps them up to date.

By hand:

1. Download the newest `DXXRebirth_YYYYMMDD.zip` from [releases](releases/) and extract it to the root of your SD card (`/media/fat`). That gives you:
   - `_Other/dnk-Descent.mgl` and `_Other/dnk-Descent II.mgl`, the games' entries in the `Other` menu
   - `_Other/dnk/dnk-DXXRebirth_YYYYMMDD.rbf`, the FPGA core
   - `games/dnk/DXXRebirth/`, the game binaries and their launch script
   - `games/dnk/SoundFonts/`, the SoundFont of the core's MIDI synthesizer
   - `Scripts/danik_hybrid_ports.sh`, the launcher (from [Hybrid_MiSTer](https://github.com/ItsDanik/Hybrid_MiSTer))
   - `downloader_danik_hybrid_ports.ini`, with which `update_all` keeps the ports up to date from then on
2. Copy the game data to `/media/fat/games/dnk/DXXRebirth/`: everything in the folder of your Descent, of your Descent II, or of both, into that one folder. Among the files are:

   | Game | Files |
   |---|---|
   | Descent | `descent.hog`, `descent.pig` |
   | Descent II | `descent2.hog`, `descent2.ham`, `descent2.s11`, `descent2.s22`, `alien1.pig`, `alien2.pig`, `fire.pig`, `groupa.pig`, `ice.pig`, `water.pig`; the movies `intro-l.mvl`, `other-l.mvl`, `robots-l.mvl` |
   | Descent II demo | `d2demo.hog`, `d2demo.ham`, `d2demo.pig` |

   The shareware version of Descent has the same two file names as the full game. Of the Descent II movies the low resolution ones (`-l.mvl`) are the size of the screen; if only the high resolution ones (`-h.mvl`) are there, they are scaled down. Missions (`.hog` with `.msn` or `.mn2`) go into `games/dnk/DXXRebirth/descent/missions/` (Descent) and `descent2/missions/` (Descent II).
3. Run **danik_hybrid_ports** from the `Scripts` menu, if you have not done so before (see Requirements).
4. Load **dnk-Descent** or **dnk-Descent II** from the `Other` menu.

The game data can go on a USB drive instead, into the same folder there (`/media/usb0/games/dnk/DXXRebirth/`): the game looks for it there first, and then keeps its settings and saved games there as well. Everything else stays on the SD card.

Loaded by itself (`_Other/dnk/`), the core shows a list of the games whose data is there. Pilots, settings, saved games and demos are in `games/dnk/DXXRebirth/descent/` and `descent2/`. The log is in `/media/fat/logs/dnk/DXXRebirth/dxxrebirth.log`.

The data of the first versions of this port, in `games/d1x-rebirth/` and `games/d2x-rebirth/`, is moved into the new folders by the launcher.

## OSD options

| Option | |
|---|---|
| Aspect ratio, Scale, Scandoubler Fx, Stereo Mix | as in other cores |
| FPS Counter | shows the pictures per second in the top left corner |
| HDMI Only | **Yes** if no CRT is connected: resolutions of 640x400 and more are then progressive instead of interlaced, and the analog output is switched off while one is shown, so that a 15kHz screen can never get such a signal. Nothing changes at lower resolutions. Not needed with `forced_scandoubler=1` (VGA monitor); not there with `direct_video=1` |
| CRT Options | for a 15kHz screen: *Horizontal Size*, *Horizontal Pos* and *Vertical Pos* fit the picture to it. The pixels stay as they are; HDMI is not affected. The size is for the game's picture: the core's own, with its messages, keeps its width. Not there with `forced_scandoubler=1`. *HUD (Top)* and *HUD (Bottom)*: in 320x240, how far the HUD is from the top and the bottom edge of the screen, to keep it out of a CRT's overscan |
| Sound Volume, Music Volume | on top of the volumes in the game's own *Sound effects & music* options |
| Resolution | **320x200**, the games' own, or **320x240**: the view fills all 240 lines from edge to edge, with the cockpit, the status bar and the HUD drawn over it at the HUD margins. Menus, briefings and movies stay 320x200 in the middle |
| Music | **MIDI**: the music is played by an MT32-pi when one is connected and on, else by the core's MIDI synthesizer with the SoundFont below. **FM chip**: by the core's OPL2, as on a Sound Blaster |
| SoundFo

thadomaloma/hnahsin-play.desc: Learn Mizo words by playing. Free word games and a Mizo house to tap and turn, on any phone, no sign-up.
thadomaloma/hnahsin-play.readme:
# Hnahsin Games

Learn Mizo words by playing. Free, on any phone, no sign-up.

**Play here: https://thadomaloma.github.io/hnahsin-play/**

![Hnahsin](og.jpg)

## What you can play

- **Rova's Journey.** Rova runs across Mizoram, from the hills to Phawngpui.
  Jump into the door with the right Mizo word. Five levels, with Mizo
  sayings (tawng upa) and sentences at the end of each level.
- **Hnahsin Playground.** 21 small games:
  - word puzzles: Spelling bee, Waffle, Strands, Word tubes, Sort it
  - quick games: Rova run, Bubble pop, Whack the rat
  - everyday Mizo: Bazar, I Spy, Count, Dress Rova, Big and small, Days and
    times, Rova says, Colour it, Rova's family, Weather report, Food stall
  - sentences and sayings: Sentence builder, Saying match
- **Touch and learn.** A Mizo house you can tap, turn and play with. Tap a
  part to see its Mizo name, look inside, change the time of day, make it
  rain or blow, meet the family, have Rova and Mami visit, pick up the hen's
  eggs, or play Find it. Also Puan tah: pi weaves a Mizo puan on her loom,
  and you pick the colours.
- **The Hnahsin app.** A preview of the app in your browser. The app is
  coming to Android and iPhone.

A **word of the day** on the home page: tap the card to see what it means.

## Words

- 1,254 Mizo words, 383 sentences and 203 sayings from the Hnahsin app
- 1,928 more words from J.F. Laldailova's English–Lushai Dictionary,
  used with permission
- photos from Wikimedia Commons (credited in the app) and pictures from
  Microsoft's Fluent Emoji

## Put it on your phone

The games work like an app and play without internet after the first visit.

- **iPhone:** open the link in Safari, tap **Share**, then **Add to Home Screen**.
- **Android:** open the link in Chrome and tap **Install Hnahsin**.

## Privacy

The site counts which pages and games are opened and won, with
[GoatCounter](https://www.goatcounter.com/). It uses no cookies and keeps
nothing that tells who you are. Your stars and levels stay on your phone.

## For developers

The pages are plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, served by GitHub Pages.
`source/` holds what the game pages are built from, and
[source/README.md](source/README.md) says how to rebuild them.

## Versions and feedback

- What changed in each version: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and
  [Releases](https://github.com/thadomaloma/hnahsin-play/releases).
- Found a wrong word, a broken game or have an idea?
  [Open an issue](https://github.com/thadomaloma/hnahsin-play/issues/new/choose).
- Where the words, pictures and tools come from: [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

## Copyright

© 2026 Maloma Thado. All rights reserved.

You are welcome to play the games. Please do not copy the code, words,
pictures or design into another site or app without asking first.

Developed by Maloma Thado.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sample IOP emulator state; boot now waits on MultiStream file load

The sampler also prints the IOP emulator's cycle/instruction counts,
module/thread/RPC-server counts and diagnostics. With FILEIO bound, main
runs game code and now waits for STREAM.IRX (emulated IOP) to finish a
SOUND_LoadFile request that never completes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bind libkernl FILEIO; add handler trace and base-context sampling

The loading screen stalled because main sat in sceFsInit's raw bind loop
on SIF RPC 0x80000001 (FILEIO). Bind sceFsInit/sceFsReset and the file
calls sceOpen/sceClose/sceRead/sceWrite/sceLseek/sceIoctl to runtime
handlers (stub_count 103 -> 111).

Found with two new diagnostics: WORMS3D_HANDLERS=1 traces handler/alarm
registration, and the sampler prints each thread's base context under
queued handler invocations (needs the PS2Recomp branch's snapshot fields).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

First graphics: loading logo renders with the PS2Recomp VIF1 fix

The VIF1 PATH2 continuation fix (PS2Recomp branch
worms3d/gif-path2-continuation) gets the loading sprites' CLUTs to the
GS; the animated Worms 3D logo now shows on Windows. Builds depend on
that branch, noted in CLAUDE.md. The WORMS half of the logo still looks
partly scrambled (suspected PSMT8-over-CT32 swizzle).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add GS watch/dump diagnostics; trace the black screen to missing CLUTs

WORMS3D_GSWATCH counts distinct GS draw states; WORMS3D_GSDUMP logs all
GS transfers from boot, prints the GS history and saves the draw/display
buffers and loading textures as PNGs in the deploy folder.

Findings: the 32->16 display copy is a strip-wise ctx2 sprite pass with
ALPHA 0x29 (plain copy). The real cause of the black screen is upstream:
the loading sprites' CLUTs (0x3600/0x3700) are never uploaded. The game
sends each CLUT as the continuation of a VIF1 DIRECT GIF packet (texture
IMAGE with EOP=0, then an NREG=3 setup without TRXPOS), and those never
reach the GS registers in the runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add an EE/GS sampler for Windows runs

WORMS3D_SAMPLE=<seconds> starts a host thread in the override that
prints the EE scheduler snapshot (thread states, waits, pc/ra/sp), the
GS display registers and the GS draw targets. run-win.sh forwards the
variable to the Windows process via WSLENV.

First findings: the game runs a loading animation thread that draws
32-bit into FBP 0xa0 while the display reads a 16-bit buffer at 0x140,
so the screen stays black until the conversion pass is handled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep handler stacks off the main thread stack; add Windows screenshots

The game's main thread stack is the top 64 KB of RAM (SetupThread with
stack 0x01ff0000, size 0x10000), and the runtime carves handler stacks
downward from the same place. The first handler overwrote main's frame,
which corrupted the argument list and cascaded into bogus string frees
and memset(ptr, 0xDD, -4). Reserve that region from the handler stack
allocator in the override.

First native Windows runs: modules load and the game runs without errors;
the window stays black so far. tools/screenshot-win.sh captures it into
the deploy folder.

  now applies to the whole build: GCC gates the runtime's SSE4.1
  intrinsics too.

  location written to; tools/run-win.sh runs it natively from there.
- Windows builds boot iso/SLUS_208.94 relative to the exe; the override

- Replace the committed host0 symlinks with tools/setup-host0.sh copies:
  Windows cannot follow WSL symlinks, and the IRXs are disc content.
- headless.sh writes its batch file into the deploy folder, not %TEMP%.
- CLAUDE.md documents the deploy folder and the iteration loop.

- Set the runtime's CD image from the .iso next to the ELF: the game

- Point host0: at game/host0, lowercase links to the disc IRXs, so the

# hmwh.men

The He Man Woman Haters Club league site, served by Cloudflare Pages behind Cloudflare Access.

- `public/index.html` is the whole site (Home, Power Rankings, Pick'em, Statistics, League History, Trades, Lore, Videos).
- `public/data/site.json` holds the league data. The scheduled update runs (Fri / Mon / Tue mornings) rewrite this file from ESPN via Flaim and FantasyCalc; the page reads it on load.

Deployed with `npx wrangler deploy`. `wrangler.jsonc` serves `public/` as static assets and runs `src/worker.js` for `/api/*`.

## Head-to-Head
- `public/data/h2h.json` holds every game since 2015 (regular season, playoffs and consolation) plus each season's owner and team name per franchise slot. Records count regular season and playoffs. Pulled from ESPN via Flaim and checked against each season's final standings. The update runs append each new week.

## Draft Results
- `public/data/draft.json` holds every pick from completed drafts (2025 and 2024 so far) with each player's year-end points under league scoring, from ESPN via Flaim. Each pick gets pts over or under expected: the k-th player taken at a position that season is expected to score what the k-th best drafted player at that position scored, and anyone below waiver-wire level (12th QB, 28th RB, 34th WR, 13th TE, 11th K that season) counts as waiver level. Team totals sum their picks. No letter grades. Add a season once its playoffs end.

## Home
- The scoreboard colors the team name by head-to-head result and the score by bonus win (top 5 weekly score). The Week 7 matchups box shows projections until `live7.kickoff` in `site.json`, then live scores from `live7.scores` (rewritten on each update run, with `asOf`).

## Lore
- Members submit a date, title, description and optional co-author from the Lore tab (login must be linked to a team via Pick'em). Submissions land in the `lore` table of the `League` Durable Object as `pending`. The Groundskeeper (`ADMIN_EMAILS`) sees a Review queue on the Lore tab: edit the text and sort year, then Publish or Reject. Published entries appear on the timeline with a byline. API: `GET/POST /api/lore`, `POST /api/admin/lore`.

## Groundskeeper
- Admin-only tab (visible only to `ADMIN_EMAILS` logins; the API enforces it). Switches are stored in the `settings` table of the `League` Durable Object: `gold` (playoff gold graphics; uses `img/hmwh-logo-gold.png` when present, otherwise tints the chrome logo), `welcome` (first-visit team picker), `loreOpen` (lore submissions) and `wireframe` (header tag). Everyone reads them from `GET /api/settings`; the admin flips them with `POST /api/admin/settings`. The Team links list shows who linked which team and can unlock one (`POST /api/admin/release`).

## Trades
- `public/data/trades.json` holds every completed 2026 trade with both sides' players and FantasyCalc values. The update runs add new trades once they clear review and re-score them.

## Pick'em
- `public/data/pickem.json` is the schedule: the current week, when picks open and lock, the five games, which one is the 2x Game of the Week, and each game's winner once it's final. The Tuesday update writes the next week's games and fills in last week's winners.
- Picks are stored in a Durable Object (SQLite) called `League`. Each member links their login to one team the first time they visit; the Groundskeeper (`ADMIN_EMAILS`) can undo a link and can save picks before a week opens.
- Scoring: 1 point per correct pick, 2 for the Game of the Week.
- Optional hardening: set `ACCESS_TEAM` (your Zero Trust team name) and `ACCESS_AUD` (the Access app's Application Audience tag) as Worker variables and the Worker will verify Cloudflare Access's signed login token instead of trusting the email header.

Status: wireframe. Design pass, all-time history, the rebuilt Trade Ledger and stored pick'em are still to come.

tsteinemann/Spotcast.readme:
# Spotcast

**Know where. Know when.** The forecast for where to fish.

Spotcast is an installable web app for Florida anglers. Pan anywhere along the Florida coast, search a town, or use your location. Spots load automatically for whatever is on screen: passes, bridges, channel drop-offs, tidal flats, mangrove shorelines, oyster bars, public docks and man-made reefs. Each one is rated Hot, Great, Good or Fair for every hour of the next seven days from live tides, wind, moon and light. Every rating shows its reasons, and every spot has a short game plan.

## Use it

Open the GitHub Pages link on your phone:

- **iPhone (Safari):** tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
- **Android (Chrome):** tap Install, or Install app from the browser menu.

## Data

All data is public and fetched live from the phone:

- NOAA CO-OPS tide predictions and water temperature
- National Weather Service hourly forecast
- NOAA NCEI elevation models (shaded relief and depth contours)
- FWC inlets and passes, oyster beds, tidal flats, mangroves, marinas and docks, artificial reefs, and hard bottom
- FDOT and local bridge locations
- Esri World Imagery, reference labels and geocoder; OpenStreetMap Nominatim as backup search

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | Page layout and styles |
| `app.js` | Spot generation, scoring, map rendering and data loading |
| `stations.json` | Florida NOAA tide and water-temperature stations |
| `sw.js` | Service worker: offline shell, tile and data caching |
| `manifest.webmanifest`, `icons/` | Home screen install |

Not for navigation. Depths are approximate.

Marcsarno/Sarno-Legends.readme:
# Sarno Legends

A family roguelike deckbuilder built on Slay the Spire's proven rules, with a small spin: Marc and Yola share one deck and one HP bar, Marc staggers zombies and Yola cashes in, and every kill plays a real finisher or death animation. Floor by floor through the hospital; weapon upgrades carry between runs. Painted 2D battle rooms, 3D animated characters.

**Play it:** https://sarno-legends.vercel.app (phone sideways, or desktop). **Watch it being built:** https://sarno-legends.vercel.app/build-log/

**Status:** act 1 is playable start to finish: title → Shift Change → the hospital floor map → fights, elites, supply closets,
pharmacy, locked rooms, a supply crate → the Shield Guard → victory or defeat → scrap into the Armory (weapon unlocks).
Story, event text and voice lines are placeholders for Marc.

## Run and check

```
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5180/  (?seed=ABC  ?speed=2  ?debug=1  ?shot=<scene>)
npm test             # 150 rules tests (node --test)
npm run playtest     # the bot plays a whole run in headless Chromium; fails on any error or softlock
npm run sim          # balance sim: tools/sim/run.mjs --runs 300 --bot all (docs/BALANCE.md)
npm run build        # vite build -> dist/ (deployed by Vercel on every push to main)
npm run assets       # rebuild public/assets from ../yola-zombie and ../survival (read-only)
npm run bake         # re-bake painted rooms, card art and icons into public/assets/baked/ (after changing painter/studio)
python tools/voice/generate.py --marc am_michael --yola af_heart   # regenerate voice barks (tools/voice/README.md)
node tools/snap.mjs --plan tools/snap-plan.json --stage N --base http://localhost:PORT/   # build-log frames
```
Test pages for each module: `labs/*.html` (render, painter, ui, screens, audio, voice). `/labs/voice.html` is also on the live site for picking voices.

## Code

- `src/game/`: pure rules (no DOM): seeded RNG, combat engine and its event contract, run layer (map, rewards, rest, shop, events), meta (scrap, weapons), all content.
- `src/render/`: three.js stage, actors, weapons, effects, the director (pacing), the room painter and the studio (card art, icons).
- `src/ui/`: cards, hand, HUD, tooltips, coach bubbles, all screens. `src/audio/`: sound, music, voice barks. `src/app/`: the app shell that wires it together, saves, the coach, the debug API (`window.__SL`).
- `docs/BUILD_SPEC.md`: the build contract. `docs/BUILD_LOG.md`: what changed, stage by stage. `docs/STATE.md`: where things stand.

## Docs

- `docs/BUILD_LOG.md` and `docs/STATE.md`: the build, step by step, and where it stands now.
- `docs/GAME_CORE.md`: **start here** for the design. The decided plan: Slay the Spire's rules plus our spins (two heroes, one deck, one HP bar; Marc staggers, Yola cashes in; the kill picks the animation), with starting numbers, zombies, the meta, and the first steps.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: Marc's words and decisions, in order.
- `docs/RESEARCH_NOTES.md`: findings and sources from six research passes, plus the critic, verifier and audit verdicts.
- `docs/RESEARCH_DETAIL.md`: the detailed proposals: card pools, family sets, scrap and the bat tree, floor 1, pacing, phone layout, game feel, the drift checklist, sim results.
- `docs/ASSETS.md`: the art we can reuse (heroes, zombies, chapter-2 survivors and looters, weapons, props) and licence notes.
- `docs/DECKBUILDER_PLAN.md`: the earlier, bigger card plan. Mostly parked; `GAME_CORE.md` wins where they differ.
- `docs/COMBAT_DESIGN.md`: the earlier turn-based design (superseded).
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`: milestones, art direction and story structure from the turn-based phase (still useful for look and story).
- `docs/reviews/`: the critic and audit inputs as they were.
- `tools/balance-sim/`, `tools/card-sim/`, `tools/turn-sim-verifier/`: the throwaway sims behind the numbers.

## Rules

- Art comes from `Marcsarno/yola-zombie` and `Marcsarno/survival`. Those repos are **read-only** for this project: copy files out, never write to them.
- Marc decides the story. Don't invent story beats.

# USA Volleyball Nutrition

Athlete nutrition app for USA Volleyball national team athletes: menus, smoothies, court snacks, a food journal, nutrition answers and RD booking.

## Updating content (no coding)

Menus, smoothies, recipes, court snacks and announcements come from the Google Sheet **USAV Nutrition App Content**. Edit the sheet and athletes see the change the next time they open the app. The "How to edit" tab in the sheet explains each column.

Rules that keep it working:
- Don't rename the tabs or the header row.
- Week = 1, 2, 3…; Day = Mon–Fri.
- Allergens: Dairy, Egg, Wheat/Gluten, Peanut, Tree nut, Soy, Fish, Shellfish, Sesame (comma separated).
- Smoothie flavor names must match the Recipes tab exactly.
- Keep the sheet's sharing at "Anyone with the link can view".

If the sheet can't be reached, the app falls back to the content built into `index.html`.

## Settings in `index.html`

Near the top of the script, `CONFIG` holds:
- `whatsapp`, `whatsappUser`, `whatsappLink`: Nutrition 411 contact
- `bookingLink`: Calendly page
- `sheetId`: the Google Sheet ID (the long code in the sheet's address between `/d/` and `/edit`)

## Privacy

Athlete profiles (including allergies), session requests and food feedback go to the dietitian's Google Form inbox, which emails the dietitian each new submission. Food journal entries stay on each athlete's phone. Nothing about athletes is stored in this repository or in the content sheet.

## Hosting

Served with GitHub Pages from the `main` branch root.

semputs/gtype.readme:
# GalType (gtype)

Claude's version of GalType, a typing game where hypnotized festival-goers run at you with love confessions and you type their lines to snap them out of it. See the design doc for the full plan (5 stages, bosses, story).

**Play:** https://semput.com/gtype/

## Current build: 2 stages
- **Stage 1 · Main Hall:** Hana, Mio, Rei, Sayaka, Nemu, then the boss **Kaede** (festival committee chair).
- **Stage 2 · Sports Complex:** Chika, Ayame, Haruka, Tomoe, Hana, Sayaka, then the boss **Akira (Super)**.
- Regular girls run or walk at their own speed (Hana and Tomoe sprint, Nemu shuffles). Each has two movement frames, a waist-up **flustered** close-up when she reaches you (1.6 s fuse to still type her word) and her own comical **rejected** pose.
- **Bosses** hover and drift down the hall with a glowing aura. Each finished line, or a line you run out of time on (yellow timer bar), makes her dash a step closer, leaving afterimages. Her **last two lines** she says right in your face as a flustered close-up; running out of time there costs a heart and knocks her back down the hall. On the very last line she slowly pushes in closer; beat it and her rejected pose fills the screen before she is blasted back down the hall.
- Clearing stage 1 gives back one heart. "Skip to stage 2" on the title screen jumps straight there. **Slow motion** (bottom left) plays at 35% speed.

Everyone wears the festival whites (white blouse, white mid-thigh skirt, white sneakers) plus their own fixed accessories; club members wear their club gear.

## Files
- `index.html` — page, styles and screens. `game.js` — the game.
- `assets/sprites/<girl>_walk1|walk2|flustered|defeated.webp` — transparent sprites; `meta.js` lists frames whose canvas is taller than walk1.
- `assets/bg/stage1.jpg`, `stage2.jpg` — one-point-perspective backgrounds (horizon at 54% of the height, `hz` in `game.js`).
- `tools/cut.py` — background removal (line art works as a wall, so white clothes survive). `tools/build_sprites.py` — turns chosen renders into aligned sprites (walk2 for regular girls = walk1 mirrored with the head kept).

All art generated in ComfyUI with Animagine XL 4.0 (832×1216 sprites, 1344×768 backgrounds, 28 steps, CFG 5, euler_ancestral). Flustered and rejected frames were partly made image-to-image from each girl's approved run frame to keep her outfit consistent.

## Branches
- `main` — the 2D game.
- `3d` — the parked three.js/VRM version.

## Hosting
Static files. Serve the folder as-is at `/gtype/`; updating is a `git pull`.

LumielX/GameByClaude.readme:
# BOO-TRAYAL — ผีป่วน เพื่อนแปรพักตร์

> เกมผีไทยตลกหลอน เล่นออนไลน์กับเพื่อน 2–8 คน · สถานะ: **alpha** (ทดลองเล่น)

ช่วยกันปิดผนึก ขนโกศกับกระถางธูปไปแท่นบูชาข้างศาลพระภูมิ แล้ววิ่งหนีผีกระสือออกประตูรั้วให้ทันก่อนรุ่งสาง — แต่ระวัง ถ้าเล่น 5 คนขึ้นไป เพื่อนบางคนอาจเป็น **ร่างทรง** ที่แอบป่วนอยู่ ตีระฆังเรียกประชุม คุยกัน แล้วโหวตไล่ให้ถูกคน

![หน้าแรก](docs/ui_screens/title-th.png)
![ในเกม](docs/ui_screens/hud-th.png)

## ดาวน์โหลดและติดตั้ง
1. ไปที่หน้า [Releases](https://github.com/LumielX/GameByClaude/releases) แล้วโหลดไฟล์ `BOO-TRAYAL-v…-win64.zip` ของเวอร์ชันล่าสุด
2. แตกไฟล์ zip ทั้งโฟลเดอร์ไว้ที่ไหนก็ได้ (อย่าเปิดจากใน zip ตรงๆ)
3. ดับเบิลคลิก `BOO-TRAYAL.exe`
   - ถ้าขึ้นจอสีฟ้า **"Windows protected your PC"** (ไทย: "Windows ได้ป้องกันพีซีของคุณ") ให้กด **More info / ข้อมูลเพิ่มเติม** แล้ว **Run anyway / เรียกใช้ต่อไป** (เกมยังไม่ได้เซ็นใบรับรอง)
   - ถ้าขึ้น **"Smart App Control blocked"** แบบไม่มีปุ่มให้ไปต่อ แปลว่า Windows 11 เปิด Smart App Control ไว้ ซึ่งบล็อกเกมที่ไม่ได้เซ็นทุกเกม (ปิดได้ที่ Windows Security → App & browser control → Smart App Control แต่ปิดแล้วเปิดกลับไม่ได้ถ้าไม่ลง Windows ใหม่)
   - ถ้า Firewall ถาม ให้กด **Allow** เพื่อเล่นออนไลน์ได้

**เครื่องที่ใช้ได้:** Windows 10/11 64 บิต, การ์ดจอที่รองรับ DirectX 11/12, อินเทอร์เน็ต (สำหรับเล่นออนไลน์), ไมค์ไม่บังคับ

## เล่นกับเพื่อน
- **คนสร้างห้อง:** เล่น → สร้างห้อง → ตั้งจำนวนคน/ความยาวคืน/ร่างทรง → ส่ง **รหัสห้อง 6 ตัว** ให้เพื่อน
- **คนเข้าห้อง:** เล่น → ใส่รหัสห้อง → เข้าห้อง (เล่นต่างเน็ต ต่างบ้านได้)
- ทุกคนต้องใช้ **เวอร์ชันเดียวกัน** (ดูที่มุมหน้าแรก)
- เสียงคุยในเกมเปิดเองในห้องออนไลน์: คุยกันตามระยะ, ตอนประชุมได้ยินทั้งห้อง, ผีจิ๋วคุยกันเอง — ตั้ง "กด V ค้างเพื่อพูด" ได้
- อยากลองก่อน: เล่น → **เริ่มซ้อม** (ออฟไลน์ ไม่มีร่างทรง)

| ปุ่ม | ทำอะไร |
|---|---|
| WASD / Shift / Space / Ctrl | เดิน / วิ่ง / กระโดด / ย่อ |
| E | หยิบ / ใช้ |
| คลิกซ้าย / G / คลิกขวา | ขว้าง / วาง / ผลัก |
| F | ไฟฉาย (ส่องหน้าผี 2 วิ ผีหนี) |
| Z | กรี๊ด (ผีจิ๋ว: บู้) |
| V | กดคุย (ถ้าตั้งไว้) |
| Q / X | ร่างทรง: ป่วนปริศนาใกล้ตัว / ดับไฟทั้งโซน |
| Esc | หยุดเกม |

## ปัญหาที่รู้แล้ว
- ภาพยังเป็นงานชั่วคราว: บ้านเป็นทรงเรขาคณิต, เส้นขอบโมเดลแตกตรงมุมบางจุด, ท่าถือของขาไม่ขยับ
- ความยากในหน้าสร้างห้องยังไม่มีผล
- เตะคนออกแล้วเข้ากลับได้ทันที
- ถ้าเครื่องเพื่อนเด้งออกจากเกม ช่องของเขาอาจค้างในล็อบบี้; คนที่ออกไปแล้วยังอยู่ในตารางอันดับ
- หยิบของทะลุกำแพงบางมุมได้

## เจอบั๊ก / ให้ความเห็น
- แจ้งที่ [Issues](https://github.com/LumielX/GameByClaude/issues) พร้อมแนบไฟล์ log:
  `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\LumielX\BOO-TRAYAL\Player.log` (วางในช่องที่อยู่ของ File Explorer)
- รายการสิ่งที่อยากให้ลองเล่น: [docs/PLAYTEST_CHECKLIST.md](docs/PLAYTEST_CHECKLIST.md)

## สร้างเกมจากซอร์สโค้ด
- Unity **6000.6.7f1** (Windows Build Support, Mono), Blender 5.2 (ถ้าจะสร้างโมเดลใหม่)
- ทุกฉาก/prefab/UI สร้างด้วยโค้ดใน `Assets/_Project/Editor/Builders` — ไม่ต้องแก้ในฉากด้วยมือ
- คำสั่ง (PowerShell, ปิด Unity Editor ก่อน):
  - `tools/unity/run-tests.ps1` — เทสต์ EditMode
  - `tools/unity/build-windows.ps1 -Zip` — build + smoke test + zip ไว้ที่ `Builds/`
  - `tools/blender/build-models.ps1` — สร้างโมเดลจาก `tools/blender/build_models.py`
- เอกสาร: [GDD](docs/GDD.md) · [แผน](docs/PLAN.md) · [ความคืบหน้า](docs/PROGRESS.md) · [เครดิต](CREDITS.md)

---

## English

**BOO-TRAYAL** is a funny-spooky Thai ghost party game for 2–8 friends online. Status: **alpha**.

Close the seals, carry the urn and incense pot to the shrine altar, and outrun the Krasue through the gate before dawn. With 5+ players a friend may secretly be the **Spy**. Ring the bell to call a meeting and vote them out.

**Install:**
1. Download `BOO-TRAYAL-v…-win64.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/LumielX/GameByClaude/releases) and unzip it.
2. Run `BOO-TRAYAL.exe`. On a SmartScreen warning, click **More info → Run anyway**. "Smart App Control blocked" means Windows 11 Smart App Control is on and blocks all unsigned apps.
3. Allow the firewall prompt.

The game needs Windows 10/11 64-bit with a DirectX 11/12 GPU.

**Play:**
- One player picks *Play → Create room* and shares the 6-character code.
- The others pick *Play → Join* and enter it. This works across different networks.
- Everyone needs the same version.

Voice chat is proximity-based; in meetings, the whole room hears everyone. *Settings* has push-to-talk (hold V).

**Keys:**
- WASD move · Shift run · Space jump · Ctrl crouch
- E grab/use · Left click throw · G drop · Right click push
- F flashlight · Z scream (mini ghost: boo) · V talk · Esc pause
- Spy: Q sabotage · X blackout

**Bugs:** open an [issue](https://github.com/LumielX/GameByClaude/issues) and attach `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\LumielX\BOO-TRAYAL\Player.log`.

**Build from source:** you need Unity 6000.6.7f1. Every scene and prefab is generated by the editor builders. Run `tools/unity/build-windows.ps1 -Zip` with the Editor closed.

Credits: [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

The car, its baked PBR textures and every physics number (mass, power, torque, grip, drag, downforce) come from the separate engineering project: [jaineil32624/hypercar-x](https://github.com/jaineil32624/hypercar-x).

Runs on **PC (Windows)**, **web browsers (WebGL)** and **Android phones**. Not VR.

![Gameplay](docs/shots/04_race_chase.png)

## Game modes
| Mode | Players | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Race vs AI** | 1 | Up to 5 AI racers, 1/3/5 laps, positions, lap times, results |
| **Time Trial vs your ghost** | 1 | Your best lap is recorded and replayed as a see-through ghost. Beat it to save a new record and a new ghost |
| **Drag race ¼ mile** | 1 vs AI | Christmas-tree start lights, false-start detection, ET, trap speed and 0-60, compared with the engineering model's prediction |
| **Free roam** | 1 or 2 | Circuit, drag strip, skid pad, slalom and jump ramps; live 0-60 / 0-100 timer |
| **Split-screen race** | 2 (+ AI) | Two players on one PC or one phone, each with their own camera and HUD |
| **AI vs AI** | spectate | Watch the AI race, cycle cars and cameras |
| **Ghost duel** | spectate | Your two best saved laps race each other |
| **Autopilot** | any | Hand your car to the AI at any time (P key / AUTO button), and take it back |

Plus a **garage** (5 variants × swappable wheels, tyres, aero, motors, battery and brakes, each with pros and cons and live stats), 7 paint colours, a **local leaderboard** (best laps, race times, quarter-mile), and settings for laps, AI count and difficulty, touch/tilt controls, units, graphics and sound.

## Controls
| | Player 1 | Player 2 (split-screen) | Touch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throttle / brake & reverse | W / S (arrows when playing solo) | ↑ / ↓ | GAS / BRAKE |
| Steer | A / D | ← / → | ◀ ▶ or tilt |
| Handbrake drift | Space | Right Shift | DRIFT |
| Camera (chase / far / bonnet / cinematic) | C | . | CAM |
| Autopilot | P | / | AUTO |
| Reset onto track | R | , | RESET |
| Pause | Esc | | II |

A gamepad also works for single-player steering and throttle.

## How the physics works
`CarController.cs` uses Unity WheelColliders with the engineering model's equations:
- **Tractive force** = min(T·G·η / r, P·η / v), split over four driven wheels, cut at the motor's 21,000 rpm limit
- **Grip**: tyre friction-curve stiffness = μ from the model (1.35 for the Electric Hypercar)
- **Aero**: drag ½ρv²C<sub>D</sub>A and downforce ½ρv²C<sub>L</sub>A applied as forces; the active rear wing flattens at speed and flips up as an air-brake
- **Suspension**: spring rate set for a 2.2 Hz ride frequency, 0.38 damping ratio, anti-roll bars, ABS
- **AI** (`AIDriver.cs`): follows the racing line with a speed-dependent look-ahead and brakes for corners using v = √(μ·g·R)·skill

## Project layout
```
Assets/
  HypercarX/Scripts/Runtime   CarController, AIDriver, GameManager, World, Ghost, ChaseCamera, VehicleSpec
  HypercarX/Scripts/Editor    ProjectBuilder: materials, scene, player settings, builds
  HypercarX/Textures          Baked PBR maps from Blender (paint, carbon, tyre, rim, disc)
  Resources/HypercarX.fbx     Car model exported from Blender
  Resources/variants.json     Five variants from the engineering model
docs/                         Website (GitHub Pages): WebGL build in /play, downloads, screenshots
```

## Build it yourself
1. Open the folder in **Unity 6000.3** (Hub ▸ Add project from disk).
2. Menu **HYPERCAR-X ▸ 1. Setup project**, then open `Assets/Scenes/Drive.unity` and press Play.
3. Builds: **HYPERCAR-X ▸ Build WebGL / Build Android APK / Build Windows**, or headless:
   ```
   Unity -batchmode -projectPath . -executeMethod HypercarX.EditorTools.ProjectBuilder.BuildAndroid
   ```

Self-test: run any build with `-hxautotest <folder>`. It plays every mode on autopilot, logs telemetry and saves screenshots.

---
Made by **Jaineil Rana**. Engineering model, Blender model and baked textures: [hypercar-x](https://github.com/jaineil32624/hypercar-x).

# Code Blue: The Ward Round

A pixel-art time-management game about hospital case coding. You are the coding specialist on a busy ward: patients arrive, clues trickle in (admission notes, labs, X-rays, OR reports, nursing notes), and you have to code every case before the patient goes home. Then the MD auditor shows up.

![Code Blue: The Ward Round](share-image.png)

**Play:** open `index.html` in any modern browser. It is a single self-contained file (fonts load from Google Fonts, everything else is inline), so you can send it to friends, drop it on GitHub Pages, or host it anywhere.

## What's in it

- **Shifts** of ~5 minutes (1 game day = 30 s). Drag ICD-10-GM diagnosis and OPS procedure cards onto the chart; a live grouper shows the resulting DRG, PCCL and euro value as you go.
- **Code early or wait?** Later documents can change everything: troponin turns chest pain into an NSTEMI, pathology turns gallstones into acute cholecystitis, a suspected embolism gets ruled out.
- **Energy actions:** *Ask the doctor* (5 doctors with different personalities) reveals what never made it into the chart; *Chase documentation* turns vague notes into codable diagnoses; *Coffee* refills energy while the ward keeps running.
- **Scoring:** billed value, clean-case bonus, "sharp eye" bonus for DRG-relevant secondary diagnoses, combo streaks. Upcoding pays now…
- **MD audit boss fight** at the end of each week: defend every challenged code by presenting the document that proves it. Unsupported codes are clawed back with a surcharge, and a bad record raises next week's audit quota.
- **Career:** 5 wards unlock week by week (Internal Medicine, Surgery, Cardiology, Geriatrics, ICU, then the whole hospital), with a perk after each audit (Speed Reader, Doctor Whisperer, Double Espresso, …).
- **Daily challenge:** the same seeded shift for everyone each day. Share your result as text; friends paste each other's results into the leaderboard (no server needed, the result code is checksummed).
- **Pause** stops the clock but only lets you read and browse; coding and actions wait until you resume. **Hard mode** (toggle on the title, quick-shift and daily screens) removes pausing and tips and pays +25% points per case.
- **Tutorial:** a scripted practice shift with two patients. Nurse Bea spotlights one part of the screen at a time (ward, patient cards, chart, documents, code finder, DRG box, energy, coffee, timeline, pause) and waits for you to try each mechanic: picking the principal diagnosis, adding treated secondaries, asking the doctor about a lab value, chasing a vague note, and replacing a diagnosis when a more specific one arrives. Offered automatically before a first career.
- Contextual tips, codebook, DRG catalogue, keyboard controls, chiptune sound effects and a lo-fi soundtrack (on by default). Progress is saved in the browser.

The coding logic follows the real German G-DRG approach (principal diagnosis → base DRG, OR procedures → surgical DRGs, CCL → PCCL → severity split, documentation requirements, MD audits), but DRG names, splits and relative weights are simplified for play. It is not a coding reference.

## Development

Source lives in `src/` (data, engine/grouper, pixel renderer, audio, game, screens). Rebuild the bundled file with:

```
python3 build.py
```

This writes `index.html` (standalone) and `dist/artifact.html` (body-only variant for hosting as a claude.ai artifact).

# Claude-chan: Risk Control

A parody mod for **The Binding of Isaac: Repentance / Repentance+**.

**Expansion in development:** [22-form community-meme gameplay](docs/CHARACTER_GAMEPLAY.md) and [50 additional collectible designs](docs/EXPANSION_DESIGN.md). Summary Stapler is the first locally implemented item: a four-charge active that compresses nearby ordinary hostile bullets into one slow native tear. It keeps normal tear effects, character limits and forks; empty use preserves charge and Car Battery does not repeat it. Thirteen forms and eighteen collectibles are currently registered. The remaining expansion designs are not implemented, and current engine acceptance remains pending.

**Experimental roster candidate:** eleven model families, eleven ZipZipPipe-based normal portraits, two darker tainted portraits, nine additional playable normal characters and in-game dossiers. Hold MAP in a cleared room to view the current character's portrait and instructions. See [the roster and mechanics](docs/MODEL_ROSTER.md), [pending engine checks](docs/TESTING.md), and [art terms](resources/ART_LICENSE.md). All thirteen gameplay skins now follow the selected portrait identities; animation polish and engine acceptance remain pending; this is not a Workshop release.

Every floor hands you a random proxy IP. The more people share it, the higher your **risk score** (风控值). The higher the risk, the tougher the enemies get, and killed enemies start coming back as "new accounts".

> Fan work. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Character illustrations are credited fan-art derivatives; see the separate art terms.

[中文](#中文) · [日本語](#日本語)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Claude-chan** (playable) | Range +1.5 (long context window), Shot Speed +0.2, Speed −0.1, 2 red + 1 soul heart, orange tears. Starts with **Ban Hammer** as a pocket item. **Usage limit:** every tear fills a usage meter that drains slowly; when it's full, her tears deal 40% damage for 5 seconds. **Account age (账号满月):** +0.2 damage for every floor reached without being Suspended (max +1.6); a suspension resets it ("Banned again" / 又封了). *Custom orange-haired sprite atlas and portraits; animation polish is in progress.* |

| **DeepSeek-chan** (playable) | **Direct connection (直连):** she needs no proxy, so in a DeepSeek-only run there is no IP, no risk and no risk-based difficulty. **Deep Think (深度思考):** not shooting builds up to 5 s of thought; the next tear deals up to ×2 and the HUD reads "Thought for N s". **Server busy (服务器繁忙):** the more enemies in the room, the more often a tear doesn't go out (3% per enemy, max 25%). **Slacking off (摸鱼):** standing still for 5 s in a cleared room recharges Lunch Break by one. | **Lunch Break** (DeepSeek-chan's pocket active, 6 charges) | "飯食ってくる / 去吃饭了": heals one red heart and slows every enemy for 3 s, but you stop shooting for 3 s. |
| **The Appeal Queue** | Four short, localised story captions during a run; chapter progress survives save/continue. |
| **Risk score** | 0–100. At **90+ your account is Suspended**: damage ×0.75 until risk drops. Each floor rolls an IP: crowded relay IPs add more risk. Getting hit +1, clearing a room without a hit −1. Shown at the bottom-left of the HUD. |

| **Hydra accounts** | From risk 40 on, a killed enemy may respawn once (tinted red), from 10% up to 50%. |
| **Relay Slime** (enemy) | A shared proxy. Appears in 25% of uncleared rooms once risk ≥ 30; splits in two on death, twice, so one slime becomes up to seven. *(Placeholder: a green-tinted vanilla Clotty.)* |
| **Agentic** (transformation) | Hold any 3 of Ultrathink, Compact, Vibe Coding, Subagent Swarm, --dangerously-skip-permissions, All Tests Passing: flight, fire delay ×0.8, damage +0.5. |

| **9.9 Yuan Relay** (passive, devil pool) | Damage ×1.5, but each room has a 30% chance of a secret model swap (×0.5 instead). Risk +15 on pickup. Based on the Chinese "cheap relay quietly swaps the model" (掺水) complaints. |
| **Ultrathink** (active, 5 s recharge) | Each use in the same room thinks harder: think +1 / megathink +2 / ultrathink +3.1999 damage (after the oddly specific 31,999-token budget). 15% of the time: "Thought for 0s", nothing happens. |

tonywang1990/AlphaAgent.readme:
# AlphaAgent

A general-purpose agent for optimization problems of one shape: data split into train / val / test, a
clearly defined goal and eval function, and code (a heuristic, a model, or a combination of components)
that must score well on the sealed held-out test.

## Contents

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `docs/case_studies/` | Two worked examples of the loop: DOTA (trading-signal ensemble search) and adsbench (pairwise ad-reach prediction) |
| `reports/Research agents for optimization.md` | Survey of existing research agents and harnesses, ten design axes, five candidate frameworks, a task contract, harness invariants, a first build and experiments |
| `research_notes/Research agents for optimization/` | The cited research notes behind the report, one file per research family |

> **Reels Wait — a personal fork.** This repository is a fork of > [AwayDoomscrollin'](https://github.com/resolvecommunity/AwayDoomscrollin) by > Resolve Community, licensed under GPL-3.0-only. It is not affiliated with or > endorsed by Resolve Community, Meta or Instagram. The fork installs as > `com.gab.reelswait` under the name "Reels Wait" and replaces the hard block > on Instagram Reels with a wait timer: a countdown (or a quick mini-game), > then a short window where Instagram is unguarded. It also keeps the Instagram > Home and YouTube feeds open (`ReelsWaitConfig.KEEP_FEEDS_OPEN`), so only Reels, > Shorts and Instagram's suggested Explore grid are blocked; search still works. The rest of this README describes the upstream app.

AwayDoomscrollin'

An open-source Android app that covers short-video feeds in Instagram and YouTube and interrupts feed scrolling in TikTok.
awaydoomscrollin.com

## About AwayDoomscrollin' is a digital wellbeing app for people who want to keep using Instagram, YouTube and TikTok for messages, search and things they chose to watch, without getting pulled into endless short-video feeds. It does not set time limits. Instead it covers the feeds themselves and stops the move from one short video to the next. The app is in public beta. It relies on accessibility information exposed by other apps, so updates to those apps, Android or the phone's software can delay detection or cause missed or incorrect detections. ## What it covers Instagram and YouTube have two modes. TikTok has a single protection setting. | App | Both modes | Balanced | Strict | |---|---|---|---| | Instagram | Home and Explore are covered and the Reels tab is blocked. Messages and account search stay open; the suggested grid under keyword search results is covered. | Profiles, profile posts, Stories, Highlights and your Saved, Liked and Reposted lists stay open. One Reel you open can be watched with its comments; moving to the next video closes it. | Profile posts are covered. Reels, including those shared in messages, Stories and Highlights are blocked. Saved, Liked and Reposted lists are closed. | | YouTube | Home and Subscriptions are covered and the Shorts tab is blocked. Search results, channels, playlists, the You tab and long videos stay open. | One Short opened from search, a channel or a link can be watched with its comments; moving to the next video closes it. | All Shorts are blocked, wherever they are opened. | TikTok: browsing, messages, profiles, search and comments stay open. The first vertical swipe in the For You or Friends feed takes you back, and switching to the Following or Community tabs is undone. The app also keeps local statistics: blocks per app, the busiest hour of the day, measured Instagram and YouTube curtain time, a daily streak and achievements. These stay on the device. ## Installation Requires Android 8.0 or newer. - **F-Droid:** [f-droid.org/packages/com.resolvecommunity.awaydoomscrollin](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.resolvecommunity.awaydoomscrollin/) - **Google Play:** [play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.resolvecommunity.awaydoomscrollin](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.resolvecommunity.awaydoomscrollin) - **GitHub:** signed APKs on the [releases page](https://github.com/resolvecommunity/AwayDoomscrollin/releases/latest) GitHub and F-Droid builds are signed with the same key. Its SHA-256 certificate fingerprint is: ``` c59c79a593d1e026f92f5ab264626dfc0799046df6b7ee83b254863db8ab8716 ``` You can compare it with the output of `apksigner verify --print-certs` for a downloaded APK. The Google Play build uses Play App Signing and may not match this fingerprint; switching between the Play build and a GitHub or F-Droid build can require uninstalling first. ### Turning on accessibility for an APK installed outside a store Android 13 and newer restrict accessibility access for apps installed from an APK file. If the AwayDoomscrollin' switch is greyed out in Accessibility settings: 1. Open **Settings > Apps > AwayDoomscrollin'**. 2. Tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner and choose **Allow restricted settings**. 3. Confirm with your PIN or fingerprint, then turn the service on in Accessibility settings. Menu names differ between phone makers. Step-by-step guides are available in [English](https://awaydoomscrollin.com/en/guide) and [Turkish](https://awaydoomscrollin.com/tr/rehber). ## Privacy - Screen information is read through Android's Accessibility Service and processed in memory on the device. The app does not take screenshots, record the screen or log keystrokes, and it does not store or send what it reads from the screen. - Before Android's accessibility settings open, the app explains what the permission is used for. Declining leaves protection off. - The `INTERNET` permission is used only for optional usage data, which is off by default and

evanstom273/Claude-test-II.readme:
# LOWLIFE

An open-world, top-down crime game for the browser. Grimsport is a wet, neon-lit port town run by three gangs and a police force that's always one phone call away. Nick cars, take jobs from ringing payphones, rob tills, pick fights you probably shouldn't, and try to stay alive until morning.

- One big city, generated from a seed: the docks, industrial yards, the Strip, downtown, a residential estate, parks and the seafront
- Three gangs with their own turf, looks and HQs: the Vipers, the Velvet Crowns and the Dock Rats. Work for one and the others notice
- Every building can be walked into, with furnished interiors you see through the walls
- Cars to steal, drift with the handbrake, crash, sell, respray or set on fire. Traffic drives on the left
- Fists, a bat, a pistol, an SMG and a shotgun; explosions
- Wanted stars, foot patrols and police cars that chase you through the streets
- Five kinds of job: steal a car, a hit, a timed delivery, torching a rival's car, thinning out a rival gang
- Shops, a chippy, bars, a hospital, a gun shop and a clothes shop (a change of clothes loses the police)
- Day and night, street lights, headlights, sirens, and four radio stations
- Three save slots, stored in IndexedDB. Save by sleeping in your flat
- No asset files: every person, car, tile, prop, tune and sound effect is generated in code at runtime

Built with React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Dexie and Phaser 4.

## Running it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run build      # production build in dist/
npm test           # city reachability, lanes, routing, sprite data checks
npm run typecheck
```

## Controls

| Action | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Move / drive | WASD / arrows |
| Attack (hold for automatic weapons) | J / Space |
| Interact: get in or out, carjack, answer, buy, rob | E / Enter / F |
| Switch weapon | Q / Tab |
| Sprint | Shift |
| Handbrake (in a car) | Shift / K |
| Horn | H |
| Radio | R |
| Eat something | X |
| Map | M |
| Phone (pause) | Esc / P |

With a mouse, you can aim with the pointer (Settings → Mouse aim); otherwise you auto-aim at the nearest threat.

On phones, tablets and foldables, touch controls switch on automatically: drag on the left half to move or steer (point the stick where you want the car to go), use the buttons on the right to attack, switch weapon, brake, honk and change station, and tap the yellow button that appears to get in cars, answer phones and so on. Portrait and landscape both work.

## How the world works

Most of the game comes from a few systems that interact:

- **Crimes** are events with a place and a noise. Anyone who sees or hears one reacts: civilians run and sometimes phone it in, shopkeepers cower or reach under the counter, gang members join in when it's one of theirs, cops add to your wanted level.
- **Wanted level** builds from heat. Each crime a cop witnesses adds some, and the stars climb no faster than one every couple of seconds. Get out of sight and they flash, then drop one at a time.
- **Gangs** remember how you've treated them. Do jobs for a gang and they like you; kill their people and they'll shoot on sight.
- **Payphones** ring around the city. Answer one for a job.

## Deploying

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` builds the game and publishes `dist/` to GitHub Pages on every push to `main` (Pages source: GitHub Actions). The build uses relative paths, so it works from the repo's Pages sub-path.

## Layout

- `src/game/city`: city generation, furnishing, tile painting and chunked streaming
- `src/game/art`: shape-based generators for people, cars and props, plus the texture atlases
- `src/game/entities`: people and cars, with the car physics
- `src/game/systems`: combat, AI, police, traffic, routing, population and jobs
- `src/game/scenes`: boot, title and the city scene that ties it all together
- `src/data`: the cast, weapons and shop stock
- `src/state`: game and UI stores, save/load session logic
- `src/db`: Dexie database for saves and settings
- `src/ui`: React overlays (title screen, HUD, phone, map, shops, jobs, touch controls)
- `preview.html` is a dev-only page for eyeballing the generated people, cars and city

Hearthlight, the top-down action RPG that used to live here, is archived on the [`hearthlight-v1`](https://github.com/evanstom273/Claude-test-II/tree/hearthlight-v1) branch.

Jazzneo/RH-launcher.readme:
# RH Launcher: Rusty Hearts Offline for Linux

A controller-friendly launcher (Steam Deck style) that runs the community **Rusty Hearts** offline server
on Linux and plays the game with Proton. One window to install the server, turn it on and off, make game
accounts, and play.

![Play tab](launcher/docs/screenshots/1_play_offline.png)

**No game files are included.** You download the server pack, the server VM and the game client
yourself from the RaGEZONE community release. The launcher finds those downloads and installs them.

## Features

- **Setup**: finds `server.7z`, `server-vm.7z` and `client.7z` in your Downloads (or SD card / USB) and
  installs everything with one button. It also checks Docker, Proton, memory and disk space.
- **Play**: PLAY starts the server if needed, then the game.
- **Accounts**: create and delete game accounts, and add Zen for the cash shop.
- **Auto-login** (optional, experimental): types your saved login into the game's login screen.
- **Server**: on / off / restart, live status of the database, login API and game servers.
- **Display**: Proton native Wayland or X11 + gamescope; Vulkan (DXVK) or OpenGL; windowed, borderless
  or fullscreen; any resolution.
- **Steam**: Add to Steam, and it works in Gaming Mode with a controller.

| Setup | Accounts | Display |
|---|---|---|
| ![Setup](launcher/docs/screenshots/0_setup.png) | ![Accounts](launcher/docs/screenshots/7_accounts.png) | ![Display](launcher/docs/screenshots/4_display.png) |

## Requirements

- Linux x86-64 (tested on Bazzite). **16 GB RAM** or more.
- **Docker Engine with the Compose plugin**, usable by your user. On Bazzite, the developer edition
  (bazzite-dx) includes Docker. **Steam Deck / SteamOS:** nothing to install, Podman is used instead
  (see below).
- **Steam with Proton Experimental** (or GE-Proton).
- About **60 GB free disk space** while installing, about 20 GB afterwards.

## Play on a Steam Deck with your PC's server (recommended)

The easiest way to play on a Steam Deck (or a second PC): your PC runs the server, the Deck only runs the
game. The Deck then needs no Docker or Podman and far less memory.

1. **On the PC:** Settings → **Network play…** → **Host**, press **Open firewall ports** (asks for your
   password), Save, and turn the server on. The window shows the address to use, e.g. `192.168.1.20`.
2. **On the Deck:** install RH Launcher, Settings → **Network play…** → **Join**, type that address, press
   **Test connection**, Save. Setup then only installs the game client.
3. Create accounts and add Zen on the PC; log in on the Deck with them. Keep the PC on while you play.

Only devices on your home network can connect; don't forward these ports on your router.

## Steam Deck (everything on the Deck)

Everything (server and game) can run on the Deck itself. SteamOS has no Docker, but it has Podman built in
(SteamOS 3.5 and later); RH Launcher uses that automatically.

- Use **Desktop Mode** for the first install: unpack the zip, then in Konsole run
  `bash RH-launcher/launcher/RHLauncher.sh` and press **Install everything** on the Setup tab. Setup turns
  on Podman's service and downloads Docker Compose by itself.
- You need about **60 GB free** while installing. A 64 GB Deck isn't enough; use a 256/512 GB model, or an
  SD card formatted by SteamOS (ext4, not exFAT).
- Then **Settings → Add to Steam**, switch to Gaming Mode and play with the controller.
- Memory is tight: 16 GB is shared by SteamOS, the database, the Wine game servers and the game. Close
  other apps; the launcher stops everything if less than 2 GB is left.

The Steam Deck / Podman mode is new and not tested on a real Deck yet. Please report how it goes.

## Install

1. Download this repository (green **Code** button → *Download ZIP*, or `git clone`) and extract it,
   for example to `~/Games/RH-launcher`.
2. Download the three game files from the RaGEZONE **RustyHeartenstein** release (see
   [docs/INSTALL-SERVER.md](docs/INSTALL-SERVER.md#where-to-get-the-files)) into your **Downloads** folder.
   Don't unpack them.
3. Run `launcher/RHLauncher.sh` and press **Install everything** on the Setup tab (20-40 minutes the
   first time).
4. **Accounts** tab: create your account. **Play**: press PLAY and log in.

Manual steps and troubleshooting are in [docs/INSTALL-SERVER.md](docs/INSTALL-SERVER.md).

Your characters live in the Docker volume `rusty-hearts-offline_sql-data`. Never run
`docker compose down -v`: that deletes them.

## How it works

- `docker/`: SQL Server for Linux, JuniorDark's Rusty Hearts API (modified for offline use), and the
  original Windows server programs running in Wine, all on localhost.
- `tools/patch-dbc-com.py`: a 23-byte fix so the server's database relay works under Wine. Its worker
  threads never initialize COM, which Windows tolerates and Wine doesn't. Originals are backed up.
- `tools/winvhdx.py`: reads the Windows database drivers out of the server VM disk, read-only, with no
  libguestfs needed.
- `tools/run-client.sh`: starts the game with Proton and the display settings from the launcher.
- `tools/autologin/`: the auto-login helper (C source included).
- `launcher/`: the GUI (Python + pygame-ce, bundled in `launcher/runtime/python`).

## Credits

- **JuniorDark**: Rusty Hearts API, Rusty Hearts Launcher and Rusty Hearts Server Manager (0BSD), and
  the RustyHearts server VM. https://github.com/JuniorDark
  This project includes a modified copy of the API (`sources/RustyHearts-API-master`) and the Server
  Manager's option templates.
- **RaGEZONE community**: the RustyHeartenstein server pack and the Rusty Hearts setup guide.
- **Stairway Games / Perfect World**: Rusty Hearts. This project is not affiliated with them.
- **7-Zip** by Igor Pavlov (GNU LGPL): `launcher/runtime/bin/7zzs`, unmodified, from
  https://github.com/ip7z/7zip ([license](launcher/runtime/bin/7zip-License.txt)).
- **Python** and **pygame-ce** (bundled runtime). The UI toolkit comes from the author's
