zeveck/bloom-hop.desc: A cozy frog puzzle on a lily pond. A browser game made with Claude Code and gamegen, with art and sound from the imagegen2, nanogen, anim8gen and audiogen plugins.
zeveck/bloom-hop.readme:
# Bloom Hop *Hop every pad, eat every fly, and make the whole pond bloom.* You're a hungry little frog on a lily pond. Every pad has a fly on it, and every pad can only take so many hops before it sinks behind you. Plan your route, flick grumpy beetles out of the way with your tongue, ride turtles before they dive, and catch gifts from friendly koi. Gulp down the last fly and the whole pond bursts into flower while your frog does a happy little dance. **[▶ Play Bloom Hop](https://bloomhop.synapticnoise.com)** in your browser. No install, works on desktop and on phones. ![Title screen](media/screenshots/title.png) ## The ponds | | | |---|---| | ![Morning Pond](media/screenshots/morning.png) **Morning Pond.** Learn to hop, leap over open water, and plan around sturdy pads that take two or three hops. | ![Sunset Marsh](media/screenshots/sunset.png) **Sunset Marsh.** Turtles that surface and dive, beetles that hog pads, and koi with presents. | | ![Moonlit Lagoon](media/screenshots/moon.png) **Moonlit Lagoon.** Bigger ponds with everything at once, under the fireflies. | ![The bloom](media/screenshots/bloom.png) **The bloom.** Clear a pond and lotus flowers open across it. | Twelve puzzles, and every one is guaranteed beatable: each pond is built by actually walking a frog through it, then a solver checks it again. Finish level 8 to unlock **Wild Pond**, 150 more ponds that keep getting trickier and then come back mirrored and spun around, so the pond never runs dry. ## The pond folk - **Lily pads.** The dots show how many more hops a pad can take. Hop off and it loses a dot. At zero, *bloop*, it sinks. Sunk pads can be hopped right over. - **Flies.** One on every pad. Eat them all to win. - **Beetles.** They sit on pads you need. Flick them with your tongue and they scuttle to the next pad along (a dotted arrow shows where). - **Turtles.** Free stepping stones, but they dive on a rhythm. The ring of dots shows how many moves a turtle will hold you; red means *you'll get wet!* - **Koi.** Land next to a ripple and a koi leaps out with a gift: a **Mend Leaf** that patches your pad, or a **Gold Feather** for one long leap. ## How to play - **Hop:** arrow keys or WASD, or click or tap a glowing pad. On a phone you can swipe, too. You always land on the first pad in line, up to three cells away. - **Tongue:** Shift + arrow (or Space, then an arrow), or tap a beetle. - **Power-up:** E, or the gift button. - **Undo:** Z, as many times as you like. **Retry:** R (and Undo takes it back). **Hint:** H. - **Pause:** Esc or P. **Mute:** M. - On a phone, the buttons sit below the pond, or beside it when you hold the phone sideways. You can install it from your browser's menu to play full screen, even offline. There's no game over here, only Undo. Win a pond without a hint to earn a **gold flower**. Your progress is saved in your browser. ## How it was made The whole game was made by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) with **[gamegen](https://github.com/zeveck/gamegen)**, a Claude Code plugin that turns an idea into a finished game. The design, the 162 levels, the art, the animation, the music, the sound effects and every line of code came from this one command: > /gg:gamegen Make an overhead puzzle game in which you're a frog hopping from lilipad to lilipad and each one can only handle so many hops before it sinks and the goal is to hop on every lilipad, perhaps each one has a fly on it or something, and there's music and maybe a dozen level that get harder as you go. They can be generated, but, should always be possible to beat. You could also use your tongue to nudge enemies or something. There could also be turtle pads that surface and sink or fish that come up and give you power ups. When you hop to every lilipad flowers around the level all bloom and you celebrate before moving on. That's it: no other instructions, no hand-drawn art, no hand-written code. From there, gamegen wrote a design, had a team of reviewer agents (a player, a builder and an art director) pick it apart over two rounds, then generated the art and audio, built the game, play-tested every level on desktop and phone sizes, and had a fresh playtester and bug hunter go over the result. The levels come from a generator that walks the frog through each pond so a winning route always exists, and `node tools/verify-levels.mjs` re-checks all 162 ponds. gamegen brings four plugins along. Here's what each one made. ### [imagegen2](https://github.com/zeveck/imagegen2): the pond folk imagegen2 creates images with OpenAI's GPT Image. It drew the frog first, and the frog then set the style for everything else: the lily pads (fresh, worn and tattered), the flies, beetles, turtle, koi, lotus flowers, power-ups, reeds and the app icon.
### [nanogen](https://github.com/zeveck/nanogen): the water nanogen creates images with Google's Gemini (Nano Banana). It painted the open pond for the morning, then repainted the same pond in sunset gold and in moonlight, so all three areas share one shoreline.
### [anim8gen](https://github.com/zeveck/anim8gen): the hops

anim8gen turns a character into short sprite animations. Starting from the frog, it had imagegen2 draw a full-stretch leap, a blink and a two-armed cheer, and checked every frame so the frog stays the same frog. ### [audiogen](https://github.com/zeveck/audiogen): the sound audiogen create

marx1980/Cardshark.readme:
# Cardshark

Briškula and Bela on your phone, against computer players.

- **Briškula** — Triestine 40-card deck, 2 or 4 players, classic (3 cards) or double (4 cards, two plays per trick).
- **Trešeta** — same Italian deck, no trumps, follow suit; 4 players in pairs or 2 head to head with a stock; akuže; play to 21/31/41.
- **Bela** — mađarice (William Tell pattern), 4 players in pairs, trump calling, declarations, bela, play to 501/701/1001.

Single-page web app, no build step. Works offline once loaded and can be added to the Home Screen.
Card art and logo are original SVG drawn in code.

jaineil32624/whiskerwag.readme:
# 🐾 Whiskerwag **Adopt a kitten or a puppy. Feed it, bathe it, tuck it in, dress it up, and teach it to talk back.** Whiskerwag is a virtual pet game for phones and the web. You pick a pet, name it, and look after it every day. It gets hungry, muddy, sleepy, and bored, and it lets you know with a little thought bubble. Talk into the mic and it repeats you in a squeaky voice. ![Whiskerwag screenshots](screenshots/banner.png) **▶ Play it:** https://jaineil32624.github.io/whiskerwag/ --- ## ✨ What you can do | | | |---|---| | 🐱🐶 **Adopt** | Choose a kitten or a puppy, one of six coats (Honey, Ginger, Cocoa, Snow, Smoke, Ink), and a name. | | 🎤 **Talk back** | Tap the mic and say something. Your pet listens with its ears perked, then repeats you in a high, squeaky voice, and its mouth moves with the sound. No mic? Type a message instead. | | 🍗 **Kitchen** | Drag food from the tray into your pet's mouth. Kittens love sardines and milk. Puppies love bones and drumsticks. Each pet turns up its nose at some foods. Buy groceries at the corner shop. | | 🛁 **Bath** | Scrub with the soap to make suds, then hold the shower to rinse. Puppies shake off the water. Kittens are *not* impressed. | | 🌙 **Bedroom** | Turn off the lamp and your pet curls up and snores. Energy refills while it sleeps, even when the app is closed. | | 🎾 **Yard** | Flick the ball and your pet heads it back. Play two mini-games for coins: **Garden Dash**, a side-scrolling runner (jump puddles, flowerpots, and gnomes), and **Paw Pairs**, a memory card game. | | 🎩 **Closet** | 12 accessories (hats, collars, bandanas, scarves, glasses) that unlock as your pet levels up. | | 💗 **Pet it** | Tap the head for a giggle, stroke it for hearts, boop the nose for a sneeze. Poke the belly too many times and you'll get a growl. | Other details: - Stats keep ticking while you're away (up to two days' worth). - A daily treat of coins and kibble is waiting each day. - The windows show day or night based on your real clock. - The pet's bowl and the doghouse have its name on them. ## 🎨 Made from scratch There are **no image or sound files** in this project: - 🖌️ Every pet, room, food, and accessory is drawn in code on an HTML canvas, in one hand-drawn sticker style with a consistent ink outline. - 😺 The pet has nine expressions: idle, happy, love, sad, tired, asleep, yuck, annoyed, and surprised. It also blinks, breathes, follows your finger with its eyes, and wags or swishes its tail depending on its mood. - 🔊 Meows, barks, purrs, growls, chomps, and bubble pops are all synthesized live with the Web Audio API. - 🗣️ The talk-back feature detects when you start and stop speaking, records your voice, and plays it back faster and higher. That's the classic chipmunk effect. ## 🛠️ Tech - One `index.html`: HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, with no frameworks or build step. - Canvas 2D for all art and animation, plus the Web Audio API for sound and voice. - An installable PWA (`manifest.json` + `sw.js`) that works offline after the first visit. - Progress is saved in `localStorage` on the device. ## 📱 Run it **In a browser:** open the GitHub Pages link above. On Android, use *Add to Home screen* to install it like an app. **Locally:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/jaineil32624/whiskerwag.git cd whiskerwag python3 -m http.server 8000 # open http://localhost:8000 ``` The microphone needs `https://` or `localhost`. **As an Android app for Google Play:** wrap the hosted PWA with [Bubblewrap](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/bubblewrap) to get a signed `.aab` you can upload to the Play Console. ```bash npm i -g @bubblewrap/cli bubblewrap init --manifest https://jaineil32624.github.io/whiskerwag/manifest.json bubblewrap build ``` ## 📸 More screenshots

--- Made by **Jaineil Rana**.

toniisound/doa3-nx.readme:
# DOA3 NX

Nintendo Switch port of *Dead or Alive 3* (Xbox, 2001), built on
[NoRain211/doa3-re](https://github.com/NoRain211/doa3-re): a native static
recompilation of the original Xbox executable with a hand-written runtime.
This repository keeps its full history and code; everything Switch-specific lives in
[`switch/`](switch), and the upstream README is kept as
[`README.doa3-re.md`](README.doa3-re.md).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This repository contains **no game files and no prebuilt `.nro`**. The
> `.nro` carries the game's own executable, translated to C and compiled, so
> each user builds it from their own legally obtained copy of the **USA**
> Xbox release, whose `default.xbe` must have SHA-256
> `e523dd15d0765899a43a1824c023e0219d129e9a8b41e8213e4e645755d2bfa3`.

## Status

**Work in progress.** The whole game runs as a libnx homebrew with audio,
input, saves and an OpenGL renderer, and plays correctly in the Eden
emulator. Bring-up on real hardware and performance work are ongoing.

The game thread runs on core 0; an OpenGL 4.3 renderer (devkitPro mesa,
a port of upstream's SDL_GPU presenter) replays each recorded frame on
core 1, and audio mixes on core 2.

| Area | Switch host layer | State |
|---|---|---|
| Lifted program + runtime | shared with doa3-re (`recomp-runtime/`) | builds for AArch64 |
| Fibers | `fiber_switch_arm64.S` (shared) | — |
| Video | `switch/src/d3d_presenter_gl.cpp` + `d3d_presenter_gl_thread.cpp` (OpenGL 4.3, render thread on core 1) | in progress |
| Audio | `switch/src/audio_output_switch.cpp` (audout, mixer on core 2) | on |
| Input | `switch/src/input_host_switch.c` (libnx pads, rumble) | 4 ports |
| Files and saves | `win32_compat.c` + `switch/include` shims | SD card |

## Building

Requirements: Linux or WSL with devkitPro (`switch-dev`, plus `switch-mesa` and
`switch-glad` from `switch-portlibs`), CMake 3.20+,
Ninja (optional) and everything [`docs/building.md`](docs/building.md) lists for the Linux
build.

Clone with submodules (the lifter is one):

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/toniisound/doa3-nx.git
cd doa3-nx
```

1. Build the desktop version once. This lifts `default.xbe` to C and checks
   it against the manifest the runtime was validated with:

   ```bash
   python3 -m venv private/venv
   private/venv/bin/pip install capstone==5.0.7
   ./build_game.sh /path/to/extracted/disc --movies
   ```

2. Build the `.nro` from that program:

   ```bash
   ./switch/build_switch.sh            # JOBS=3 for more parallel jobs
   ```

   Each generated chunk needs about 3 GB of RAM to compile. The build needs a 256x256 JPEG homebrew menu icon (not included) in
   `private/icon.jpg`.

## Installing

```
sdmc:/switch/doa3-nx/doa3-nx.nro
sdmc:/switch/doa3-nx/disc/default.xbe     <- the whole extracted USA disc
```

Start it from the homebrew menu, preferably through a game (title takeover)
for the full memory budget. Saves go to `disc/.recomp-storage`, and each boot
rewrites `sdmc:/switch/doa3-nx/doa3-nx.log`.

Held at launch, **R** runs unpaced (as fast as the CPU allows). The CPU is not
boosted by the app, since boost mode slows the GPU; use sys-clk to raise the
CPU clock. `-DDOA3_NX_PRESENTER=probe` builds the stage 1 CPU-only presenter.

Controls: Switch B/A/Y/X are Xbox A/B/X/Y by position; L/R are Black/White,
ZL/ZR the triggers, + is START and - is BACK. Quit with HOME or
ZL+ZR+(-)+(+).

## Credits

- [NoRain211](https://github.com/NoRain211): [doa3-re](https://github.com/NoRain211/doa3-re),
  its runtime (from [doaxbv-re](https://github.com/NoRain211/doaxbv-re)) and the
  [xboxrecomp](https://github.com/NoRain211/xboxrecomp) lifter fork.
- [devkitPro](https://devkitpro.org) and [switchbrew](https://github.com/switchbrew/libnx):
  devkitA64, libnx, mesa and glad for Switch.
- Switch port: Toniisound.

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later, as doa3-re. Dead or Alive 3 and its assets belong to Koei
Tecmo; nothing from the game is distributed here.

## Donations

This emulator is completely free and open-source. Optional donations to support the development are always welcome:

[![Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-Support%20me-FF5E5B?style=for-the-badge&logo=ko-fi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/toniisound)

servaltullius/SkeeHeadPartLookupFix.desc: SKSE plugin: removes RaceMenu's slow head part lookup (string-pool scan over every head part) that stutters sculpted face rebuilds. RaceMenu 0.4.20.0 Steam/GOG, 0.4.19.16, 0.4.16 SE.
servaltullius/SkeeHeadPartLookupFix.readme:
# Skee HeadPart Lookup Fix

An SKSE plugin that removes a slow head-part lookup in RaceMenu (`skee64.dll`). In load orders with
many head parts, this lookup causes stutter whenever the face of a sculpted character is rebuilt:
after loading a save, when the character's 3D is reloaded, and when mods ask for a face or body
update.

## The problem

When RaceMenu applies **sculpt** data (the face sculpt brush) to a character, it looks up each face
mesh's head part by name. The lookup walks the game's head part list **from the start, one by one**,
until it finds a match (or reaches the end when there is none), and on each step it
creates and releases an engine string (`BSFixedString`). Each create/release locks the engine's
global string pool.

- Cost per face rebuild ≈ (number of sculpted face meshes) × (number of head parts in the load order).
- In the author's load order (~36,800 head parts, a sculpted UBE character with 15 face meshes), one
  rebuild meant roughly 440,000 string-pool create/release pairs. The player's face is rebuilt
  several times right after a save loads, which showed up as a cluster of 80–120 ms hitches in the
  first seconds.
- With a typical head part count (a few thousand) the cost is smaller, but it is still paid on every
  rebuild.

## What it does

At startup it builds a case-insensitive `name → head part` table once. The lookup is then answered
from the table, with the same result as the original: the first match in load order. RaceMenu's own
code still applies the sculpt, and nothing in your save or presets changes.

When the table cannot give an exact answer, the plugin falls back to the original full scan:
- the table is not built yet,
- the head part list has changed,
- the name contains non-ASCII characters.

In the author's game the log showed, for one save load: 75 lookups from the table, 0 fallbacks, and
about 2.2 million string-pool create/release pairs avoided.

## Supported RaceMenu builds

| RaceMenu (`skee64.dll`) | Game | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| 0.4.20.0 (Steam) | AE 1.6.1170 | sculpt lookup + `GetHeadPartByName` |
| 0.4.20.0 (GOG) | AE (GOG) | sculpt lookup + `GetHeadPartByName` |
| 0.4.19.16 | AE 1.6.1170 | sculpt lookup + `GetHeadPartByName` |
| 0.4.16 | SE 1.5.97 | `GetHeadPartByName` (the sculpt code calls it on this build, so all 5 callers get faster) |

**Safety check.** The plugin recognises the exact `skee64.dll` build from its PE header. It then
checks every instruction it relies on: 18 code locations on AE, 9 on SE. If anything differs, it
**does not patch** and writes the reason to its log. That covers an unknown build, an edited or
recompiled `skee64.dll`, or another plugin having changed the same code. Without a patch, RaceMenu
just runs as it always did.

**Not supported:**
- RaceMenu VR
- Edited or recompiled `skee64.dll` builds
- Any RaceMenu build not in the table, including future builds for newer game versions

## Requirements

- SKSE for your game version
- [Address Library for SKSE Plugins](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/32444)
- [RaceMenu](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/19080), one of the builds above

## Installation

Install with a mod manager, or copy `SKSE/Plugins/SkeeHeadPartLookupFix.dll` into `Data`.
Load order does not matter. It can be added or removed at any time; it changes nothing in saves.

## Compatibility

- The patches were tested in game on RaceMenu 0.4.20.0 (Steam, AE 1.6.1170) with version 2.0.0, alongside
  *RaceMenu OverlayFix and Various Mod Fixes* and *Racemenu(SKEE) cosave Load Crash Fix*. 2.1.0 changes
  no patch code; it removes the diagnostic options and shortens the log.
- GOG 0.4.20.0, 0.4.19.16 and SE 0.4.16 support was verified against the original DLLs (build
  identification, every checked instruction, and no branches into the patched bytes). **It has not
  yet been tested in game.** Reports with the log file are welcome.
- If another plugin patches the same code first, this plugin steps aside: the byte check fails and
  it logs which address differed.

## Log

`Documents\My Games\Skyrim Special Edition\SKSE\SkeeHeadPartLookupFix.log` (the folder can differ
depending on your INI location).

```
RaceMenu 0.4.20.0 (AE, Steam): patched skee64+BDDF4 (sculpt head part lookup) -> ...
RaceMenu 0.4.20.0 (AE, Steam): patched skee64+582C0 (GetHeadPartByName) -> ...
Lookup cache built: 36775 head parts, 36775 named, 33086 unique names (...)
[this load, first 30 s] head part lookups: 75 from the cache, 0 not found, 0 used the original scan; ~2179590 string-pool create/release pairs avoided
```

The figures are for one save load (they restart when a save starts loading). A line saying
`not patching` gives the reason. Please include the whole log when reporting a problem.

## Limitations

- It only helps when a character with RaceMenu sculpt data has its face rebuilt. It does not raise
  average FPS; it removes the hitches those rebuilds cause.
- On AE builds, three more copies of the same lookup are inlined into RaceMenu code paths that did
  not show up in profiling (they look like preset handling). Those keep the original scan.

## Credits

- RaceMenu by **Expired** (expired6978). This plugin only speeds up one lookup; all features are
  RaceMenu's.
- Built with CommonLibSSE-NG.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Source: https://github.com/servaltullius/SkeeHeadPartLookupFix

## Building from source

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 and vcpkg with `commonlibsse-ng`. Run `build.cmd`. The output is
`G:\skyrim-build\SkeeHeadPartLookupFix\package` (mod layout) and
`SkeeHeadPartLookupFix-<version>.zip`. Paths are set in `CMakeLists.txt` / `CMakePresets.json`.

# MWI 战斗动画（mwi-battle-fx）

银河奶牛放置（Milky Way Idle）油猴脚本：在战斗页"交战"旁加一个"舞台"标签，用杀戮尖塔式的侧视画面播放战斗——
角色和怪物的 AI 生成立绘（待机 / 蓄力 / 出手 / 受击 / 施法 / 倒下）、按地点和难度变化的背景、攻击跑位、弹道、受击、阵亡。

- 只在打开"舞台"标签时运行；不修改游戏原有界面，只读取游戏的 WebSocket 消息，不发送任何请求。
- 立绘从本仓库经 jsDelivr 加载：`assets/manifest.json` 列出已有素材。
- 角色用**游戏原版形象**：直接引用游戏自己的精灵图，画出战斗卡片上的头像 + 服装，手里拿着专门画的侧视武器和副手
  （复用纸娃娃的武器贴片，没有贴片的装备退回游戏图标；自己的装备总能读到，队友的要点开过一次对方的资料卡）。
  动作是整体前冲 / 后仰 / 倒下，加上武器按斩刺钝远程魔法挥动。
- 左上角显示当前地图和难度（如"魔像洞穴 T4"，普通 / 精英 / 噩梦三色），迷宫 / 公会试炼各有标签；中文界面下怪物用官方中文名。
- 公会试炼：公会页"进行中"标签里的试炼画面也换成舞台（读 `new_guild_battle` / `guild_battle_updated`）。全部玩家按阵型站位：
  坦克（放过嘲讽 / 挑衅 / 刺盾等或手持盾牌）在前，然后近战、远程，法师在最后；滚轮缩放、拖动平移、双击或 ⟲ 复位。
  只有自己和点开过资料卡的队友显示原版形象，其他人用职业通用立绘。
- 迷宫：战斗消息与普通战斗相同，`labyrinth_updated` 只用来切换背景。
- 远程：箭有发光尾迹和火花，出手时弓前闪光、命中沿弹道溅碎片；贯穿射击穿出光束，快速射击连发，箭雨先落一轮箭。
- 手持武器 / 副手按强化等级带光晕：+5 蓝、+8 紫、+10 橙（呼吸）、+12 红金（快速呼吸）、+15 起彩虹流转。
- 暴击伤害（按 `critCounter`）用金色大号斜体数字 + "暴击"标签，命中时加光环和更重的受击晃动。
- 95 级武器特效触发时武器闪一下对应颜色的光（炽焰 / 绽放 / 涟漪三叉戟、混沌连枷、裂空之弩、咒怨之弓、狂怒长枪、君王之剑、
  狮鹫重盾）。游戏不发送触发标记，按同一次战斗更新里的血量 / MP / 受击次数推断，机制参照 mwi-fastsim。
  有整图专属立绘的形象仍优先用专属立绘。
- "动画测试"标签里每个我方单位可选"游戏形象"，任意组合头像 / 服装 / 武器 / 副手预览；"武器闪光"按钮可预览特效光。
- 纸娃娃（`assets/doll/`）不再整体拼装（v0.9.1 起），只用其中的武器 / 副手贴片。

安装（发布版，推荐）：[release/mwi-battle-fx.user.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wow121/mwi-battle-fx/main/release/mwi-battle-fx.user.js)
——只有战斗画面，不带"动画测试"标签和调试菜单。

Greasy Fork 上的版本用"从网址同步"跟随 `release/mwi-battle-fx.user.js`（发布版不带 `@updateURL` / `@downloadURL`，
按油叉规则由各自的安装来源负责更新）。许可证：MIT（见 `LICENSE`）。

开发版：[mwi-battle-fx.user.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wow121/mwi-battle-fx/main/mwi-battle-fx.user.js)，多一个"动画测试"沙盒标签和调试菜单。
两个版本不要同时启用。发布版由 `tools/build-release.py` 从开发版生成（`publish.sh` 每次自动运行），不要直接改。
访问不了 GitHub 时用 jsDelivr 的固定版本地址。

## 素材生成（tools/）

参考图是游戏自身的精灵图（栅格化后作为 Codex 图像生成的参考），原始姿势表不入库。

1. `make-jobs.py <raw> base|tier` — 怪物姿势表、地点背景、难度变体的生成任务
2. `make-looks.py <raw> <looks.json>` — 玩家形象（脚本导出的待生成清单）
3. `gen.sh <raw> <jobs.tsv> [并发]` — 用 `codex exec` 逐个生成，已有的跳过
4. `build-assets.py` / `remote-build.sh` — 抠图、切帧、压缩为 webp，写 `assets/manifest.json`

纸娃娃（`tools/doll.py`）：`doll.py <raw> rig` 画一个纯色侧视假人（1024 画布）和各部件蒙版，
`doll.py <raw> jobs <gamedata 归档>` 为每个头像 / 服装 / 装备写一个任务——Codex 把它画**在假人身上**，所以所有图层天然同一坐标系。
`build-assets.py` 抠掉背景色和假人色，按蒙版切成 head / torso / arm / leg / weapon / off / back 部件（被遮住的躯干、腿根自动补色），
每层打成一张 `assets/doll/<id>.webp`，部件位置、武器朝向写进 `assets/doll/index.json`。
`tools/test/run-doll.sh <out> <spec.json>…` 在 109 上用真实脚本渲染组合 × 姿势的检查图。

立绘为基于游戏素材的二次生成，版权归原游戏所有，仅供玩家个人使用。

jamiemtaylor95/Technically.readme:
# Technically!

**Argue first. Find out who's right.**

A pass-and-play party game for people who love being right about ridiculous things. Built with Expo (React Native) and played on iPhone through Expo Go, so no Mac is needed.

## How it plays

1. **Debate your take.** Each question has two answers: the one everyone assumes and the one that's *technically* true.
2. **Beat the timer.** The group argues until the countdown runs out.
3. **Lock in.** Pass the phone around; everyone picks A or B.
4. **See the real answer.** Right answers score 100. If you're right while most of the group is wrong, you get a +50 underdog bonus.
5. **Learn fun facts.** Every answer explains the story behind it.

## Playing it on your phone

Every push to `master` runs `.eas/workflows/publish-update.yml` on Expo's servers, which publishes a new version. Open Expo Go on your iPhone, sign in with your Expo account, and open the **Technically!** project to load the newest version.

## Releasing to the App Store

- `eas.json` has a `production` build profile, and `store.config.json` holds the App Store listing (text, keywords, category, age rating).
- `.eas/workflows/release-ios.yml` builds the app on Expo's servers and uploads it to App Store Connect, where it appears in TestFlight. Run it from the project's **Workflows** page on expo.dev.
- `store/screenshots/` has the iPhone 6.9" screenshots (1320×2868) for the listing.
- `docs/` has the privacy policy and support pages, ready for GitHub Pages.

## Developing

```bash
npm install
npm test            # game logic tests (Vitest)
npm run typecheck   # TypeScript
npx expo lint       # lint
npx expo start      # local dev server, if you have a computer handy
```

## Project layout

```
App.tsx                     Screen switching and font loading
src/game/                   Game rules, question picker, storage, questions
src/game/questions.ts       All questions and fun facts
src/screens/                Home, setup, how-to-play
src/screens/game/           Debate → Vote → Reveal → Results
src/components/             Buttons, cards, decorations, background
src/theme.ts                Colors and fonts
```

### Adding questions

Add an entry to `src/game/questions.ts`:

```ts
{
  category: 'animals',
  emoji: '🦀',
  prompt: 'How many legs does a crab have?',
  correct: '10',
  wrong: '8',
  fact: 'Crabs are decapods, which literally means "ten feet."',
},
```

Which side (A or B) the right answer appears on is randomized every game.

pat-pat-patrick/boot-mod-loader.readme:
# Boot Mod Loader

Starts Lua mods on Helldivers 2 again after the game update of 2026-10-20
(Steam build 25988413, the switch to Easy Anti-Cheat).

That update changed how the game runs Lua:

- Lua is now **PUC-Rio Lua 5.1.4** inside `helldivers2.exe`. LuaJIT
  (`bin/lua51.dll`) is gone, and with it `ffi`, `bit` and `jit`.
- The game ships only 11 Lua scripts. `core/wwise/lua/wwise_flow_callbacks`,
  the script that Bingus Shared Loader starts from, is no longer one of them, so
  no loader-based mod starts.
- The game still loads its `boot` script from a mod's patch archive, as plain
  source. `io`, `os`, `debug` and the engine's `stingray` API are all there, and
  the engine calls `init`, `update` and `render`.

Boot Mod Loader replaces `boot`. It runs the game's own boot bytecode first,
unchanged. When the engine calls `init`, it starts every mod that declares
itself the Bingus Shared Loader way.

## For players

Install it with your mod manager like any other mod, next to the Lua mods you
use. It needs no settings.

- Its log is `%APPDATA%\Arrowhead\Helldivers2\boot_mod_loader.log`. The log
  lists the archives read, every mod found, and whether each mod loaded, did not
  compile, or failed (with a traceback).
- **Only one mod can replace `boot`.** Do not install a second loader that does
  the same.
- After a game update the log says either `game version: ... (Steam build
  ...)` or `NOT THIS GAME VERSION`. The second means the loader's copy of the
  game's `boot` script was not checked on that build. Mods still start, because
  `boot` has not changed in an update so far. If the game misbehaves, update
  the loader.
- **Settings of mods made for Mod Options Menu.** That menu's in-game tab is
  gone with the update. The loader takes its place: those mods' settings show in
  [HD2 Mod Setting GUI](https://github.com/pat-pat-patrick/hd2-mod-setting-gui),
  a small window outside the game, and a change applies in the game within a
  second. Settings you had made in Mod Options Menu carry over.
- A mod written for LuaJIT does not run on this game, loader or not. That
  includes mods that use `ffi` to read game memory, mods that use the `bit`
  library, and mods that use `goto`. The log says which mods failed and why.

## For mod authors

Your mod is found if it meets the same conditions as under Bingus Shared
Loader:

- it is a **plain-text** Lua resource in `9ba626afa44a3aa3.patch_<n>`;
- its first line is `-- HD2-Addon: mods/<author>/<name>`;
- the resource name is `mods/<author>/<name>`.

The loader looks for mods in this way:

- It reads the deployed `data\9ba626afa44a3aa3.patch_0`, `_1`, ... with `io`.
- It stops after 64 numbers in a row are missing.
- When a name appears in several patches, the highest patch number wins.
- Mods run in patch order. Each mod runs under `xpcall`, so a mod that raises
  does not stop the others.

Mods start inside the engine's `init`, just as under Bingus Shared Loader.
`_G.update` and `_G.shutdown` exist by then and can be wrapped.

`_G.CowboyBingusModLoader` is provided with the parts that need no `ffi`:

- `api = 1`;
- `open_log(name)`, which opens a file in
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CowboyBingus\Helldivers2\Logs\` with `io`;
- `after_startup(fn)`;
- `on_shutdown(fn)`, which runs `fn` when the game quits, after every
  shutdown handler that mods installed while loading. It is meant for work
  that must come last, such as swapping files. Each function runs under
  `pcall`; an error in the game's own shutdown is raised again after them;
- `capabilities` (`after_startup`, `on_shutdown`, `open_log`, `mod_options`;
  `ffi` and `jit` are false);
- `game`: `build_identifier`, the game's `Application.build_identifier()`,
  and `checked`, true on a build whose `boot` this loader was checked on.

Its `revision` names this loader. It is set only if no other loader has set it.

Each mod's return value (or `true`) is stored in `package.loaded["mods/<author>/<name>"]`,
so mods can check for each other.

### Mod Options Menu

When no other mod defines it, the loader sets `_G.ModOptionsMenu` before any
mod loads, with the API of Mod Options Menu v1.2 (`api = 1`, `version = 3`):
`register_option(id, spec)`, `get(id)`, `set(id, value)`, `on_change(id, fn)`
and `ready()`, which is true. Registrations are checked by the menu's rules
and limits (toggle, choice and slider; texts may be functions; 32 options a
mod).

Instead of an in-game tab, each mod's options become a list for
[HD2 Mod Setting GUI](https://github.com/pat-pat-patrick/hd2-mod-setting-gui),
in `%APPDATA%\Arrowhead\Helldivers2\`:

- `mom_<mod>_options.json`: the list, written when it changes. `<mod>` is the
  `mod_id`, else the addon's name.
- `mom_<mod>_settings.txt`: the values. The window writes it whole; the loader
  reads it once a second, and each value it changed goes to the mod's
  `on_change` callbacks, as the menu's apply did.
- `mom_<mod>.log`: a line for each change applied, for the window's status line.

The list names a mod's profile option as `"profile"`, for the window's profile
switcher: an option registered with `profile = true` (an extra field the menu
itself ignores), else a choice whose id ends in `.profile`. A mod that registers
any option with `profiles = true` (another extra field) gets `"profiles": true`,
which lets the window offer its own saved sets of values; this is never inferred. When the window
switches the profile, its file still holds the old profile's other values: the
loader applies only the switch (the mod loads the new profile's values and
`set()`s them) and writes the file back, so the old values are never saved
into the new profile.

A value the window has not set yet comes from Mod Options Menu's own saved
values (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\CowboyBingus\Helldivers2\Logs\ModOptionsMenu.values`).
A mod that already writes its own list for the window (`<addon name>_options.json`)
is refused, so its settings are not listed twice. Nothing is hooked or read
until a mod registers an option.

Treyyy-dev/Dream-Ball.readme:
# Dream Ball

A hi-bit pixel-art 3-on-3 basketball game you can install on your phone. Collect 87 players and show off your starting three on the home screen, pull six banners with Basket Bucks for players, cards and shoes, build a deck of up to 50 cards from 68 play, dribble, shot, pass and defense cards, and play a story-mode season where you hold 8 cards and spend stamina to make plays. Hold shot cards and release on green. The Shop lists Basket Bucks packs in US dollars (checkout is not open yet). Frame rate (30/60/120) and pixel size (Low to Max) are in Settings.

## Play

Open the GitHub Pages link for this repo on your phone, then:

- **Android (Chrome):** tap **Install** in the top bar, or use the menu's "Add to Home screen".
- **iPhone (Safari):** tap Share, then "Add to Home Screen".

After the first load it works offline. Progress saves on the device.

## Files

- `index.html` — the whole game
- `manifest.webmanifest` — app name, icons and portrait lock
- `sw.js` — service worker for offline play
- `icons/` — home-screen icons

When you change `index.html`, bump `VERSION` in `sw.js` so installed copies pick up the update.

MathCatsMathCats/ChromaticDrift.readme:
# Chromatic Drift website

Website for **Chromatic Drift**, the color-rules puzzle for iPhone and iPad (code name "Chroma", app repo
`MathCatsMathCats/Chromatic-drift`). Plain HTML and CSS. Nothing to install and nothing to build.

Live at **https://mathcatsmathcats.github.io/ChromaticDrift/** (repo `MathCatsMathCats/ChromaticDrift`, GitHub Pages
from `main`, root folder).

| Page | File |
|---|---|
| Home, with the playable demo | `index.html` |
| Support (the App Store "Support URL") | `support/index.html` |
| Privacy (this website + a summary of the app) | `privacy/index.html` |
| Impressum (German) | `impressum/index.html` |
| Page not found | `404.html` |

- Colors and layout: `assets/site.css`. The colors and fonts follow the app's title screen
  (`design_handoff_title_screen`, option 2b).
- The demo: `assets/demo.js`. It's a small copy of the game's rules (`Chroma/Core/Simulation.swift`). Its words are
  at the top of the file. The 28 × 28 field and the "balanced start" check keep the starting loop from collapsing on
  its own before the visitor changes a rule. One change (for example Blue + Red → Red wins) solves it in about
  10–15 seconds.
- Fonts: Big Shoulders Display and Archivo, self-hosted and cut down to Latin characters (`assets/fonts/`, SIL OFL).
  The site loads nothing from other servers.

## Editing text

Open a page and search for `EDIT`. Each numbered comment marks text you can change.
Change only the words between `>` and `<`, then commit and push. The change is live in about a minute.

What the site may say about the app:
- No counts of levels, chapters, achievements or skips (keep numbers off).
- No Sandbox and no gravity, for now.
- Never call it "for kids". No price in the text: say "one-time purchase".

## Screenshots

From the iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro) with the app's debug launch arguments, for example
`-noAds -screen game -level 45 -begin -seconds 60 -style emotions -zoom 3`. The game is deterministic, so the same
level and seconds give the same field in every ball style. Saved as WebP at 600 px wide (`assets/img/`).
Avoid the level intro card: it shows the number of skips left.

## When the app is live on the App Store

In `index.html`:

1. **EDIT 4**: swap "Coming soon" for the App Store link (or the official badge, downloaded from Apple Marketing Tools).
2. **EDIT 11**: change the closing text and add the App Store link.
3. **LINK EDIT** near the top: add the App Store ID for Safari's app banner.

## App Store Connect

- **Support URL:** `https://mathcatsmathcats.github.io/ChromaticDrift/support/`
- **Marketing URL:** `https://mathcatsmathcats.github.io/ChromaticDrift/`. AdMob looks for `app-ads.txt` at the root
  of that domain, `https://mathcatsmathcats.github.io/app-ads.txt`, which already exists in the
  `MathCatsMathCats.github.io` repo. Keep that file.
- **Privacy Policy URL:** stays `https://mathcatsmathcats.github.io/ChromaticDrift-privacy/privacy-policy.html`,
  because that address is also built into the app (Settings → Privacy policy). This site links to it.
  Never reuse the names `ChromaticDrift-privacy`, `MakoCatsMath-privacy` or `MathCats-privacy`.

`app-ads.txt` in this folder is a copy for a future custom domain, where AdMob would look for it at the domain root.

## A custom domain later

`chromaticdrift.com` was taken (checked October 2026). If you buy another domain:

1. Repository **Settings → Pages → Custom domain**: enter it and save.
2. At the registrar, add A records for `@` to `185.199.108.153`, `185.199.109.153`, `185.199.110.153`, `185.199.111.153`,
   and a CNAME for `www` to `mathcatsmathcats.github.io`.
3. When the certificate is ready, tick **Enforce HTTPS**.
4. Switch the site address in the link-preview tags, `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` (replace `example.com`):
   ```
   grep -rl 'https://mathcatsmathcats.github.io/ChromaticDrift/' --include='*.html' --include='*.xml' --include='*.txt' . | xargs perl -pi -e 's#https://mathcatsmathcats\.github\.io/ChromaticDrift/#https://example.com/#g'
   ```
5. Update the Support and Marketing URLs in App Store Connect.

`404.html` works on both addresses (it picks its base path from the host name).

symyoulater/Thin-Place-VR.readme:
# Thin Place VR

**See your real wheel, hands and kit inside VR.**

*A thin place is where the veil between two worlds wears thin. This makes a few of them in your cockpit.*

Thin Place VR adds flat "windows" to any OpenXR game, filled with Virtual Desktop's chroma-key colour (magenta). Virtual Desktop replaces that colour with the Quest 3's passthrough cameras, so your real kit shows through exactly where it sits. The wheel window turns with your Simucube, so it hugs the rim at any steering angle.

**Version 0.12.2** — wheel window (Conspit 300GT and 310 APEX), Stream Deck window, hotkey placement.

---

## One-time setup

### 1. Virtual Desktop

On the PC, in the **Virtual Desktop Streamer** app:
- Set the OpenXR runtime to **VDXR** (not SteamVR).

In the headset, open Virtual Desktop's menu → **Streaming** tab:
- Set the frame rate to **90 fps or lower** — the passthrough options can't be ticked above that.
- In the passthrough section, tick **Environment**. Leave **Tracked keyboard**, **Hands** and **Desk portal** off.
- Press **Configure** next to the tickboxes and set the chroma key colour to **Red 255, Green 0, Blue 255** (magenta).
- Start with **Similarity 4%**, **Smoothness 10%**, **Opacity 100%**, so only the windows turn into passthrough.

### 2. Install

1. Download `ThinPlaceVR-Setup-x.x.x.exe` from the **Releases** page of this repo.
   After that, the **Thin Place VR** app's **Check for updates** button keeps it up to date.
2. Run it. Windows will warn about an unknown publisher because the installer isn't signed yet: click **More info** → **Run anyway**.

That's it — the next OpenXR game you start will load it.

---

## The app

Open **Thin Place VR** from the Start menu or desktop.

- **Home** — whether everything is ready: the VR layer, the runtime, your wheel base and live steering, your windows, and recent games.
- **Windows** — pick a window and its shape (rectangle, rounded, circle/oval, or traced from a photo), then **Place where I'm looking**, nudge, tilt, turn and roll it while a game is running. You can click these from Virtual Desktop's desktop view without taking the headset off. Add, rename, resize, hide or remove windows here too.
- **Wheel** — choose the fitted rim, set the steering range and direction, watch the live angle and set the centre. **Add a rim** either traces a rim's outline from a front-on photo, or uses a standard shape: named rims (Fanatec ClubSport Steering Wheel RS, ClubSport Formula V2.5 and V3, Conspit 310 APEX) or a round, D-shape, GT or formula rim of any width. Choose your **wheel base** here too — automatic detection covers Simucube, Fanatec, Moza, Simagic, Logitech, Thrustmaster, Asetek, VRS, Cammus, Conspit and more, or click **Find it** and turn the wheel.
- **Passthrough** — the key colour, a Virtual Desktop checklist, step sizes, and troubleshooting tools.
- **Updates** — the panel in the bottom-left corner checks for new versions and installs them.
- **Send a report** (bottom of the sidebar) — saves a zip of the logs and settings to your desktop, to send to whoever is helping you.

Changes apply straight away, even mid-drive.

---

## First drive

1. Start **Le Mans Ultimate** or **Assetto Corsa EVO** in VR and get into a car.
2. After a few seconds a window appears straight ahead of you, outlined in yellow, showing your real surroundings. That confirms it's working.
3. Press **Ctrl+Alt+H** to switch on **edit mode**. While it's on, the adjustment keys below go to Thin Place VR instead of the game; every other key works as normal.
4. Fit the rim you're using (the **Conspit 300GT** is selected to begin with; **W** swaps to the **310 APEX**).
5. Hold the wheel straight, sit in your driving position, point your nose at the centre of the wheel and press **P**. The wheel window jumps there (aiming slightly below where your head points, since eyes look lower). Set how far away it lands in the app.
6. Nudge it with the keys below until the real rim fills it.
7. With the wheel dead straight, press **X** to set the centre.
8. Turn the wheel. If the window turns the wrong way, press **I**.
9. Press **Tab** to select the **Stream Deck** window, look at the Stream Deck, press **P**, then nudge and resize it the same way.
10. Press **Esc** (or **Ctrl+Alt+H** again) to leave edit mode and drive.

Everything saves automatically and stays in place next time. Edit mode also switches itself off after 30 seconds without an adjustment key.

---

## Keys

While driving, only two shortcuts are used — everything else goes to the game:

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Ctrl+Alt+H | Edit mode on / off |
| Ctrl+Alt+V | All windows on / off |
| Ctrl+Alt+K | Setup panel on / off — your windows, the selected one's position, the steering angle and these keys, floating in the headset (also shown in edit mode) |

In **edit mode** (selected window has a yellow outline; the help board appears too):

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Select next window (wheel → Stream Deck) |
| P | Place the selected window where you're looking |
| W | Swap wheel: Conspit 300GT ↔ Conspit 310 APEX |
| X | Set steering centre (wheel straight) |
| I | Flip steering direction |
| Arrow keys | Move left / right / up / down |
| R / F | Move away / closer |
| T / G | Tilt top away / towards you |
| Q / E | Turn left / right |
| Z / C | Roll left / right |
| = / − | Selected window bigger / smaller |
| O | Selected window on / off |
| S | Change the selected window's shape (rectangle, rounded, oval, traced) |
| B | Bring the setup panel back in front of you |
| [ / ] | Scroll the selected panel (web page or PDF) |
| M | Turn the selected window to face you |
| A | Move all windows together so the wheel window is where you're looking — use after the headset has slept or been recentred |
| Esc | Leave edit mode |

Hold **Shift** as well for fine steps (1 mm or 0.25°).

---

## Settings and logs

Everything lives in **Documents\Thin Place VR**:

- `config.json` — window positions, wheel choice, s

# StarterSpells

A [BepInEx](https://github.com/BepInEx/BepInEx) IL2CPP mod for **The Spell Brigade** that lets you pick **any spell as your wizard's starting spell**, including the spells no wizard starts with.

**Download:** [Thunderstore — girthy_mods/StarterSpells](https://thunderstore.io/c/the-spell-brigade/p/girthy_mods/StarterSpells/) (install with r2modman or Gale).

- An in-menu picker: click ◀ ▶ or press F6/F7, and F8 hides it. Each wizard remembers its own pick.
- One dropdown per wizard in your mod manager's config editor.
- The game's wizard info panel previews your pick, and spell names use the game's own translations.
- **Only your wizard changes, so other players don't need the mod.** It works with [MoreWizards](https://github.com/kamikaze-skynet/MoreWizards) and in vanilla lobbies.

See [`thunderstore/README.md`](thunderstore/README.md) for the player-facing description and config options.

## Building

Requirements: [.NET SDK 8](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download), plus the game with **BepInExPack IL2CPP 6.0.788** installed and launched once.

```powershell
dotnet build src\StarterSpells.csproj -c Release -p:GameDir="D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\The Spell Brigade"
# r2modman/Gale profile:  -p:BepInExDir="$env:APPDATA\r2modmanPlus-local\TheSpellBrigade\profiles\Default\BepInEx"
# copy into BepInEx\plugins: -p:CopyToPlugins=true

.\package.ps1 -GameDir "D:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\The Spell Brigade"   # -> dist\girthy_mods-StarterSpells-<version>.zip
```

## How it works

`CharacterResource.GetInitialSpell(skin)` returns a wizard's starting spell: its `InitialSpell`, or `InitialPrestigeSpell` for prestige skins.

The game equips the starting spell in `GameplayPlayerIdentity.InitializeOnClientsRpc` / `Initialize`. The equip only runs where `IsOwner` is true, meaning on that player's own machine, and `SpellEquipper.EquipSpell` adds the spell to an owner-written `NetworkList` that syncs to everyone. So changing your own starting spell needs no networking, and other players don't need the mod.

The mod postfixes `GetInitialSpell`, but only changes the answer inside these contexts:
- **Your own wizard being set up:** `InitializeOnClientsRpc`, `Initialize` and `EquipInitialSpell` on the owner.
- **The main-menu wizard panel:** `StatButtonsPanel.OnWizardButtonClicked`, for the preview.
- **Your own spells asking "am I the starting spell?":** `PlayerSpell.HasLifeStealOnSpell`, so the Vampire Mage's life steal follows your pick.

Other players' wizards are never touched.

`PickerUI` is a `MonoBehaviour` injected with `ClassInjector` (`BasePlugin.AddComponent`). It builds its panel from TextMeshPro text and `UnityEngine.UI.Button`, because IMGUI's `GUI.Button` is stripped from this game. It reads keys through the Unity Input System. Names come from the `SpellName_<SpellType>` and `Character_<CharacterId>` localization keys, falling back to cleaned-up enum names.

## Layout

```
src/Plugin.cs          config (one entry per wizard) and startup
src/StarterPatches.cs  the GetInitialSpell override and its contexts
src/Spells.cs          choices, unlock checks, localized names
src/LocalWizard.cs     which wizard you have selected (remembered from the game, with fallbacks)
src/PickerUI.cs        in-menu picker
thunderstore/          manifest, icon, README, CHANGELOG for the Thunderstore zip
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). The Spell Brigade is © Bolt Blaster Games. This is an unofficial fan mod.

patrickscaptainslog/Struggle-Bus-World.readme:
# Struggle Bus

A wheezing yellow school bus flies over real San Francisco and barfs rainbows.
Wherever it splats, grey Victorians bloom into Painted Ladies.

Phase 1: single player, no server. iPhone Safari first (portrait, one thumb).

## Play
- **Drag anywhere**: the bus follows a springy bungee from where you touched.
  It's also a yoke. Sideways carves and banks. **Pull down** to climb
  (harder = faster, the bus slows as it trades speed for height) up toward
  a soft ceiling high above the city (~520 m), where it wheezes and
  struggles. **Push up** to nose down: dive back to the rooftops, gaining
  speed; at the rooftops it surges (about 250 mph).
- **Let go**: it cruises and holds its altitude with a wheezy bob; at the
  rooftops it skims them automatically, as ever.
- Up high the camera pulls back into a vista (it holds perfectly still while
  you hold your altitude): climb out of the marine layer and the west side
  and the bay lie under a fog sea, with Sutro Tower, Twin Peaks, the
  downtown towers and the bridge towers poking through, the hills on the
  horizon. Over the Golden Gate the bus can't climb until it has passed
  under the deck.
- **Tap** (a second finger works while steering): dragon breath. The bus
  rears back and blasts a rainbow jet forward; it explodes on the building
  ahead (when the belly is full, that building glints, and the glinting one is
  the one you hit; lifting your thumb to tap keeps it): a flash, a rainbow
  shockwave, and every building within ~60 m blooms, the street and the trees
  around them splattered too. From altitude it lands where you're looking,
  mid-screen, after a longer flight, and the blast is bigger the higher you
  fire from. The belly glows fuller as the next blast recharges.
- Keyboard: arrows / WASD fly the same yoke (Down/S climbs, Up/W dives or
  surges), Space breathes.
- Blast an already-painted block to escalate it: rooftop gardens, then full
  Hundertwasser.
- Paint is saved on your phone.
- Three-finger tap (or `?tune`) opens the hidden tuning panel; `?fps` shows the
  frame-rate meter.

## Develop
```
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
npm run build        # dist/
```
Dev pages: `dev/city.html` (real city viewer), `dev/flight.html` (autopilot
flight test), and one page per module (`dev/bus.html`, `dev/fx.html`, ...).
Screenshots: `node tools/shot.mjs <url> out.png`, `node tools/shots.mjs`,
`node tools/blast.mjs <url> <outDir> [perf] [seq] [top] [reload] [escalate] [tap] [drop] [layouts]`
(blast QA at the Painted Ladies: frame sequence, top-down view, persistence, perf).
Feel QA: `node tools/feel-sim/run.mjs s_aim.ts` (and the other scenarios in
its header) runs the real flight / aim / splat code offline on the baked city;
`node tools/feel.mjs <baseUrl> shots/feel [strip] [glint] [taps]` shoots the
tap -> jet -> impact -> hit-stop strip and checks real taps in the browser.
Altitude QA (climb shots, flight log, taps, perf at cruise vs ceiling):
`node tools/altitude.mjs <baseUrl> shots/altitude downtown|west|gate|opening [--seq]`;
`--seq` also captures frames exactly 1/30 s apart, and
`python3 -I tools/seqstat.py shots/altitude/<phase>-seq-ceiling 5` counts what
changes between them (shimmer).

## City data (city-agnostic pipeline)
`tools/bake/` turns a city config (`tools/bake/cities/sf.json`) into compact
gzip'd binary region bundles in `public/city/<slug>/`:
```
python3 -m pip install geopandas pyogrio pyarrow rasterio pyproj scipy shapely
python3 -I tools/bake/bake.py sf       # footprints + 1 m DEM -> tiles
python3 -I tools/bake/pack.py sf       # tiles -> 1 km gzip regions
python3 -I tools/bake/horizon.py sf    # hills around the city
```
Sources: USGS 3DEP 1 m and 1/3 arc-second DEMs; FEMA/ORNL USA Structures
footprints (public domain). See `DECISIONS.md` for every call we made.

Paint state is a separate per-building array (faction, color, level, bloom
time) keyed by a stable building id, so a server can own it in Phase 2.

## Deploy
Vercel: import the repo; `vercel.json` is set up (build `npm run build`,
output `dist`). Add to Home Screen on iPhone for full-screen play.

# The Crown Oddity

브라우저에서 바로 하는 작은 액션 RPG다. 3D 블록 지형 위에 픽셀 그림 캐릭터를 세우고, 화면 위아래를 흐리게 하는 틸트시프트와 빛번짐을 걸어 미니어처 정원을 내려다보는 느낌을 냈다. 전투는 이스 시리즈처럼 빠르게 베고 구르고 막는 방식이다.

**지금 하기:** https://destory1984.github.io/the-crown-oddity/ (첫 로딩 약 45MB)

![제목 화면](docs/shots/title.jpg)

## 이야기

소라는 갈대늪에서 기억 없이 깨어난다. 가진 것은 머리 위의 작은 금관 하나뿐이다.

이 땅은 옛날 달지기들이 만든 커다란 태엽 정원이다. 달지기들은 여덟 밤마다 왕관으로 정원의 태엽을 감아 물이 흐르고 풀이 자라게 했다. 마지막 달지기 한결이 백 년 전 정원 한가운데로 혼자 들어가 돌아오지 않았다. 그 뒤로 아무도 태엽을 감지 않아 땅이 장난감 벽돌로 굳어 가고 있다.

소라가 왕관을 쓰고 나타나자, 굳은 벽돌들이 "왕관을 정원 한가운데로"라는 옛 명령을 따라 깨어나 달려든다.

![보리 할머니와 이야기](docs/shots/talk.jpg)

### 휴대폰 (가로 화면)

안드로이드와 아이폰 브라우저에서는 터치 조작이 켜진다. 세로로 들면 가로로 돌려 달라는 안내가 뜬다. 안드로이드에서는 처음 손을 대면 전체 화면이 된다.

| 터치 | 하는 일 |
|---|---|
| 화면 왼쪽 어디든 엄지를 대고 밀기 | 이동. 끝까지 밀면 달리기 |
| 칼 단추 (오른쪽 큰 마름모) | 공격 |
| 화살 단추 | 구르기 |
| 방패 단추 (누르고 있기) | 막기 |
| 왕관 단추 | E와 같다 |
| 손 단추 | Space와 같다 |
| 오른쪽 아래 기술 그림 넷 | 스킬 셋과 회복약 |
| 미니맵 아래 돋보기 둘 | 확대·축소 |
| 미니맵 왼쪽 단추 넷 | 조작법, 소리, 일지, 설정 |

휴대폰에서는 화면 기준을 1138x640으로 잡아 글자와 단추가 데스크톱의 약 1.4배로 보인다. 빠르게 돌도록 그림자를 끄고 풀을 절반만 그린다.

## 전투와 성장

- 기세는 베기를 맞힐 때마다 5, 섬광 피하기 20, 섬광 막기 25씩 찬다. 4초 동안 못 때리면 줄어든다.
- 적을 맞히면 0.05 → 0.14초 동안 화면이 멈춰 손맛을 준다. 괴물은 때리기 전에 0.45초 동안 빨갛게 부풀고 머리 위에 "!"가 뜬다.
- 레벨이 오르면 최대 체력 +12, 공격력 +3을 얻고, 몇몇 레벨에서 새 기술이 열린다.

| 레벨 | 새 기술 |
|---|---|
| 2 | 4타 연속기 (넷째 타는 한 바퀴 베기) |
| 3 | 달려 베기 (Shift로 달리며 J, 3m 앞으로 베며 나감) |
| 4 | 모아 베기 (L로 1초 막아 빛을 모은 뒤 J, 피해 3배) |
| 6 | 5타 연속기 (다섯째 타는 땅 내려찍기) |
| 8 | 빛 칼날 (연속기 마지막 타가 빛 칼날을 날림) |

- 왕관의 달빛 눈금은 8칸이다. 등불 켜기, 벽돌 풀기, 풍차 감기에 쓰고, 밤에 켜진 등불 곁에서 쉬면 10초마다 1칸 찬다. 낮에는 왕관 힘이 약해 더 많이 든다.
- 보스는 10마리다. 벽돌왕 950, 수레두더지 650, 노을 550과 830, 벽돌 거북 900, 벽돌 게 760, 벽돌 매 780, 벽돌 허수아비 820, 벽돌 기사 1100, 굳은달 거푸집 1700의 체력을 가진다. 벽돌 기사는 앞에서 오는 공격을 방패로 막는다. 옆이나 뒤를 치거나 섬광 막기로 틈을 만든다.
- 동료 물결은 장대로 찌르고, 노을은 벽돌 가루를 던져 함께 싸운다.

## 바뀐 것

날짜별로 바뀐 것은 [CHANGES.md](CHANGES.md)에 따로 적는다.

## 만든 방법

- 엔진은 Godot 4.7이고, 웹으로 내보낸 결과를 이 저장소 맨 위에 둔다. 게임은 거의 모두 코드로 짓는다. 지형, 집, 나무, 괴물은 상자를 쌓아 만들고, 풀과 부들과 물 무늬는 코드에서 찍는다.
- Godot 프로젝트 원본은 `godot/` 폴더에 있다. Godot 4.7에서 그 폴더를 열고 F5를 누르면 돈다.
- 그림은 GPT 이미지 생성(Codex CLI)으로 그렸다. 걷기 8방향, 주민과 노을의 픽셀 그림, 초상화, 이야기 삽화 12장, 상점 물건 아이콘이 그렇다. 소라가 가만히 서서 하는 몸짓 49가지는 같은 작가의 다른 프로젝트 Space Oddity의 그림을 가져왔다.
- 화면에 나오는 글 약 540줄은 번역 표(`godot/i18n/text.csv`)를 거친다. 지금은 한국어만 채웠고, 영어·일본어·중국어 칸은 비어 있다.
- 효과음은 코드에서 합성한다. 글꼴은 Pretendard를 쓴다.
- 자동 시험 88개가 처음 깨어나기부터 끝 장면까지 따라가며 확인한다.

## 이 폴더에서 직접 열기

로컬 서버를 띄운다.

```
python -m http.server 8765
```

그다음 `http://localhost:8765` 를 연다.

## 라이선스

- 코드: MIT 라이선스. 마음대로 고치고 써도 된다.
- 소라 캐릭터(디자인과 모든 그림, 게임 데이터에 든 것 포함)와 제목 그림: destory1984의 것이다. 모든 권리를 가진다(All rights reserved). MIT에 들어가지 않으므로 허락 없이 복사, 수정, 배포, 다른 작품에 쓰기를 할 수 없다. 코드를 가져다 쓰려면 캐릭터를 자기 것으로 바꿔야 한다.
- 글꼴: Pretendard, SIL 오픈 폰트 라이선스 1.1.

tjballworm/age-three.readme:
# Age Three

A browser strategy game. It's planned for web, Steam and mobile, all on one shared server.

## Getting started

Requires Node.js 20.11 or newer (22 LTS recommended, see `.nvmrc`).

```
npm install        # once, from this folder
npm run dev        # start the web client at http://localhost:5173
```

| Command             | What it does                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`       | Web client dev server with hot reload                   |
| `npm run build`     | Production build of the web client into `apps/web/dist` |
| `npm run typecheck` | Type-check every package and the Svelte app             |
| `npm test`          | Run unit tests (Vitest)                                 |
| `npm run lint`      | ESLint                                                  |
| `npm run format`    | Prettier                                                |

## Structure

```
age-three/
├─ apps/
│  ├─ web/            Svelte 5 + PixiJS client (Vite)
│  │  └─ src/
│  │     ├─ game/     PixiJS: engine setup, scenes (world map, town, outskirts)
│  │     ├─ ui/       Svelte: HUD, windows, shared components
│  │     ├─ state/    client game state (Svelte runes), read by game and UI
│  │     ├─ net/      connection to the server
│  │     └─ styles/   design tokens and global CSS
│  ├─ server/         authoritative game server (not started)
│  ├─ desktop/        Electron + Steamworks shell for Steam (not started)
│  └─ mobile/         Capacitor shell for iOS and Android (not started)
└─ packages/
   ├─ core/           shared rules, data and types; pure TS, runs on client and server
   │  └─ src/ types · data · rules · combat
   └─ protocol/       client/server message types
```

**How the client is layered:** PixiJS owns one full-screen canvas for anything with lots of sprites (the
world map, town and outskirts). Svelte renders the HUD and windows as regular HTML on top. Both read the
same state in `apps/web/src/state`.

**Why `core` is separate:** game rules (costs, build times, distances, combat) live in one place, with no DOM
code, so the server can run exactly the same logic the client uses for previews.

Import aliases in the web app: `$game/…`, `$ui/…`, `$state/…`, `$net/…`. Shared packages are imported as
`@age3/core` and `@age3/protocol`.

## Design

See `../docs/style-guide.md` for colours, fonts and component specs. The tokens are mirrored in
`apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css`. The display font (Cinzel) and body font (Noto Sans) are not bundled
yet; they fall back to system fonts until they're added under `apps/web/public/assets/fonts`.

1990jjhh-ctrl/Beyond-Mastery.readme:
# Beyond Mastery

SKSE plugin for Skyrim AE 1.6.x and 1.7.x: raise each skill's cap above 100 in +10 steps, paid with perk points, dragon souls and filled black soul gems. Skill effects above 100 continue sub-linearly or asymptotically.

- Requirements: [PRD.md](PRD.md)
- Engine hook design: [docs/hook-points.md](docs/hook-points.md)

## Status

Supported runtimes: AE 1.6.x and 1.7.x. SE 1.5.97 is out of scope for now
(PRD §3): the plugin loads there but stays inactive.

Verified in-game on 1.7.104 (SKSE64 2.3.1, Proton):
- The plugin loads, with no warnings in its log.
- Every patch site resolves to the address `scripts/verify_sites.py` predicts
  ([docs/hook-points.md](docs/hook-points.md) §9a).
- Skills level normally and stop at their limit.
- The Legendary menu: Upgrade pays with perks, dragon souls and black soul
  gems (The Black Star included). It shows what is missing when the player
  can't afford it, and names the level still to reach below the limit.
- Reset Skill, re-training, and dragon-soul gates paid again on each climb.
- Caps and gates survive save and reload.
- The Reset Skill confirmation names the reset, the returned perks, the kept
  cap and any dragon souls lost (FR-31).
- The first level past a raised limit or a paid gate costs its full XP (FR-8).
- Formula scaling above 100 (FR-24 … FR-30), described below: spell cost
  follows the PRD curve (Destruction 100 → 200 cut a spell's cost by the
  predicted 0.69×), Speech 1000 buys at exactly 1.2× the sell price, weapon
  damage grows sub-linearly, enchanting keeps a cost per hit. The skills menu,
  the crafting menus, the skill-increase notification and the level-up screen
  all show the real level.
- The optional character-XP clamp, `bClampCharXPAbove100` (FR-11): a skill
  level-up above 100 gives the character XP of one at 100, checked to the
  point through the plugin's `Character XP … (+N)` log line.
- The optional skill XP scaling, `bScaleXPGainAbove100` (FR-9): above 100,
  skill XP from use is multiplied by `√(100/skill)`; trainers and skill books
  still grant exact levels.

Implemented, but not yet verified in-game:
- A one-time log warning if a skill's XP threshold ever passes float
  precision, around level 3,500 (FR-10).
- The conflict warning (FR-20).

Deferred: FR-10's double-precision XP accumulator, until a reachable level
needs it.

## Skills above 100

Above 100, skills keep paying off, but less and less:

- Most effects (weapon damage, armor, smithing, alchemy, enchanting
  magnitude, block, lockpicking, pickpocket, sneak) grow with the square root
  of the skill rather than linearly.
- Spell cost keeps falling towards a floor: the skill's part of the cost never
  drops below 25% (`fSpellCostLimit`).
- Buying always costs at least 1.2× what the same item sells for
  (`fBarterMinRatio`), after perks and Fortify Barter.
- Enchanting charge per use falls towards half its value at 100
  (`fEnchantChargeLimitFraction`), so enchanted weapons never become free.

Only the player is affected; NPCs stay vanilla. Everything other mods or
scripts read as the player's current skill above 100 is this *effective*
value, not the level shown in the skills menu. A script that sets a skill
from its own reading (`SetActorValue(x, GetActorValue(x) + 1)`) would
therefore lower a skill above 100. `bEnableFormulaScaling=false` in
`BeyondMastery.ini` turns all of this off.

## Install

Requires [SKSE64](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/30379?tab=files)
and [Address Library for SKSE Plugins](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/32444).

Each [release](https://github.com/1990jjhh-ctrl/Beyond-Mastery/releases) has two
archives with the same files:

- `BeyondMastery-<version>.zip`: install it with a mod manager (Mod Organizer 2,
  Vortex), or extract it into `Data/`.
- `BeyondMastery-<version>-SKSE-Plugins.zip`: extract it straight into
  `Data/SKSE/Plugins/`.

Neither contains `BeyondMastery.ini`: the plugin writes it on first start, and
an update keeps your settings.

## Uninstalling

Skills already above 100 keep the level they reached — the engine stores skill
levels as floats, so nothing resets — but they stop progressing once the plugin
is gone, and nothing above 100 will rise again.

Reinstalling with the co-save intact restores every cap. Reinstalling *without*
it (a new save, or a co-save that was deleted) puts every cap back to 100 while
those skills keep their higher levels; they simply sit above their cap and stop
earning XP until the cap is raised past them again. No resource you already
spent is refunded.

## Development

Building, testing and the architecture: [docs/development.md](docs/development.md).

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later (CommonLibSSE-NG is GPL-3.0-or-later and statically linked).

fix: link the C++ runtime statically so the plugin loads

SKSE disabled the plugin on load ("fatal error occurred while loading
plugin"). The first std::mutex::lock() faulted: we compiled against MSVC
STL 14.44, whose std::mutex has had a constexpr-initialised layout since
14.40, while the game loaded msvcp140.dll 14.0.24215.1 (VS 2015 Update 3)
from its Proton prefix. That runtime's _Mtx_lock cannot read the new
layout. Isolated with load tracing: every SKSE interface call succeeded on
its own, and a bare std::mutex died on lock().

Linking the CRT statically puts the STL implementation in the DLL, built by
the same toolset as the headers, so the two cannot drift apart. The plugin
now imports only OS DLLs (5, down from 18) and no longer depends on whatever
redistributable a player has -- this hits plain Windows users with a stale
redist just as much as Proton.

The triplet has to pass the runtime explicitly. vcpkg turns
VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE into /MT only inside its own windows.cmake toolchain, and
uses that toolchain only when none is chainloaded; ours chainloads, so
VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE static on its own would have been silently ignored.

scripts/check_runtime_deps.py fails the build if msvcp140 or vcruntime140
ever reappears in the import table. It failed on the old build, naming all
three runtime DLLs, before passing on this one.
