playingpossumm/cellbound.readme:
# Cellbound

Cellbound is a variant sudoku game that runs in the browser and installs as an app on phones and laptops. It opens straight into the day's puzzle, and every board is made or stored on your device. Progress stays in the browser's local storage, so there is no server, no account and no advertising, and after the first visit the whole app works offline.

Play it at [cellbound-sudoku.vercel.app](https://cellbound-sudoku.vercel.app).

![The Daily in the six looks, on a phone](docs/six-looks.png)

## Modes

The Daily is one puzzle a day, the same for everyone. Monday to Saturday bring a 6x6 board and Sunday a 9x9, and the difficulty climbs from a gentle Monday to a hard Saturday. Each Daily is named after a constellation, and solving it on its own day keeps your streak going.

Run is a short roguelite. You play five boards in a row with three hearts, and every wrong digit costs a heart. Between boards you take one of three cards. A boon helps on the next board, a curse makes it harder and raises its score, and a bargain does a little of both. There is a daily run with the same boards and offers for everyone, free runs that are new every time, and five more cards to unlock by reaching milestones.

Fog hides most of the board. A correct digit clears the cells around it and shows the givens and clues underneath, while a wrong digit clears nothing.

Free play lets you pick 6x6 or 9x9, any mix of rules and a difficulty from 1 to 5, then plays an endless stream of boards. Sharing a result shares a link to that exact board.

Learn has a short lesson for the basics and for each rule, and every lesson ends with a small practice puzzle. Until you have done a rule's lesson, its chip on the board carries a New mark that opens it.

## Rules

Every board keeps the classic rule that each row, column and box holds each digit once, then adds one or more of these.

| Rule | What it asks |
| --- | --- |
| Thermo | Digits rise from the round bulb to the far end of the line. |
| Arrow | Digits along the arrow add up to the digit in its circle. |
| Cage | Digits in the cage add up to its small total and never repeat. |
| Renban | The line holds a run of consecutive digits, in any order. |
| Whisper | Neighbours on the line differ by at least 3 on a 6x6 board and 5 on a 9x9. |
| Dots | A white dot joins digits one apart, a black dot a digit and its double. |
| XV | An X joins digits that sum to 10, a V digits that sum to 5. |
| Diagonal | Each diagonal holds every digit once. |
| Anti-knight | Equal digits are never a knight's move apart. |

## Playing

Tap or click a cell, then a number. On a keyboard, type the digit, move with the arrow keys or WASD, and erase with Backspace, Delete or 0. N switches to notes and Shift with a digit writes a single note, Z undoes and Y redoes (Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work too), H asks for a hint, P pauses and Escape clears the selection.

A hint comes in three steps for the same deduction. The first shows where to look, the second names the rule that does the work, and the third places the digit and explains why. Mistake checking can be off, can show only digits that break a rule, or can mark every digit that differs from the solution. Fog and Run always check against the solution, because clearing fog and losing hearts depend on it.

![A Daily on a laptop](docs/laptop.png)

## Looks

Cellbound has six looks, each with a light and a dark version. On Auto it follows your device.

- Star atlas puts gold hairlines on ink-blue chart paper under a slow star field, with each Daily's constellation in the band.
- Paper and ink is newsprint with graphite pencil and a blue pen under a newspaper masthead.
- Washi and sumi has rice paper, brushed box lines and a vermilion seal for every finished box.
- Swiss poster uses flat red, blue and yellow, heavy type and a thick rule, and turns finished boxes into blocks of colour.
- Prism sets digits on dark glass, with one spectrum colour for every digit.
- Letters in space is a monospaced grid with rules spelled along the lines and the board drawn above it as a turning cube of letters.

Every look honours reduced motion, from the device or from Settings.

## Run it

You need Node.js 22.12 or newer.

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open the address Vite prints. `npm run build` makes a production build in `dist/` with a service worker, and `npm run preview` serves it.

## Scripts

- `npm run dev` starts the dev server.
- `npm run build` type-checks and builds to `dist/`.
- `npm run preview` serves the production build.
- `npm test` runs the unit tests once, and `npm run test:watch` keeps them running.
- `npm run typecheck` checks the types.
- `npm run e2e` runs the browser tests in Edge, in WebKit (the engine of Safari) as an iPhone and an iPad, and in Firefox. They start a dev server and a production preview on their own. Run `npx playwright install webkit firefox` once first. Edge is the installed Microsoft Edge unless `PW_CHANNEL=chromium` is set.
- `npm run e2e:edge` runs the Edge projects only, which is the quick check.
- `npm run gen:daily` regenerates the stored Daily puzzles. Pass a range of months to choose them, for example `npm run gen:daily -- 2028-01 2028-12`.
- `npm run gen:practice` regenerates the Learn practice puzzles.
- `python scripts/lining-digits.py` rebuilds the small lining-digit fonts of the Star atlas look from the installed Cormorant Garamond (it needs `pip install fonttools`).

## How it is built

The app uses React 19 and TypeScript 7, built with Vite 8. Game state lives in zustand stores saved to local storage, and vite-plugin-pwa provides the service worker and the web manifest. Fonts come from Fontsource packages, so nothing is fetched from a font service.

The puzzle engine in `src/engine` is plain TypeScript. It has a solver that proves each puzzle has one solution, a generator that grades difficulty by the techniques a logical solver needs, the hint explainer built on that solver, and the fog layouts. Bo

pkinvest4-ux/nfl-pricing.desc: Pricing NFL spreads the day before and grading against the closing line
pkinvest4-ux/nfl-pricing.readme:
# Pricing NFL Spreads the Day Before

Prices every NFL game with what was known by the end of the day before, and grades the price against
the pre-game closing line. The starting model was 2.10 points off the close on 2025; with the
improvements, it's **1.78**.

A companion to [nba-pricing-trial](https://github.com/pkinvest4-ux/nba-pricing-trial), built the same way.

## Start here

1. **[WRITEUP.md](WRITEUP.md):** the one-page summary.
2. **[HOW_IT_WORKS.md](HOW_IT_WORKS.md):** a walk through the code, in the order a game gets priced.
3. **[EXAMPLE_GAME.md](EXAMPLE_GAME.md):** one real game, start to finish.
4. **[DETAILS.md](DETAILS.md):** every number, season by season.
5. **[results_by_game.csv](results_by_game.csv):** every game of 2025 and 2026 so far: how each number was
   built, the close and the result. [results_summary.csv](results_summary.csv) has the season totals.

## Run it

Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only.

```bash
python3 fetch_data.py         # download everything into data/ (cached)
python3 evaluate.py           # grade 2025, the test season
python3 evaluate.py 2026      # grade this season so far
python3 walkforward.py        # each season 2016 to 2025, tuned on the 5 before it
python3 explain.py SF NO 2025-09-14   # how one game was priced, piece by piece
python3 export_results.py     # rewrite the spreadsheets
python3 pick_window.py        # how the 5-season tuning window was chosen
```

## Files

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `data.py` | Everything known the day before a game: the closing line, rest, quarterbacks, other starters out |
| `model.py` | The spread model: price each day's games, then learn from them; choose the settings |
| `totals.py` | The over/under model |
| `evaluate.py` | Grade each step against the close, check which gains are real, win probability, totals |
| `walkforward.py` | Ten seasons, each tuned on the 5 before it |
| `pick_window.py` | How many past seasons to tune on, chosen on 2024 |
| `explain.py` | Show how one game's number was built |
| `export_results.py` | Write `results_by_game.csv` and `results_summary.csv` |
| `fetch_data.py` | Download games, injury reports, rosters, player stats, snap counts (nflverse) and closing lines (ESPN) |
| `common.py` | Web requests |

## Rules the code follows

- A day's games are priced before any of that day's results or lines are used.
- Injuries come from the final injury report, published before game day. Game-day inactives are not used.
- Every setting is chosen on seasons before the one being graded.
- 2024 on is graded against one book's pre-game close, as recorded by ESPN.

# פאקמן

משחק קלאסי של אכילת נקודות. אתר (PWA) שעטוף כאפליקציית אנדרואיד עם Capacitor.
פרויקט האנדרואיד כבר נוצר בתיקייה `android/`, כולל אייקונים.

## הרצה בדפדפן
    npm run serve        # http://localhost:8080

## בניית APK

### אפשרות א': GitHub Actions (בלי להתקין כלום)
1. העלה את התיקייה ל-repo חדש ב-GitHub (branch בשם `main`).
2. הקובץ `.github/workflows/build-apk.yml` יבנה את ה-APK אוטומטית בכל push.
3. בלשונית Actions בוחרים את הריצה האחרונה, ומורידים את `chomper-apk` מתחתית העמוד.
4. מעבירים את `app-debug.apk` לטלפון ומתקינים (צריך לאשר "התקנה ממקורות לא ידועים").

### אפשרות ב': על המחשב שלך (Android Studio + JDK 21)
    npm install
    npm run android:sync
    cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug
    # הקובץ: android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

או `npm run android:open` ואז Run מתוך Android Studio.

## טבלת שיאים (Firebase Realtime Database)
הטבלה כבויה עד שממלאים את `LB_URL` ב-`index.html`. הגדרה חד-פעמית:
1. https://console.firebase.google.com > פרויקט > Build > Realtime Database > Create database.
2. בלשונית Rules מדביקים את התוכן של `database.rules.json` ולוחצים Publish.
3. בלשונית Data מעתיקים את הכתובת שמופיעה למעלה (`https://...firebasedatabase.app`) לתוך `LB_URL`.

ההגנה היא החוקים: אפשר רק להוסיף שחקן או להעלות לו ניקוד, לא למחוק ולא להוריד.
מי שמבין בקוד יכול לשלוח ניקוד מזויף. לטבלה בין חברים זה מספיק.

## העלאה לגוגל פליי
ה-APK של debug טוב להתקנה ישירה, לא לחנות. בשביל החנות:
Android Studio > Build > Generate Signed App Bundle > `.aab`.
צור keystore ושמור אותו וגם את הסיסמה במקום בטוח. אם תאבד אותו לא תוכל לעדכן את האפליקציה.

- חשבון מפתח בגוגל פליי עולה 25$ חד-פעמי, ודורש גיל 18+ (חשבון של הורה).
- חשבון אישי חדש חייב Closed testing עם 12 בודקים ל-14 ימים רצופים לפני שאפשר לפרסם.
- השם "פאקמן" והדמויות הם סימן מסחרי של Bandai Namco. לשיתוף בין חברים זה בסדר, אבל לפני גוגל פליי חייבים לשנות שם, אחרת האפליקציה תיחסם.

kinnuworks/accomplice.desc: A murder-mystery party game for Fire TV where one of your friends is secretly helping the killer. Phones as controllers, AI suspects you question out loud, an Alexa+ add-on, deployed on AWS.
kinnuworks/accomplice.readme:
# Accomplice

**Demo video:** https://youtu.be/TiMqMkAqtYM · **Play live:** http://Accomp-Alb16-mcZdJ1MHVPFR-1726733199.ap-south-1.elb.amazonaws.com/tv/ · **Fire TV package:** [v1.0.0 release](https://github.com/kinnuworks/accomplice/releases/tag/v1.0.0)

A murder-mystery party game for Fire TV. Up to six people question AI suspects out loud from their phones, and one of the people on the couch is secretly helping the killer.

- **TV (Vega OS):** the case, the suspects, the evidence board and the reveal. D-pad only.
- **Phones:** scan the QR code, no install. Your phone holds your secret role, your clues, hold-to-talk and your votes. Works with VoiceOver and TalkBack.
- **Alexa+:** the same game as an MCP add-on, with an Echo Show style board. You can also say "send it to the TV".

Every case is generated fresh and checked by a solver before anyone sees it: exactly one culprit fits the clues, every key clue is needed, and the case can be solved by round 3. That engine is open source as [`fairplay`](packages/fairplay).

## How a game goes

1. The TV plays a 60-second cold open. Everyone scans the QR code.
2. Each phone shows a sealed role. One player may be the accomplice: they know who did it and try to steer the room away.
3. Hold your phone and ask a suspect anything. They answer in their own voice within about two seconds. They lie only where the case says they lie, and every sentence is checked against the case before it is spoken.
4. Pin clues on the board, use your one **Objection!**, survive the blackout in round 3.
5. The room accuses the culprit and votes on the accomplice. The reveal replays the chain of clues that proves the answer, the culprit confesses, and you get a newspaper front page to keep.

Cozy mode swaps the murder for a stolen cake and keeps everything else. Players can ask questions and read captions in Hindi.

## Repository

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `apps/server` | Fastify + WebSocket game server. Suspects, voices (Amazon Polly), speech to text (Amazon Transcribe), Hindi (Amazon Translate), MCP endpoint, DynamoDB snapshots. |
| `apps/tv-web` | The 10-foot TV stage (React). Served at `/tv/`. |
| `apps/vega` | The Vega OS app that hosts the TV stage. |
| `apps/phone` | The phone controller (React). Served at `/p/`. |
| `apps/echo-sim` | Echo Show style client for the Alexa+ add-on. |
| `packages/fairplay` | Case generator and Z3 verifier. MIT. |
| `packages/mcp-game` | MCP server for Alexa+ (spec 2025-11-25, Streamable HTTP, tasks, elicitation, MCP Apps). |
| `packages/protocol` | Shared message types. |
| `infra` | AWS CDK stack: ECS Fargate, ALB, S3, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, Budgets. |
| `e2e` | Full-game audit harness with screenshots and accessibility checks. |

## Run it locally

Needs Node 22+, pnpm, AWS credentials with Polly, Transcribe and Translate, and a model API key in `apps/server/.env` (see `apps/server/.env.example`).

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm --filter @accomplice/server start
```

Open `http://localhost:8787/tv/` on a big screen and scan the QR code with your phones. Phones need HTTPS for the microphone, so for real devices set `PUBLIC_URL` to an HTTPS tunnel.

Tests:

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm --filter @accomplice/e2e run audit
```

## Deploy

See [docs/AWS.md](docs/AWS.md).

## More

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Friction log](docs/FRICTION_LOG.md)
- [Product feedback](docs/PRODUCT_FEEDBACK.md)

## License

MIT

# Gullin' It

A six-level, data-driven seaside arcade prototype for Godot. Aim a gull, hold climb, and dive to steal food while avoiding defensive beachgoers and competing gulls. Tested with the local Godot 4.7.2 Windows build.

The opening now progresses from **Training Day** (a compact, calm teaching beach), to **Family Picnic** (two picnic groups and their kiosk trips), to **Boardwalk Bustle** (customers, a dog owner, and a pier diner). These three maps have authored rosters, boundaries, landmarks, and small repeatable placement variations. **Dog Day Afternoon** (level 4) is also hand-built: a fast off-lead terrier barks, chases the gull along the sand and in low flight, and stuns it on a catch, so climbing or flying away is the escape. **Three's a Crowd** (level 5) is hand-built too: Chip, a fast kittiwake, joins after your first swallow and taunts; he, Gary and you fight over two pier diners' fried fish. Level 6 retains the larger generated route.

Training Day teaches takeoff and steering, landing and crumbs, a timed swoop followed by a safe climb, bag raiding, pecking a bin for scraps, and an independent swoop. Selecting its level card always opens the lessons, including after completing the tutorial; completed saves show **REPLAY LESSONS** and start from lesson one. There is no timer or snatch quota. Completed lessons save automatically; unfinished courses resume their checkpoint. Practice snacks are restored during training. Finishing unlocks Family Picnic without awarding stars or setting a Practice best time. **TRAIN AGAIN** explicitly starts over. Existing scores and unlocks are preserved. Gary enters Boardwalk Bustle after the first non-scrap snack is swallowed.

See `docs/OPENING_LEVELS.md` for the map contracts and tuning notes.

## Run

Import `project.godot` into Godot and press F6 on `scenes/main.tscn`, or F5 to run the project. The local engine is also available at `.tools/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe` (ignored by Git).

## Controls

| Action | Mouse / keyboard | Controller |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aim | Mouse, WASD, or arrow keys | Left stick |
| Climb | Hold left mouse or Space | Hold A |
| Dive | Right mouse or Shift | B |
| Peck during a dive / nearby stash or toddler food on foot | Tap E | Tap X |
| Pause / resume | Escape or HUD pause button | Start |
| Restart | R | Back |
| Fullscreen | F11 | Options menu |
| Debug overlay / reload JSON | F1 / F2 | — |

Touch: drag the beach to aim, hold FLAP, and tap DIVE. Enable the touch overlay in Options when previewing on desktop. The first level waits for **LET'S GULL IT** at the bottom of its opening panel; click, tap, or confirm the focused button to begin. Other level introductions dismiss on the first button press or after two seconds. Controller A, Space, or left mouse flaps; keyboard A remains leftward aiming.

Holding flap beats the wings in short strokes (about three a second) that outpace a gentle gravity, so climbing is steady rather than instant and a single stroke only lifts a few pixels. Wind eases the sinking in either direction. Swoops with the wind are much faster, swoops against it much slower, and flap strokes are weaker when flying into the wind (stronger with it), so lifting out of an upwind dive is hard. Tuning lives under `flight.stroke_*`, `flight.gravity` and `wind.lift_*`/`wind.dive_drag`. Without flapping, the gull descends and lands on the sand. Collectables glint now and then (full picnic bags, bins with scraps, loose food and crumbs the gull has room for); `scripts/pickup_shine.gd` draws the pixel shine and `juice.shine`, `juice.shine_cycle` and `juice.shine_step` tune it. Aim left or right to walk on visibly stepping feet with folded wings, at one fifth of normal flying speed. Landing immediately limits movement to this walking pace. Ground crumbs award 5 points and single chips award 10; both reappear after 18 seconds. Hold flap to take off. Scraps do not count toward the 15 practice snatches or build a combo.

At the end of a run, the frozen beach stays visible beneath a hanging wooden score sign. Earned points, the clean-run bonus, snatches, stuns, special-event counts, and the final total tally in sequence before the stars appear. Click, tap, or press confirm to finish the tally immediately. A perched gull celebrates successful and Practice runs with a short screech, while a failed run gets a gag and a falling fish skeleton; these one-shot sounds follow the SFX and Master volume settings.

Sunbathers keep all food inside a large picnic duffle beside their feet. There is no exposed snack to steal by walking or diving. Land and peck the bag to scatter food, then catch or collect it for normal score, combo and Practice credit. Other beachgoers still carry food that can be stolen in a swoop.

Sunbather picnic bags show straps, a handle, a zip and small stock markers. All three snacks stay inside until pecked; newly scattered snacks fly for 0.3 seconds before either the gull or owner can collect them. Sunbathers remain on the sandy beach and retrieve snacks at 40 pixels/second after waking. The sunbather never automatically takes one out. An empty bag does not refill. Toddlers are linked to a specific mum through level data. A robbed toddler walks to that mum for a visible handover from the family's shared supply. Each mum starts with two crisp bags total, including the one already in her hand, plus a separate two-cookie reserve. These counts and the approach/handover timing are editable in `data/tuning.json`.

Beach bins also respond to the peck button (E / controller X / touch PECK). Four taps scatter three objects per burst. Each bin has nine objects per level attempt: two crumbs, three half-eaten foods, and four pieces of litter. Edible scraps become available after 0.3 seconds and award their listed food points without combos or practice credit. Garbage stays visible on the ground and cannot be eaten. Restarting the level resets the bin contents and litter.

brendongl/hello-reskin.readme:
# Hello-Reskin

Put your own character into **Hello, Luigi!** on Nintendo Switch: face, eyes, mouths, voice, items, music and on-screen text.
You build the mod on your own computer from your own copy of the game, then load it with Atmosphère's LayeredFS.

The repo includes a full worked example, **Pikachu over Luigi**, as a recipe: every slot mapping, prompt, loop point and fix we needed.
It does **not** include any game files or finished Pikachu assets. You regenerate those yourself (see `recipes/pikachu/`).

> **Unofficial fan project.** Not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Nintendo, The Pokémon Company or Game Freak.
> No game files, keys, or copyrighted assets are included or will be accepted. You need your own legally owned copy of the
> game and your own console. Nothing here is for sale.

## What you can change

| Part | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Face (head, ears, cheeks, nose, ~25 mouths) | Vector meshes rebuilt from one flat drawing | `tools/make_face.py`; the hardest part |
| Eyes (pupil, highlight, blink/sleepy lids) | Recoloured eye texture atlas | `tools/pika_atlas.py` + a params file |
| Items, enemies, hands, buttons, backgrounds | PNG replacements by texture name | `template/MANIFEST.csv` lists all 195 slots |
| Voice (191 lines) and sound effects | WAV replacements by clip name | `template/AUDIO_SLOTS.csv` lists all clips |
| Music (6 tracks × 4 layers, looping) | WAV + loop points | `audio/music/` finds seamless loops |
| On-screen text ("Luigi", enemy names) | Text map, all 12 languages | the game font has a limited character set |

## Quick start

1. Read **[docs/GUIDE.md](docs/GUIDE.md)**: dump the game and keys from your Switch, extract it, set up Python, export the slot templates.
2. Read **[docs/PAINPOINTS.md](docs/PAINPOINTS.md)**: everything that went wrong for us and how we fixed it.
3. Copy the recipe layout from **[recipes/pikachu/](recipes/pikachu/)** into `packs/<your-character>/` and replace the art and sounds.
4. Build: `python tools/build_mod.py packs/<your-character>`, then copy `build/<name>/atmosphere` to the root of your SD card.

## Requirements

- A Switch with custom firmware (Atmosphère) and your own copy of Hello, Luigi! (title ID `0100D8C0251AE000`, v0)
- Your own `prod.keys` / `title.keys` (Lockpick_RCM), and the game dumped with nxdumptool
- Linux or WSL, Python 3.12, ffmpeg, .NET 8 SDK (for the RomFS extractor), Il2CppDumper
- Optional: an OpenRouter API key for AI art and audio labelling, and yt-dlp for sourcing audio

## Layout

```
tools/          build + extraction scripts (build_mod, make_face, pika_atlas, fsb5, hx RomFS extractor, ...)
audio/          clip splitter, AI labeller, music loop finder/renderer
template/       slot lists only (texture names/sizes, audio clip names/lengths): no game data
recipes/pikachu worked example: mappings, prompts, loop points, sources, fix settings, scripts
docs/           GUIDE.md (step by step) and PAINPOINTS.md (lessons)
packs/          your packs go here (ignored by git)
```

## Sharing your character

Share your **pack sources** (your own art and sounds, plus the json files), never the built `atmosphere/` folder:
that folder contains modified copies of the game's files. Don't use other people's copyrighted art or audio in a public pack.

## License

Code: MIT (see `LICENSE`). Game names and characters belong to their owners.

Fazerdino1/geysermcnewextra.readme:
# GeyserMCNewExtra

Java Edition features and handy extras for **Bedrock Edition players** on Java Edition servers running
[GeyserMC](https://geysermc.org/). Built and maintained for the **CrossPlayMC** network (Java & Bedrock),
including the public PvP server **CrossPlayMC-SMP**, with a focus on stability and fair PvP between
both editions.

Source code and issues: **https://github.com/Fazerdino1/geysermcnewextra**

> **Status:** `2.1.0-alpha.1`, in development; no build is published yet.
> See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Supported platforms

Requires **Geyser 2.12.0** (Minecraft Java 26.3 protocol; older servers through ViaVersion) and Java 21.

| Jar | Platform | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GeyserMCNewExtra-Spigot.jar` | Paper, Purpur, Spigot with Geyser-Spigot | Primary target (CrossPlayMC runs Purpur + Geyser-Spigot + Floodgate) |
| `GeyserMCNewExtra-Velocity.jar` | Velocity with Geyser-Velocity | Builds, less tested |
| `GeyserMCNewExtra-BungeeCord.jar` | BungeeCord / Waterfall with Geyser-BungeeCord | Builds, less tested |
| `GeyserMCNewExtra-Extension.jar` | `Geyser/extensions` folder (incl. Geyser Standalone) | Builds, less tested. Do **not** use it together with a plugin jar |

[PacketEvents](https://modrinth.com/plugin/packetevents) is optional; some features need it.

## Installing

1. Put the jar for your platform in `plugins/` (or `Geyser/extensions/` for the extension).
2. Start the server once. Settings live in `plugins/GeyserMCNewExtra/config.yml`.

**Coming from GeyserExtras?** Remove its jar. On the first start, GeyserMCNewExtra copies the old
`plugins/GeyserExtras/` folder (config, player preferences, optional packs) into
`plugins/GeyserMCNewExtra/` and renames the two options that carried the old name. The old folder is
kept as a backup and can be deleted afterwards. The main command is now `/geysermcnewextra`
(`/ge` still works).

## Commands

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/geysermcnewextra` | `/ge` | Opens the menu (Bedrock players) |
| `/playerlist` | `/l`, `/players`, `/listplayers`, `/tab`, `/tablist` | Java tab list as a Bedrock form |
| `/emotechat` | `/muteemotechat`, `/unmuteemotechat` | Java players: toggle Bedrock emote chat |

Aliases can be turned off with `disabled-command-aliases` (e.g. to free `/l` for a local chat plugin).

## Features

### Combat
- Java Edition combat sounds (critical, sweep, knockback and weak attacks), can be turned off
- The Java-style attack cooldown indicator is provided by Geyser (`cooldown-type` in Geyser's config);
  each player can pick crosshair, hotbar or off, defaulting to the server's setting
### Parity
- Emote chat sent to nearby Java players (muted with `/muteemotechat`)
- Bedrock forms for Java-only menus: player list with tab header/footer, server links,
  advancements, statistics
- Experimental Block Display support using FMBE
- Experimental Bedrock capes shown to Java players (requires PacketEvents; see
  [docs/ANTICHEAT.md](docs/ANTICHEAT.md) before enabling it on a PvP server)
### Utility
- Rebind some Bedrock actions to Java actions (e.g. swap offhand), including **emote shortcuts**:
  link an emote to an action once from the bindings menu
- Optional resource packs (`.mcpack` or `.zip`) players can toggle from `optionalpacks/`
- Save player skin, geometry and animation data to `skins/` (off by default)
- Menu opened by double tapping the inventory button or typing `/ge`
- `debug-mode: true` traces players, forms and shortcuts in the console

## Languages

Every text comes from `plugins/GeyserMCNewExtra/lang/<locale>.yml`: English, French and 10 more
languages are included. Bedrock players see their own client language when a file exists for it;
otherwise, and for the console, `default-locale` is used (French by default). Edit any text in
these files, or add a language by adding a file; texts added by a new version are appended to your
files automatically.

## Documentation

- [docs/TEST-CHECKLIST.md](docs/TEST-CHECKLIST.md): in-game test checklist
- [docs/ANTICHEAT.md](docs/ANTICHEAT.md): anti-cheat friction points and recommended settings
- [docs/ISSUES-STATUS.md](docs/ISSUES-STATUS.md): status of the issues inherited from the original project
- [docs/AUDIT.md](docs/AUDIT.md) and [docs/FORKS-COMPARISON.md](docs/FORKS-COMPARISON.md): code audit and fork survey

## Building

Requires a JVM to launch Gradle; the JDK used for compilation is downloaded automatically.

```bash
./gradlew build
```

Jars are written to `<module>/build/libs/`.

## Credits

GeyserMCNewExtra is based on **GeyserExtras by LetsGoAway** (MIT) and on fixes from several community
forks. The full list of authors and contributors is in **[CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md)**.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The original copyright notice (Copyright (c) 2024 LetsGoAway) is kept as
required by the license.

turned off after the rename. It now reads the releases of
Fazerdino1/geysermcnewextra and compares versions by Semantic Versioning
precedence (string equality used to call any different version an
update). Servers on a stable version are only offered stable releases;
drafts and non-SemVer tags are ignored. The check runs on a daemon
thread with 5 s timeouts, can be turned off with check-for-updates, and
a failed check is logged as such instead of 'up to date'.

ci: publish a GitHub release with the jars for each v* tag

ci: build all modules and run the tests on every push and PR

docs: changelog and issue status for priorities 3 and 4

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: let admins turn off command aliases (upstream #35)

Short aliases like /l and /tab clash with other plugins (local chat).
New option disabled-command-aliases (config version 7, empty by default
so nothing changes) removes them from GeyserExtras' own commands and, on
Spigot, from the server command map, handing the alias to another plugin
that also registered it. /geyserextras cannot be disabled.

Also registers /playerlist, the Spigot command name from plugin.yml,

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: GELocale works without downloaded language files (upstream #57)

Covers the crash behind upstream #57, fixed in dc35986.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: accept .zip optional packs and skip broken ones (upstream #60)

optionalpacks/ only picked up .mcpack files while Geyser's own packs
folder also takes .zip. Accept both (case-insensitive), load them in a
stable order, and skip a pack that fails to load with a warning instead
of aborting the whole resource loading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: write preference files atomically and in order (upstream #61)

Each save started a new thread that opened the file with FileWriter
(truncating it) before deciding whether to write or delete it. Saves
racing each other, or a shutdown between the truncation and the write,
left empty or half-written files, and the player came back with default
settings and no selected packs. Saves now serialize on the calling
thread and go through a single writer thread that writes a temporary
file and moves it into place (or deletes the file when the preferences
equal the defaults); auto-reconnect on shutdown waits up to 5 s for
pending writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: try to show GeyserExtras settings in the Bedrock settings screen with Floodgate

With Floodgate installed the settings were never offered in the game's
settings screen (players only got a toast) because on some platforms the
form classes come from Floodgate's copy of Cumulus and Geyser's form
cache rejects them with a LinkageError. Whether that happens depends on
class loading, so try the Geyser path and, on the first LinkageError,
log one explanation and fall back to the toast for the rest of the run.
The unconditional startup warning about it is removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: keep the player list menu in sync with the Java tab list

- Players that left stayed in the menu forever: handle
  ClientboundPlayerInfoRemovePacket (also how proxies clear the list when
  switching servers).
- Entries are created on ADD_PLAYER and each action only updates its own
  field, like the Java client; an update without ADD_PLAYER no longer
  stores a profile-less entry, and such entries get a fallback name
  instead of throwing when the menu opens (likely cause of upstream #43,
  #53).
- The entries are shared between packet translation and form building,
  so access is now synchronized and the menu works on a copy.
- The menu follows the server's list order (UPDATE_LIST_ORDER).
- A LinkageError (extension jar inside Geyser-Spigot, upstream #54, #56,
  #69) disables the player list once with an explanation instead of
  failing every player list packet.

docs: track the status of upstream issues and fork fixes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: default players' cooldown display to Geyser's cooldown-type

New players (and preference files without a value) got CROSSHAIR even
when the server set cooldown-type: hotbar in Geyser. Use Geyser's
configured value as the default; saved player choices are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: stop deleting packs from Geyser's packs folder

Every start removed GeyserExtrasPack.mcpack and GeyserOptionalPack.mcpack
from Geyser's own packs folder, silently undoing an admin's choice. Warn
about them instead (the GeyserExtrasPack copy is skipped by UUID anyway,
the deprecated optional pack may conflict with the integrated pack).
Cleanup of GeyserExtras' own cache folder is unchanged.

Based on h4-hub/GeyserExtras@a352538 by h4-hub (MIT).

docs: changelog for shutdown, tick and Velocity kick fixes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: isolate player tick failures and stop ticking disconnected players

- A null dimension (before the Java server sent it, e.g. on the code of
  conduct screen) threw on every tick (upstream #67); the fog check now
  skips it.
- Ticks go through ExtrasPlayer.safeTick(), which logs the first failure
  per player instead of letting it escape: on Spigot one failing player
  aborted the tick loop for everyone, on the extension it silently
  cancelled the task, on Bungee it stopped the self-rescheduling tick.
- Disconnected players stop ticking. Velocity never cancelled its
  repeating task and Bungee rescheduled forever, keeping every past
  session in memory; the extension added one more fixed-rate task on
  each tick rate change. These are likely causes of the proxy memory
  leak reported in upstream #32.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(velocity): reconnect only the kicked player, not every Bedrock player

The KickedFromServerEvent listener called autoReconnectAll(), so any
player kicked from any backend server (ban, anti-cheat, full server)
transferred every Bedrock player on the proxy. Reconnect only the kicked
player, and only when they are a Bedrock player and auto-reconnect is on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: never throw while disabling, even after a failed start

onDisable called CORE.autoReconnectAll() and PacketEvents terminate()
unconditionally, so when the start had failed (CORE null, config never
loaded, PacketEvents never initialised) disabling threw as well and
hid the original error (upstream #47). Shutdown and reload steps now go
through GeyserExtras.runSafely, which logs a failure instead of
propagating it; autoReconnectAll tolerates a missing config and one
player's failed reconnect no longer stops the others; PacketEvents is
only terminated when it was initialised; the Spigot, Bungee and
Velocity listeners ignore events while the core is missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: changelog for the security, command delay and null guard fixes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: create the player maps before any packet can be translated

connections and javaConnections were assigned at the end of the
GeyserExtras constructor, after the extension had already registered
its packet injectors and run the network-bound cache setup, so packets
in that window failed with 'GE.connections is null' and desynced the
player (issues #29, #76). Initialize both maps at declaration and guard
the join and emote event handlers against unknown players.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: fall back to Geyser when a packet's player is not tracked

Every injector dereferenced ExtrasPlayer.get(session) without a check,
so a packet arriving before the player was created or after it was
removed threw inside Geyser's translator and was lost ('Could not
translate packet', issues #36, #54). Each injector now behaves exactly
like Geyser when the player is unknown: Bedrock interactions, pick
block, settings and commands go to super (the inventory still opens,
unknown players' commands reach the server), and our extra bookkeeping
is skipped.

Based on OneCraftES/GeyserExtrasPlus@7114bb5 by Undecimer (MIT), with
the interact and command cases changed to call super instead of
dropping the packet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: delay GeyserExtras commands typed by Bedrock players

The Bedrock client silently discards forms that arrive while its chat
screen is still open, so /geyserextras typed in chat often showed
nothing (seen on the test server) while the inventory double-tap worked.
Run Bedrock players' GeyserExtras commands bedrock-command-delay-ms
later on their Geyser event loop, on every platform (Spigot, Bungee,
Velocity, extension). Java players are unaffected.

Based on paper0319/GeyserExtras@35d1877 by paper0319 (MIT), which
applied a fixed 500 ms delay on Velocity only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(config): add bedrock-command-delay-ms and fix the config version

Add the bedrock-command-delay-ms option (default 500) and bump the
config to version 6 so existing files get it written. This also fixes
LATEST_VERSION, which was 4 while a 4->5 transformation existed: configs
migrated from older versions ended up at 5 and were rewritten on every
start, and configs already at 4 never dropped enable-custom-cooldown.
Migration is now testable (ConfigLoader.migrate) and covered by tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(security): validate client skin data before writing it to disk

With enable-skin-saving on, SkinSaver used the client-controlled SkinId
and CapeId as folder names, so a modified Bedrock client could use
'../' to create folders and write skin.png / skin.geometry.json (with
content it controls) anywhere the server can write. It also allocated
images of client-declared size, letting a client exhaust memory, and an
image shorter than width*height*4 threw outside the IOException catch.

Keep plain ids (letters, digits, . _ -, at most 64 chars) as folder
names and hash anything else, check the resolved folder stays inside
skins/ or capes/, cap images at 512x512 and require enough pixel data,
cap written JSON at 2 MiB, and catch runtime errors so a bad skin only
logs a warning.

Surveys the 34 GitHub forks of GeyserExtras plus Modrinth (the
geyser-extras-fork project does not exist there: 404) and classifies
each extra commit as already done, to adopt, to adapt or rejected, with
licenses checked (all MIT). Also records security issues found in the
skin saver (client-controlled path segments and image size) that no
fork fixes.

A form element that threw while applying a response (wrong index, type

form title and element index (stack trace in debug mode), and still run
onSubmit. In debug mode also log every custom form response, queued
emote links and the player's links/actions when an emote arrives.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: link emote bindings to a recorded emote

Geyser 2.11+ discards the Bedrock emote list, so the wheel slot of an
emote is unknown and the Emote 1-4 bindings could never trigger. Each
binding now remembers a specific emote: in the bindings menu the player
ticks 'Link an emote', saves, then performs the emote once; from then on
that emote runs the bound action wherever it sits in the wheel. An emote
triggers at most one binding, linking emotes are not broadcast to emote
chat, and the menu shows the currently linked emote.

The links are stored in the player's preferences (emoteLinks); files
written by older versions load with no links. The unused slot-based
emotesList is removed.

feat: ship translations for strings added by the fork

GeyserExtras downloads its language files from the GeyserExtras/data
repository, which the fork cannot update. Strings missing there are now
looked up in lang/cpmc/<locale>.json inside the jar (same language,
then English, then the key). English and French are provided. GELocale
also no longer throws when no en_US file was downloaded.

fix: stop sharing binding and pack collections between players

copyFrom() copied the remappable action map, the selected packs and the
subpacks by reference. Every player without a preferences file got
DEFAULT's own collections, so a binding or pack chosen by one of them
applied to all of them (and to new players), and save() then saw no
difference with the defaults and deleted the player's file instead of
writing it. Copy the collections (null-safe) instead.

Geyser 2.12 freezes the built-in Java entity registry right after

GeyserPostInitializeEvent threw IllegalStateException ('must not be
frozen to register new entries') and aborted the rest of GeyserExtras'
post-init handler when enable-block-display-workaround was on. Register
it from GeyserDefineEntitiesEvent instead; if that is not possible (e.g.
GeyserExtras started too late) log a warning and keep the workaround off
instead of throwing.

Action.OPEN_INVENTORY copies Geyser's BedrockInteractTranslator logic
but predates nautilus mounts. It runs for every inventory press while
the double-tap shortcut is on (the default), so a Bedrock player riding
a saddled nautilus got the player inventory path instead of the mount

The sound injectors reimplemented Geyser's translators for all sounds
whenever combat sounds were enabled, so Geyser changes were lost: since
2.11 Geyser pairs brush sounds with dust particles (#6620) and plays

fix: do not Base64-decode skin data twice

BedrockClientData decodes SkinData, SkinResourcePatch and
SkinGeometryData itself (StringToByteDeserializer, as Geyser's
SkinManager relies on). Decoding again, as adapted in the 2.11 port,
throws IllegalArgumentException on the raw RGBA bytes, which is not
caught and would abort SessionJoinEvent handling when skin saving is
enabled.

Player preference files written before Geyser 2.11 store TITLE or

passed to Geyser's preferences cache and break the cooldown menu. Map
TITLE to CROSSHAIR, ACTIONBAR to HOTBAR and anything unknown or null to
CROSSHAIR (the previous default).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

port: handle Geyser discarding the Bedrock emote list

Since Geyser commit 864c62cd (server-side Bedrock emotes) the codec
ignores EmoteListPacket, so the emote list injector never received any
emote and every emote hit the 'not in emote list' early return: emote
chat to Java players stopped working. Remove the injector and treat an
emote whose wheel slot is unknown as unbound, which restores emote chat.

the lookup is also bounded to the four emote bindings instead of
indexing every Remappable.

ajoshi1education/allenamento.readme:
# Allenamento: Italian B2 → C1

An adaptive Italian trainer for an English speaker at about B2 who is aiming for C1.

**Main mode, the path (Percorso):** 10 units in learning order (B2 consolidation, then C1). Each concept is a short lesson made of bite-size cards with quick checks, then a practice round (which also brings back earlier mistakes that are due), then a harder challenge. Each unit has games and a checkpoint at the end, and each of the two sections ends with a **mock CEFR exam** (B2, C1): reading, listening (two plays, as in the real exam), grammar, vocabulary, writing and speaking, scored per section with a 70% pass mark (`js/games/exam.js`, `content/games/exam-*.json`). Steps unlock in order, but you can start any step anyway or "jump ahead" by passing a unit checkpoint. XP, a daily goal and a streak keep track. The order lives in `content/path.json`.

**Convos:** spoken conversations with a tutor (`content/convos/`). The tutor speaks, you answer out loud (or type). Each reply is scored on task (target structures), grammar (detectors for typical spoken mistakes, `js/core/speechcheck.js`), fluency (words per minute) and clarity (how confidently the recogniser understood you, a proxy for pronunciation). There is also a "repeat after me" drill. Mistakes go to the Error Bank. 46 conversations, including finance/banking at work, sport (football, cricket), food & wine, travel, film and music, and Italian history. In the dock you can change the tutor speed (🐢 / 1× / 🐇) and hide the tutor text until you have answered, for pure listening practice.

**Interface:** menus and buttons are in Italian; grammar explanations and feedback stay in English.

**Audio modes** (top-bar button): 🔇 silent, 🔊 questions and answers read aloud, 🎤 also answer by microphone (Chrome/Edge). Pick voices and test the microphone in Settings.

**Ripasso:** retest due mistakes in new sentences, and review flashcards.

**Esplora (free mode):** everything below, in any order:

- **Learn**: 61 lessons across the B2→C1 curriculum.
- **Play / Test**: 42 games linked to those lessons, including culture and history readings and listenings, and **Dettato** (dictation: hear a sentence from the course, write it or say it back).
- **Verbi**: a conjugation trainer for 91 verbs (pick the tenses; verbs you get wrong come back more) and searchable conjugation tables (`content/verbs.json`, `js/core/verbs.js`).
- **Vocabulary**: a 517-entry library (including finance, sport, food & wine, travel, culture) plus spaced-repetition flashcards.
- **Google Translate import**: turns your translation history into flashcards, exercises and games.
- **Error Bank**: a permanent record of your mistakes, retested until mastered.
- **Progress**: per-skill progress, recommended next steps, achievements and weekly challenges.

Everything works as silent text, so you can use it in public. Audio (text-to-speech) and speaking (speech recognition) are used when the browser supports them.

## Live site

On your phone: open Settings (⚙️) on a computer and scan the QR code, or type the address below. Then install it: iPhone → Safari → Share → *Add to Home Screen*; Android → Chrome → ⋮ → *Install app*.


**https://ajoshi1education.github.io/allenamento/**: works on any PC or phone (Chrome or Edge for voice). After changing anything, publish the update with `npm run deploy` (it builds and pushes to the `gh-pages` branch). Progress is stored in each browser: use Settings → Download backup / Restore to move it, or set up the optional sync.

## Run it locally

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/serve.ps1 -Port 8010
```

Open http://localhost:8010. No install is needed. Your data is saved in the browser's IndexedDB database. In **Settings** you can download a backup file and restore it on any device.

## How it works

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| Curriculum map (61 concept IDs, CEFR) | `content/curriculum.json` |
| Lessons + exercises per unit | `content/units/*.json` |
| Games (detective, dialogue, gauntlet, builder, duel, reading, listening, debate) | `content/games/*.json` |
| Vocabulary library | `content/vocab/core.json` |
| Authoring rules for content | `content/SCHEMA.md` |
| Answer checker (alternatives, accents, typos, known mistakes, writing checklists) | `js/core/evaluate.js` |
| Error Bank rules (capture, mastery, retest in new contexts, patterns) | `js/core/errors.js` |
| Spaced repetition | `js/core/srs.js` |
| Placement test | `js/core/diagnostic.js` |
| Google Translate parsers | `js/core/importer.js` |
| Progress, achievements, challenges | `js/core/progress.js` |
| Database (IndexedDB) + backup | `js/db.js`, `js/store.js` |
| Optional sync (Supabase) | `js/sync.js`, `supabase/schema.sql` |
| Optional AI helper (off by default) | `netlify/functions/ai.mjs`, `js/ai.js` |

**Mastery rule:** an Error Bank entry only counts as mastered after correct answers on 3 different days, 2 of them in a different sentence from the original. A correct answer on the same day as the mistake doesn't count. Mastered entries still come back for occasional revision, and a new slip reopens them.

## Checks

```
npm test
```

```
node scripts/validate-content.mjs
```

The validator runs every accepted answer through the real answer checker. It also confirms that every "known mistake" is graded wrong, that model answers pass their own writing checklist, that IDs are unique and links resolve, and it reports curriculum coverage.

## Getting your Google Translate history in

There's no API for personal history. These are the routes that work:

1. **translate.google.com → Saved → Export to Google Sheets**, then *File › Download › CSV*. This has both the phrase and its translation. Star history items first to move them into Saved.
2. **Google Takeout → My Activity → Translate** (JSON or HTML). This usually contains only the text you looked up.
3. Paste lines into the Translate tab.

## Deploy (free)

The app deploys to Netlify like the cricket site: `ne

Ander-tsx/horror-game.readme:
# Ghost vs Jason — Halloween Kombat

Juego de peleas retro en pixel art (estilo Mortal Kombat) hecho en Unity para la campaña de becados de videojuegos
de Halloween. Gore pixel art, desmembramiento, FINISH HIM / FATALITY, filtro CRT de maquinita y 6 escenarios.

## Jugar

- **En el navegador:** https://ander-tsx.github.io/horror-game/ (no hay que instalar nada).
- **Windows / Mac:** descarga el zip de la última versión en
  [Releases](https://github.com/Ander-tsx/horror-game/releases), descomprime y abre `GhostVsJason`.
  - En Mac, la primera vez: clic derecho sobre la app → *Abrir* (no está firmada).

## Controles

| Acción | Jugador 1 | Jugador 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Moverse / saltar / agacharse | `A` `D` / `W` / `S` | Flechas |
| Golpe | `F` | `K` |
| Golpe fuerte | `G` | `L` |
| Patada | `H` | `;` (Ñ en teclado español) |
| Agarre | `R` | `P` |
| Especial | Adelante + `G` | Adelante + `L` |
| Patada giratoria | Atrás + `H` | Atrás + `;` |
| Bloquear | Mantener atrás (abajo + atrás = bloqueo bajo) | igual |

- Combos: `F F F` (jab, cross, uppercut), `G G`, `H H`.
- Al bajar la vida se pierden extremidades: sin un brazo, sin brazos, en una pierna o arrastrándose sin piernas.
- **FINISH HIM:** fuerte = decapitación, patada = en trozos, golpe o agarre = explota en mil pedazos.
- `Esc` pausa, `F1` activa o desactiva el filtro CRT, `Enter` o `F` para confirmar en menús.

### Mando (gamepad)

Se puede jugar con un mando (Xbox, PlayStation o genérico) junto al teclado: uno con mando y otro con teclado.

| Acción | Mando (Xbox / PlayStation) |
|---|---|
| Moverse / saltar / agacharse | Stick izquierdo o cruceta |
| Golpe | `X` / `□` |
| Golpe fuerte | `Y` / `△` |
| Patada | `A` / `✕` |
| Agarre | `B` / `○` o `RB` / `R1` |
| Pausa | `Start` / `Options` o `Back` / `Share` |

- En menús: `A` / `✕` o `Start` confirma, `B` / `○` regresa.
- Contra el CPU el mando siempre es el Jugador 1. En **2 JUGADORES**, la opción **MANDO** del menú principal elige
  si el mando juega como Jugador 1 (el otro usa flechas) o Jugador 2 (el otro usa WASD). Con dos mandos, el segundo
  toma el otro lado.

## Abrir el proyecto

1. Instala **Unity 6000.6.4f1** con Unity Hub (con soporte WebGL / Windows / Mac si quieres compilar).
2. `git clone https://github.com/Ander-tsx/horror-game.git` y ábrelo desde Unity Hub.
3. Abre `Assets/Scenes/Game.unity` y dale Play. En el objeto `Game`, `quickFight` salta los menús.

Compilar desde la terminal (con el editor cerrado):

```sh
"/Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/6000.6.4f1/Unity.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity" -batchmode -quit -projectPath . \
  -executeMethod GameBuilds.BuildAll
```

## Arte y pipeline

Los personajes y escenarios se generaron con generación de imágenes de Codex sobre plantillas
(`Tools/art_src/templates`) y se procesaron con los scripts de `Tools/pixelart` (ver `CLAUDE.md`). Las imágenes
fuente originales (cientos de MB) no están en el repo: se descargan como `codex-source-art.zip` desde Releases y se
descomprimen en `Tools/art_src/` para volver a procesarlas.

## Créditos

- Sonidos de impacto e interfaz: [Kenney](https://kenney.nl) (CC0), ver `Assets/Audio/Licenses/`.
- Algunos efectos y la voz de "FATALITY": ElevenLabs. Música chiptune sintetizada en `Tools/audio/chiptune.py`.
- Ghost y Jason son personajes inspirados en franquicias de terror existentes; este es un proyecto de fans sin fines
  comerciales.

Snenjih/cp2077-archive-xl-2.5.readme:
# ArchiveXL

ArchiveXL is a modding tool that allows you to load custom resources without touching original game files,
thus allowing multiple mods to expand same resources without conflicts.

With the mod you can:

- Load custom entity factories (necessary for item additions)
- Add localization texts that can be used in scripts, resources and TweakDB
- Edit existing localization texts without overwriting original resources
- Override submeshes visibility of entity parts
- Add visual tags to a clothing item
- Spawn widgets from any library without registering dependencies

## Getting Started

### Compatibility

- Cyberpunk 2077 2.31
- [redscript](https://github.com/jac3km4/redscript) 0.5.31+

### Installation

1. Install requirements:
   - [RED4ext](https://docs.red4ext.com/getting-started/installing-red4ext) 1.29.0+
2. Extract the release archive `ArchiveXL-x.x.x.zip` into the Cyberpunk 2077 directory.

## Documentation

- [Dynamic appearances](https://github.com/psiberx/cp2077-archive-xl/wiki#dynamic-appearances)
- [Body types](https://github.com/psiberx/cp2077-archive-xl/wiki#body-types)
- [Appearance suffixes](https://github.com/psiberx/cp2077-archive-xl/wiki#appearance-suffixes)
- [Components overrides](https://github.com/psiberx/cp2077-archive-xl/wiki#components-overrides)
- [Visual tags](https://github.com/psiberx/cp2077-archive-xl/wiki#visual-tags)
- [Extending resources](https://github.com/psiberx/cp2077-archive-xl/wiki#extending-resources)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

macOS: Test allocator readiness through the vault pool registry

The readiness test on non-Windows was "CRTTISystem::Get() exists", which
does not say whether the allocators are up, and Get() creates the system on
first use. Use the same test as Windows instead: the PoolEngine pool is
registered in the vault's pool registry.

Vault::Get() cannot be resolved on macOS, so the vault is read from the
game's exported PoolStorageProxy<PoolEngine>::GetAllocator(), found with
dlsym. That storage is set up when the game image loads, its allocator is
the DefaultAllocator at the start of the vault, and the getter only reads a
static, so it never allocates and cannot fail early.

Windows side unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

macOS: Build the support header without the Windows API

The header includes <libloaderapi.h> and <minwindef.h>, reads the Vault
pool registry to tell that the game is ready, and finds the plugin
folder through GetModuleFileNameW. None of that exists on macOS.

On non-Windows builds the header now includes <dlfcn.h>, uses the
presence of the RTTI system as the readiness test (the macOS SDK has no
Vault global), and takes the folder from the image that holds
GetModulePath, found with dladdr. The code under _WIN32 is the code that
was there before, so the Windows build is unchanged.

Merge pull request #22 from IvanShift/fix/appearance-map-shared-lock

Don't mutate the appearances map under a shared lock

Don't mutate the appearances map under a shared lock

GetAppearanceDefinition holds a shared_lock, but its fallback calls
operator[], which inserts the {} key when absent. That insert can rehash:
allocate a new bucket array, copy, and free the old one - while other
threads are concurrently walking the same map under the same shared lock.

It is reached from PatchPackageResults on the OnEntityPackageLoad
streaming jobs, which run concurrently for many entities, so concurrent
callers are the normal case. Observed as a wild pointer read inside
hopscotch_hash's rehash bucket-copy loop.

The fallback only needs to read the default entry, so a plain find keeps
the whole function read-only and safe under the shared lock.

Lunar-feedmob/omamori-hanafuda.desc: 御守花札：日本庭院主题的花札记忆配对小游戏
Lunar-feedmob/omamori-hanafuda.readme:
# 御守花札

日本庭院主题的花札记忆配对小游戏。记住花札的位置，在步数用尽前翻出成对的两张，沿着四季走完八处庭院。适配手机竖屏。

在线游玩：https://lunar-feedmob.github.io/omamori-hanafuda/

## 玩法

- 开局所有牌亮出几秒，记住位置。
- 一次翻两张算一步；相同便留下，不同就合上。
- 在步数用尽前配完，点亮下一处庭院。
- 「重新看牌」让未配的牌再亮一瞬，不耗步数。
- 难度三档：悠闲（不计步数）、标准、挑战。
- 连续配对会盖下朱印：三連多给一步，五連多一次回看，七連下一阵花吹雪。
- 翻错后点任意处，牌立刻盖回，不用等待。
- 第一次进入庭院前，会先进「练习庭」：四张牌演示看牌、翻牌、回看三件事，随时可以跳过；设置里可以再看一遍。
- 桌面端（宽于 960px）左侧是信息栏，右侧是牌阵；方向键选牌，空格或回车翻开，R 再看一眼。
- 支持震动的手机（如安卓 Chrome）在配对、翻错、连击和通关时会轻震，可在设置里关闭。
- 设置里可以清除全部进度（保留主题等设置）；主页底部的「清空记录，重新开始」会清掉浏览器里的全部游戏记录和设置，并刷新页面。

## 试玩统计

设置 → 游玩统计：按庭院记录开局、通关、失败、平均步数、回看、翻错和用时，以及新手演示看完或跳过的次数、主题切换次数。数据只存在本机，可以一键复制成表格，方便试玩时收集反馈。

## 收集

- **花札图鉴**：完整 48 张，附寓意、介绍、收集日期，以及「役」的进度。
- **御守帖**：48 枚御守徽章，获得即点亮，未获得只显示剪影。同一枚收得越多越华丽：布面 → 金线（3 枚）→ 満願（6 枚，金线织锦加流苏），升级时会有提示。
- **朱印帖**：三連、五連、七連、無垢、一目、八景、全札。

## 主题

七种主题共用同一套玩法和布局，每个主题有自己的卡背、牌桌、转场和一组乐器（季节决定音阶），切换时不会打断正在进行的一局。设置里可以分别调音乐和音效的音量。

| 分组 | 主题 | 主页 | 推荐卡面 | 声音 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 传统和风 | 浮世锦绘 | 按季节展示广重《名所江户百景》的版画海报 | 彩绘 | 三味线，通关敲拍子木 |
| 传统和风 | 京都和纸 | 文库本封面，按季节换神坂雪佳的画 | 墨绘 | 琴与笙，翻页声 |
| 传统和风 | 砂纹石庭 | 一圈砂纹，一块石 | 墨染 | 钵铃与尺八，风声 |
| 节令生活 | 灯火夜祭 | 广重「两国花火」上的灯笼与摊位 | 朱缘 | 篠笛与太鼓，通关远处烟火 |
| 节令生活 | 旅行手账 | 纸页、印章集、北斋草花小稿 | 剪纸 | 八音盒，盖章声 |
| 动画漫画 | 四叠青春 | 四叠半杂志页 | 剪纸 | 轻快拨弦与拍手 |
| 动画漫画 | 昭和漫画 | 以《北斋漫画》为刊头的连载目次 | 网点 | 玩具钢琴，唱片底噪，连击「咚」 |

## 本地运行

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 打开 http://localhost:8000
```

`tools/make-decks.mjs` 用来重新生成三套原创牌面：`node tools/make-decks.mjs cards`。

## 素材致谢

- 花札「彩绘」(`cards/classic`)、「墨染」(`cards/sumi`)、「朱缘」(`cards/shu`)：Louie Mantia 绘制，后两套另有すけじょ参与；来自 [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:SVG_Hanafuda)，[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)，未作修改。
- 花札「花图」(`cards/hwatu`)：韩式 Hwatu，Marcus Richert 以 Louie Mantia 的花札为基础制作，Spenĉjo 整理上传；[Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:SVG_Hwatu)，CC BY-SA 4.0，未作修改。文件按日式月份重命名（韩式的十一月桐、十二月柳已对调）。
- 花札「墨绘」「剪纸」「网点」(`cards/ink`、`cards/kirie`、`cards/tone`) 与御守徽章：本项目原创，由程序绘制；御守花纹取自传统和柄。
- 主页插图（`art/`）：神坂雪佳《百々世草》（1909–10）、葛饰北斋《北斋漫画》、歌川广重《名所江户百景》中的「两国花火」「龟户梅屋敷」「大桥阿宅骤雨」「月之岬」「浅草金龙山」（1856–58），均为公有领域作品，图像来自[芝加哥艺术博物馆开放馆藏](https://www.artic.edu/open-access)（CC0），仅缩放与裁切取景；纸纹为 [ambientCG Paper006](https://ambientcg.com/view?id=Paper006)（CC0）。
- 纸牌音效（`sfx/`）：Kenney「[Casino Audio](https://kenney.nl/assets/casino-audio)」，CC0，已转码为 MP3。
- 琴声、风铃、尺八与环境音：[Tone.js](https://github.com/Tonejs/Tone.js)（MIT）实时合成。
- 落花特效：[canvas-confetti](https://github.com/catdad/canvas-confetti)（ISC）。
- 字体：每个主题两到三种。日文显示字体 Shippori Mincho B1、Zen Old Mincho、Shippori Mincho、Kaisei Decol、Klee One、Yusei Magic、Zen Antique；中文 Noto Serif SC、Noto Sans SC；点缀用 Yuji Syuku、ZCOOL XiaoWei、ZCOOL KuaiLe（SIL OFL 1.1），经 Google Fonts 提供。
- 俳句：服部嵐雪、松尾芭蕉、山口素堂、与謝蕪村的作品（公有领域），中文译文为本项目所作。

xsota/filegarden.readme:
# FileGarden

**Watch your code grow.**

FileGarden is a terminal app that shows files being created, modified, deleted and renamed in a
directory as it happens. Start it in one terminal, run Claude Code, Codex, an editor or a build in
another, and watch the tree come alive: new files glow green, edits flash yellow, deletions turn
red and fade out, moves shine blue. A defrag-style **Activity Grid** gives every file a block that
lights up when it changes.

![FileGarden demo: files appear, change and disappear while an AI agent works](docs/demo.gif)

- **No integration needed.** FileGarden watches the file system, so it works with any AI agent,
  editor or tool, with or without Git.
- **Read-only.** It reads directory listings and file metadata only. It never opens file
  contents, never writes, and never touches the network.
- **Light.** A single static binary. ~0% CPU when idle, about 13 MB of memory for 10,000 files.
- **Two modes.** The default *calm* mode is made for leaving open next to your work. *Game*
  mode (`--mode game`, or `x`) adds particles, floating points, combos, levels and achievements.

## Install

### Prebuilt binaries

Download the archive for your platform from the [Releases page](../../releases), extract it and
put `filegarden` (`filegarden.exe` on Windows) somewhere on your `PATH`.

| Platform              | Archive                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Linux x64             | `filegarden-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`  |
| Linux ARM64           | `filegarden-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `filegarden-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`       |
| macOS (Intel)         | `filegarden-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`        |
| Windows x64           | `filegarden-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`        |

Linux binaries are statically linked and run on any distribution. On macOS, a binary downloaded
through a browser may need `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine filegarden` before the first run.

### From source

Requires Rust 1.84 or newer.

```bash
cargo install --path .        # from a checkout
```

## Usage

```bash
filegarden                    # watch the current directory
filegarden watch .            # same
filegarden watch ~/projects/my-app
filegarden watch . --exclude "*.log" --exclude tmp/
filegarden watch . --poll     # network drives, WSL /mnt/*, some containers
filegarden watch . --no-animation
filegarden demo               # simulated AI-agent session; touches no files
filegarden watch . --mode game  # game mode
filegarden demo --mode game   # ...the demo as a game
```

The screen has four parts:

- **File tree** (left): the directory, updated live. A marker shows what happened to each file
  (`+` created, `~` modified, `-` deleted, `→` renamed) and `×N` counts repeated edits. Changed
  files flash, then fade back to normal over about two seconds. Directories glow softly when
  something inside them changes, and collapsed directories open automatically so you can see the
  change. In **follow** mode (the default) the view scrolls to keep the latest change in sight.
- **Activity Grid** (top right): one block per file, defrag style. Blocks keep their position;
  when the grid is full, a newly active file takes over the block that has been quiet the
  longest. Files that change often stay faintly warm, so hot spots become visible over time.
- **Statistics** (bottom right): current file and directory counts, created / modified /
  deleted / renamed since start, events in the last 60 seconds with a one-minute sparkline, and
  elapsed time. Files present at startup are not counted as created.
- **Activity feed** (bottom): the latest changes with time stamps. Consecutive saves of the same
  file are merged into one line (`×3`).

On small terminals the feed, statistics and grid are dropped in that order; the footer then shows
compact counters.

### Game mode

Start with `--mode game` (or press `x` at any time) to turn your agent's work into an arcade game:

![FileGarden game mode: combos, FEVER, level ups and achievements](docs/fx.gif)

- lit grid cells burst into sparks, and deleted entries **shatter** letter by letter and fall
  out of the tree;
- every change scores points (`+100` create, `+25` modify, `+75` delete, `+150` rename, more
  for directories), floating up from the file that changed;
- changes less than 2.5 s apart build a **combo** that multiplies points, with NICE! / GREAT! /
  AWESOME!! / UNSTOPPABLE!!! banners and rainbow **FEVER** borders from 50×;
- levels, LEVEL UP fireworks, screen shake on big bursts and directory deletions, and
  achievement toasts (Seedling, Reaper, Demolition, Marathon, ...).

Score, level and combo are shown in the header. `x` switches between calm and game mode while
running. Game mode is unavailable with `--no-animation`.

### Keys

| Key                   | Action                                  |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `q` / `Esc` / `Ctrl+C`| Quit                                    |
| `↑` `↓` (`k` `j`)     | Move the selection (leaves follow mode) |
| `PgUp` `PgDn`         | Move by a page                          |
| `Home` `End`          | First / last entry                      |
| `←` `→` (`h` `l`)     | Collapse / expand a directory           |
| `Enter`               | Toggle a directory                      |
| `f`                   | Follow the latest change again          |
| `Space`               | Pause / resume the display              |
| `r`                   | Rescan the directory                    |
| `a`                   | All files / only files that changed     |
| `x`                   | Switch calm / game mode                 |
| `?`                   | Help                                    |

Pausing freezes the picture, including fades. Changes keep being recorded and appear when you
resume.

### Options

```
filegarden [watch] [PATH] [OPTIONS]

  -e, --ex

maxihan1/control_cli.readme:
# control_cli

Unity 게임을 자동화 테스트로 조작하는 SDK 와 CLI.

- **SDK** (Unity UPM 패키지) — QA 빌드에서만 폰 안 `127.0.0.1` 에 포트를 열고, 오브젝트 트리 읽기 · 찾기 · 누르기 · 끌기 · 글자 넣기 · 속성 읽기를 받는다. 터치는 빌드 때 이름이 같은 가짜 `Input` 으로 바꿔치기한다
- **CLI** — appium-cli 꼴. snapshot(줄인 트리 + 스크린샷) → ref → 액션, 액션마다 케이스에 붙일 코드 한 줄(`Ran:`)을 찍는다. 폰은 디바이스 팜 게임 명령 주소 또는 USB `adb forward` 로 잇는다
- **라이브러리** — CLI 와 같은 드라이버(`Game`)와 두 길(`farmLink` · `usbLink`). test_platform kit 이 CLI 를 띄우지 않고 쓴다

0단계 실측 결과는 [docs/step0.md](docs/step0.md).

## 게임에 넣기 (QA 빌드만)

게임 저장소에는 SDK 를 넣지 않는다. QA 빌드 잡에서 Unity 를 켜기 전에 한 번 돌린다.

```bash
git clone -q https://github.com/maxihan1/control_cli.git /tmp/control_cli
git -C /tmp/control_cli checkout -q <커밋>
npm --prefix /tmp/control_cli ci          # 받으면서 CLI 를 빌드한다
node /tmp/control_cli/dist/main.js instrument <Unity 프로젝트 폴더> --ref <커밋>
```

`npx github:maxihan1/control_cli` 는 쓰지 않는다 — npm 10 이 git 패키지를 npx 로 받을 때 「GitFetcher requires an Arborist constructor」로 멈춘다(GitHub Actions 에서 확인).

1. `Packages/manifest.json` 에 SDK 패키지를 `--ref` 로 고정해 더한다(없으면 `main`)
2. `Assets/` · `Packages/`(내장 패키지) 아래 asmdef 의 `references` 에 `ControlCli.Input` 을 더한다 — 에디터 전용 · `noEngineReferences` 는 건너뛴다. asmdef 없는 스크립트(Assembly-CSharp)는 자동으로 참조한다
3. `namespace` 안에 `using UnityEngine;` 을 둔 파일 · `namespace UnityEngine.*` 안의 파일은 `UnityEngine.Input` 이 먼저 잡혀 가짜 터치를 못 본다 — 경고로 알려 준다
4. 깨진 asmdef 가 있으면 파일 이름을 알리고 아무것도 바꾸지 않는다

그리고 **QA 빌드 스크립트가 정의 심볼 `CONTROL_CLI` 를 더한다** — 없으면 SDK 코드가 빌드에 아예 안 들어간다. Release 빌드는 손대지 않으면 된다.

가짜 `Input` 은 `UnityEngine.Input` 의 멤버를 다 감싼다(펜 · `mousePositionDelta` 는 빠짐). 터치만 가짜를 섞고 나머지는 그대로 넘긴다. `touchSupported` 는 늘 `true` 다.
알려진 한계 — `Assets/Plugins` 의 스크립트(Assembly-CSharp-firstpass)도 가짜 `Input` 을 보게 되어, 빠진 멤버를 쓰면 QA 빌드에서만 컴파일이 깨진다. 그런 게임이 오면 그 멤버를 더한다.

## CLI

```bash
npm i -D github:maxihan1/control_cli#v0.1.0
npx control-cli help
```

### 루프 — 디바이스 팜

```bash
export PLATFORM_APPIUM_URL=http://<팜>:4723/wd/hub PLATFORM_APPIUM_TOKEN=pat_…   # 팜이 인증을 켰을 때만 토큰
npx control-cli hold --minutes 30                 # 빈 폰 하나를 잡는다(--udid 로 고를 수도)
npx control-cli open --app https://…/qa.apk       # 잡은 폰에 깔고 켠 뒤 게임이 답할 때까지 기다려 첫 화면을 찍는다
npx control-cli snapshot                          # - Snapshot: .control-cli/default-….yml · - Screenshot: ….png
npx control-cli type e2 qa_user01                 # Ran: await game.type('IdInput', 'qa_user01')
npx control-cli click e3                          # Ran: await game.click('LoginButton')
npx control-cli wait e5 --text 아이디는           # Ran: await game.waitFor('StatusText', { text: '아이디는' })
npx control-cli close                             # Appium 세션을 닫는다
npx control-cli release                           # 폰을 놓는다 — 팜이 깐 게임 · 데이터를 지운다
```

화면 파일 한 줄이 오브젝트 하나다. 글자 · 버튼이 아니고 갈림길도 아닌 외길 오브젝트는 빠진다. ref 는 마지막 화면에서만 쓴다.

```
# 장면 Boot · 화면 2400×1080
- LoginView [ref=e1]
  - InputField IdInput "" [ref=e2]
  - Button LoginButton [ref=e3]
    - Text Text "로그인" [ref=e4]
  - Text StatusText "" [ref=e5]
```

`-s=<이름>` 으로 세션을 여럿 둔다(기본 `default`). 세션 파일 · 화면 파일은 `.control-cli/` 에 떨어진다.

### 루프 — USB

```bash
npx control-cli open --usb --app ./qa.apk         # 내 컴퓨터 Appium(PLATFORM_APPIUM_URL, 없으면 127.0.0.1:4723)이 깔고 켠다
npx control-cli open --usb                        # 이미 켜 둔 게임에 붙는다 — Appium 세션이 없어 스크린샷이 없다
npx control-cli open --usb --udid <serial> --port 13100
```

USB 는 `adb forward tcp:13100 tcp:13100` 을 걸고 TCP 로 보낸다. adb 는 `ANDROID_HOME` → `~/Library/Android/sdk` → PATH 순서로 찾는다.

### 명령

| 명령 | 하는 일 | Ran 줄 |
|---|---|---|
| `click <ref\|주소>` | 가운데를 가짜 터치로 누른다. 월드 오브젝트는 주 카메라로 비춘 자리 | `game.click('LoginButton')` |
| `drag <ref\|주소> <ref\|주소>` | 앞 자리에서 뒤 자리로 10프레임에 걸쳐 끈다 | `game.drag('/Hud/Bag/Slot[0]', '/Hud/Bag/Slot[3]')` |
| `type <ref\|주소> <글자>` | InputField 에 바로 넣는다(화면 키보드 없이). 글자 수 제한 · 거르기는 InputField 가 한다. 비밀번호 칸이면 Ran 줄에 글자 대신 `'***'` | `game.type('IdInput', 'qa_user01')` |
| `text <ref\|주소>` | 글자 읽기 | `game.text('StatusText')` |
| `get <ref\|주소> <컴포넌트.칸>` | 속성 읽기 — 게임이 폰에서 셈하는 값. `material` · `materials` · `mesh` 는 읽기만 해도 사본을 만들어 거절한다(`shared…` 를 읽는다) | `game.get('Player', 'PlayerController.moveSpeed')` |
| `find <ref\|주소>` | 있으면 `{path, text, interactable}`, 없으면 `null` | `game.find('ShopPanel')` |
| `wait <ref\|주소> [--text 글자] [--gone] [--timeout 초]` | 뜰 때까지 · 글자가 들 때까지 · 사라질 때까지(기본 10초) | `game.waitFor('ShopPanel', { gone: true })` |
| `layout [ref\|주소]` | 누를 수 있는 UI 가 안전 영역 밖이거나 서로 겹치는지(팝업에 가린 것은 뺀다) | `game.layout('LoginView')` |
| `errors [번호]` | 게임 예외 · 에러 로그(최근 200개). 답의 `last` 를 받아 두고 다음에 그 번호 뒤만 받는다 | 없음 |
| `tap <x> <y>` | 좌표 누르기(왼쪽 아래가 0,0) — 살펴볼 때만. 케이스는 좌표를 쓰지 않는다 | 없음 |
| `ping` · `tree` | 게임 답 · 켜진 오브젝트 트리 JSON | 없음 |

**주소**는 오브젝트 이름(켜진 것 중 하나뿐일 때) 또는 `/` 로 시작하는 경로다. 같은 이름 형제는 경로 칸에 `[순번]`(0부터)을 붙인다 — `/HudCanvas/Inventory/Grid/Slot[2]`. 이름이 겹치면 고르지 않고 실패한다.
액션 뒤에는 트리가 두 번 같을 때까지(3초 상한) 기다렸다 화면을 찍는다. **기다리기**는 0.3초마다 짧은 `find` 를 되풀이한다 — 명령 하나가 팜 15초 · SDK 10초 한도에 안 걸린다.

### 창 훑기

```bash
npx control-cli crawl                                  # → .control-cli/crawl/list.json · 001.yml …
npx control-cli crawl --max 30 --minutes 5 --exclude '/설정|settings/i' --exclude 'GmButton' --out ./crawl
```

지금 화면의 버튼을 하나씩 눌러 새로 뜬 창(앞 화면에 없던 오브젝트 묶음)을 찍고 닫는다 — 창 안 닫기 버튼 → 저절로 사라지기(알림) → 폰 뒤로 키 차례. 창 안 버튼은 한 단계 더 누른다(창 밖에 뜬 팝업만 다시 닫는다). 같은 이름 형제(목록 줄 · 슬롯)는 `[0]` 하나만, 같은 틀(순번을 뗀 경로)의 창은 한 번만 적는다.
안 누르는 것 — 이름이나 글자에 삭제 · 탈퇴 · 로그아웃 · 종료 · 나가기 · delete · remove · logout · quit · exit 가 든 버튼 · 닫기 버튼 · `--exclude`(`/정규식/깃발` 이나 든 글자). 되돌리지 못하면 그 자리에서 멈춘다. 상한은 창 60개 · 10분(`CRAWL` 상수).
로그인 · 캐릭터 고르기 · 순간이동은 하지 않는다 — 부르는 쪽이 그 화면에 맞춰 둔 뒤 다시 부른다.

| 파일 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| `NNN.yml` | `# <주소>` · `# 연 곳: <창> 의 <버튼> 「글자」` · 줄인 목록 |
| `list.json` | `[{주소, 이름, 틀, 파일, 지문, 글자지문, 연곳: {창, 버튼, 글자} \| null}]` — 첫 줄은 시작 화면 `scene:<장면>`. 지문은 순번을 뗀 구조, 글자지문은 글자 |
| `summary.json` | `{멈춘까닭, 창, 누름, 초}` |

### 연결

| 값 | 옵션 | 환경값 |
|---|---|---|
| Appium · 팜 입구 | `--url` | `PLATFORM_APPIUM_URL` (없으면 `http://127.0.0.1:4723`) — 잡기 · 게임 명령 주소는 여기서 `/wd/hub` 를 뗀 곳 |
| 팜 토큰 (Bearer) | `--token` | `PLATFORM_APPIUM_TOK

yashnimde-ship-it/sonions.readme:
# Bandit

A top-down pixel-art heist game set in a cozy suburban estate at dusk. Sneak in
from the street, explore the house and grounds, and steal everything worth taking.

Built with the same stack as the FireRed remake: **TypeScript + Canvas + Vite**.
The map art is cut straight out of the reference image at build time and compiled
into a tilemap, so the game looks exactly like the reference.

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run assets      # paint the estate and compile tiles, collision and data
npm run dev         # http://localhost:5173 (any free port)
```

Open the printed URL in Chrome. Other scripts:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run assets` | Regenerate everything in `public/assets/` from the reference and `map/` |
| `npm run assets -- --procedural` | Same, but with the older hand-written painters instead of the reference art |
| `npm run check` | Flood-fill the collision map from the spawn point and confirm every room and interactable is reachable |
| `npm run build` | Type-check and build for production into `dist/` |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build |

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| W A S D / Arrow keys | Move |
| Shift | Sprint |
| E (or Enter / Space) | Interact: open or close doors, examine, steal loot. Also closes messages |

Every wooden door starts **closed** and blocks the way. Walk up to one and press E to
open it (E again closes it; a door won't close while you're standing in it). That
includes the front door, the patio and back doors, the roll-up garage door, and the
side doors in vertical walls (drawn open as pale strips in the reference; closed, a
wooden leaf fills the gap). If you close a door while just brushing its edge, the
bandit is nudged clear.

Nine items are worth stealing (look for the twinkle): the toolbox, cookie jar, TV,
laptop, jewelry box, gold watch, game console, piggy bank and silverware.

## Map

- **96 x 64 tiles, 32 x 32 px each on screen (3072 x 2048 px).** Art is painted at 16 px
  per tile, the reference image's own resolution, and drawn at 2x for a crisp 16-bit look.
- Layout recreated from `public/reference/estate-map-reference.png` (16 reference pixels
  = 1 tile): garage with the red car and driveway, storage room, kitchen, three
  bathrooms, master bedroom, living room, study, dining room, two more bedrooms,
  hallways, front porch, pool with deck and floats, pergola deck, vegetable garden,
  shed, doghouse, fences and gates, sidewalk and road.

## Architecture

```
map/                      build-time map definition and painters (Node, ES modules)
  mapData.mjs             the layout: rooms, hallways, doors, windows, grounds, objects,
                          trees, lights, interactables, spawn — all in tile coordinates
  tileDefinitions.mjs     ground, floor, wall, door, window, fence and road painters
  referenceExtract.mjs    separates furniture and props from floor and lawn in the reference
  referenceLayers.mjs     builds the art layers and per-object sprites from the reference
  referenceConfig.mjs     reference path, extraction settings, extra window walls
  artWalls.mjs            reads the house walls from the reference (for collision)
  furniture.mjs           procedural object painters (only with --procedural)
  mapBuilder.mjs          house plan (used for collision and areas) + procedural layers
  collisionMap.mjs        collision grid derived from the data (not from the art)
  bandit.mjs              PLACEHOLDER bandit sprite (the real one comes from the art team)
  draw.mjs                pixel drawing primitives and the dusk palette
scripts/
  generate-assets.mjs     paints, dedupes 16x16 tiles into a tileset, writes the map JSON
  check-reachability.mjs  verifies every room and interactable can be reached
  preview-extract.mjs     debug view of what the extraction counts as furniture
src/                      the game (TypeScript, Canvas 2D)
  main.ts                 loading, input, fixed 60 fps loop, rendering order
  config.ts               zoom, speeds, hitbox, camera easing
  map/TileMap.ts          builds the layers from the tileset; collision and area queries
  entities/Bandit.ts      movement with per-axis collision, sprinting, animation
  systems/CameraSystem.ts follow with easing, clamped to the world, resize-aware
  systems/InteractionSystem.ts  what's in reach, prompts, loot tracking
  systems/LightingSystem.ts     dusk, lit interiors, lamp light (visible area only)
  ui/HUD.ts               fixed DOM HUD: loot, area name, prompt, messages
public/assets/            generated: tiles/tileset.png, map/estate.json, map/doors.png, furniture/*.png (+ furniture.json),
                          characters/bandit-placeholder.png
                          provided by the art team: characters/bandit.png
```

**How the map is built.** `mapBuilder` builds a plan from `mapData`: room interiors,
then walls (shared walls stay walls), then any hallway edge facing outdoors becomes an
exterior wall, then doors and windows are carved in. The plan was traced from the
reference and drives collision and area names.

The art comes from the reference itself (16 reference pixels = 1 tile, so nothing is
scaled). For each room, the floor colors are learned along the walls and the floor
is flood-filled away; what's left is furniture. Outdoors, the same happens against
the lawn. That gives four layers:

1. **floor**: the reference's floors, walls and ground, with the area under each
   piece of furniture filled from the same floor pattern a tile or more away
2. **walls**: empty in reference mode (walls are part of the floor art)
3. **objects**: the furniture and props cut out of the reference (drawn under the bandit)
4. **overhead**: tree canopies (drawn over the bandit, so he walks behind them)

Every object in `mapData` is also exported as its own transparent PNG in
`public/assets/furniture/`, listed with its position in `furniture.json`.
