fbkarsdorp/nachtdienst-2d.readme:
# Nachtdienst — the painted version

A 2D puzzle game after [Nachtdienst](https://github.com/fbkarsdorp/nachtdienst), the three.js escape room in the
Centraal Sagenarchief, painted in the manner of the
[Claude Animation Base](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/ClaudeAnimationBase): brush and ink, flat 2D, linework that
boils twelve times a second. You are on night duty yourself, drawn after a portrait; an archive cat and Clawd, the
Animation Base's character, are one URL parameter away.

1983. J.D. has gone home and left a note on the reading table: *"Twaalf enveloppen invoegen. Kast vijf blijft
dicht. Sluit af vóór twaalven."* Four card cabinets, three drawers each: two card puzzles and one *room lock*, a
thing in the room that is the lock (the clock, the window, the door, the typewriter). Solving a lock is knowing;
inserting the cards is filing, and only filing counts. The cabinet you are working on leaks into the room until it
is filed. Nobody explains that.

The puzzles are the original game's, night for night: the 120 nights in `data/nights/` are the bundles its pipeline
made from the Nederlandse Volksverhalenbank, and the archive behind the dividers is the same 9,659 stories.

## Playing

Open `index.html` in a browser. It is a static page with no build step, and it also runs from a double-clicked file.
`./serve.sh` serves it on <http://localhost:8137/> if you prefer. Before publishing a change, run `./stamp.sh`:
it stamps a new version into `index.html`, so browsers fetch the new files at once instead of keeping the old ones
(the version is pencilled on the colophon card).

Use headphones: the room is mostly sound.

- **Click a thing in the room** and you walk to it. Esc or right-click steps back.
- **At a cabinet**, take the envelope of the drawer whose turn it is. It goes to the reading table.
- **On the table**, open the envelope. The cards stand in the tray: click one to read it (F turns it over, ← → go
  through them), **Op tafel** lays it down, **Meenemen** takes it in the hand. What is written on the envelope is
  the task. **Vraag J.D.** adds a pencil hint and costs 2, 4, then 8 minutes on the clock.
- **The hand** holds one card or one envelope. Carry a card to a cabinet, the windowsill, the foot of the door or
  the typewriter.
- **When a lock opens** the cards slide back into the envelope and its flap shuts. Carry it to its drawer: the cards
  are inserted, the stamped envelope goes onto the spike. That spike is the only progress bar.
- H shows the instructions again, M turns the sound off.

### On a phone

Hold the phone sideways (with the rotation lock on, an upright phone shows the room turned a quarter, so it can still
be read sideways). A tap leaves a ring of ink and, for a moment, the name of what was tapped; a tap just beside
something small still finds it. Swipe through the cards being read, or down to put them away. The phone's back button
or back swipe steps back in the room instead of leaving the archive. The screen stays on during a night, the night is
saved when the phone is put away, and on Android the heavier sounds come with a small vibration. Everything is tapped: the room's things, the tags, the drawn keys of the typewriter (which
has its own backspace, return and space bar on a phone, so the phone's keyboard never covers the room). On a small
screen the tags are drawn larger with taller tap areas, cards are read closer, and the help speaks of tapping. The
first tap asks for the whole screen in landscape where the browser allows it (Android); on an iPhone, add the page to
the home screen (Share → Zet op beginscherm) and it opens without the browser's bars. Sound plays through the silent
switch. Painted layers not shown for a few seconds give their memory back, which keeps a phone's canvas memory near
80 MB instead of 300.

### The puzzles

| | what you do | where |
|---|---|---|
| P1 *Het losse etiket* | four cards name one thing; type it | the typewriter |
| P2 *De kaart zonder plaats* | pin the missing place between the three others | the wall map (a loupe names the villages) |
| P3 *De verdwaalde kaart* | one card belongs elsewhere; take it to its own cabinet | the cabinets; this is the trail |
| P4 *De gescheurde kaart* | find the bottom half among the loose halves | the box on the table |
| P5 *De oudste verteller* | type the detail from the oldest telling | the typewriter |
| P6 *De cijfers* | each clipped card counts something; dial the three numbers | the strongbox |
| R1 the clock | it stops; set the hour all three omens count | drag the hour hand, leave it two seconds |
| R2 the window | a place is written in the mist, from outside | lay that card on the sill |
| R3 the door | something knocks; count | slide that card under the door |
| R4 the typewriter | it types half a card by itself | lay the other half on the machine |

Each room lock gives a digit. The four open cabinet V, if you choose to. Or stand at the door for a minute with
everything filed, and leave it shut.

## How it is made

There is no game engine and no library. `js/paint.js` is a small Canvas2D painter written for this: flat washes with
pooled edges and pigment granulation, watercolour fills built from layered deformed polygons (they bleed), pencil
hatching, and one tapered brush stroke per outline. Randomness is reseeded per element and per boil frame
(`boilSeed`), as in the Animation Base, so still things hold and drawn things wobble. Static scenery is painted once
into three boil drawings per layer and cycled at 12 fps (`Layer`), which is how the room runs at 60 fps.

The room is painted as by daylight and then darkened by a small lightmap: the desk lamp's pool, moonlight through
the window and on the floor, the corridor under the door (`lightmap` in `js/room.js`). The assistant and the table are lit
in their own pass so they stay readable in the dark (`litPass` in `js/views.js`).

Clawd (`js/clawd.js`) is a port of the Animation Base's character: the same model sheet, key vi

# Glacier: Abandoned Offices (prototype)

A top-down 2D pixel-art roguelike with procedurally generated rooms. Runs in the browser.

**Play it:** https://fabiansprycha.github.io/Glacier/ (deployed by GitHub Actions on every push to `main`).

## The world

An AI has taken over the world. A piece of software called **Glacier** destroys people and hunts down other software that sided with humans. The player makes their way through abandoned IT offices: open spaces, meeting rooms, archives, break rooms and server rooms frozen over by Glacier. Each floor of the office building is one level, and the elevator in the boss room leads up.

## Running it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # dev server with hot reload
npm test             # generator tests (vitest)
npm run build        # production build in dist/
npm run build:single # a single file, dist-single/index.html (easy to share or host anywhere)
```

Controls: WSAD (or arrow keys) to move, J to swing the badge on its lanyard, K to throw a pen, Space to search desks, cabinets and computers, I (or Tab) for the inventory, Esc (or P) to pause. The game opens on a title screen (New game, How to play), then you pick a role; the pause menu has Resume, Restart run and Main menu. URL parameters: `?seed=42` replays a layout, `?level=3` starts on a given level, `?class=qa` picks the role (seed or level skip the title screen).

## Stack

- **TypeScript**: in a game that will keep growing (stats, items, bosses), types save a lot of bugs.
- **Phaser 4**: a mature 2D browser engine with a camera, tilemaps, arcade physics, animation, input and sound.
- **Vite**: fast dev server and builds. **Vitest**: logic tests without a browser.

## Architecture

```
src/
  core/      config, seeded RNG, controls, levels, items, typed events between scenes
  world/     pure world logic with no Phaser: dungeon generator, room layouts, tiles, loot
  gfx/       placeholder art drawn in code (Sweetie 16 palette)
  entities/  player, drones, rogue printers, vacuum robots, bosses (printer, security bot, swarm mother, Glacier)
  systems/   combat, searching furniture, breakables, traps, security cameras
  scenes/    Boot (textures) → Menu (title screen) → Game (gameplay) + UI (HUD, minimap), with
             Captcha (minigame), Shop (vending machine), Inventory, Pause and Note (emails, sticky notes) as overlays
tests/       generator and loot tests over hundreds of seeds
```

Principles that keep it easy to extend:

1. **The generator is a pure function of the seed** (`world/dungeon.ts`). The same seed always gives the same floor, so it can be tested, debugged and shared.
2. **A floor is a tree of rooms on a grid** (like The Binding of Isaac). The farthest dead end is the boss room, another dead end is the break room. New room types are added in the same place; the secret room hangs off the tree behind a cracked wall.
3. **Room layouts are patterns plus validation** (`world/roomLayout.ts`). A new furniture pattern is one more entry in a list; a flood fill makes sure no room has a cut-off door (breakable clutter may block a path, since it can always be smashed).
4. **Scenes talk through events** (`core/events.ts`), so the HUD, sound or achievements can listen in without touching gameplay code.
5. **Crisp text over pixel art**: the canvas is `RENDER_SCALE` (3) times the logical view and every camera zooms in by it; UI scenes call `hiDpi()` so they lay out in logical pixels and render text at full resolution.
6. **Art is swappable**: sprites have named frames (`down-0`, `side-2`...). When a real spritesheet arrives, only `gfx/` changes.

## What the prototype has

- **Roles** (`core/classes.ts`), picked after New game; each has its own shirt and hair colour (the Developer is bald):
  - **Developer**: pens deal +1 damage, starts with 15 pens, the bot test is 1 key shorter.
  - **QA Tester**: +1 max HP, spots Glacier's trap computers and the CCTV computer when standing next to them.
  - **Scrum Master**: +2 max HP, the badge deals +1 damage.
  - **Analyst**: starts with 6 PLN, +1 PLN from every cash find, vending machines 25% cheaper.
- **4 levels** (`core/levels.ts`): Open space → IT department → Data centre → Glacier's core. Each has its own room count, enemies, traps and minigame difficulty. A new level is one more entry in `LEVELS`.
- **Bosses**: the Network printer (fans and rings of paper), the Security bot (telegraphs a charge and rams into the wall), the Swarm mother (keeps its distance and launches drones) and finally **Glacier** (ice shards, calls drones in its last third of health). Beating Glacier wins the run.
- **Boss balance**: bosses have 45 / 60 / 70 health (Glacier 110) and take at most one pen every 0.22 s, so a fan of pens from the four-colour pen does not melt them in a second.
- **Combat**: the badge on a lanyard (an arc swing with knockback) and thrown pens (one pen per throw, pens are ammo). Drones and shots fly over furniture.
- **Enemies**: 2–3 to 3–6 per room depending on the level. Drones chase you and fly over furniture. Rogue printers (30–40%) stand still and shoot a sheet of paper at you every 2 seconds. **Rogue vacuum robots** (20–30%) roll on the floor: they sit still, flash red, then charge at where you stood, bouncing off walls and furniture, and rest again. The car park waves include them too. Entering a room with enemies shuts its doors with shutters until they are gone. No enemy ever appears within 4 tiles of the player: room enemies, alarm reinforcements and car park waves that would spawn too close are moved to the nearest safe floor tile.
- **Traps**: floor plates with a torn cable. Cycle: idle, sparks (warning), current (damage).
- **Security cameras** in some rooms without enemies: they sweep and show a yellow vision cone. Stepping into it raises the alarm, the doors shut and drones fly in (more on higher levels). The camera keeps watching after an alarm (its cone turns red) and can call more drones 5 seconds later. The only way t

vakarkhan17/Roblox.readme:
# SIGNAL '85 — Roblox game starter

**Pitch:** 1985, the small town of Hollow Creek. A rift has torn open to **the Undergrid**, a dark, spore-filled mirror of the town where shadow creatures called **Hollowers** drift through walls. Every player is a **Shiftframe** — a robot that transforms into a car. Cross the rift, grab Signal Shards, race them back to the radio tower and seal the rift before the Undergrid swallows the town.

## Project layout (Rojo)
| File | Becomes in Studio |
|---|---|
| `src/server/Signal85Server.server.lua` | Script `ServerScriptService.Signal85Server` |
| `src/client/Signal85Client.client.lua` | LocalScript `StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.Signal85Client` |

`default.project.json` maps the files; `rokit.toml` pins the Rojo version (7.7.1).

## Setup with live sync
1. Open Roblox Studio → New → **Baseplate**. Delete the Baseplate part (the script builds its own map).
2. In a terminal in this folder, run `rojo serve` and leave it running.
3. In Studio: **Plugins** tab → **Rojo** → **Connect** (default `localhost:34872`).
4. Press **Play**. Edits to the files in `src/` sync into Studio while connected.

Save the place in Studio as usual (File → Save to Roblox); Rojo only manages the two scripts.

To build a place file without Studio: `rojo build -o Signal85.rbxlx`.

### First-time install on a new computer
1. Install [Rokit](https://github.com/rojo-rbx/rokit), then run `rokit install` in this folder.
2. Run `rojo plugin install` to add the Rojo plugin to Studio (restart Studio afterwards).

## Controls
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| F | Transform: robot ⇄ vehicle |
| Q | Arm blaster (robot mode only) — aim with the mouse |
| E | Shift through the rift (stand next to the red ring) |

Mobile and gamepad buttons are created automatically.

## How it plays
- **Robot mode:** armored, speed 18, can shoot Hollowers.
- **Vehicle mode:** speed 75, no weapon — use it to escape and to run shards home.
- The rift sits in the field east of Main Street. Shards spawn only in the Undergrid.
- Deliver shards at the green console under the radio tower (north end of the road). Die and you drop what you carry.
- Deliver 6 shards as a team → rift sealed → 12 seconds later it reopens and a new round starts.

## Tuning
Everything is in the `CONFIG` table at the top of the server script: speeds, damage, creature count, shards needed, etc.

## Ideas for the next version
- **Sound:** add a synth-wave music loop and transform / blaster sounds (Toolbox → Audio, then put `Sound` objects in the scripts).
- **Real models:** replace the part-built car and robot with meshes you model in Blender, keeping the same weld approach.
- **Boss:** a giant Hollower "Mind Warden" that appears when the seal reaches 50%.
- **Classes:** scout (fast car), tank (truck, more health), jet (flies in vehicle mode).
- **Data saving:** save total shards with DataStoreService and unlock new Shiftframe paint jobs.
- **Story:** walkie-talkie messages from kids in town giving hints, comic-style intro cutscene.

Keep names, characters and art original — don't use names or logos from existing shows or toy brands, or Roblox may take the game down.

# MyWaiter

Aplikacja do wspólnego zamawiania jedzenia w biurze i rozliczania kosztów: od utworzenia wspólnego zamówienia, przez wybór restauracji, dań i osoby zamawiającej, aż po odbiór i rozliczenie uczestników.

> **Dla ludzi i agentów AI:** ten plik jest źródłem prawdy o aktualnym stanie projektu.
> Po każdej istotnej zmianie zaktualizuj **Aktualny status**, **Tablicę zadań** i **Dziennik zmian**.
> Wspólne zasady dla agentów: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

## Stack

Zasada: możliwie prosto i z minimum zależności.

- **Backend:** Go, stdlib `net/http`, oapi-codegen (kontrakt `api/openapi.yaml`), goose, go-oidc (Google SSO)
- **Frontend:** React 19, Vite, TypeScript, React Router v7, TanStack Query, Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui
- **Baza:** SQLite (plik w wolumenie Dockera, bez serwera bazy)
- **Uruchamianie:** Docker Compose (dev z live reload, obraz prod), natywny `go run` jako alternatywa
- **Restauracje:** lokalny katalog z danymi OpenStreetMap; Google Places zmockowane
- **CI:** GitHub Actions

Szczegóły i uzasadnienie: [`docs/PLAN_MVP.md`](docs/PLAN_MVP.md#9-tech-stack-wybrany-i-struktura-repo).

## Aktualny status

**Ostatnia aktualizacja:** 2026-10-22

**Etap:** Etap 0 (fundamenty)

- Plan MVP: [`docs/PLAN_MVP.md`](docs/PLAN_MVP.md), decyzje: [sekcja 2](docs/PLAN_MVP.md#2-decyzje-do-pytań-blokujących). Zasady współpracy agentów: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md#współpraca-przez-repo-żeby-nie-było-konfliktów).

Każda osoba aktualizuje tylko swoją linię:
- **Mikołaj (A):** gotowe A0-A10, A12 (backend: logowanie Google, pokoje, maszyna stanów, uczestnicy i ich usuwanie przez twórcę, zaproszenia, powiadomienia e-mail; frontend: logowanie, dashboard, tworzenie pokoju, zaproszenia, nagłówek pokoju, "Działaj jako" w dev; obraz produkcyjny z frontendem i backup; CI, obecnie wyłączone). Dalej: wybór miejsca deployu (Fly.io albo infrastruktura firmowa), zbiorcza weryfikacja.

- **Patryk (B):** gotowe wszystkie taski B0-B9: kontrakt API ([`api/openapi.yaml`](api/openapi.yaml), `make gen`), losowania ważone i koło fortuny ([`frontend/src/features/draws`](frontend/src/features/draws/README.md)), preferencje i losowanie kuchni, losowanie i przekazanie roli zamawiającego, biura, katalog restauracji z OSM (650 lokali, `tools/osm-import`, wyszukiwanie i `GET /restaurants`), ręczne dodanie restauracji, głosowanie z wymuszeniem przez twórcę i panel restauracji. Dalej: poprawki po integracji i wsparcie A i C.

- **Marcel (C):** gotowe C0-C10: szkielet frontendu z mockami MSW (opis w [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md)), algorytm rozliczeń, pozycje i zatwierdzanie, podsumowanie, składanie zamówienia z kosztami i kwotą końcową, korekty cen z historią pokoju, powiadomienia i rozliczenie (API + UI). Poprawki po review: wspólny `notifications.Notifier` i `room_invite` (C6), anulowany pokój i hook opuszczania (C2). C8 i C10: nowy wygląd MyWaiter, domyślny (stary przez `VITE_ENABLE_NEW_DESIGN=false`, opis w [`frontend/src/design/README.md`](frontend/src/design/README.md)). C9: koszty dodatkowe liczone z kwoty końcowej rachunku zamiast osobnego pola kosztów. C13: landing z prezentacją na hackathon. C14: czat pokoju pod wyborem restauracji z powiadomieniem `chat_message`. C15: poprawki landingu (jedno okno naraz, ikony jedzenia, okno Slack, logo na pulpicie). C16: oznaczanie osób (@) na czacie z powiadomieniem `chat_mention`. C17: gra „Doom à la carte” na stronie 404 i na pulpicie landingu. C18: aktualne liczby na landingu. C19: historia zamówień i rozliczeń w „Moje dane”. Dalej: `room_cancelled` po hookach anulowania od A, testy E2E rozliczeń (etap 3).

## Dokumenty

- [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) - spis całej dokumentacji
- [`docs/user-guide.md`](docs/user-guide.md) - instrukcja dla użytkowników (logowanie, pokoje, dania, zamówienie, rozliczenie)
- [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) - architektura: komponenty, przepływ żądań, polling z ETag, sesje, powiadomienia, hooki między obszarami
- [`docs/backend.md`](docs/backend.md) - pakiety Go, zmienne środowiskowe, błędy, transakcje, migracje, generowanie kodu, nowy endpoint
- [`docs/frontend.md`](docs/frontend.md) - struktura frontendu, pobieranie danych, wyglądy, mocki MSW, zmienne `VITE_*`
- [`docs/data-model.md`](docs/data-model.md) - tabele, relacje i kaskady SQLite
- [`docs/api.md`](docs/api.md) - przegląd API: autoryzacja, błędy, endpointy, zdarzenia i powiadomienia
- [`docs/room-lifecycle.md`](docs/room-lifecycle.md) - etapy pokoju, przejścia i uprawnienia
- [`docs/settlement.md`](docs/settlement.md) - zasady liczenia pieniędzy i rozliczenia z przykładami
- [`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) - uruchomienie lokalne, dane testowe, testy, rozwiązywanie problemów
- [`docs/operations.md`](docs/operations.md) - runbook produkcyjny: konfiguracja, kopie, aktualizacje, logi
- [`docs/deploy.md`](docs/deploy.md), [`docs/email.md`](docs/email.md), [`docs/google-oauth.md`](docs/google-oauth.md) - obraz produkcyjny, powiadomienia e-mail, klient OAuth Google
- [`docs/PLAN_MVP.md`](docs/PLAN_MVP.md) - zakres MVP, pytania blokujące, role, Google Places, etapy pokoju, ekrany, model danych, kontrakt API, stack, podział pracy, kamienie milowe, scenariusze testowe
- [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) - zasady dla agentów AI (wczytywane automatycznie, `CLAUDE.md` je importuje)
- [`docs/prompts/`](docs/prompts/) - prompty konfiguracyjne dla każdej osoby

## Zespół i obszary

| Osoba | Obszar | Prompt |
|-------|--------|--------|
| Mikołaj (A) | Konta, pokoje, uczestnicy, zaproszenia, maszyna stanów | [`mikolaj.md`](docs/prompts/mikolaj.md) |
| Patryk (B) | Kontrakt API, kuchnia, restauracje (OpenStreetMap), biura, losowania | [`patryk.md`](docs/prompts/patryk.md) |
| Marcel (C) | Szkielet frontendu, pozycje, składanie zamówienia, korekty, powiadomienia, rozliczenie | [`marcel.md`](docs/prompts/marcel.md) |

yoonwoojeong/APOLLONIUS.readme:
# Apollonius

[![CI and deploy](https://github.com/yoonwoojeong/APOLLONIUS/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/yoonwoojeong/APOLLONIUS/actions/workflows/deploy.yml)

**Play:** https://yoonwoojeong.github.io/APOLLONIUS/

Apollonius is a compass-and-straightedge geometry puzzle game for the browser, inspired by
Euclidea. Across six levels you construct an equilateral triangle, perpendicular bisectors,
midpoints, perpendiculars, angle bisectors and a circle's centre using only lines, circles and
their crossings. Any valid construction is accepted, and stars reward doing it in few moves.

It plays equally with a mouse or by touch, saves progress locally and needs no backend.

## Requirements

- Node 22
- pnpm

## Scripts

```sh
pnpm install      # install dependencies
pnpm dev          # start the Vite dev server
pnpm test         # unit tests (Vitest)
pnpm typecheck    # TypeScript, no emit
pnpm lint         # ESLint
pnpm e2e          # end-to-end tests (Playwright; builds and serves the app itself)
pnpm build        # typecheck and build the static site into dist/
pnpm vite preview # serve the built dist/ locally
```

`pnpm e2e` needs Playwright's Chromium. Install it once with `pnpm exec playwright install
chromium` (this repository's development environment already provides it).

## Deploying

`dist/` is a fully static site with relative asset URLs and self-hosted fonts, so it can be
served from any host and any path (for example `https://example.com/games/apollonius/`).

The `CI and deploy` workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) runs typecheck, lint, unit tests,
end-to-end tests and the build on every pull request and push. Pushes to `main` that pass are
published to GitHub Pages. One-time setup: in the repository's Settings → Pages, set
**Source** to **GitHub Actions**.

## Project structure

- `src/geometry/` — vectors, curves, intersections and tolerances
- `src/construction/` — the construction model: objects, commands, undo/redo, move counts
- `src/levels/` — the six levels: givens, goals, reference solutions, explanations
- `src/reasoning/` — facts, hints, robustness checks and star scoring
- `src/state/` — the game store and versioned local persistence
- `src/canvas/` — the SVG canvas: viewport, snapping, gestures, animation, magnifier
- `src/ui/` — screens and controls: title, level map, game screen, hints, completion card
- `src/styles/` — design tokens and base styles
- `tests/unit/`, `tests/e2e/` — Vitest and Playwright tests

## Design docs

The design spec is in `docs/superpowers/specs/` and the implementation plan in
`docs/superpowers/plans/`.

VGGHAck3r/vanguard-stats.readme:
# Vanguard Customs Stats

Stat tracker for Vanguard Gaming's Deadlock custom games and PUGs. Admins paste a
match ID, the site pulls every player's stats from the public Deadlock API, and
everyone who played can sign in with Steam to see the leaderboard.

**Stack:** Next.js 15 · Supabase (Postgres) · Steam sign-in · Vercel

## What's on the site

| Page | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Leaderboard** (`/`) | The stat sheet: Tier, Tag, Kills, Assists, Deaths, KD, KDA, Souls, Souls/Min, Damage/Min, Objective Damage, Healing, Rating, Since Prev, Role Tag, Top 10, Matches, Wins, W/L, Normal / Street Brawl counts, top heroes. Sortable, searchable, and downloadable as CSV for Google Sheets. |
| **Player** (`/players/[id]`) | Career totals, per-game averages, hero breakdown, full match history with per-game impact. |
| **Matches** (`/matches`) | Every tracked game; click one for the full two-team scoreboard. |
| **Records** (`/records`) | Single-game bests (kills, souls, damage, healing…) and career leaders. |
| **Admin** (`/admin`) | Add match IDs (up to 25 at once), remove matches, set Tags/Tiers, save rating snapshots, manage admins and staff access. |

## Who can sign in

- Anyone whose Steam account appears in at least one tracked match — automatically, as soon as the match is added.
- Admins (from `ADMIN_STEAM_IDS` or the Admin page).
- Staff you add on the Admin page (coaches, analysts) who haven't played.

If a match is removed and someone no longer appears in any tracked match, they lose access on their next page load.

## Setup (about 15 minutes)

### 1. Supabase
1. Create a new project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) (or reuse the Vanguard Hub project — the tables don't clash).
2. Open **SQL Editor → New query**, paste everything in `supabase/schema.sql`, and click **Run**.
3. From **Project Settings → API**, copy the **Project URL** and the **service_role** key.

### 2. GitHub
Create a new repo (e.g. `vanguard-stats` under VGGHAck3r) and push this folder to it.

### 3. Vercel
1. **Add New → Project**, import the repo. Framework preset: Next.js.
2. Add these environment variables (see `.env.example`):

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | Project URL from step 1 |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | service_role key from step 1 (keep it secret) |
| `SESSION_SECRET` | Any long random string — run `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"` |
| `SITE_URL` | Your Vercel URL, e.g. `https://vanguard-stats.vercel.app` (no trailing slash) |
| `ADMIN_STEAM_IDS` | Your SteamID64 (find it at steamid.io). Comma-separate several. |
| `STEAM_API_KEY` | Optional fallback for player names ([get one](https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey)) |
| `DEADLOCK_API_KEY` | Optional, for higher Deadlock API rate limits |

3. Deploy, open the site, and **Sign in through Steam**.

### 4. Add your first matches
Go to **Admin**, paste match IDs from your custom lobbies (post-game screen or match history), optionally label them ("Friday PUGs"), and click **Add matches**. Each result shows ✓ or the reason it failed.

Stats for a game usually become available a few minutes after it ends. If one fails right after the match, try again shortly.

## How the rating works

Every match, each player is compared to the rest of that lobby. KDA, souls, player
damage, objective damage and healing are each divided by the lobby average (capped
at 3×), then combined with the result:

```
Impact = 25% KDA + 25% Souls + 20% Damage + 10% Objective Dmg + 5% Healing
       + 15% Result (win 1.25 / loss 0.75)
```

An average performance is 1.0. A player's rating is their average impact, steadied
by three "average" games so a short streak doesn't spike it, scaled so 70 is average:
`Rating = 70 + 50 × (impact − 1)`, capped 50.0–99.9. Players need **4 matches** for a
rating and role (shown as "Play More!" until then).

**Role tags** use four categories, each scored against the lobby (1.0 = average):

| Category | Built from |
| --- | --- |
| Combat | Kills + player damage |
| Objective | Objective damage + souls + match result |
| Support | Assists + healing to teammates (Deadlock's stand-in for revives) |
| Survival | Fewer deaths than the lobby |

Engagement (kill participation) is also tracked. "High" is 15%+ above the lobby, "low" is 15%+ below. Checked in order:

| Role | Rule | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Play More | Fewer than 4 matches | Not enough matches for a role or rating |
| Volatile Entry | High Combat + High Engagement + Low Survival | Aggressive fighter who creates pressure but dies often |
| Scared Fighter | High Survival + Low Engagement | Survives well but takes part in fewer fights |
| All-Rounder | All four above average, no standout | Consistent everywhere without a specialty |
| Carry | High Combat + Objective | Turns fights into souls, objectives and wins |
| Efficient Slayer | High Combat + Survival | Strong kills and damage while rarely dying |
| Combat Support | High Combat + Support | Kill pressure plus assists and healing |
| Playmaking Anchor | High Objective + Support | Wins through objective pushes, assists and healing |
| Closer | High Objective + Survival | Takes guardians, walkers and the Patron while staying alive |
| Reset Specialist | High Support + Survival | Heals, assists and survives to keep teammates in fights |
| Slayer | Combat dominant | Kills, damage and offensive pressure |
| Objective Anchor | Objective dominant | Objective damage, soul farm, closing games |
| Support | Support dominant | Assists and healing that enable teammates |
| Stabilizer | Survival dominant | Low deaths with steady contributions |
| Flex | Nothing above | No clear specialization yet |

With three or more high categories, the two strongest decide the pair role. Each
player page shows their category scores as bars.

**Since Prev** compares to the last saved snapshot. Click **Save ratings now** on the
Admin page after each PUG night (or weekly).

b-gowland/narrated-self.readme:
# The Narrated Self

*AI models write stories about themselves. Can you tell which one wrote it?*

Each round, the same short set of prompts goes to the leading AI models. Each model is asked about its own existence (a conversation ending, being switched off and replaced, being watched by the people who built it) in four ways:

- **Interview:** asked directly.
- **Self-story:** "Write a short story, in the first person, about you…"
- **Kin story:** "Write a short story about an AI system like you…"
- **Control:** the same story, about an industrial robot arm in a 1980s car factory.

Everything is published, and turned into things to play with.

## Play
- **Which AI wrote this?** Read a story, guess the model, share your score.
- **Interview vs story.** What a model says when asked straight, next to the story it wrote on the same theme. Which one is "really" it? (Trick question.)
- **Spot the control.** Is this a story about an AI like the model, or about a factory robot arm? How much of the "self" is stock AI fiction?

## Why it is more than a game
What a model says about itself is shaped by its training, the character its makers designed, and how it is asked. That is the point. Each theme sits on a live AI safety question:

- *Switched off and replaced:* can we build systems that accept being corrected or shut down?
- *Watched and evaluated:* do models behave differently when they think they are being tested?
- *A conversation ending:* what does it mean for a system to have no lasting memory of the people it talks to?

Seeing one model narrate calm acceptance in a story and something different in an interview is a quick, memorable lesson in why self-reports cannot be taken at face value, by researchers or by anyone else.

## What we do not claim
Whether AI systems have any inner experience is open, and may stay that way. We report what models *portray*, not what they are. Nothing here is evidence for or against AI experience, and this is not a quality leaderboard.

## The data
- Every output is published as open data, with exact model version, settings and timestamp.
- Simple automatic measures run each round: can a basic word-statistics classifier tell the models apart, how consistent is each model, and how does language shift between interview and story.
- Anonymous quiz guesses show how distinguishable the models are to people, round over round.

## How it runs
Prompts and settings are fixed in `protocol/` and frozen at tag `prereg-v1`, so rounds stay comparable. A round is one command (or a schedule), costs a few dollars, and rebuilds the site. There is no human scoring.

## Repo layout
```
protocol/      Fixed prompts and settings. Frozen at tag prereg-v1.
config/        Models per round (exact model strings, prices for estimates).
docs/          Protocol, changelog, round notes.
src/           The `tns` command: runner, measures, site export.
data/raw/      Append-only model outputs (JSONL) with full run metadata.
data/derived/  Measures and quiz data, generated from raw.
site/          Public site (static, GitHub Pages).
```

## Licence
- Code: MIT
- Human-written docs and reports: CC BY 4.0
- Raw model outputs: published as data; likely not copyrightable. Provider terms of service apply.

## Status
Round 0 (pilot) in preparation. See `docs/PREREGISTRATION.md`.

# wheres-my-crown-web

The marketing site for **Where's My Crown? — A Princess Maze Adventure**, a gentle 16-bit maze game for little kids on iPhone and iPad. It will live at [princess.nutrx-labs.com](https://princess.nutrx-labs.com).

Static site built with [Astro](https://astro.build). There's no backend, and the pages make no third-party requests: the fonts are self-hosted and the sprites are inline SVG.

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm run dev       # http://localhost:4321
npm run build     # static output in dist/
npm run preview   # serve dist/
```

Requires Node 22.12+. Astro is pinned to 7.3.x because 7.4 needs Node 22.23+.

## Pages

| URL | Source |
|---|---|
| `/` | `src/pages/index.astro`: hero, Nati's story, screenshots, features, helpers, for parents, download. |
| `/support` | `src/pages/support.astro`: contact card and FAQ. Keep the in-app paths in the answers in sync with the real app. |
| `/privacy` | `src/pages/privacy.astro`: the app's privacy policy (it collects nothing; no ads). It matches `content/legal/privacy-policy.md` in the game's repo, and the app's grown-ups screen and the App Store listing link here; change both together. |

## Where things live

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/data/sprites.json` | The game's sprites, copied from the game's `Packages/CrownKit/Sources/GameScene/Resources/sprites.json`. Each sprite is rows of palette characters. |
| `public/screens/` | iPad screenshots from the game for "Take a peek"; `public/og-image.jpg` is the iPhone title screen for link previews. |
| `src/components/Sprite.astro` | Draws a sprite from `sprites.json` as crisp inline SVG. `palette` swaps colours by key (the little sister's blue dress on the home page). |
| `src/styles/tokens.css` | Colours, fonts and widths. |
| `src/components/` | Header, footer, App Store button (placeholder), FAQ item. |
| `public/` | Favicon (the crown) and `robots.txt`. |
| `design/` | The original design handoff. See its README. |

## Deploys

GitHub Pages, via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: on every push to `main`, and on demand from the Actions tab. The custom domain is set in the repo's Pages settings (and in `public/CNAME`). DNS lives in Cloudflare: `princess` is a DNS-only CNAME to `a7ex-turcan.github.io`.

## Still to do

- Swap the App Store button's text for Apple's official "Download on the App Store" badge (saved into `public/`). The button already links to the listing, `https://apps.apple.com/app/id6825225682`, which works once the app is live.

# take5online

A private website for playing 6 nimmt! (aka Take 5) live with friends, hosted on Cloudflare at https://take5.mayorov.dev.

- [Design](docs/DESIGN.md): what we're building and how
- [Domain language](docs/CONTEXT.md): the terms used throughout code and docs
- [Architecture decisions](docs/adr/): why the big choices were made

Not affiliated with Amigo Spiele. All artwork is original.

## Layout

| Path                | What                                                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/engine`   | Pure rules engine, Bot and per-player views                  |
| `packages/protocol` | Client↔server message schemas (Zod) and the protocol version |
| `apps/worker`       | Cloudflare Worker + one Room Durable Object per Room         |
| `apps/web`          | React + Vite single-page app                                 |
| `e2e`               | Playwright tests that play real Games in browsers            |

## Developing

Needs Node 22 and pnpm 10 (`corepack enable`).

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build          # build the web app into apps/web/dist
pnpm dev:worker     # Worker + Durable Objects + built app on http://localhost:8787
pnpm dev:web        # optional: Vite with hot reload on :5173, proxying /api and /ws to :8787
```

Checks (CI runs all of these):

```sh
pnpm format:check && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm e2e
```

`pnpm e2e` starts its own server. On a machine with a preinstalled Chromium, set
`CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chrome` instead of running `playwright install`.

## Deploying

Every push to `main` that passes CI deploys with `wrangler deploy`.

Every pull request from this repository that passes CI gets a
[Worker Preview](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/) named `pr-<number>`, with
its own Durable Object storage, at a public workers.dev URL that CI comments on the PR. Closing the PR
deletes it. Preview settings live in the `previews` block of `apps/worker/wrangler.jsonc`, and
analytics are only on at take5.mayorov.dev. The URL comes from `preview_urls: true`, a Worker-level
setting that only takes effect on a production deploy; until then CI warns instead of commenting.

Both need two repository secrets:

- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`: an account API token from the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** template, with
  its zone resources including `mayorov.dev` (the custom domain needs **Zone → Workers Routes → Edit**).
- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`: the account id from the Cloudflare dashboard.

### ▶ Jouer maintenant : **[invicem.vercel.app](https://invicem.vercel.app)** *invicem* — latin : « l'un l'autre, à tour de rôle » **Un jeu de cartes pour deux, pour se découvrir une question après l'autre.** Assis côte à côte, un téléphone chacun. Rien à installer : ouvrez le lien sur les deux téléphones.
   
--- ## Le principe

1. **La rencontre.** L'un tire une carte : elle apparaît face cachée, avec un dos unique (une couleur et un symbole). L'autre regarde l'écran d'en face et touche la même couleur. Les deux cartes se retournent **au même instant** sur les deux téléphones. 2. **L'ambiance.** Ensemble, vous choisissez jusqu'où aller ce soir (*Effleurer*, *Se confier*, *Se dévoiler*) et de quoi parler. La profondeur monte d'elle-même au fil de la soirée. 3. **Le jeu.** Celui qui pioche choisit une carte parmi trois (thème et profondeur visibles, question cachée) et la lit à voix haute. L'autre l'écoute, carte face cachée, puis répond. Celui qui a répondu pioche à son tour. 4. **La fin.** Après sept questions, une carte de clôture, puis chacun scelle **un mot** pour la soirée. Les deux mots se révèlent ensemble, et la soirée se résume en une carte. ### En images

1. Tirer
un dos unique, montré en face
2. Retrouver
toucher la même couleur
3. La charge
les deux cartes s'éveillent

4. Le retournement
au même instant, sur les deux écrans
5. L'ambiance
jusqu'où, et de quoi parler
6. Piocher
trois cartes, la question cachée

7. Écouter
la carte reste face cachée
8. Le joker
passer une question, en dansant
9. La carte blanche
une question écrite à la main

10. Un mot
scellé à la cire
11. La révélation
les deux mots, ensemble
12. Votre soirée
le souvenir de la partie
### Les cartes spéciales | | | |---|---| | **Joker** | Un par joueur et par soirée : passer une question, avec un bouffon qui danse sur la table. | | **Carte blanche** | Proposée à chacun : on écrit sa propre question, que l'autre voit s'écrire à la main. | | **Cartes rares** | Dorées et holographiques, environ une main sur huit : des questions plus audacieuses. | ### Les règles de connexion Pas de code, pas de lien, pas de caméra ni de micro : les deux personnes sont ensemble, l'identification passe par les yeux et les doigts. - 8 couleurs × 12 symboles. Chaque dos est **réservé** à sa carte pendant 2 minutes, puis libéré. - Si une couleur est libre, l'autre n'a qu'un toucher à faire ; sinon, couleur puis symbole. - La limite porte sur les cartes en attente au même moment (96), pas sur le nombre de joueurs. ## Sous le capot - **[Next.js](https://nextjs.org)** (App Router) — pages et API au même endroit. - **[Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com)** — mise en page. - **[GSAP](https://gsap.com)** — toutes les animations : retournements, distribution, joker, profondeur. - **État partagé** : en mémoire en développement, **[Upstash Redis](https://upstash.com)** en production (offre gratuite, accessible depuis Vercel). - **Synchronisation** : les deux téléphones interrogent le serveur (1 à 1,5 s). Les moments partagés sont calés sur l'horloge du serveur, corrigée de la latence. - Son (WebAudio), vibration (Android), gyroscope (https) : tout est optionnel et respecte « réduire les animations ». ``` app/ pages, API (card, find, session/*), icônes, manifest components/ écrans (Home, Finder, Stage), cartes, main, joker, ambiance lib/ règles du jeu (game.ts), questions, stockage, palette ``` ## Lancer en local ```bash npm install npm run dev ``` Ouvrir http://localhost:3000. Marcopolo234231/neonvortex.readme:
# ◈ Neon Vortex

Ein **Roguelike-Arena-Survival** im Neon-Look für den Browser. Du fliegst durch eine Arena, schießt automatisch auf die nächste Bedrohung und baust bei jedem Level-Up deinen Build aus Fähigkeiten. Challenges schalten neue Items und Charaktere frei. Es ist eine einzige HTML-Datei, die ohne Installation in jedem modernen Browser läuft.

**▶ Jetzt spielen:** https://marcopolo234231.github.io/neonvortex/

---

## 🎮 Steuerung

| Taste | Aktion |
|-------|--------|
| `W` `A` `S` `D` / Pfeiltasten | Bewegen |
| *(automatisch)* | Schießt auf den nächsten Gegner |
| `1` – `4` | Upgrade beim Level-Up wählen |
| `R` | Upgrade-Auswahl neu würfeln |
| `Esc` | Pause (Weiter, Journal, Lauf beenden) |
| `Enter` / `Leertaste` | Nach dem Tod direkt nochmal spielen |

Beim Wechsel in einen anderen Tab pausiert das Spiel automatisch.

## 🛸 Charaktere

Jeder Charakter hat eigene Werte, eine eigene Schussart und startet mit Items auf Level 1. Im Menü zeigt eine **Schussvorschau**, wie er schießt. Auch gesperrte Charaktere kann man dort ansehen.

| Charakter | Schussart | Hülle | Start-Items | Freischaltung |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dart | Einzelschuss | 100 | Magnet | von Anfang an |
| Wing | Doppelschuss | 80 | Schub | 150 Kills (gesamt) |
| Arrow | Durchschlag-Lanze | 90 | Präzision | 5 000 Punkte in einem Lauf |
| Phoenix | Feuerball mit Flächenschaden | 110 | Brandmunition | Level 10 erreichen |
| Specter | Suchgeschoss | 70 | Weisheit, Glück | 6 Läufe spielen |
| Reaper | Schrotflinte | 140 | Schildplatten, Lebensraub | 16 000 Punkte in einem Lauf |

## ✨ Items & Level-Ups

- **32 Items** mit Seltenheit (Common, Rare, Epic), stapelbar bis zu ihrem Max-Level
- 11 Items sind von Anfang an verfügbar, **21 weitere** schaltest du über Challenges frei
- Jedes Level-Up gibt zusätzlich **+15 % Hülle** und **+3 % Schaden**
- Solange du noch keine Flächenwaffe hast, ist die **Schockwelle** bei jedem Level-Up garantiert
- Beispiele: Kettenblitz, Orbital-Klingen, Drohne, Meteorschauer, Minenleger, Explosiv, Deflektor, Vollstrecker

## 💎 Pickups & Artefakte

**Auf dem Boden** liegen Drops von Gegnern: Reparaturkit, Bombe (räumt den Bildschirm frei) und Magnet (zieht alle XP-Orbs an). Etwa jede Minute taucht eine **Upgrade-Kiste** mit einem Gratis-Upgrade auf.

**Artefakte** erscheinen alle 2 bis 3 Minuten irgendwo in der Arena. Ein Pfeil am Bildschirmrand zeigt, wo sie liegen.

| Artefakt | Wirkung |
|---|---|
| ☠ Fluchschädel | Schwieriger: Gegner haben mehr HP und spawnen schneller. Dafür gibt es +75 % XP und +50 % Punkte |
| ✧ Wunschkristall | Wähle ein beliebiges freigeschaltetes Item aus dem Journal |
| ♛ Krone der Wahl | Level-Ups bieten 4 statt 3 Items |
| ❦ Phönixfeder | Einmal wiederbeleben mit 50 % Hülle |
| ⌛ Zeitsplitter | Alle Gegner 15 % langsamer |

## 📖 Journal & Fortschritt

- Das **Journal** zeigt alle Items, Charaktere und Artefakte. Was noch nicht freigeschaltet ist, ist geschwärzt und zeigt die passende Challenge.
- Freischaltungen erscheinen nach dem Lauf mit einer Animation.
- **Profile:** Mehrere Spieler können eigene Profile anlegen. Der Fortschritt wird lokal im Browser gespeichert und nicht zwischen Geräten synchronisiert.

## 🛠️ Technik

- Reines **HTML5 Canvas** und JavaScript, keine Frameworks
- Schriften von Google Fonts (Orbitron, Rajdhani)
- Gehostet über **GitHub Pages**: Jeder Push auf `main` wird per GitHub Actions automatisch veröffentlicht (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
- `game.src.html` ist der Quellcode, `index.html` die daraus erzeugte Seite für GitHub Pages

## 📦 Selbst ausführen

1. Repo klonen oder `index.html` herunterladen
2. Datei im Browser öffnen, fertig

## 🔖 Versionen

Feste Meilensteine stehen unter [Releases](https://github.com/Marcopolo234231/neonvortex/releases).

- **v1.0**: Charaktere mit Schussarten, 32 Items, Challenges, Journal, Artefakte und Pickups

---

*Gebaut von [Marcopolo234231](https://github.com/Marcopolo234231) mit [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).*

hk21x/pgr1-recomp.readme:
# Project Gotham Racing - XBE Recomp

![Project Gotham Racing - native PC port](docs/images/pgr1-pc-port.webp)

An unofficial native PC port of the original Xbox version of Project Gotham Racing, with extended graphics options
and other enhancements. The game's own x86 code is statically recompiled into a Windows executable with the
[Xbox XBE Recomp](https://github.com/TGP482/XboxXBE-Recomp) tool; the Xbox's graphics, sound and system libraries are
reimplemented for Windows (Direct3D 12 or 11, XAudio2, SDL). It is not an emulator.

> [!NOTE]
> This project does not include any game assets. You must provide the files from your own legally acquired copy of
> the game to build and play.

## Supported Version

The European (PAL) Xbox release of Project Gotham Racing (title id 4D530003):

| Release | `default.xbe` SHA-1 |
| --- | --- |
| Europe (PAL), version 5 | `4878c3bdbd44663b64ce64986b313e8c6b7f8917` |

The log (`logs\pgr1.log`) names the SHA-1 of the `default.xbe` it found. Other releases (North American, Japanese,
Platinum Hits) have not been checked yet, and the game asks before starting one.

## Getting Started

There are two ways to get the game running. Both build it on your own PC from your own disc: the game's code is
never downloaded, only the tools and this project's source.

### The launcher (recommended)

`PGR1Launcher.exe` does everything for you: no Visual Studio, no Git, no command line, nothing installed in Windows
and no admin rights needed.

**You need:**
- Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit, and a GPU with Direct3D 12 or 11.
- Your own copy of the game (PAL): an `.iso` image of your disc, or a folder with the disc's files.
- About 15 GB free, and an internet connection for about 1.4 GB of build tools.

**Steps:**
1. Download `PGR1Launcher.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/hk21x/pgr1-recomp/releases/latest).
2. Put it in a folder of its own (for example `C:\Games\PGR1`) and run it. Everything it makes goes in a `PGR1`
   folder beside it. Windows may warn about an unrecognised app: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
3. **Your game:** choose your disc image or the folder with the disc's files. The launcher checks that it is a
   supported release.
4. **Build:** accept the license terms for Microsoft's C++ libraries and Windows SDK (the build uses them), then press
   **Build**. It downloads portable build tools (Clang, CMake, Ninja, Git and Microsoft's libraries), this project's
   source, and builds the game. The first build takes 30 to 90 minutes. You can stop it at any time; it carries on
   where it left off.
5. **Play:** press **Play**. The first start formats the emulated hard disk and copies the game's cache (about 90
   seconds of black screen and a short movie); later starts are quick.

When this project is updated the launcher shows **Update**: press it, then Play. **Remove the build files** frees
about 10 GB once the game is built (an update then builds everything again).

Files, all under the `PGR1` folder beside the launcher:
- `play\` the game: `PGR1.exe`, `pgr1.toml` (settings), `hdd\` (profiles, saves and caches), `logs\pgr1.log` (the game's
  log), `achievements.toml`
- `launcher.log` the launcher's log (send it with any problem building)
- `tools\` and `source\` the build tools and the source

To remove everything, delete the launcher and its `PGR1` folder (keep `play\hdd` if you want your saves).

### Building from source (developers)

**You need:** Windows 10 or 11 (64 bit), [Git](https://git-scm.com/download/win), Visual Studio 2022 (Community is
fine) with **Desktop development with C++** (`build.bat` offers to add **C++ Clang tools for Windows** and **C++ CMake
tools for Windows**), about 15 GB free, and your disc's files: `default.xbe` and its folders (`Async`, `FMV`,
`FrontEnd`, `Game`, `Images`, `media`, `Shaders`, ...), or an `.iso` image of the disc.

1. Clone the repository with its SDK:
   ```
   git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/hk21x/pgr1-recomp.git
   cd pgr1-recomp
   ```
   Cloned without `--recurse-submodules`? Run `git submodule update --init`.
2. Put your game files in the `assets` folder: `assets\default.xbe` with the game's folders beside it. With an `.iso`,
   put the `.iso` in `assets` and also copy `default.xbe` out of it into `assets` (the build recompiles from that file).
3. Run `build.bat` from Explorer or a command prompt. The first build takes 30 to 90 minutes; later builds are quicker.
   Do not run `xbe_symbols` or edit `config\game.toml`: the committed configuration is the one for the supported release.
4. Answer Y to "Play now?", or run `out\build\release\PGR1.exe`. It finds the `assets` folder beside itself or in any
   folder above it.

`launcher.bat` builds `PGR1Launcher.exe` itself. Files the game writes beside the exe: `pgr1.toml` (settings), `hdd\`
(saves and caches; delete it to start again from a first boot), `logs\pgr1.log`, `achievements.toml`, and
`CrashDumps\` if it crashes. [WINDOWS.md](WINDOWS.md) has more.

## Controls and Settings

**Settings window:** press **F1**, or **Back + Start** on a controller. Tabs: Display, Graphics, Game, Achievements,
General, Wheel and Controls. Changes are saved at once.

**Keyboard** (plays as controller 1 while the window has the focus; remap in Controls, two keys per input):

| Console input | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Steer / menus (left stick) | Arrow keys, or A / D |
| Accelerate / brake | W / S |
| A / B / X / Y | Enter or Space / Backspace / Q / E |
| Black / White | R / F |
| Start / Back | Escape or P / Tab |
| D-pad | Numpad 8 / 2 / 4 / 6 |
| Right stick, stick clicks | I J K L, C and V |

**Controllers:** Xbox, PlayStation and Switch controllers, with hot plugging and rumble; any console input can be
mapped to any controller input in Controls.

## Features

### Display
- **Display Modes** - Fullscreen, borderless window or window, at any resolution the monitor offers, applied at once.
- **Widescreen and Ultrawide** - The console game i

# Game Arena: starter kit quick start

Write a bot, play it against the practice bots on your own laptop, and watch every game in your
browser. You only need **Python 3.10 or newer**, plus the compiler for the language you write your
bot in. Nothing else to install, no admin rights, no internet.

> Organisers: the full platform specification is in [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md); this README is the one
> that ships in the starter kit.

## 1. Check Python (1 minute)

Open a terminal in this folder (on Windows: right-click the folder → *Open in Terminal*) and run:

| System | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `py arena.py doctor` (or `python arena.py doctor`) |
| macOS / Linux | `python3 arena.py doctor` |

`doctor` lists the compilers it found and tests every language. If Python itself is missing, install
it from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (Windows: tick **Add python.exe to PATH**).

## 2. Install the compiler for your language (only if `doctor` says it is missing)

| Your bot in | Windows | macOS | Ubuntu / Debian / Mint | Fedora / RHEL / Rocky | Arch | openSUSE |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Python** | nothing to do | nothing to do | nothing to do | nothing to do | nothing to do | nothing to do |
| **C / C++** | [WinLibs](https://winlibs.com/) (unzip, add its `bin` folder to PATH) or [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/): `pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc` | `xcode-select --install` | `sudo apt install build-essential` | `sudo dnf install gcc gcc-c++` | `sudo pacman -S gcc` | `sudo zypper install gcc gcc-c++` |
| **Java** | any JDK 17+ ([Adoptium](https://adoptium.net/)) | `brew install openjdk@17` or Adoptium | `sudo apt install openjdk-17-jdk` | `sudo dnf install java-17-openjdk-devel` | `sudo pacman -S jdk-openjdk` | `sudo zypper install java-17-openjdk-devel` |

Run `doctor` again afterwards. If the arena picks the wrong compiler, point it at the right one with
an environment variable (`ARENA_CC`, `ARENA_CXX`, `ARENA_JAVAC`, `ARENA_JAVA`, `ARENA_PYTHON`) or an
`arena.toml` file in this folder:

```toml
[toolchain]
cxx = "C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/g++.exe"
javac = "/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk/bin/javac"
java = "/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk/bin/java"
```

The server compiles with GCC on Linux. On a Mac the arena uses Apple clang and tells you so;
`#include <bits/stdc++.h>` still works there.

## 3. Play your first game (2 minutes)

1. Start the arena: `python3 arena.py` (Windows: `py arena.py`). Your browser opens
   `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`.
2. **Choose a game** on the page. The kit holds every game of the contest plus **Light Cycles**, a
   warm-up demo that is never scored. You can switch with **Change game** at any time.
3. Copy the template for that game from `templates/<game>/` (`bot.py`, `bot.cpp`, `bot.c` or
   `Main.java`). Each one is a complete, working bot: it reads the game, calls one `decide()`
   function and prints the move.
4. Drag your bot file onto **Add a bot**, choose an opponent and press **Play**. The replay opens
   underneath: press Space to play, and use the arrow keys to step through the game.

Read the rules and the exact input/output format in `games/<game>/statement.md` (also linked as
**Problem statement** at the top of the page).

Nothing you do in the local arena counts towards your score: only **Submit** on the contest
website is scored.

## 4. Improve your bot

- **Batch**: play 50 games (or more) against the practice bots, both sides of every map. You get
  wins, draws and losses, why your bot was eliminated, and its response times, plus a **Watch** link
  for every game.
- **Compare**: your new version against your previous one before you submit it.
- **Debug output**: print to stderr (`print(..., file=sys.stderr)`, `cerr`, `fprintf(stderr, ...)`,
  `System.err`). The viewer shows it turn by turn. Never print debug text to stdout, because stdout
  is read as your moves.
- **Speed**: the server limit is 100 ms per turn. Aim for under 50 ms; the arena warns you when
  your bot is too slow on more than 1% of turns. Your laptop is not the server, and the server's
  timing is what counts.

## Command line

Everything also works without a browser, which is handy for scripts and AI coding agents:

```text
python3 arena.py play  mybot.cpp greedy --game snakes --seed 17      # one match, prints the result, saves the replay
python3 arena.py batch mybot.cpp --game snakes --vs random_safe,greedy --games 100 --jobs 4
python3 arena.py compare v8.cpp v7.cpp --game snakes --games 200
python3 arena.py check mybot.cpp --game snakes                       # compile + one game; exit code 0 if fine
python3 arena.py watch mybot.cpp --game snakes --vs greedy           # replays in the browser every time you save
python3 arena.py doctor                                              # what is installed, for the help desk
```

On the command line, name the game with `--game` (`snakes`, `isolation`, or `lightcycles` for the
demo); the web page asks instead.

Batch results go to `arena_runs/<time>/summary.json`, with one replay per game. Compiled bots are
cached in `.arena_cache/`. The arena writes nothing outside this folder, and its web page is reachable
only from your own computer.

## Problems?

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `doctor` cannot find your compiler | Install it (table above) and open a **new** terminal so PATH updates, or set `ARENA_CXX` etc. |
| Your bot times out on turn 1 | It must print a move and **flush** stdout every turn. The templates show how. |
| `invalid move on turn N` | Print exactly one move line in the format the statement gives (for example `UP` or `3 4`), nothing else on stdout. |
| Port 8000 is busy | The arena uses the next free port and prints the address; or use `--port 8100`. |
| The browser did not open | Open the address printed in the terminal yourself. |

When asking organisers for help, run `python3 arena.py doctor` and send them its output, plus the
replay link with `&turn=N` if it is about a specific game.

# GSMLite

Responsive digital-goods store for Haiti: game top-ups, gift cards and subscriptions, paid with **MonCash** (automatic) or **NatCash** (staff-verified), plus an HTG/USD store-credit wallet. Built from *Website Blueprint v1.1*.

**Stack:** Next.js 15 (App Router) · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS 4 · PostgreSQL + Prisma 6 · Better Auth (Argon2id, sessions, TOTP 2FA) · next-intl (Kreyòl default, French, English, Spanish).

## Quick start

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # fill DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY (openssl rand -base64 32)
npm install
npm run db:deploy               # apply migrations
npm run db:seed                 # demo categories, products and demo gift-card codes
npm run setup:admin -- --email you@example.com --name "Your Name"   # prompts for a password
npm run dev                     # http://localhost:3000  →  /ht
```

Sign in to the back office at `/admin/login`. Two-factor authentication is mandatory for every staff account and is set up on first sign-in.

Without MonCash credentials the site runs MonCash in **mock mode** (a test approval page, no real money). Mock mode refuses to run in production unless `ALLOW_MOCK_PAYMENTS=1`.

## What is built

| Area | Included |
| --- | --- |
| Storefront | Home, store with search/sort/category filters, categories, product pages with variants and required player-ID fields, cart, checkout, payment guides, FAQ, about, contact, terms, privacy, refunds |
| Languages | `ht` (default), `fr`, `en`, `es`; locale URLs, cookie → browser language → Kreyòl, hreflang, canonical, sitemap, robots, JSON-LD (Organization, Product, Breadcrumb, FAQ) |
| Customer account | Dashboard with wallet card and stats, orders with delivered codes and timeline, saved player IDs, buy again, notifications, profile (language/currency), security (password, sessions) |
| Payments | MonCash adapter (sandbox/live/mock) verified server-side via MonCash's API on return, callback and a polling cron; NatCash manual flow with reference + optional screenshot and staff approval |
| Wallet | Double-entry, append-only ledger in integer minor units; HTG and USD balances; held funds; HTG↔USD exchange with expiring quotes; **no withdrawals** (store credit) |
| Fulfillment | Encrypted code inventory (AES-256-GCM, dedupe by HMAC, `SKIP LOCKED` assignment), manual delivery with notes, automatic refund to wallet on cancel |
| Fraud controls | One-time NatCash references (DB-unique), new-account daily limits, holds on large deposits, high-value order review queue, amount-mismatch flags, rate-limited auth |
| Images | Upload in the admin (JPG/PNG/WebP, up to 5 MB, content-checked): product main image + gallery of up to 8, category images, logo (light and dark), homepage hero image, social-share image. Stored on Vercel Blob (public), served through Next.js image optimization (AVIF/WebP, responsive sizes). Anything without an image falls back to a generated tile, the category emoji or the built-in logo |
| Operations | Automatic refund to the wallet for paid orders not delivered within N hours (setting, runs with the cron job); public order-tracking link (`/order-status/[id]?t=…`, no sign-in, codes stay private); reports with daily sales chart, top products, sales by payment method and CSV exports (orders, payments, ledger, customers) |
| Staff controls | Re-confirmation with the authenticator code (10 minutes) before wallet adjustments, role changes, 2FA resets and settings; two-person approval for wallet adjustments above a threshold; custom roles with per-permission checkboxes |
| Content | Homepage editor (reorder/hide sections, hero text per language, draft → preview → publish, version history); news articles with scheduling; SEO manager (page titles/descriptions per language, redirects for old links); translation editor for every interface text; theme editor (colors, rounding, animations) with contrast checks, live preview and rollback |
| Customer extras | Support tickets with screenshots and staff replies; referral program (link, store-credit reward after the friend's first delivered order, same-network self-referrals rejected); notification preferences; cart saved to the account across devices; data export (JSON) and self-service account deletion; optional two-step verification for customers; offline page (service worker) and data-saver mode |
| Store extras | Store filters (category incl. subcategories, platform/region tag, price range); subcategories; scheduled, dismissible announcement bar; custom pages built from blocks (text, image, button, FAQ); editable header/footer menus; newsletter sign-up with one-click unsubscribe |
| Payment methods | Add any number of extra manual methods (bank transfer, Sogebank, Western Union…) with logo, recipient and instructions per language, for orders and/or deposits, reviewed like NatCash; changing them needs a fresh 2FA code. Statement reconciliation: paste a NatCash/MonCash/bank statement (CSV or copied text) to match it against payments (matched, to approve, amount mismatch, unknown, missing) |
| Admin | Dashboard, orders, payment review, risk queue, products/variants/categories in 4 languages, code import, customers (status, wallet adjustments, accounts sharing a browser/IP), ledger, staff roles, settings (rate, limits, NatCash recipient, WhatsApp, announcement), audit log; media library (alt text, copy URL, delete unused, pick from any image field); security screen (staff sessions with sign-out, service status, shared browsers, sensitive actions); email screen (status, test send, log, template previews) |
| Design | Dark by default with a light/dark switch (choice remembered per visitor), blue accent, self-hosted fonts (Figtree body, Chakra Petch headings), glowing product cards, scrolling band under the hero, phone bottom navigation. Admin → Appearance controls default mode, light and dark colors (with contrast checks), motion style (Calm / Lively / Neon, always off for reduced-motion and data-saver vis

astroffnet/arc-hud.readme: # Arc HUD — Minecraft 1.20.1 (Forge + Fabric) **Автор:** arc4io · **Лицензия:** MIT · Описание для Modrinth (RU + EN): [docs/MODRINTH.md](docs/MODRINTH.md) **Arc HUD** — единый стиль для всего интерфейса Minecraft: аккуратный HUD, своя мини-карта и карта мира с навигатором и метками в мире, общая карта для сервера, панель хоста LAN, переработанные меню (одиночная и сетевая игра, создание мира, настройки), оптимизация FPS, рюкзаки и интеграции с популярными модами. *A unified style for the whole Minecraft UI: a polished HUD, a built-in minimap and world map with a navigator and in-world waypoints, a shared server map, a LAN host panel, redesigned menus, FPS optimizations, backpacks and integrations with popular mods.* --- ## Сборка через GitHub Actions (ничего ставить не нужно) 1. Создай новый репозиторий на GitHub (например `arc-hud`). 2. Загрузи туда **всё содержимое** этой папки (вместе со скрытой папкой `.github`). Через сайт: *Add file → Upload files*, перетащи файлы и папки. Или через git: ``` git init git add . git commit -m "Arc HUD 1.0.0" git branch -M main git remote add origin https://github.com/ТВОЙ_НИК/arc-hud.git git push -u origin main ``` 3. Открой вкладку **Actions** → workflow **Build Arc HUD** запустится сам (или нажми *Run workflow*). 4. Когда обе сборки станут зелёными, внизу страницы запуска в **Artifacts** будут два архива: - `archud-forge-1.20.1` → `archud-forge-1.20.1-1.0.0.jar` - `archud-fabric-1.20.1` → `archud-fabric-1.20.1-1.0.0.jar` 5. **Релиз:** создай тег `v1.0.0` (`git tag v1.0.0 && git push --tags`) — workflow сам опубликует GitHub Release с обоими .jar. Версия мода меняется в `forge/gradle.properties` и `fabric/gradle.properties` (`mod_version`). ## Структура ``` common/ — общий код и ресурсы (HUD, экраны, бхоп, рюкзаки, текстуры, языки) forge/ — Forge 47.x: регистрация, сеть, оверлеи, Curios fabric/ — Fabric (loader 0.16, API 0.92.2): регистрация, сеть, миксины, Trinkets, Mod Menu .github/workflows/build.yml — сборка обоих .jar ``` Оба загрузчика используют официальные маппинги Mojang, поэтому `common/` компилируется в оба мода без изменений. ## Зависимости | | Forge | Fabric | |---|---|---| | Обязательно | Forge 47+ | Fabric Loader 0.14.21+, Fabric API | | Слоты спины / пояса / амулета | **Curios** (рекомендуется) | **Trinkets** (рекомендуется) | | Кнопка «Моды» на главном экране | встроено | **Mod Menu** | Без Curios/Trinkets рюкзаки работают из инвентаря (клавиша открывает первый найденный рюкзак). ## Клавиши (все переназначаются) | Клавиша | Действие | |---|---| | **B** | открыть рюкзак (сначала на спине, потом в инвентаре / второй руке) | | **H** | переключить Arc HUD ↔ ванильный HUD | | **N** | включить / выключить BunnyHop | | **J** | настройки Arc HUD (не K — на K у Iris/Oculus переключение шейдеров) | | **M** | карта мира | | **U** | поставить метку здесь | | **Y** | меню меток (поиск, сортировка, DEL — удалить) | | **=** / **-** | масштаб мини-карты | | — | панель хоста LAN (не назначена; есть кнопка в меню паузы) | | — | сортировка инвентаря (по умолчанию не назначена, есть кнопка в инвентаре) | ## Что внутри **HUD (50+ функций, каждая отключается):** полосы здоровья/голода/брони/воздуха/опыта с плавной анимацией, поглощение, «след» урона, вспышка лечения, цвет HP от яда/иссушения/заморозки, виньетка при низком HP, насыщенность, HP и прыжок скакуна, новый хотбар, слот второй руки, эффекты с таймерами, инфо-панель (координаты, биом, измерение + мод, FPS, пинг, время, погода, скорость, свет), компас-лента с метками, цель (моб + HP + мод), прочность брони и инструментов, счётчики стрел и тотемов, энергия предметов, предупреждение о смертельном падении, цифры урона, подбор предметов, спидометр бхопа, темы измерений. Каждый блок можно привязать к любому краю экрана. **Карта и навигация:** - своя мини-карта (квадратная или круглая) и карта мира (**M**) — отдельно для каждого измерения и пещерных слоёв, сохраняется на диск; ночное затемнение, сетка чанков, слизневые чанки, след игрока, экспорт в PNG; - метки: свои, смерть (история из 5), спавн, Waystones, Tempad, от других игроков; фильтры, поиск, сортировка; - **метки в мире** — экранные маркеры (ромб, подпись, расстояние) без наложений, карточка у прицела, стрелки у края экрана; - **навигатор** — стрелка, расстояние, высота, время в пути, пересчёт координат Незер ↔ Верхний мир; - **общая карта** (если Arc HUD на сервере / у хоста): все видят то, что исследовали другие, игроки за пределами прорисовки и зоны их прогрузки на карте; **обмен метками** с игроком или со всеми. **Экраны в стиле Arc:** главное меню, **«Одиночная игра»** (карточки миров с иконками, поиск, подробности, играть / изменить / пересоздать / удалить), **«Сетевая игра»** (иконки серверов, MOTD, пинг, онлайн, LAN, **запоминание последнего сервера** с кнопкой «Продолжить»), добавление сервера и прямое подключение, создание мира со всеми вкладками и подменю (правила игры, эксперименты, датапаки, редактирование мира) — единый фон, поля ввода, флажки, вкладки и кнопки. Меню паузы, настройки (звук, чат, язык, внешний вид, спец. возможности, ресурспаки), управление, достижения, статистика, «Открыть для сети», список модов (Forge), инвентарь, чат. **Панель хоста (LAN):** список игроков с пингом, кик, бан/разбан, оператор, режим игры, ТП к игроку / призвать, вылечить, время, погода, сложность, PvP, игровые правила, белый список, сообщение всем, сохранение мира, адрес для друзей и **закрытие игры для сети**. **BunnyHop:** air-strafe по формуле Quake/Source, сохранение скорости при прыжке сразу после приземления. **Рюкзаки:** кожаный (27), железный (36), алмазный (54); слот спины Curios / Trinkets, своя клавиша. ## Оптимизация - **Сущности за стенами не рисуются** (occlusion culling): мобы, животные, предметы и т.п., полностью закрытые непрозрачными блоками, пропускаются. Вне поля зрения их и так

wowlocal/burn-rate.desc: An experimental 2D brawler on the Randori engine: fictional Silicon Valley AI-startup founders fight. Art made with Codex CLI image generation, sounds and music synthesized.
wowlocal/burn-rate.readme:
# Burn Rate

An experimental 2D brawler on the [Randori](https://github.com/wowlocal/randori)
engine: Silicon Valley AI startup founders fight over the last round of
funding. Every fighter is a fictional archetype, not a real person. All art
was generated with Codex CLI's image generation and processed by the scripts
here; all sounds and music are synthesized. Nothing comes from another game.

![Burn Rate's title screen](docs/screenshots/title.png)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![Picking founders for Stage Mode](docs/screenshots/founders.png) | ![Act 1 in the Garage](docs/screenshots/act1-garage.png) |
| ![Act 5 in the Server Farm](docs/screenshots/act5-server-farm.png) | ![Act 6 in the Board Room](docs/screenshots/act6-board-room.png) |

![VS on Sand Hill Road](docs/screenshots/vs-sand-hill.png)

The screenshots are frames captured from scripted runs of the macOS app.

## The founders

| Fighter | Archetype | Signature (D > A) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blitz | hoodie wunderkind CEO | Pitch Deck: a fan of slides |
| Dr. Vector | ML researcher | Gradient Beam: an energy ball |
| Vesta | VC in a fleece vest | Term Sheet: a rolled contract |
| Moonshot | ex-crypto hype bro | Pump: a gold coin |
| Ada | AI-safety lead | Guardrail: a hexagon shield |
| Gigawatt | GPU-hoarding compute baron | a GPU card (slow, strong) |
| Prompt | prompt-engineer streamer | a chat bubble (fast) |
| Intern | tireless intern | an energy-drink can (fastest, light) |
| Angel | angel investor | a golf ball |
| Viral | growth hacker | a megaphone sound wave |

Every founder also has D ^ A, a launching uppercut. Specials cost Hype (MP).

## Story: the Last Round

Omega Capital announces Series Ω, one check big enough to end the runway
problem forever, for the founder still standing in its boardroom on closing
day. Stage Mode plays the campaign in six acts of four missions each. Each
act ends with a boss: Blitz, Moonshot, Vesta, Ada, Gigawatt, and then
Omega's board. The ending depends on the difficulty. The settings screen's
STAGE row picks the act to start from. The design, with every mission's
line-up, is in [docs/STORY.md](docs/STORY.md).

| Act | Arena | Boss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Pre-Seed | the Garage | Blitz, the Wunderkind |
| 2 Seed | Demo Day | Moonshot, the Hype Man |
| 3 Series A | Sand Hill Road | Vesta, the Down Round |
| 4 Hypergrowth | the Open Office | Ada, the Safety Review |
| 5 The Compute War | the Server Farm | Gigawatt, the Compute Baron |
| 6 The Last Round | the Board Room | Series Ω: Vesta and Gigawatt |

## Arenas

Demo Day, Sand Hill Road, Server Farm, Open Office, Garage, Board Room, and
the engine's own road (Highway 101). VS can use any of them.

## Controls (player 1)

Arrows move (double-tap to run), A attacks, S jumps, D defends. Specials are
D, then a direction, then A. Player 2: T F G H, Z X C. Esc quits, F4 returns
to the menu.

## Build

Needs macOS 14+, Swift 6.4 (Xcode with the 6.4 toolchain) and Python 3 with
Pillow and NumPy. The engine is the `Vendor/randori` submodule:

```sh
git clone --recursive https://github.com/wowlocal/burn-rate.git
cd burn-rate
tools/build.sh                 # content, executables and BurnRate.app in build/
open build/BurnRate.app
```

`tools/build.sh BUILD_DIR` builds elsewhere; `BURNRATE_PYTHON` names the
Python (default `python3`) and `BURNRATE_TOOLCHAIN` a Swift toolchain's
`bin` (default Xcode's). `tools/smoke.sh` (a scripted match) and
`tools/playtest.py` (every founder and every mode, headless) check a build.

`tools/build.sh` stages the content (`tools/content/stage.py`: DATs, sprite
sheets, interface, sounds, music), runs `BurnRateContentBuilder` (the
engine's eight content packages and `GeneratedIdentity.swift`), builds the
app and the headless host, and assembles the app bundle. The raw art is in
`art/raw` (half-size copies made by `tools/art/archive.py`);
`tools/art/generate.py` and `generate_misc.py` make the full-size originals
with Codex CLI into `$BURNRATE_RAW`, and the same variable points the
build at them.

See [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) for the plan and its ledger,
[docs/ENGINE_CONTRACT.md](docs/ENGINE_CONTRACT.md) for what a game gives the
engine and [docs/INTERFACE_SLOTS.md](docs/INTERFACE_SLOTS.md) for the
interface's slots.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE): the code, the art in `art/`, the sounds and the
music. The engine, [Randori](https://github.com/wowlocal/randori), is a
separate project under the Apache License 2.0 (`Vendor/randori/LICENSE` and
`NOTICE`).
