gth27/repackd.desc: Install, update and play local game repacks on Linux with Proton (umu) or emulators
gth27/repackd.readme:
# repackd

Install and play game repacks on Linux with Proton.

> **Note**
> repackd is in early development. Expect bugs and changing behaviour. Back up your saves. To report an issue, include the output of "Copy diagnostics" (in a game's settings).

repackd is a desktop app for Linux, written in Rust with egui. It installs game repacks you already have (setup.exe-style installers such as the FitGirl format) into a separate Wine prefix per game, using umu-launcher and GE-Proton, and then launches them. Console games run through emulators you set up yourself.

Tested on Arch-based systems; builds and passes its tests on Debian 13 and Fedora 42. Other distributions should work but are untested.

repackd does not download games, torrents or updates. It only works with files you already have on your disk. Use it only with games you are entitled to use.

## Requirements

- `umu-launcher` (required, runs the games)
- `curl`
- A Vulkan-capable GPU driver
- `xdg-desktop-portal` (the folder and file pickers) and `xdg-utils` (opening folders); desktop environments ship both
- Rust 1.85 or newer (edition 2024), only to build. Distro-packaged Rust on Debian/Ubuntu is usually too old, so use rustup.
- Optional: `winetricks`, `7zip`, `libnotify`, `mangohud`, `gamemode`, `gamescope`

When a tool is missing, repackd detects your distribution and shows the matching install command.

## Install

### Arch-based

```
sudo pacman -S base-devel rust umu-launcher
sudo pacman -S --asdeps winetricks 7zip libnotify mangohud gamemode gamescope
git clone https://github.com/gth27/repackd
cd repackd
makepkg -si
```

### Debian / Ubuntu

Also applies to Mint. Get `umu-launcher` from the .deb on the [releases page](https://github.com/Open-Wine-Components/umu-launcher/releases).

```
sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libudev-dev curl
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
# install the umu-launcher .deb from the releases page, then optionally:
sudo apt install winetricks 7zip libnotify-bin mangohud gamemode gamescope
git clone https://github.com/gth27/repackd
cd repackd
cargo build --release
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin ~/.local/share/applications
cp target/release/repackd ~/.local/bin/
cp repackd.desktop ~/.local/share/applications/
```

### Fedora

```
sudo dnf install gcc pkgconf-pkg-config systemd-devel curl umu-launcher
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
sudo dnf install winetricks 7zip libnotify mangohud gamemode gamescope
git clone https://github.com/gth27/repackd
cd repackd
cargo build --release
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin ~/.local/share/applications
cp target/release/repackd ~/.local/bin/
cp repackd.desktop ~/.local/share/applications/
```

### Other distributions

openSUSE build dependencies (untested): `gcc pkg-config systemd-devel`. Install `umu-launcher` from your package manager or the [releases page](https://github.com/Open-Wine-Components/umu-launcher/releases).

```
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
git clone https://github.com/gth27/repackd
cd repackd
cargo build --release
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin ~/.local/share/applications
cp target/release/repackd ~/.local/bin/
cp repackd.desktop ~/.local/share/applications/
```

The `repackd.desktop` copy is optional. Make sure `~/.local/bin` is in your `PATH`.

## Usage

### Add a game
1. Press "Add game". Pick a repack folder (it gets installed) or a game that is already unpacked (it gets imported).
2. To add many at once, press "Import a folder…". It finds every repack and unpacked game inside.

### Install
1. Press "INSTALL" on the game's page. It shows the disk space it needs.
2. With "Check the files before and after installing (FitGirl's checksums)" on (default), the files are verified first. Bad files are reported.
3. By default the installer runs without its own windows. Turn off "Install games without the installer's own windows" in Settings to click through them yourself. Update installers show their windows, except FitGirl's own (see Updates).
4. If an install fails, press "INSTALL AGAIN". The log is in Settings.
5. Already-unpacked games show "SET UP", which only creates the Wine prefix.

### Play
Press "PLAY". The game page shows playtime and a ProtonDB rating. If a known problem is detected, a fix button may appear (for example a winetricks verb or another Proton).

### Settings per game
Press "Game settings" on the game page.
- Proton: pick which version this game uses. Download more under Settings, "Proton versions".
- Launch options, Environment and Switches (MangoHud, GameMode, Gamescope, FSR, DXVK FPS counter, dedicated GPU). Only tools you have installed are listed.
- "Run .exe in this prefix…" for mod installers and trainers, and "Run winetricks".
- "Show in the app menu" adds a menu entry.
- "Check files", "Clear shader cache", "Copy diagnostics".

### Updates
1. Put the update folders (FitGirl) or archives (scene .rar/.7z/.zip) next to the game or in Downloads.
2. A game with an update shows "Update available" and a "Review" button. You can also press "Check for updates", "Add update folders…" or "Add update archives…" in Game settings, Updates.
3. Check the order, then press "Apply". Updates run oldest first. The installer window appears and waits for your click.
FitGirl's own updates install without a window (like her base repacks), and RUNE updates are checked before their window opens: a game whose files differ from what RUNE expects is refused with those files named.
HDiffPatch updates (PATCH.exe + Patch.bin) are applied natively; repackd downloads the official hpatchz once if it isn't installed.
4. With "Back up the files an update changes, so it can be undone" on (default), "Undo update to v…" puts the files back.

### Steam
1. Close Steam. It overwrites its shortcut list on exit, so repackd refuses while it runs.
2. Press "Add to Steam" on the game page. Steam then starts the game through its launch script.
3. For artwork, add a free SteamGridDB key in Settin

commits.msg:
Window-free updates for FitGirl, a pre-check for RUNE

- FitGirl's own update installers run unattended like her base repacks
  (detected by her MD5 list, fg-*.bin files or her name in the header)
- RUNE updates: the 116 files and CRC32C values RUNE checks are read
  from its Setup.exe and checked before its window opens; a game whose
  files differ is refused with those files named, before any undo copy
- Apply hover says which updates open a window

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Apply HDiffPatch updates natively instead of through the patcher window

TENOKE-style updates (Update/PATCH.exe + Patch.bin) wrap hpatchz in a
GUI that fails under Wine (exit status 5). repackd now patches in place
with hpatchz -C-all -f: the one on PATH, or the pinned official v4.6.8
build downloaded once and checked against its SHA-256. The window is
the fallback when the tool can't be had.

Drop the undo copy when an update fails without touching the game

A PATCH.exe update snapshots the whole game first; on NTFS that is a

seooohyun526-hue/badang-sorang-webzine.desc: 제주 해녀의 바다와 삶을 담은 웹진 '바당소랑' (바당은 바다, 소랑은 사랑)
seooohyun526-hue/badang-sorang-webzine.readme:
# 바당소랑 웹진

제주 해녀의 바다와 삶을 담은 웹진입니다. '바당'은 바다, '소랑'은 사랑이라는 뜻의 제주어예요.

- 웹진 주소: https://lxwebzine.hankyung.com/2026-1/team6/
- 서버(한경닷컴)는 이 저장소의 **`site/` 폴더만** 올려요. 첫 화면은 `site/index.html` 이에요.

## site/ (서버에 올라가는 폴더)

```
site/
  index.html      웹진 (글 · 디자인 · 동작이 모두 들어 있어요, 약 350KB)
  en/index.html   영어판 주소 (…/en/) — 내용은 같고 영어로 · 제목 · 공유 미리보기도 영어
  ja/index.html   일본어판 주소 (…/ja/)
  media/          사진(webp) · 첫 화면 영상(mp4) · 파도 소리(m4a) — index.html 이 상대 경로(media/…)로 불러와요
  fonts/          글꼴(woff2)
  og.jpg          공유 미리보기 그림 (1200×630)
  webzine.json    웹진메인 카드 정보 (이름 · 문구 · 사진 · 칸 링크)
```

`site/` 안의 파일은 모두 아래 빌드로 만들어져요. 직접 고치지 말고 `build/` 를 고친 뒤 다시 빌드해요.

## 미리 보기 (GitHub Pages)

- 주소: https://seooohyun526-hue.github.io/badang-sorang-webzine/
- `gh-pages` 브랜치에 `site/` 폴더만 올라가 있어요. `site/` 를 다시 만든 뒤 커밋하고, 아래 명령으로 Pages 도 갱신해요.

```bash
git push origin `git subtree split --prefix site main`:refs/heads/gh-pages --force
```

## 웹진 구성

| 칸 (주소) | 내용 |
|---|---|
| 첫 화면 | 사라지는 해녀 — 1970년부터 줄어든 해녀 수를 '색이 빠지는 해녀'로 보여 줘요 |
| 해녀 이야기 (`#stories`) | 해녀 인터뷰 카드 (영상 · 사진) |
| 목적 (`#purpose`) | 유네스코 인류무형문화유산 — 해산물 인형을 누르면 물질 · 잠수굿 · 해녀노래 · 공동체 이야기 팝업 |
| 바다 지키기 (`#ocean`) | 갯닦기 · 금채 · 바다 쓰레기 수거 BEFORE / AFTER + '응원 온도' 창 |
| 해녀의 바당길 (`#badatgil`) | 미니 게임 안내와 HIGH SCORE (게임: https://haenyeo-ocean-online.vercel.app/) |
| 바당소랑 (`#about`) | 우리 소개 — 같이 잇다, 가치를 잇다 |

화면 오른쪽에는 '게임하러 가기' · '해녀 응원하러 가기' 미니 팝업이 떠 있어요.

## 다시 만들기

Python 3 · Pillow · NumPy · OpenCV 가 필요해요 (카드 사진은 playwright + 크롬도). 저장소 맨 위에서 실행해요.

```bash
BS_FONT=gotgam BS_PURPOSE=v2 BS_GAME=v2 BS_OCEAN=v2 BS_SEABG=v2 PYTHONUTF8=1 python build/build_sea.py build/base_loader.html build site/index.html media/haenyeo-line.svg
```

- 지금 올라간 웹진은 글씨체 `BS_FONT=gotgam`(제목 상주곶감체 · 본문 학교안심 보드마카)이에요. 빼면 예전 기본 글씨체로 만들어져요.
- 상주곶감체 파일은 저장소의 `build/fonts/` 에 없어요(글꼴 파일 수정 · 재배포 금지). 다시 만들 때는 눈누(https://noonnu.cc/font_page/786)에서 받은 `SANJUGotgam.woff` 를 `build/fonts/` 에 넣어 두세요. 웹진(`site/fonts/`)에는 웹폰트로 쓰기 위해 원본 그대로 담겨요.

- 결과: `site/index.html` 과 `site/media/` · `site/fonts/` (사진 · 영상 · 글꼴을 HTML 안에 넣지 않고 파일로 따로 둬요. 사진은 webp · 한 장 500KB 이하)
- 웹진 이름(브라우저 탭 · 공유 미리보기)은 `바당소랑_웹진_1` 이에요. 바꾸려면 `BS_SITE_NAME=…` 을 앞에 붙여요.
- `BS_SEABG=v2` 를 빼면 실사 바다 배경이 없는 판이 만들어져요.

웹진메인 카드(`site/webzine.json`) · 카드 사진 · 공유 미리보기 그림(`site/og.jpg`)은 빌드한 다음에 이렇게 만들어요. 지금 웹진 화면을 찍어 잘라 쓰고, 문구는 웹진 안의 글에서 그대로 가져와요.

```bash
python build/tools/make_cards.py
```

내 컴퓨터에서 미리 볼 때는 파일을 두 번 눌러 열기보다 간단한 서버로 여는 게 정확해요 (파도 소리 · 배경 물결이 브라우저 보안 규칙 때문에 파일로 열면 안 될 수 있어요).

```bash
python -m http.server 8000 -d site
```

## 폴더

```
site/            서버에 올라가는 완성본 (빌드가 만들어요)
build/           빌드 스크립트와 재료
  build_sea.py   빌드 스크립트 (base_loader.html 에 각 칸의 코드 · 그림을 차례로 넣고, site/ 로 내보내요)
  *_data.js      글 · 숫자 데이터 (문구를 바꿀 때는 여기를 고쳐요)
  *.js / *.css   각 칸의 동작과 모양
  tools/         그림 배경 지우기 · 장면 그리기 · 글꼴 줄이기 · 카드 만들기 도구
media/           그림 원본 (캐릭터 · 털실 인형 · 장면)
```

## 글씨체 시안

`BS_FONT=gumi` 를 붙여 빌드하면 제목 = 낭만있구미체(구미시), 본문 = 학교안심 보드마카(KERIS · OFL)로 바뀐 시안이 만들어져요 (게임 칸은 그대로).
낭만있구미체 파일은 배포가 금지라 저장소에 없어요. 시안을 만들 때 `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/projectnoonnu/2410-1@1.0/GumiRomanceTTF.woff2` 를 `build/fonts/` 에 받아 두세요.
시안은 `site/` 가 아닌 다른 폴더로 내보내요 (예: `preview/gumi/index.html`).

다른 제목 글씨체 시안도 같은 방식이에요 (본문은 학교안심 보드마카, 유네스코 칸 제목 · 게임 칸은 그대로):

| BS_FONT | 제목 글씨체 | 글꼴 파일 (`build/fonts/`) | 라이선스 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gotgam` | 상주곶감체 (지금 올라간 판) | `SANJUGotgam.woff` (저장소에 없음) | 웹 임베딩 가능 · 수정 · 재배포 금지 |
| `cafe24` | 카페24 클래식타입 | `Cafe24ClassicType-Regular.woff2` | SIL OFL 1.1 |
| `keris` | 케리스 케듀체 B | `KERISKEDU_B.woff2` | SIL OFL |
| `mulgyeol` | 학교안심 물결 B | `TTHakgyoansimMulgyeolB.woff2` | SIL OFL |

## 문구 · 링크 바꾸는 곳

| 바꿀 것 | 파일 |
|---|---|
| 게임 주소 · 게임 미니 팝업 문구 | `build/game_data.js` (`GAME.url`, `popButton`, `popBubble`) |
| 응원 미니 팝업 문구 | `build/float_data.js` (`SUPPORT`) |
| 바다 지키기 칸 글 · 응원 온도 창 · 후원 · 박물관 주소 | `build/clean_data.js` (`CLEAN`, `CLEAN.cheer`, `CLEAN.cta`) |
| 목적 칸 글 · 해녀문화 팝업 | `build/explore_data.js` (`SEA`) |
| 해녀문화 팝업 사진 | `media/popup/` 에 `01_물질_대표.jpg` 같은 이름으로 넣고 다시 빌드 |
| 영어 · 일본어 번역 | `build/i18n_en.js` · `build/i18n_ja.js` (왼쪽 한국어 원문 → 오른쪽 번역) |

## 응원 온도 창 — 모두의 응원 (공용 저장소)

- '바다 지키기' 칸의 응원 창은 `build/clean_data.js` 의 `CLEAN.cheer.supabase`(url · anonKey)가 있으면 모든 방문자의 좋아요 · 응원을 함께 보여 줘요. 비어 있으면 예전처럼 각자 브라우저에만 저장돼요.
- 저장소는 Supabase 하나예요 (서버 따로 없음). 만들기 · 연결 방법은 [cheer-supabase/README.md](cheer-supabase/README.md) 에 있어요.

## 게임 '해녀의 바당길' (웹진 안 /game/)

- Unity 게임을 웹진 주소 `…/2026-1/team6/game/` 에서 바로 실행해요. 화면 · 실행 파일은 `site/game/`, 통합 코드는 `game-integration/` 이에요.
- 점수 · 랭킹 · 응모는 기존 Vercel 서버와 Neon DB 를 그대로 써요. 한경 서버에 API 연결(Node + Apache 경로 한 줄)이 있어야 동작해요.
- 분석은 웹진과 같은 GTM `GTM-M2LF732B` (GA4 `G-Z57PKSMHPK`). 남은 서버 · GTM 설정은 [game-integration/WEBZINE-INTEGRATION-KO.md](game-integration/WEBZINE-INTEGRATION-KO.md) 에 있어요.

## 언어 (한국어 · English · 日本語)

- 언어마다 주소가 따로 있어요: 한국어 `…/` · 영어 `…/en/` · 일본어 `…/ja/`. 오른쪽 위 언어 줄을 누르면 그 주소로 이동하고, 보던 칸 · 상세 화면은 그대로 따라가요. 세 페이지는 서로를 검색엔진에 알려 줘요(hreflang).
- 한 파일 판(`BS_SPLIT=0`)은 주소가 하나라, 고른 언어를 브라우저에 기억해서(`localStorage 'bs-lang'`) 같은 자리로 다시 열어요.
- 번역 사전은 `build/i18n_en.js`(English) · `build/i18n_ja.js`(日本語) 예요. 두 사전의 왼쪽(한국어 원문)은 똑같아요. 한국어 글을 고치면 두 사전의 왼쪽도 똑같이 고쳐 주세요. 한 글자라도 다르면 그 글만 한국어로 남아요.
- 다른 언어를 더하려면 사전을 복사해 `build/i18n_<언어>.js` 로 저장하고, 맨 위를 `I18N.<언어> = {` 로 바꾼 뒤 오른쪽만 고쳐요. 언어 줄 버튼은 `build/lang.js` 의 `LANGS` 에 있어요.

- 번역 입히는 코드는 `build/i18n.js`, 언어별 모양 맞춤은 `build/i18n.css` 예요 (그 언어일 때만 적용돼요). 일본어는 컴퓨터 · 휴대폰의 일본어 고딕 · 명조로 보여요.

### Max FPS. Low latency. Smooth frame times. Tuned to *your* rig, not someone else's.   **[Features](#-features) · [Quick start](#-quick-start) · [What it changes](#-what-it-changes) · [Pro tips](#-pro-tips-outside-the-game) · [FAQ](#-faq) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)**
--- ## 🔥 What's new in v1.7 > **Field of view slider** that starts at your current FOV · **camera shake down to Minimal** · audio sliders keep your volumes · > **tick boxes** to choose exactly which changes apply · **HUD tuning**: square rotating minimap, magenta enemies and a HUD you can pull toward your crosshair. > [Full changelog →](CHANGELOG.md) --- ## 📸 In action
See every change before it happens. Tick what you want, hover any row to learn what it does and why it suits your rig.

Locked and loaded. Run it any time to check your config is still tuned.
--- ## ⚡ Features Most config packs copy one person's file onto every PC. That overwrites your monitor, GPU, audio device and driver info with theirs, and ignores what your hardware can actually do. **This tool reads your own config, detects your rig, and only changes the values that matter.**
#### 🎯 Built for your rig CPU cores, GPU, video memory, resolution and refresh rate decide the settings, from a GTX 1650 to an RTX 5090. #### 🔍 See every change Each setting shows what it is now and what it becomes. Hover for what it does, how much it matters, and **why**. #### ☑️ You choose Tick boxes on every change. Keep what you like, apply the rest. Your choices are remembered.
#### 🗺️ A HUD that works Square, rotating minimap (about 27% more map), magenta enemies that pop, and a slider to pull the HUD toward your crosshair. #### 🎧 Hear them first Headphone mode keeps 3D headphone audio and cuts music and speaker processing, so footsteps come through clean. #### 👁️ Steady view FOV slider from 90 to 120 and camera shake at the game's minimum, so your crosshair stays put.
#### 🛡️ One-click undo Every apply makes a timestamped backup. Pick one and hit **Restore**. #### ✅ Game-checked Every value is checked against what the game allows. Anything invalid is skipped, never forced. #### 🔄 Auto-updates The tool checks for a new version when it opens. One click and it updates itself.
--- ## 🚀 Quick start > [!IMPORTANT] > Launch Call of Duty **once** first and get to the main menu, then close it. That creates the settings files the tool tunes. | Step | | |:---:|---| | **1** | **[Download the latest release](https://github.com/FiTH-g1gGLe/COD-MW4-Config-Tool/releases/latest/download/MW4-Performance-Tool.zip)** and unzip it anywhere. | | **2** | Close the game, then double-click **`Run MW4 Config Tool.bat`**. | | **3** | **YOUR RIG** fills in by itself. Pick your **LOADOUT** (goal, audio, HUD position, FOV). Hover anything for a recommendation. | | **4** | Untick anything in **CHANGES TO APPLY** you'd rather keep, then hit **APPLY**. | | **5** | In game: **Graphics → Restart Shaders Pre-Loading**, then restart the game. | > [!TIP] > If the game asks to *"Set Optimal Settings & Run In Safe Mode"*, choose **No**. It would undo your tuning. --- ## 🧩 What it changes ### Smart settings, from your hardware | Your hardware | Controls | Rule | |---|---|---| | 🧩 **CPU cores** | Render worker threads | physical cores − 1 (P-cores on Intel 12th–14th gen) | | 🎮 **GPU vendor** | Latency | NVIDIA **Reflex** · AMD **Anti-Lag 2** · Intel **XeLL** | | 🖼️ **GPU + VRAM + resolution** | Image | Native **SMAA + CAS sharpening**; **DLSS / FSR / XeSS** at 4K or under 8 GB VRAM (GTX cards get FSR) | | 💾 **Video memory** | VRAM budget, textures | 12 GB+ → 0.9 · 8–11 GB → 0.8 · under 8 GB → 0.7 | | 🖥️ **Refresh rate** | FPS cap | refresh − 3 to keep G-SYNC/FreeSync active (uncapped above 300 Hz) | ### Your loadout | Option | Choices | |---|---| | **Goal** | **Max FPS** (lowest textures, 2× filtering) or **Visibility** (sharper textures and 8× filtering, scaled to your VRAM) | | **Image** | Auto · Native + SMAA + sharpening · Upscaler | | **FPS cap** | Auto · U

# Johnson Family Game Night

Party games on the TV, played on everyone's phones. Open the site on a TV or laptop, pick a game, and everyone joins with a 4-letter PIN or by scanning the QR code. No accounts, no app.

## Games

- **Flaugin** (Memphis slang for lying, fronting, faking it). Everyone gets the secret word except whoever is flaugin'. Give one-word clues, sniff out the faker, vote them out. 3 to 30 players. Also has a one-phone pass-and-play mode.

## How it works

- `index.html` + `app.js`: static site, served by GitHub Pages.
- Live rooms use Supabase Realtime (broadcast + presence).
- Secret cards come from the `flaudjer` Supabase edge function, so each phone only receives its own card. The word and Flaugin list never reach other phones until the reveal.
- Data lives in `flaudjer_rooms` / `flaudjer_players` (RLS on, no browser access). Rooms older than a day are cleaned up automatically.

# ディクテオンの迷宮

女神あてなのお宝さがし ― 女神あてなと相棒のフクロウ・グラウクスが主人公の、トルネコ／シレン風ローグライク。
スマホのホーム画面に追加すると、オフラインでも遊べます。

**遊ぶ：** https://chorry00.github.io/Athena/

## スマホに入れる

一度だけ、通信できる場所で次の操作をします。2回目からは機内モードでも起動できます。

**iPhone（Safari）**
1. 上のURLを Safari で開く
2. 共有ボタン（□に↑）→「ホーム画面に追加」
3. ホーム画面のアイコンから起動する

**Android（Chrome）**
1. 上のURLを Chrome で開く
2. 右上の︙ →「ホーム画面に追加」または「アプリをインストール」
3. ホーム画面のアイコンから起動する

## セーブデータ

- セーブは自動で、その端末の中に保存されます。
- 別の端末や Claude 版から引っこすときは、神殿の「設定と遊び方」→「データを書き出す」で出た文字をコピーし、引っこし先の「データを読み込む」に貼りつけます。
- ホーム画面のアプリを削除すると、セーブデータも消えます。先に書き出しておいてください。

## 更新のしかた（開発用）

ゲーム本体は `game.html` です。直したあとに公開用ファイルを作りなおします。

```sh
pip install fonttools brotli pillow
python3 tools/build.py
```

`index.html`・`sw.js`・`manifest.webmanifest`・`fonts/`・`icons/` が作りなおされます。
`sw.js` の版番号が変わるので、スマホ側は次の起動時に新しい版へ切りかわります。

## ライセンス

フォント DotGothic16 は SIL Open Font License 1.1 です（`fonts/OFL.txt`）。
`fonts/DotGothic16-subset.woff2` は、ゲームで使う文字だけに絞った派生版です。

NaraKitty/DBZ64.readme:
# Dragon Ball Z on the Nintendo 64

**Game Boy Advance classics, recompiled to run natively on N64 hardware.**

![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Nintendo%2064-red)
![Also runs on](https://img.shields.io/badge/runs%20on-Analogue%203D-black)
![Resolution](https://img.shields.io/badge/view-320%C3%97240-blue)
![Target](https://img.shields.io/badge/target-60%20FPS-brightgreen)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial-lightgrey)

| Game | Status |
|---|---|
| **Dragon Ball Z: The Legacy of Goku II** (USA) | Playable. Runs on real hardware (tested on the Analogue 3D). |
| **Dragon Ball Z: Buu's Fury** (USA) | In progress: next on the list. |

This is not an emulator running on the N64. Every ARM and Thumb instruction
of the original cartridge (2,282 functions, 67,500 instructions for *Legacy of
Goku II*) is translated ahead of time into C. That C is compiled for the N64's
VR4300 CPU and linked against a runtime that stands in for the GBA hardware:
graphics, sound, DMA, timers, interrupts and saves. The result is a normal
N64 ROM that you can play on a console, on an Analogue 3D, or in an
emulator.

## Highlights

- **A true 320×240 view.** Field maps are not stretched. You see more of the
  world: the extra margins are drawn from the game's own map data. Enemies,
  projectiles and NPCs live in the wider view because the game's culling is
  widened at every check. The HUD and dialogue boxes are moved out to the
  screen edges. Title, menu and status screens stay pixel-exact and centred.
- **Hardware-accelerated graphics.** The GBA's tile and sprite engine is
  rebuilt on the N64's RDP. It covers background layers, sprites, flips,
  alpha blending and brightness effects. Its output is pixel-identical to a
  reference software renderer in every frame tested.
- **The real soundtrack.** The game's own music engine and sound effects run
  as recompiled code. Its hottest mixing loops are replaced by native C that
  produces byte-identical audio.
- **Saves.** The cartridge's EEPROM is emulated and stored in the N64's
  cartridge SRAM, with a checksum and a backup copy.
- **Built for real consoles.**
  - Guest memory is mapped through the VR4300's TLB, so a guest memory access
    is a single load or store.
  - Frame skip keeps the game speed and music steady if a frame runs long.
  - At boot, a self-test checks the CPU features the port relies on and names
    any that misbehave instead of showing a black screen.
- **Verified against a reference.**
  - The PC build of the same recompiled code was compared frame by frame
    with the mGBA emulator, covering pictures, audio and RAM.
  - The N64 build matches the PC build pixel for pixel.

## Controls

| GBA | N64 |
|---|---|
| D-pad | D-pad or analog stick |
| A, B | A, B |
| L | L or Z |
| R | R |
| Start | Start |
| Select | C-Down |

C-Up shows a performance overlay with fps, frames drawn, CPU time and
cartridge reads.

## Playing it

**You need your own copy of the game.** No ROM, BIOS or game data is included
in this repository. The build reads your cartridge dump and checks its SHA-1:

| Game | Dump | SHA-1 |
|---|---|---|
| The Legacy of Goku II | USA, `ALFE` | `18e0715dec419f3501c301511530d2edcd590f8b` |
| Buu's Fury | USA, `BG3E` | `f1c4b07554d2a3b1ad2f325307051e775ce68087` |

The ROM you build contains your dump, so don't share it.

**Hardware:**
- An N64 with an Expansion Pak (8 MB), or an Analogue 3D.
- A flash cart such as SummerCart64 or EverDrive 64.

**Analogue 3D:**
- The built-in Expansion Pak can be switched off per game. If the ROM says
  it is missing, turn it on in the game's settings in the Library.
- SummerCart64 is known to work well. EverDrive carts need current cart
  firmware.

**EverDrive 64:**
- The ROM header requests SRAM 256 Kbit saves. If your cart OS ignores
  that, set the save type to SRAM 32K by hand.
- Saves are written to the SD card when you reset back to the EverDrive menu,
  so do that before powering off.

**Emulators:** ares is recommended, as it is accurate enough for the
TLB-based memory model. Enable the Expansion Pak.

## Building

You need:
- WSL (Ubuntu) with the [libdragon](https://github.com/DragonMinded/libdragon)
  toolchain (`preview` branch) installed at `/opt/libdragon`.
- Python 3 with `capstone`.

The build runs through a space-free path to the repository:

```bash
ln -s "/mnt/c/path/to/this/repo" ~/dbzn64
```

1. **Find the game's code.** The ROM is only read:

   ```bash
   python3 tools/analyze.py baserom.gba games/log2/game.toml gen/analysis
   ```

2. **Translate it to C.** The output is derived from your ROM, so keep it
   local:

   ```bash
   python3 tools/recomp.py baserom.gba gen/analysis/functions.json gen/c 24 --game log2
   ```

3. **Build the N64 ROM** from a build directory outside the repository.
   `dbz.z64` is written to the current directory:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ../n64build && cd ../n64build
   make -f ~/dbzn64/platform/n64/Makefile GAME=log2 BUILD_DIR=$PWD \
        GEN=$OLDPWD/gen/c BASEROM=$OLDPWD/baserom.gba
   ```

   The ROM contains your GBA dump, so don't share it, and keep it out of
   synced folders. From Git Bash on Windows, `tools/build_release.sh OUT.z64`
   runs the same build through WSL. It also removes any leftover test
   script, which would otherwise boot the ROM in test mode. The RDP renderer
   is the default; `USE_RDP=0` builds the CPU reference renderer.

A PC test build (`GAME=log2 platform/host/build.sh GEN OUT`) runs the same
recompiled code headless. It writes screenshots, audio and saves for
validation; it is the test bench every change is checked on.
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` explains how everything fits together, and
`docs/WIDESCREEN.md` covers the 320×240 view.

### Games

The framework is shared by Webfoot's GBA *Dragon Ball Z* games. Everything
specific to one game lives in `games/<game>/`: `game.toml` (code discovery),
`game.h` (what the runtime needs: IRQ dispatcher, save magic, ROM identity,

Pace the game by the audio clock: full speed and steady music at 50 Hz too

On the Analogue 3D the ROM ran in PAL timing: the overlay showed 49.9 fps
with only ~9 ms of work per frame.  Frames were paced by vsync, so the

- The game is now scheduled in real time at audio_frequency / 267.52
  frames per second (each GBA frame makes 280896/1050 samples), which is
  the N64's own refresh on a 60 Hz console.  When it falls more than half
  a frame behind, the frame is not drawn and the next game frame runs at
  once (at most 2 in a row).  The vsync re-anchoring that locked the game
  to a 50 Hz display is gone; banked time is capped at one frame.
- The ROM header now says USA (region E): flash carts set the console's
  TV mode from it and may pick PAL when it is unset.

20 of 120 frames undrawn, audio never short.  At 60 Hz nothing changes
(0 frames skipped).

ppu_soft: transparent OBJ texels still pass their priority down

The hardware (and mGBA, the oracle) builds the OBJ line in OAM order and,
where a later OBJ with a better priority has a transparent texel over an
OBJ pixel already drawn, gives that pixel the later OBJ's priority (and
semi-transparency) while keeping its colour.  A low-priority OBJ can then
show through a higher-priority BG.  ppu_soft ignored transparent texels.

Found by rendering mGBA's own video state with ppu_soft over a
200,000-frame random-input Buu's Fury run: on the map screen the player
marker (OBJ 3, priority 3) sits under the scroll arrow (OBJ 4, priority 0,
transparent at the tip) and shows over the frame (BG0, priority 0).  mGBA
draws 1-4 orange pixels there, ppu_soft drew the frame; 75 of 200 frames
the per-frame comparison could not explain.  With the quirk: those
checkpoints match mGBA, the 200k run's remaining 125 differing frames are
all scan-out timing, and 1,453 renderer checkpoints (gameplay script,
fuzz runs, multiplayer) match except 9 frames whose state changes after
scan-out.  LoG2: the oracle's 404 video states still render identically
and LoG2's host output is byte-identical to base (727 files).

The N64 RDP renderer (platform/n64/render, not in this branch) needs the
same rule.

Interpreter fallback: keep the registers recompiled callees preserve

Recompiled code keeps the registers a function saves and restores in C
locals; only its callers' summaries say they survive.  After it returns,
cpu.r[] can hold a callee's working values for them (sp, r4-r11, zeroes
for registers it pushed without loading).  The interpreter, which runs a
function that has no recompiled code (a dispatch miss) and continues from
cpu.r[], then lost its own sp and callee-saved registers whenever that
function called recompiled code.  The top-level loop had the same problem
after running a recompiled continuation.

tools/recomp.py now emits gba_func_mod[] (each function's ABI summary MOD,
parallel to gba_func_table).  The interpreter's calls and tail jumps into
recompiled code and gba_run_from() save r0-r14 and the flags before and,
after a normal return, put back what the callee's summary says it keeps.
Only the interpreter paths change; generated function bodies are the same.

Test: a scratch harness interprets a pseudo-random half of the functions
without their callees (every interpreted function calls recompiled code
and the other way round, as on a dispatch miss).  Before: Buu's Fury hangs
at boot within ~150 interpreted calls on every seed; LoG2 crashes or
diverges.  After: the Buu gameplay script (4 seeds, 10,200 frames) and a
60,000-frame random-input run (2 seeds), and LoG2 20,000 fuzz frames (2
seeds) give PNGs, RAM outside the stack, WAV and save identical to the
all-recompiled run.  LoG2's normal output stays byte-identical to the base
commit (5 runs, 727 files).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recomp: enter functions with code below the entry; fix fused compares

Two code generation bugs found bringing up Buu's Fury:

- A function body is emitted in address order. When the walk reaches code
  below the entry (a shared tail reached by a branch, like newlib's ARM
  memset falling into the word-fill loop above it), the C function started
  executing at the lowest address instead of the entry. It now jumps to the
  entry first. LoG2's only such function enters with an unconditional
  branch to its first instruction, so its code is unchanged.

- A compare fused with a later conditional branch reads the compare's
  temporaries (fa, fb, fr). LDM/STM and other instructions between the two
  reuse fa as their address temporary, so e.g. 'cmp r0, #0; ldm r7, {r6,
  r7}; bne' tested r7 instead of r0. Such conditions now read the flags.
  This changes seven branches in LoG2's generated code (all of the form
  cmp; push/ldm/stm; beq/bne); LoG2's host PNGs and WAVs over the 8000-frame
  check runs stay byte-identical.

Fix saves never loading: slow-path writes to EWRAM/IWRAM were dropped

gba_wr*_slow only handled I/O, palette, VRAM, OAM and EEPROM, on the

jenniferevangelista-de/night-guard.readme:
# 🛡️🌙 Night Guard

**Helps kids understand what happened in an online chat, and choose how to ask for help.**
Runs on the child's own computer with **Gemma** (Google's open-weight model) through Ollama.
Chat analysis stays on the device in local mode. Optional link checks send the selected URL to external services.

> Existing tools watch kids. Night Guard watches out *for* them.

**Try the online demo:** https://night-guard-demo.onrender.com
(fictional examples only; it runs the Tinker fine-tuned model in the cloud so anyone can try it. The real app runs
on the child's computer with Gemma. Free instance: the first visit after a quiet period takes ~50 s to wake up.)

> ## 🚧 Next step: mobile apps and in-game chat
> Today, on a **Windows computer**, Night Guard reacts **on its own, as messages arrive**: a Chrome extension
> watches web chats (Discord web, WhatsApp Web, experimental), and a **screen guard** uses Gemma's vision to read the
> chat inside **installed apps** like the Roblox and Discord apps, all on-device.
> **It does not yet protect phones.** On **Android**, the plan is an app that reads message notifications
> (the same permission parental tools use there) and runs the detector on-device. On **iPhone**, Apple doesn't let
> any app read other apps' messages, so the realistic path is working with Apple's own Communication Safety.
> Bringing Night Guard to the phone, where most kids chat, is the project's next milestone.

## What it does

| Screen | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Something felt off** | Paste a chat. Before showing results, Night Guard asks *"did anything feel off to you?"*, then highlights the exact phrases that match common pressure tricks (secrecy, moving to another app, free-stuff links, password requests…) with a calm one-line explanation. If nothing is found, it says so, and reminds the child that their feeling still counts. |
| **Practice** | Short, pre-reviewed fictional scenarios (fake moderator, free Robux link, "don't tell your parents"). Choose a reply, then see why it works or not. |
| **Tell someone** | Pick which quotes to share, and Gemma drafts a short, editable message to a trusted adult ("I didn't do anything wrong, but I need help"). Nothing is sent automatically. |
| **Family** | Kids don't always recognize a bad intention, so parents set **family rules**: which signals are shared with them automatically (default: photo requests, meeting in person, password requests, secrecy, and any high-risk combination). The child is always told when that happens. Parents see the risk type, the app and the flagged phrase, never the whole chat. |

### Proactive: it doesn't wait for the child to paste anything

Pressure can escalate during a chat session. Night Guard can check messages as they arrive, without waiting for
the child to paste a conversation. The live overlay sends the **12 most recent messages** to each check:

- **Live demo:** open `/game` (also on the online demo): a fictional game chat where a stranger writes and Night Guard
  reacts on its own.
- **Chrome extension** (`extension/`): load it unpacked (`chrome://extensions` → Developer mode → Load unpacked →
  pick the `extension` folder). It reads new messages on Discord web and WhatsApp Web (experimental) and sends them
  **only to the local server** (`http://localhost:...`); the extension refuses any non-local address. A
  "🛡️ Guard on" badge is always visible, so the child knows the guard is there.

- **Screen guard for installed apps** (`guard/screen_guard.py`, Windows): web chats are only half of it, because
  kids chat inside the **Roblox app, the Discord app, Minecraft, TikTok**. Every few seconds, if the window in
  front is one of those apps, Night Guard takes a screenshot of that window **in memory**, and **Gemma's vision**
  reads the chat locally. The text goes to the same detector; the image is never saved and never leaves the
  computer. Any other window (bank, email, school) is never captured. Run:
  `python -m guard.screen_guard --server http://localhost:8765 --lang en --me <child's username>`

### What the child sees vs. what the family sees

| | Child | Family |
|---|---|---|
| Tone | Plain words, says **"DANGER"** when it is, and compares it to something kids already know: *"It's like a stranger on the street saying 'come with me, but don't tell your mom'. You don't go, and you tell an adult."* Never blames the child. | What happened, why it matters (with sources), and **what to do now**: talk calmly without punishment, keep screenshots, block and report, and for image requests, threats or money demands report to SaferNet / NCMEC and the police. Don't pay. |
| Content | The flagged phrase and three actions: don't reply, block, tell an adult | Risk level, app, contact, flagged phrase. Never the full chat |

### The gap no platform covers

Instagram supervision, Discord Family Center, TikTok Family Pairing and Roblox parental controls each protect **their own app**. The classic pressure path starts in a game and moves to a private app. Night Guard records where each check happened, so the family sees:

> ⚠️ Same name seen in more than one app (possibly the same person): **Alex_17 (Roblox → Instagram)**

**The lazy part:** the tutor repeats less as you learn. Lessons you already know collapse to a single ✓ line, so the guard gets lazier as the kid gets wiser.

## Privacy model

**Local app (the real Night Guard)**
- Analysis and message drafting run **locally** (Ollama + `gemma4:e4b`). Chat text never leaves the computer.
- Full conversations are never stored. For family alerts, only the flagged phrase, risk type, app and contact name
  are saved on that computer (`data/`, git-ignored). Learning progress lives in the browser's localStorage.
- The Family area is a local, single-family view. Optional Auth0 login is implemented for the local Ollama app:
  it requires `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET` and `SESSION_SECRET`, plus verified parent
  email addres

meyerkesmaat/backlog.readme:
# Backlog

My game and TV log: a dashboard, library, backlog with play order, journal and a shows tracker.
It runs entirely in the browser and works as an iPhone home-screen app.

- **Live site:** served by GitHub Pages from the `docs/` folder.
- **Your data** is saved in the browser of each device. Use **Data → Export backup / Import backup** to move it between devices.

## Updating

```
node tools/build.js
```

This rebuilds `docs/` from `src/app.html` (the app) and `src/data.json` (the starting data).
Commit and push, and GitHub Pages publishes it within a minute or two.
The version stamp at the bottom of the **Data** menu shows which build a device is running.

## Sources

- Covers: Wikipedia
- Game lengths: HowLongToBeat (Main + Extra)
- Show info and episode lengths: TVmaze

glitchless-gg/glitch-arcade.desc: Small Three.js games in different genres, instrumented with Glitchless: each tracks its own genre, ships with planted problems, and has its own dashboard
glitchless-gg/glitch-arcade.readme:
# The Glitch Arcade

Small Three.js games, one per genre, instrumented with [Glitchless](https://github.com/glitchless-gg/glitchless)
(game observability for players and coding agents). Each one tracks what its own genre cares about, ships with planted,
genre-typical problems for Glitchless to find, has an autoplay bot to fill its dashboard, and comes with the dashboard
its coding agent designed for it. None of them is a platformer: that's the point.

| Game | Genre | What it tracks | Planted problems | Port |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**Blastpit!**](games/blastpit) | arena shooter (FPS) | shots, hits and kills by weapon, deaths by cause, rounds | an error in one weapon (the shotgun), a stutter when a swarm spawns | 5176 |
| [**Slipstream**](games/slipstream) | arcade racer | laps and lap times, wrecks by track section, finishing positions, boosts, overtakes, tracks | a boost pad into a hairpin, a skid-mark leak that slows every race | 5177 |
| [**Gatekeep**](games/gatekeep) | tower defense | towers built, upgraded and sold, gold spent, leaks and kills, waves | a wave that ends most runs, a health-bar texture per enemy that stutters in big waves | 5178 |
| [**Undervault**](games/undervault) | metroidvania (2.5D) | rooms visited and backtracking, relics found, saves, boss attempts | a room that kills most players, an error that only fires when you backtrack | 5179 |
| [**Gemfall**](games/gemfall) | match-3 puzzle | matches by size, shape and cascade depth, specials made and used, boosters, hints, stars and moves left per level | a level that's a wall, a cascade effect that leaks, a hint that throws at the board's edge | 5180 |
| [**Flapjack**](games/flapjack) | one-button flappy | runs and where they end, medals, biomes, new bests, retries | a squeeze at pipe 12, pipes that are never recycled | 5181 |
| [**Ashvale**](games/ashvale) | action RPG (top-down) | kills, loot and gear by rarity and slot, level-ups, skills, rooms cleared, boss attempts, floors | a legendary item that throws when you pick it up, an overtuned floor, damage numbers that pile up in the page | 5182 |

Every game's README lists its events, its planted problems (with file:line), its dashboard pages and what Glitchless
found when bots played it. Screenshots of each game and its dashboard are in [`assets/screenshots`](assets/screenshots).

| Game | Its dashboard |
| --- | --- |
| ![Blastpit](assets/screenshots/blastpit-game.png) | ![Blastpit's dashboard](assets/screenshots/blastpit-dashboard.png) |
| ![Slipstream](assets/screenshots/slipstream-game.png) | ![Slipstream's dashboard](assets/screenshots/slipstream-dashboard.png) |
| ![Gatekeep](assets/screenshots/gatekeep-game.png) | ![Gatekeep's dashboard](assets/screenshots/gatekeep-dashboard.png) |
| ![Undervault](assets/screenshots/undervault-game.png) | ![Undervault's dashboard](assets/screenshots/undervault-dashboard.png) |
| ![Gemfall](assets/screenshots/gemfall-game.png) | ![Gemfall's dashboard](assets/screenshots/gemfall-dashboard.png) |
| ![Flapjack](assets/screenshots/flapjack-game.png) | ![Flapjack's dashboard](assets/screenshots/flapjack-dashboard.png) |
| ![Ashvale](assets/screenshots/ashvale-game.png) | ![Ashvale's dashboard](assets/screenshots/ashvale-dashboard.png) |

## Run a game

```bash
npm install
npm run blastpit          # or slipstream, gatekeep, undervault, gemfall, flapjack, ashvale; each prints its URL
```

The games send telemetry to a Glitchless server at `http://localhost:7777`. Run one from the Glitchless repo
(`npm run server`; the dashboard is on the same port), or send to Glitchless Cloud with
`?intake=https://api.glitchless.gg&token=gl_pub_…` and your project's client token. Without a server the games still run.
Press `` ` `` in any game for the Glitchless overlay.

The games use the published SDK (`glitchless` on npm): `src/telemetry.js` in each one is the whole integration, a small
facade that loads the SDK, calls `Glitchless.init()` and `instrumentThree()`, and keeps telemetry from ever breaking the
game. `src/agent-tools.js` gives coding agents game tools over WebMCP (jump to a level, trigger the planted problem,
read the game's state).

## Fill a dashboard with bots

Every game has an autoplay bot: `?autoplay=1&skill=0..1&seed=N` (its sessions are marked synthetic).

```bash
npm run gatekeep                                           # in one terminal
npm run bots -- --game http://localhost:5178/ --seed 5000  # 20 bots, skills 0.3 to 0.95
```

`--parallel` (default 2) is how many play at once; bots share your GPU, so keep it low (Blastpit wants 1). Each game also
has a `glitchless.playtest.json` for [`glitchless-playtest`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/glitchless-playtest), which
compares two builds.

## The dashboards

Each game's dashboard was designed by a coding agent with the Glitchless `dashboard` skill and saved with the
`glitchless_set_dashboard` MCP tool. The spec is in each game's folder as `glitchless.dashboard.json`; to put it on your
Glitchless server, ask your agent to save that file's pages for the game with `glitchless_set_dashboard` (the
[`glitchless-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/glitchless-mcp) server).

Nothing in them assumes a genre: the shooter's pages are weapons and rounds, the racer's are wrecks by track section and
laps, the tower defense game's are waves, towers and gold (no heatmap, no deaths: it has no avatar), the metroidvania's
are exploration, backtracking and the boss, the match-3's are stars, cascades and boosters (a puzzle has no world to
map), the flappy game's are where runs end and retries, and the action RPG's are floors, loot and combat.

## License

MIT

# Umapastèque

Umamusume support card planner: a release timeline per running style, with filters by card type and verdict.

Live site: https://kevinpoteau.github.io/Umapasteque/

## Layout

```
index.html              page markup only
admin.html              admin page: rate entries, publish as a pull request
css/
  base.css              colour tokens, header, filter bar
  timeline.css          horizontal timeline, date ruler, needle reader
  card.css              support card (v1 Notion callout layout)
  admin.css             admin page
js/                     ES modules, no build step
  main.js               entry point: loads data, wires everything
  config.js             roles, card types, verdicts, image paths
  state.js              filter state (remembered in the browser)
  filters.js            search, type chips, verdict scale
  timeline.js           scenario sections, Today marker, scrolling
  ruler.js              date ruler + scenario art under the needle
  card.js               card markup
  util.js               helpers, image fallback (local copy → original URL)
  admin.js              admin page: entry list, rating form, live preview
  github.js             GitHub API calls used by the admin page
data/
  scenarios.json        scenario names, start dates, colours, art source
  support.json          support cards, one entry per card, rated per running style
  uma.json              Umas, same idea
assets/
  icons/types/          card type icons (SVG)
  icons/verdicts/       verdict arrows
  icons/roles/          running style badges      ┐ downloaded by
  cards/<id>.webp       card art (id = game id)    │ scripts/fetch_assets.py
  umas/<id>.webp        Uma art (id = outfit id)   │
  scenarios/            scenario art               ┘
scripts/fetch_assets.py downloads missing images into assets/
scripts/validate_data.py checks data/ (runs on every pull request and deploy)
scripts/import_new.py   adds newly announced SSR cards and Umas to rate (source: GameTora)
scripts/gametora_text.py turns GameTora's numbers into card texts (effects, unique, skills)
.github/workflows/
  pages.yml             deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main
  fetch-assets.yml      downloads new images when data changes and opens a PR with them
  import.yml            every Monday: new cards and Umas to rate → one PR
  validate.yml          checks data/ on every pull request
```

Images not yet in `assets/` are loaded from their original site, so the page works before and after the sync.

## Rating entries (admin page)

Open `admin.html` on the site (e.g. https://kevinpoteau.github.io/Umapasteque/admin.html).

1. **GitHub token** (once per browser): create a [fine-grained token](https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new) with *Repository access → Only select repositories → Umapasteque*, permissions *Contents: Read and write* and *Pull requests: Read and write*, and an expiry date. Paste it in the dialog. It stays in that browser only.
2. Pick Support cards / Umas, and optionally a running style. **To rate** lists entries with no running style yet, a style without a verdict, or `"todo": true`; **Changed** lists what you edited in this session.
3. Add the running styles the entry is good for (**+ Pace Chaser**…), then rate each one: verdict, stars, text. Dates and **Card text** (effects, unique, key skills) are shared. The preview shows the card as it will look. Changes are kept in the browser until published.
4. **Publish** opens one pull request with every change. The *Check data* run on it must be green; merge it and the site redeploys.

## New cards and Umas (weekly import)

Every Monday, *Import new cards and Umas* looks at [GameTora](https://gametora.com)'s data for SSR support cards and Umas whose global release (real, or GameTora's prediction) is within the next ~14 months and not in `data/` yet. It fills their effects, start bonus, unique, stat bonus and key skills from GameTora's data (`scripts/gametora_text.py`, worded like the hand-written entries; white skills are listed together on one line, to trim on the admin page), and adds them with `"todo": true` and no running style, and opens (or updates) one pull request listing them. It can also be run by hand from the Actions tab.

After merging, they appear in the admin page's **To rate** list, but not on the site: an entry only shows once a running style is added to it. **Don't track** removes an entry and records its id in `data/ignored.json`, so the import never adds it again.

When those dates reach a scenario we don't have yet, it is added to `data/scenarios.json` too (GameTora's estimated start, colour, and picture when GameTora has one; check them in the pull request). A scenario shows as *live* once its start date is past.

The import never changes an existing entry; if GameTora has a confirmed global date that differs from ours, the pull request only mentions it.

## How to edit

| I want to… | Edit |
|---|---|
| Rate, or show an entry on another running style | the admin page (above), or `roles` in the data file |
| Add or change a card | `data/support.json`: one object per card. `id` is the game's card id (it names the image), `iso` is the release date, `color` the card background (`blue`, `red`, `orange`, `pink`, `green`, `yellow`, `purple`). `roles` lists the running styles the card is shown on, each with its own rating: `{"pace": {"rank": 4, "verdict": ["…"], "stats": 3, "skills": 4, "longevity": "…", "bonus": [["Speed", "+1"]]}}` (`rank`: 5 = Highly recommended … 1 = Very bad). A style missing from `roles` never shows the card. |
| Add or change an Uma | `data/uma.json`: same idea, with `runner` / `inherit` / `evolved` stars, `aptitudes`, `outfit` and `style` (her own running style); each role holds `rank` and `verdict` |
| Check my edits by hand | `python3 scripts/validate_data.py` |
| Change a scenario date, colour or picture | `data/scenarios.json` (`gt` = GameTora's id, used by the import) |

KB-retro/Monoloco-Saga.readme: # Monoloco Saga Port para Android de las recompilaciones estáticas de una trilogía clásica de plataformas de 16 bits. Las tres entregas en una sola app, con el mismo lanzador, el mismo menú rápido y los mismos controles táctiles. Pensado para consolas Android como Retroid, AYN Odin 2 Portal y RG477M. > **Aviso.** Proyecto no oficial y gratuito, sin relación con los propietarios de los juegos. > No incluye ninguna ROM ni datos de los juegos. Necesitas tus propias copias. No se vende. ## Cómo funciona - **Lanzador:** eliges la entrega y pulsas **Jugar**, **Ajustes** o **Cambiar carpeta**. En la carpeta pones tus ROM (USA, sin cabecera o con cabecera de 512 bytes). La app las reconoce por su huella SHA-256 y las copia a su carpeta (`Android/data/com.monolocosaga`). Elegir carpeta no arranca el juego. Los ajustes de imagen y sonido son los mismos para las tres entregas (por defecto, pantalla completa y píxel cuadrado). El inicio automático es opcional y se cancela tocando la pantalla o pulsando el mando. - **Menú rápido** con el botón Atrás: pausa el juego. Incluye imagen (formato, filtro, efecto, proporción de píxel; filtros Nítido, Suave, Nítido suavizado, HD, xBR, CRT Lottes y CRT Hyllian), sonido, guardado y carga rápida, controles táctiles y contador de FPS. - **Controles táctiles** con editor (mover, cambiar tamaño, cuadrícula y preajustes en XML). Se ocultan solos si hay un mando conectado. ## El código del juego Las recompilaciones convierten el código de la ROM en C **en tu propio equipo**. Ese código generado y los núcleos compilados (`libmonoloco_gameN.so`) contienen código del juego, así que **nunca se suben a este repositorio**. Hay tres formas de tener un juego en la app: 1. **Compilar tú la APK** con tus ROM (ver abajo). 2. **GitHub Actions con el secreto opcional** `MONOLOCO_ROMS_URL`: enlace privado a una carpeta (o .zip) con tus ROM, por ejemplo de Dropbox tal cual. Cada ROM se reconoce por su huella. También valen `MONOLOCO_ROM1_URL`… uno por juego. Sin ellos la APK sale sin juegos. 3. **Importar un núcleo** hecho en tu PC con `tools/build_cores.sh`: copia el `.so` a la carpeta elegida junto a las ROM y pulsa **Cambiar carpeta**. ## Compilar Requisitos: JDK 21, Python 3.10+, Rust/Cargo (opcional, acelera el análisis), Android SDK platform 37, NDK 30.0.16248370 y CMake 4.1.2. Gradle 9.8.0 y AGP 9.4.1 están fijados. ```sh git submodule update --init --recursive ``` `local.properties` en la raíz: ```properties sdk.dir=/ruta/al/Android/Sdk # Opcional: una línea por juego que quieras incluir monoloco.rom1=/ruta/privada/juego1.sfc monoloco.rom2=/ruta/privada/juego2.sfc monoloco.rom3=/ruta/privada/juego3.sfc ``` ```sh ./gradlew assembleRelease ``` Gradle genera el código de cada juego con su ROM (en `android/app/build/`, fuera de Git), compila su núcleo y lo mete en la APK. Sin ROM, ese juego queda fuera. Solo núcleos, para importarlos en una APK ya instalada: ```sh ANDROID_NDK=/ruta/al/ndk tools/build_cores.sh --rom1 /ruta/juego1.sfc ``` ### APK con GitHub Actions Actions → **Android APK** → **Run workflow**. La APK se firma con la clave guardada en los secretos `MONOLOCO_KEYSTORE_B64` y `MONOLOCO_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` (alias `monolocosaga`), así cada versión se instala encima de la anterior. La versión es `0.1.`. Las ramas `ci/**` solo comprueban que compila. ## Créditos - Recompilaciones originales de **elliotttate** y colaboradores: [DKC1Recomp](https://github.com/elliotttate/DKC1Recomp), [DKC2Recomp](https://github.com/elliotttate/DKC2Recomp) y [DKC3Recomp](https://github.com/elliotttate/DKC3Recomp) (MIT). - [snesrecomp](https://github.com/elliotttate/snesrecomp) (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0) y sus avisos de terceros. - [SDL2](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL) (zlib). - Port Android, lanzador, menú y controles: **KB-retro** Los avisos de licencia completos están en [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) y en cada submódulo. Los nombres y marcas de los juegos pertenecen a sus propietarios.

bassettijonathan-rgb/Colony_game.readme:
# Colony game

A RimWorld-like colony game that runs in the browser. The whole game builds into one HTML page.

## Commands

```
npm install
npm run build     # dist/colony.html
npm run sim       # determinism, save round trip and bot colonies (node tools/sim.mjs [worlds] [days] [landfall|stress] [colonists])
POLICY=careless npm run sim   # the same bots playing with long shifts and no safety rules
NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node tools/browser-check.mjs   # headless Chromium: orbit, landing, printing, crews, evening, save and continue, a built-up colony, placing a building
V2_SAVE=old.json ...  browser-check.mjs                 # also continue a colony saved by milestone 2
```

## Layout

- `src/core`: plain-data simulation with no browser APIs. World generation, landing sites and the landing (`world.js`), pathfinding (`path.js`: chunk-level graph, local A*, flow fields), the colony (`sim.js`), people's days, minds and ties (`life.js`), bodies and wounds (`body.js`), first aid and medicine (`care.js`), the fabricator, crews, building projects and the player's commands (`work.js`), what can be built and what it costs, load checks, power and stock (`build.js`), the founders' archive (`founders.js`), constants and the seeded rng.
- `src/sim`: runs the simulation in a Web Worker (`worker.js`) through a small message protocol (`host.js`). The page falls back to running it in place if the worker cannot start.
- `src/render`: WebGL2 renderer in the Lumen style. Map chunks are painted once into texture arrays (and again when trees come down); each frame lights height, shadows and up to 24 lights. Buildings, the yard, stumps and quarried rock are drawn stage by stage in `buildings.js`.
- `src/ui`: the page and its game interface (a top bar with the colony's stock and the clock, colonist portraits, open projects, a dock that opens the archive, crews, build and log windows, cards for the person or building you pick and for a building being placed, a menu with saving, music, news settings and the controls), the news (`news.js`: event cards, letters that pause the game, standing alerts and first-time explanations), the connection to the simulation, saving (this browser, the player's account, a file) and the music (`music.js`).
- `src/bot`: headless bot runner used by `tools/sim.mjs` to balance and test without players.
- `src/sealed-stub`: stand-ins for texts the player must not read. The real ones live outside this public repository and are never committed.

## Numbers

Map 600 x 600 tiles in 32-tile chunks; 30 simulation ticks per second at normal speed; one day lasts 12 minutes at normal speed.

## Music

Generated live with Web Audio, with no audio files: a pad changing chord every two bars, a bass note, a plucked melody built from a short motif that repeats with small changes and rests now and then, and an occasional bell, through a generated reverb and an echo. The mood follows the clock (orbit, dawn, day, evening, night) and changes only on a chord change. It starts on the first click or key, as browsers require. `M` or the music button turns it on and off; the slider sets the volume; both are kept in this browser.

## How a game starts (milestone 2)

1. From orbit, the Seed offers three landing sites with what it knows and doesn't know about each. You also choose the season it comes down in (Thaw by default); the year runs on from there, so a landing in Deep cold starts in snow with twenty days to the thaw. `SEASON=0..3` does the same for the bot sims.
2. It lands where you choose; the burn clears a ring and the shelter plot and the cook fire are laid out.
3. The fabricator has feedstock for six bodies out of the forty minds in the archive. You choose who, about four hours each.
4. Founders wake with bodies, skills, traits, memories and old ties. The Seed sorts them into a shelter crew and a survey crew until you change anything.
5. Crews have a lead, a shift and rules (back by dark, nobody walks alone, stop when exhausted). Survey crews reveal the ground and plant ten sensor stakes; the shelter crew turns the lander's modules into a twelve-bunk shelter in five stages.
6. Fatigue, strain and trust in the Seed rise and fall with the work and the rules; bonds form at work and at meals.

## Building (milestone 3)

1. The Build tab (`B`) lists stock, power, the two local materials and their load tests, the buildings you can plan, saved blueprints and the project list.
2. Pick a building and drag its outline on the map; `R` turns the door. The Seed checks the plot (surveyed, dry, reachable, clear of the camp and other plots) and shows what each stage takes, whether the roof needs posts, and what the colony's power would be. A plan can be saved as a blueprint and placed again.
3. Each building goes up in five stages, worked by a build crew: marking out, foundations (stone), frame (timber), systems (airlock seal, pipe runs, power units), fit-out. Trees and boulders on the plot are cleared into the yard; from foundations on, the plot can't be walked across.
4. Stone is cut from boulders and rock faces and timber felled from trees, by quarry and timber crews that fill the yard, or by builders themselves when the yard is empty. Seals, pipes, power units and solar panels are made from the lander's salvage at workshop benches, or three times slower by the fabricator when it has no body to print.
5. Until a load test shows how strong the local stone and timber really are, designs carry 40% extra as a margin and roofs wider than four tiles need posts. Tests use three loads at the rig in the yard. Loads are worked out when each stage starts, so testing early makes the rest cheaper.
6. The lander makes 8 kW; solar fields add more. Finished buildings take power in list order and any that don't fit stay dark and unused. Projects show what they are waiting for, stall, and pick up again.
7. Click a building, finished or not, for its card: what it is, its five stages, what the current stage still needs and who is w

JakaMale/BombLine.readme:
# BombLine

A game project. Full description to come.

## Dots & Boxes

A local Dots & Boxes game for 2–4 players taking turns on one device (grid from 4x4 up to 16x16 boxes, chosen in the menu) built with Angular 17, standalone components and signals.

### Run

```bash
npm install
npm start          # dev server at http://localhost:4200
npm run build      # production build in dist/bomb-line
```

### Structure

- `src/app/game/game-engine.ts` — pure, immutable game rules (no Angular)
- `src/app/game/game.service.ts` — signal-based state facade
- `src/app/game/game-settings.service.ts` — grid size (4–16) and player count (2–4) picked in the menu
- `src/app/game/game-history.service.ts` — finished games (last 100) persisted in `localStorage`, shown on `/history`
- `src/app/pages/` — routed pages: `menu` (`/`), `game` (`/game`), `history` (`/history`)
- `src/app/components/` — `game-board` (SVG board), `scoreboard`, `game-over`

jaybecina/hearthvale.desc: Hearthvale: a cozy 3D farming-life game for the browser and phones. Clear grandpa's farm, grow 8 crops through 4 seasons and weather, and save the valley. React Three Fiber + a pure, tested TypeScript rules engine.
jaybecina/hearthvale.readme:
# Hearthvale

A cozy 3D farming-life game that runs in the browser, on desktop and on phones. Take over grandpa's
overgrown farm, clear the field, grow eight crops through four seasons, ship your harvest, and keep the farm
going through rain, storms and snow.

Hearthvale is an original game inspired by the classic farm-sim genre. Part 1 (this release) is the farm loop;
the town, festivals, romance and the valley's story follow in later parts (see
[the design spec](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-hearthvale-part1-design.md), Appendix A).

| Spring                           | Summer                           |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| ![Spring](docs/media/spring.png) | ![Summer](docs/media/summer.png) |
| **Fall**                         | **Winter**                       |
| ![Fall](docs/media/fall.png)     | ![Winter](docs/media/winter.png) |

**Live:** _added after the first deploy_

## Play

| Action               | Keyboard         | Gamepad    | Touch                    |
| -------------------- | ---------------- | ---------- | ------------------------ |
| Walk                 | W A S D / arrows | Left stick | Drag on the left side    |
| Use tool             | Space            | A          | ✦ button                 |
| Interact, plant, eat | F                | X          | ✋ button                |
| Pick a tool or item  | 1–8, mouse wheel | LB / RB    | ⇄ button, tap the hotbar |
| Turn the camera      | Q / E            | LT / RT    | ⟲ ⟳ buttons              |
| Zoom                 | + / −            |            |                          |
| Menu                 | Esc / Tab        | Start      | ☰                       |

Sleep in your bed to end the day and save. Anything in the shipping bin sells overnight. Sol's cart on the
east road sells seeds from 9 AM to 5 PM, spring to fall.

## Develop

Requires Node 24 and pnpm 10.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # http://localhost:5173
pnpm test         # unit tests (core + web)
pnpm e2e          # Playwright: Chromium, WebKit, Pixel 7, iPhone 14
```

| Script                         | What it does                                              |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm lint` / `pnpm typecheck` | ESLint (strict, type-checked) and TypeScript              |
| `pnpm test:coverage`           | Unit tests; `packages/core` must stay at ≥ 90% coverage   |
| `pnpm build`                   | Production build into `apps/web/dist`                     |
| `pnpm --filter web size`       | Bundle budget: initial JS ≤ 500 KB gzipped                |
| `pnpm --filter web perf`       | Load time on a throttled phone profile (production build) |

## How it's built

```
packages/core   Pure TypeScript rules: applyCommand(state, cmd) → { state, events }. Deterministic, no DOM.
apps/web        Vite + React 19 + React Three Fiber. Fixed 50 ms simulation step, DOM HUD over the canvas.
```

- **Rendering:** instanced tiles, wind-swayed grass and trees, a time-of-day sun and sky, shader snow cover,
  GPU rain and snow, a pond shader, and post-processing (ambient occlusion, bloom, AgX tone mapping, a
  seasonal colour grade). Quality adapts to the device and frame rate.
- **Saves:** IndexedDB with three slots and an automatic backup per slot, validated with zod and versioned for
  migrations. Export and import as a file.
- **Tested:** property-based invariants, a scripted bot that plays a full year, component tests, and
  Playwright end-to-end tests with axe accessibility checks.

More detail: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Asset credits: [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md).

## Roadmap

1. **Farm loop** — this release
2. Town, villagers, friendship, cloud saves
3. Story: the Hearth Tree, Kindlings, festivals, romance
4. Animals, mining, fishing, upgrades
5. Phone app (Expo shell around the web game)

thevermin/VRmin.desc: Play SteamVR games on your Mac, streamed to your Meta Quest. Free and open source.
thevermin/VRmin.readme:
# VRmin **Play your SteamVR games on a Mac. Streamed to your Meta Quest.** Free and open source · Apple Silicon Mac + Meta Quest + Steam [**Download**](../../releases/latest) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#install) · [FAQ](#faq) · [☕ Support on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/thevermin)
> [!NOTE] > **Yes, VRmin is vibe-coded.** It was built by describing what I wanted to an AI (Claude) and testing every > version on my own Mac and Quest. [More about that below.](#a-note-on-vibe-coding) --- ## What is VRmin? Macs can't run SteamVR games. VRmin makes it happen: it runs the **Windows version** of your Steam VR games on your Mac (using Wine and a Metal translation layer), and streams the picture to your **Meta Quest** over Wi‑Fi, with your head and hand movements going back the other way. It is two apps that work together: | | App | What it does | |---|---|---| | 💻 | **VRmin Host** (Mac) | Installs and runs Steam for Windows, opens your VR games, and streams them (plus your Mac's screen, windows and sound) to the headset. | | 🥽 | **VRmin** (Quest) | Your virtual room: the game stream, your Mac's desktop and windows, menus, hands and controllers. | ## Features ### 🎮 SteamVR games on your Mac Your SteamVR library, running on Apple Silicon. Tested with games like **SUPERHOT VR**, **Beat Saber**, **Aircar** and **Kayak VR: Mirage** ([full list](../../discussions/6)). VRmin picks the right VR runtime for each game automatically (OpenXR directly, or OpenVR through OpenComposite). ### 🖥️ Your Mac in your room Your whole desktop, or any single window, floating wherever you want. Watch, browse and work on a giant screen. ### ✋ Your real hands, over every window Hand tracking with your real (passthrough) hands, so you always see what you're doing. Controllers are always visible too. Touch windows directly, or point with the laser. ### 🌌 Pick your room A living room, space, a cinema… or mixed reality with your real desk still there. ### ⚙️ Game settings without leaving the game Quality, sharpness, frame rate, codec and more, per game, from a menu inside VR. ### 🚪 Need the real world? Draw a portal Draw a circle in the air with your hand and see through to your real room (and pet your cat). ### 🛋️ Sentinel Mode: play without wearing the headset Put the Quest on your monitor: it tracks you with its cameras while the game shows on your Mac's screen. ### And more - **Flat games** on a giant screen, and **side‑by‑side 3D videos** that pop with one tap - **Direct GPU copy**: game frames go from the game to the video encoder without leaving the GPU - **Foveated encoding**: sharper in the center, where you look - **Your Mac's sound** in the headset, and the **headset keyboard** types on your Mac - English and Spanish ## How it works ``` Steam VR game (Windows) Meta Quest │ ▲ Wine + DXMT ── DirectX 11 → Metal │ H.265 / H.264 video + sound (Wi‑Fi) │ │ VRmin OpenXR runtime ── frames (shared GPU textures) ──► VRmin renderer (Mac) ── encoder ▲ │ └──────────────── head & hand tracking ◄────────────────────────┘ ``` ## Requirements - A Mac with **Apple Silicon** (M1 or newer), **macOS 14.2** or newer, and Rosetta 2 - A **Meta Quest 3 or 3S** (recommended). **Quest 2** works too (confirmed by testers); **Quest 1** and **Quest Pro** are experimental: see [Older headsets](#older-headsets) - The Mac and the Quest on the **same Wi‑Fi** network (5/6 GHz, or the Mac on Ethernet, works best) - A Steam account with your VR games, and space for them (VRmin installs its own Steam for Windows: games are downloaded again there) ### Older headsets VRmin runs on Quest 1, Quest 2 and Quest Pro. Quest 2 has been confirmed working by testers; Quest 1 and Pro haven't been tested yet, so expect some rough edges. These features need hardware that older headsets don't have, so they probably won't work (or will work differently): | Feature | Quest 2 / Pro | Quest 1 | |---|---|---| | Passthrough (portal, mixed reality room, seeing your room) | Black and white on Quest 2, color on Pro | Not available | | Real hands with soft edges | Hard edges (needs Quest 3's camera access) | Not available | | USB-C cable connection | Works with recent system updates | Probably not (old system) | | Refresh rate | Up to 120 Hz | 72 Hz only | | Several Mac windows at once | Works | May be limited (old system) | Older headsets also have weaker video decoders: if the picture stutters, lower the quality in VRmin Host's settings (this also makes the Mac work less). If you try VRmin on an older headset, please tell us how it went in an [Issue](../../issues)! ## Install ### 1. On your Mac 1. Download **`VRmin Host .zip`** from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and double‑click it. 2. Drag **VRmin Host** to your **Applications** folder. 3. The first time, **right‑click → Open** (macOS warns because the app isn't from the App Store). On newer ma

commits.msg: Build the OpenXR runtime DLL

OpenXR runtime: skip closing WinINet connection handles instead of locking

The shared/exclusive lock could stall every download behind one slow request.
Wine only crashes when a connection or session handle is closed while its
requests are still in use, so those closes are now skipped; request handles
still close normally.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Build the OpenXR runtime DLL

OpenXR runtime: serialize the game's WinINet calls around Wine's handle close

Wine's wininet walks a handle's child list without a lock when it is closed,
so Google Earth VR crashed (access violation in InternetCloseHandle) while
other threads were still downloading map data. Opening and closing handles
now take an exclusive lock; sending and reading share it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Build the OpenXR runtime DLL

OpenXR runtime: give OpenComposite the GL 4.3/4.5 calls macOS lacks

OpenComposite's OpenGL compositor needs glGetTextureLevelParameteriv and
glCopyImageSubData, but macOS stops at OpenGL 4.1. Its wglGetProcAddress now
gets equivalents built from older calls (bind + query, framebuffer blit).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Build the OpenXR runtime DLL

OpenXR runtime: answer OpenComposite's missing GetFrameTimeRemaining

Google Earth VR calls IVRCompositor::GetFrameTimeRemaining, which OpenComposite
never implemented, so it aborted before the first frame. The runtime now finds
that function in the loaded vrclient_x64.dll and replaces it in memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Build the OpenXR runtime DLL

OpenXR runtime: OpenGL support (XR_KHR_opengl_enable)

- OpenGL games (like Google Earth VR through OpenComposite) can now send frames:
  swapchain images are GL textures in the game's context, read back with PBOs
  into the shared memory for the Mac.
- macOS only offers core OpenGL contexts, so a 3.2+ compatibility-profile request
  (Google Earth VR) is turned into a core one instead of failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Build the OpenXR runtime DLL

Vulkan: turn off GPU features the Mac doesn't have when a game creates its device

DOOM VFR asks for features Metal lacks (vkCreateDevice failed with
VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT). The runtime now hooks the game's vkCreateDevice and
drops only the unsupported features, logging which ones.

afdude08/MillionaireGame-Showcase.desc: A tour of The Millionaire Game: screenshots and how a show runs (no source code)
afdude08/MillionaireGame-Showcase.readme:
# The Millionaire Game 2.0

A Windows desktop **game controller** for running live *"Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?"*-style shows at home, on Discord, or on a YouTube/Twitch livestream. An operator drives the game from a Control Panel; dedicated Host, Contestant and Audience/TV windows go on separate monitors or capture sources. A tour of the game: what it looks like and how a show runs. The source code lives in a separate, private repository. | TV / audience screen | Host screen | |---|---| | ![TV screen](docs/screenshots/tv-final-answer.jpg) | ![Host screen](docs/screenshots/host-screen.jpg) | ![Control Panel](docs/screenshots/control-panel.png) ## Running a show The Control Panel opens on **Show setup** (everything you set once before the show); the game itself is run from **Live game**. 1. **Open the screens** on *Show setup*: switch on **Host**, **Contestant** and **TV / Audience** (or **Open them all**). - Pick each screen's monitor from its list, and **⛶ Fullscreen**. On the screen itself, F11 or a double-click also toggles fullscreen and Esc exits. - Placements are remembered between runs. - **Ready for the show?** beside them checks the screens, the sound files, the questions left, phone voting and the show clock, with a button to fix each one. The props to print and **Single player…** are on this tab too. 2. On **Live game**, choose the contestant under *Next game* (or **🎲** for a random one), then press the big green button: **New game** → optionally **Risk Mode** (under *Next game*) → **Start game ▶**. - Between games the left column has *Next game* and *Explain the rules*; during a game it shows the contestant's **money ladder**. - The big green button is always the **next step** (Show question, Reveal next answer, Final answer, Reveal answer, Next question, Start the clock, Walk-away music, New game…), with Take back, the amount won and Walk away in a row beside it. Buttons that only sometimes apply (Reveal all answers, Reveal switched answer) show only then. - **Question category** (in the same card) picks where tonight's questions come from, e.g. *General Knowledge*, or *All categories (mixed)*. It shows how many games' worth are left and warns before a game would run out at some level. Fastest Finger rounds use it too, it's remembered between runs, and a game keeps its category once it has started (and when it carries on after a restart). 3. **Each question:** **Lights down** → **Show question** → **Reveal next answer** (F8) until all four show. - Select the contestant's answer with F1–F4, then **Final answer** (F5) → **Reveal answer** (F6) → **Next question** (F7). - **Take back** (Ctrl+Z) undoes a mis-press, one step at a time: the wrong letter locked in, Reveal a moment too early, a lifeline by accident. The game, screens and music go back to how they were. A finished game that's taken back takes the contestant's result with it. 4. **Lifelines** use Ctrl+1–4 or the buttons. Phone a Friend and Ask the Audience have two steps: - The lead-in plays first. - Phone a Friend rings twice and connects by itself; then press **Start the clock** when the host has read the question. For Ask the Audience, press **Open audience voting**. - Finish with **Complete lifeline**. 5. **On the TV** controls what the Contestant and TV screens display: logo, contestant intro, question, winnings, or the money-tree overlay beside the question. - The Host screen always shows the live game, including the correct answer and host notes. - **Walk away** asks "is that their final answer?" on the Live game tab itself (no pop-up): **Yes, walk away** (or press Walk away again) and the music fades. Then **Show what they'd have won**, then **♪ Walk-away music**: the TV shows their total prize money and the contestant's screen goes black. - **🧹 Clear the screens** (Live game, once a game is over, and on the Fastest Finger First tab) takes the last game off every screen, the host's too, so they show the logo, ready to introduce the next Fastest Finger players. 6. **After Switch the Question**, **Reveal switched answer** shows everyone what the discarded question's answer was. The Host screen sees it straight away. 7. **Soundboard:** **Opening** (the opening titles on every screen, to the opening theme, finishing on the logo), Main theme, Next Player (plays by itself when the FFF winner goes to the hot seat), Lights down (the Next Player music fades out under it), **Break** / **Return** (commercial breaks), Ready to play, **Credits**, **Out of Time** and **Stop all**. 8. **Winners** (On the TV) puts tonight's winners on every screen: everyone who has played since the contestants were last reset, biggest winnings first. 9. **The top prize:** ticker tape pours down over the contestant and TV screens at the reveal, and again on the total-winnings screen. ### Keyboard shortcuts Every main-game button can have a key: **Settings → Keyboard shortcuts** (click a key, then press the one you want). The defaults are F1–F4 (select A–D), F5 (final answer), F6 (reveal answer), F7 (next question), F8 (reveal next answer), F9 (amount won), Ctrl+1–4 (lifelines) and Ctrl+Z (take back). The keys also work when a show screen has focus, so a keypad, presenter clicker or Stream Deck that sends keys can run the game. ### If the game closes mid-game The game in progress is saved after every step. If the app is closed or crashes part-way through, the Control Panel offers to **carry on** next time: the same contestant, question, lifelines and money, under the rules the game started with. The question goes back on the TV with its music. ### Single player **Single player…** on the Control Panel's Show setup tab opens a game for one person with no host: the computer hosts, and the player clicks their own answers on

# Zombie Co-op

Game 2D sinh tồn zombie, thế giới mở, góc nhìn từ trên xuống, chơi trên trình duyệt, co-op online tối đa 4 người.
Mạng P2P (WebRTC) — không cần server, miễn phí hoàn toàn.

Thiết kế đầy đủ và quy tắc làm việc: **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)**.

## Chạy trên máy

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # mở http://localhost:5173
```

Mở 2 tab cùng một link (có `?room=...`) để thử 2 người. Bấm **F3** để bật/tắt bảng giả lập mạng xấu.

## Lệnh hay dùng

| Lệnh            | Việc                                                         |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `npm run dev`   | Chạy thử                                                     |
| `npm run check` | Kiểm tra kiểu + lint + test (chạy trước khi mở Pull Request) |
| `npm test`      | Chỉ chạy test                                                |
| `npm run build` | Build bản phát hành vào `dist/`                              |

## Cấu trúc

| Thư mục   | Nội dung                                                                                            |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client/` | Phaser, giao diện                                                                                   |
| `net/`    | Lớp mạng: `Transport`, Trystero, mạng giả (loopback), giả lập mạng xấu, phòng chờ                   |
| `shared/` | Logic dùng chung, không phụ thuộc trình duyệt (`types/`, `util/rng.ts`, `sim/`, `mapgen/`, `data/`) |
| `host/`   | Mô phỏng thế giới trên máy host (giai đoạn 2)                                                       |
| `tools/`  | Bot, đo tải                                                                                         |

Mỗi lần merge vào `main`, GitHub Actions tự đưa game lên GitHub Pages.
