Oliverszkcs/songdle-hu.readme:
# Songdle HU

Magyar dalfelismerős játék (Heardle-stílusban), végtelen móddal és kategóriákkal.

- Tiszta HTML/CSS/JS, nincs build lépés, nincs backend – GitHub Pages-en fut.
- A dalok 30 mp-es előnézetei a [Deezer](https://www.deezer.com) nyilvános API-jából jönnek
  (JSONP-n keresztül, így nem kell CORS proxy). Hangfájlt nem tárolunk.
- Telepíthető (PWA): „Hozzáadás a kezdőképernyőhöz”.

## Játék

1 mp → 2 → 4 → 8 → 15 → 30 mp. Rossz tipp vagy kihagyás után hosszabb részletet hallasz.
6 próbálkozás után (vagy ha eltalálod) jön a megoldás borítóval, majd a **Következő dal**.
A sorozat és a statisztika a böngésző `localStorage`-ában tárolódik.

## Módok

- **Végtelen**: 5 dalos körök kategóriánként vagy évtizedenként (60-70-es évek … 2020-as évek).
  A **🔥 Nehéz** kapcsolóval a részlet a dal közepéről indul (5–15. mp), ×1,5 pontért.
- **Napi**: mindenkinek ugyanaz a dal, három nehézségi szinten; a statisztikában havi naptár mutatja a napokat.
- **Előadó**: napi előadó-találós. 4 rossz tipp után kérhető a „Hallgass bele” és a
  „💡 Egy dala” súgó (ez utóbbi −40 pont).
- **🎯 Kihívás**: egy befejezett kör megosztásakor a szövegben egy link van (`?k=…&p=…&n=…`),
  amivel a barátod ugyanazt az 5 dalt kapja, és látja, hány pontot kell megvernie.
- **⚔️ Párbaj**: két játékos élőben, ugyanazzal az 5 dallal. A kapcsolat [PeerJS](https://peerjs.com)-sel
  jön létre (a nyilvános PeerJS-közvetítő csak az összekötést végzi, utána a két böngésző közvetlenül,
  WebRTC-n beszél). Meghívó link: `?parbaj=KÓD`. Szigorú (pl. egyes mobil-) hálózatokon TURN-szerver
  nélkül előfordulhat, hogy nem jön létre a kapcsolat.

Offline: a legutóbbi 30 dal hangja a böngészőben marad (Cache Storage), így térerő nélkül is lehet játszani.

## Eszközök (`tools/`)

```sh
node tools/build-years.mjs     # data/years.json – megjelenési évek az évtized-kategóriákhoz
node tools/check-foreign.mjs   # gyanús, nem a magyar előadótól származó dalok (→ BLOCKED_TRACKS)
node tools/check-foreign.mjs Desh Vini   # csak a megadott előadók
```

Új előadó felvétele után érdemes mindkettőt lefuttatni. A Deezer/MusicBrainz-válaszok a
`tools/.cache` mappában maradnak (nincs a repóban), így az újrafuttatás gyors.

## Látogatottság (GoatCounter)

Ingyenes, sütimentes számláló. Regisztrálj a [goatcounter.com](https://www.goatcounter.com)-on
(pl. `songdlehu` kóddal), és írd be a kódot a `js/config.js`-be: `GOATCOUNTER: "songdlehu"`.
Az oldalletöltések mellett néhány esemény is beérkezik (pl. `battle-start`, `challenge-won`, `artist-title-hint`).

## Előadók és kategóriák szerkesztése

Minden a [`js/config.js`](js/config.js) fájlban van:

```js
CATEGORIES: [{ id: "rap", label: "Rap" }, ...],
ARTISTS: [{ name: "Majka", id: 281118, tags: ["rap", "pop"] }, ...],
```

- Az `id` a Deezer előadó-azonosító (deezer.com/artist/**281118**). Elhagyható – ekkor név alapján keresünk.
- A `tags` dönti el, melyik kategóriában szerepel az előadó. A „Mind” kategória mindenkit tartalmaz.
- Az előadók dallistája 24 órára gyorsítótárazódik a böngészőben.

## Helyi futtatás

Bármilyen statikus szerver jó, pl.:

```sh
npx serve .
```

(A service worker miatt `http://localhost`-on vagy HTTPS-en futtasd, ne `file://`-ként.)

Ha módosítasz az alkalmazás fájljain, emeld meg a `CACHE` verziót az `sw.js`-ben.

JRDevo/ETS2-ATS-VR-Controls.desc: Use your VR controllers as keyboard and mouse in Euro Truck Simulator 2 / American Truck Simulator: button mapping, stick + air mouse, an in-headset menu and a full on-screen keyboard. Unofficial fan mod (OpenXR API layer).
JRDevo/ETS2-ATS-VR-Controls.readme:
# ETS2 ATS VR Controls Play **Euro Truck Simulator 2** and **American Truck Simulator** in VR with **only your headset and its own controllers**. No steering wheel, no gamepad, no keyboard, no mouse, no extra hardware. - **Drive with the controllers:** one stick steers (smooth, like a gamepad), the triggers are gas and brake. - **Every key on a button:** indicators, horn, lights, anything. Pick the keys in a menu in the headset. - **A mouse in your hand:** a stick or the controller's aim moves the pointer, a button clicks. For the game's menus and the map. - **A full keyboard in the headset:** point and pull the trigger. For the few things that need typing. Start the game in VR, put the headset on, and play. You never need to reach for the desk. > [!NOTE] > **Status:** v0.1.0, the first release: controller buttons as keys and mouse, **a VR menu and a full keyboard in the > headset**, and **driving with the controllers** (smooth steering, gas and brake). Planned: the keyboard pinned to the > cab, and single buttons you place anywhere (for example over a cab switch) that press a key. > [!IMPORTANT] > **OpenXR only.** The mod works when the game runs in its **OpenXR** VR mode (`-openxr`). It does not work in the game's > `-openvr` (SteamVR native) or `-oculus` (Oculus native) modes. Every headset can use OpenXR, see > [Which VR mode?](#which-vr-mode). ## Screenshots | Buttons tab: picking a key | Buttons tab: with the modifier | Mouse tab | |---|---|---| | ![The Buttons tab while a key is picked](docs/images/menu-pick.png) | ![The Buttons tab, with modifier](docs/images/menu-modifier.png) | ![The Mouse tab](docs/images/menu-mouse.png) | | Panels tab | Look tab | The keyboard | |---|---|---| | ![The Panels tab](docs/images/menu-panels.png) | ![The Look tab](docs/images/menu-look.png) | ![The on-screen keyboard](docs/images/keyboard.png) | | Driving tab | Pointing at a setting: its help at the bottom | The compact keyboard (Panels tab > Compact) | |---|---|---| | ![The Driving tab](docs/images/menu-driving.png) | ![The Driving tab while the pointer is on "Wheel follows the stick": its help line at the bottom](docs/images/menu-driving-help.png) | ![The compact keyboard](docs/images/keyboard-compact.png) | ![The white pointer dot on the G key of the keyboard](docs/images/keyboard-pointer.png) **Menu:** [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Which VR mode?](#which-vr-mode) · [What it does](#what-it-does) · [Default buttons](#default-buttons) · [Driving](#driving-with-one-controller) · [VR menu](#the-vr-menu) · [Install](#install) · [Privacy](#what-runs-when--privacy) · [Settings](#settings) · [Problems](#problems) · [Report a problem](#reporting-a-problem-what-to-upload) · [Build](#build-from-source) · [License](#license)

Which VR mode?

 ETS2 / ATS have three VR modes, chosen by a launch option (Steam: right-click the game > Properties > Launch options). This mod works **only** in the OpenXR one: | Launch option | VR system | This mod | |---|---|---| | `-openxr` | OpenXR | **works** | | `-openvr` | SteamVR's own system (OpenVR) | does not load | | `-oculus` | Meta's old Oculus system | does not load | SCS also recommends OpenXR: it is the only VR mode in the normal game builds (1.55+; there, also add `-experimental_vr`), while `-openvr` and `-oculus` exist only in the `oculus` beta branch on Steam. How to use OpenXR with your headset: - **Quest via Virtual Desktop:** `-openxr`, with Virtual Desktop's VDXR as the OpenXR runtime (Virtual Desktop sets it). - **Quest via Link / Air Link:** `-openxr`, with the Meta Quest Link app as the OpenXR runtime (Meta app > Settings > General > OpenXR Runtime). - **Valve Index, HTC Vive, Pico and other SteamVR headsets:** `-openxr`, with SteamVR as the OpenXR runtime (SteamVR > Settings > OpenXR > Set SteamVR as OpenXR runtime). The game then still runs through SteamVR. - **Windows Mixed Reality:** `-openxr`, with the Windows Mixed Reality OpenXR runtime. Only one OpenXR runtime is active at a time; the last one you set wins.

What it does

 - Each controller button sends a key or a mouse button that you choose in `config.ini`. - One stick moves the mouse pointer (the right stick by default). - **Air mouse**: hold the right grip and turn the controller. The pointer follows, like a laser pointer. (Or set it to toggle: one press on, the next press off.) - **Modifier**: while you hold the modifier button (right grip), buttons can send something else. Default: **right grip + A or right trigger = left click, right grip + B = right click** -- so one controller does everything: hold the grip (the pointer follows), press A or the trigger to click, hold B to right-click (drag the map). Set any button's modified key in the VR menu. - **Driving**: the left stick steers, the right trigger is the gas pedal, the left trigger the brake. Smooth, like a gamepad, not on / off keys. Gas and brake can go on any button. See [Driving](#driving-with-one-controller). - **VR menu + keyboard**: hold both grips + the left stick click for 1 second. A menu opens in front of you. See [The VR menu](#the-vr-menu). - The game's own VR controls (the trigger and the left menu button) still work. - It only works in the games named in `config.ini`. In every other VR program it does nothing. - It only sends input while the game window is in front. It never types into another program. It is an OpenXR API layer: a small add-on that the VR system loads into the game. It does not change any game file, and it works next to the ETS2 / ATS DLAA mod, VR EyeCapture, Virtual Desktop, OpenXR Toolkit and VectorXR.

Default buttons

 Made so that **one controller (the right one) does the whole mouse**: point with the right stick or the air mouse, A = left click, right

AleksandrsJuska/west-wings-essen.readme:
# West Wings Essen: team stats site

Stats site for West Wings Essen in the 1. Bundesliga of the Deutsche Roundnet Liga 2026/27.
A Python scraper collects data from [Playerzone](https://playerzone.roundnetgermany.de) (with Roundnet Germany's permission, about once a month).
It writes JSON to `data/`, and a plain HTML/CSS/JS site (no build step) shows it on GitHub Pages.

- Site: https://aleksandrsjuska.github.io/west-wings-essen/
- Spec: [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) · reasons: [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) · structure and data model: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

## Setup (Windows)
```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Scraper
```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python -m scraper              # scrapes only if a matchday was yesterday or a run was missed
.venv\Scripts\python -m scraper --dry-run    # only report whether a run is due (no requests)
.venv\Scripts\python -m scraper --force --no-publish   # scrape now, don't commit/push
```
After scraping it commits `data/`, and pushes if a git remote is configured. Log: `logs\scraper.log`.

## Daily task
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\install_task.ps1            # daily at 10:00
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\install_task.ps1 -Uninstall
```
The task runs daily, and the scraper decides whether anything is due. Missed starts run as soon as possible.

## Site locally
```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python tools\serve.py    # http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

## Tests
```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
```
The tests use the saved pages in `tests/fixtures/` and make no requests.

counts. END_TURN logs roundCompleted when the turn wraps, and the END_TURN
that completes round 15 (10 in kids mode) ends the game with gameEnded
{ reason: 'roundLimit' } and the winner current. Winner at the limit:

tuankun-279/Caro_XO.readme:
# Caro X-O

**Caro X-O** is a hand-drawn notebook-style **Caro (Gomoku, five in a row)** game for Android, built with Unity. Play against a three-level AI or with a friend on the same phone. [**⬇ Download the APK**](https://github.com/tuankun-279/Caro_XO/releases/latest) · Unity 6000.0.76f1 · URP 2D · Portrait ## Features - **Vs AI** with three clearly different levels (Easy, Medium, Hard) or **2 players** on one device - **Growing board**: starts at 15 × 15 and expands up to 20 × 20 when a move lands near the edge - Pinch to zoom, drag to pan, **undo** and resume an unfinished game - **Pen-and-paper feel**: X and O are drawn stroke by stroke, undo erases them diagonally, with recorded pencil sounds - Choose who moves first, sound, vibration and volume settings; recent scores per mode - Vietnamese UI, with all text rendered by the engine (no text baked into images) so it can be localized ## The AI The AI lives in a plain C# assembly (`Caro.AI`) with no Unity dependency, so it runs on a background thread and is fully unit-tested. - **Candidate moves**: only empty cells within two cells of a stone, ranked by a shape score for both attack and defence (five, open four, four, open/broken three, twos) with bonuses for double threats. - **Easy** plays like a beginner: it takes a win about 80 % of the time, blocks a four about 60 % of the time and otherwise plays loosely near existing stones. - **Medium** always wins or blocks fours, blocks open threes, looks one move ahead and sometimes picks the second-best move. - **Hard** plays in three stages within a 1.4 s budget: 1. **VCF search** (*Victory by Continuous Fours*): looks for a forced win where every attacking move makes a four the opponent must block, up to 10 attacking moves deep (capped at 30 000 nodes and 60 % of the time). 2. **Defensive VCF**: among the 16 best candidates, drops moves that would let the opponent start their own VCF. 3. **Iterative-deepening alpha-beta** (negamax with alpha-beta pruning) up to depth 8, keeping the best move from the last fully searched depth when time runs out. ## Tests **57 EditMode tests** (NUnit, Unity Test Framework) cover the pure C# core and AI: | Area | What is checked | | --- | --- | | Placement | Legal and occupied cells, turn order, choosing who starts, cells outside the board | | Win detection | Five in a row in all four directions, gaps, six-in-a-row (no overline rule), edges and corners, game end | | Board growth, undo, draw | Expanding toward each edge up to 20 × 20, undo after a win, full-board draw | | AI tactics | Takes an immediate win, blocks fours and open threes, finds double-four wins, always plays legal moves, Easy's deliberate mistakes | | AI tournaments | Levels play each other (3 slow tests, marked `Explicit`) | The 54 regular tests all pass. Of the 3 tournament tests, *Medium crushes Easy* and *Easy is beatable by a novice* pass; **Hard vs Medium currently wins 9 of 12 games against a target of 11**, so Hard is still being tuned. Run them in Unity with **Window → General → Test Runner → EditMode**, or from the menu **Caro → Run EditMode tests**. ## Getting started 1. Install **Unity 6000.0.76f1** with **Android Build Support** (Unity Hub). 2. Clone this repository and open the folder in Unity Hub (**Add project from disk**). 3. Open `Assets/_Caro/Scenes/Game.unity` and press Play. 4. To build: **File → Build Profiles → Android → Build**. The UI is generated from the art in `Assets/_Caro/Art/UIv2` by the editor menu **Caro → Build UI (mockups)**. ## Project structure | Folder | Contents | | --- | --- | | `Assets/_Caro/Scripts/Core` | Rules: board, growing grid, win check, undo (`Caro.Core`) | | `Assets/_Caro/Scripts/AI` | AI: move ranking, VCF, alpha-beta (`Caro.AI`) | | `Assets/_Caro/Scripts/UI` | Screens, board rendering, input, sound (`Caro.Game`) | | `Assets/_Caro/Editor` | UI builder and test tooling | | `Assets/_Caro/Tests` | EditMode tests (`Caro.Tests`) | | `Assets/_Caro/Art`, `Assets/_Caro/Audio` | Sprites, fonts, shader, sound effects | ## License Code is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The Pangolin and Liberation Sans fonts are under the SIL Open Font License (see the OFL files next to them). Game art and sound effects are part of this project for demonstration; please ask before reusing them elsewhere.

# Escape-Game: Einkaufen

Differenziertes Escape-Game für die Förderschule. Alle Schüler:innen spielen dasselbe Abenteuer mit 3 Räumen (🍎 Obst und Gemüse, 🥖 Bäckerei, 💶 Kasse), jede:r auf dem eigenen Niveau.

Jeder Raum ist als gezeichneter Raum dargestellt. Die Schüler:innen tippen auf 5 Gegenstände (Kiste, Regal links, Tisch, Regal rechts, Korb), lösen dort Aufgaben und sammeln so den Code für die Tür.

| Datei | Niveau | So wird gespielt |
|---|---|---|
| `niveau1.html` | ● basal | Ein großer Knopf, Ursache-Wirkung, kein Richtig und Falsch |
| `niveau2.html` | ●● Symbole | 2 Bild-Antworten, Vorlesen, Bild-Code antippen |
| `niveau3.html` | ●●● erstes Lesen | 3 Antworten mit Emoji, Buchstaben-Kacheln antippen |
| `niveau4.html` | ●●●● Lesen und Schreiben | 4 Antworten, Codewort schreiben |

`index.html` ist die Startseite zur Auswahl des Niveaus.

Jede Niveau-Datei ist in sich geschlossen und funktioniert auch einzeln, zum Beispiel in der App HTML-Klick.

Codewörter (Niveau 3 und 4): BIRNE, TORTE, KASSE.

Die Vorlage, mit der weitere Spiele erzeugt werden können, liegt in `vorlage/prompt-escape-game.md`.

## Spiel ändern

Die Spiel-Logik liegt in `quelle/engine.html`, die Aufgaben in `quelle/build.py`. Nach einer Änderung neu erzeugen mit:

```
python3 quelle/build.py .
```

Triston0130/lgtv-airpods-bridge.readme:
# lgtv-airpods-bridge

Play an LG webOS TV's audio on AirPods, even when the TV has no Bluetooth. A helper on the rooted TV captures the audio straight from the TV's DSP and streams it over Wi-Fi to a Mac. The Mac plays it on AirPods connected to it:

```
TV DSP ──(native capture)──► UDP over Wi-Fi ──► Mac ──► Bluetooth ──► AirPods
```

- **Lossless 48 kHz 16-bit stereo PCM.** No compression on the TV-to-Mac hop.
- **About 60–70 ms of network buffering.** Lost packets are re-requested and resent instead of buffered around. The AirPods themselves add their usual Bluetooth delay (macOS reports 160 ms).
- **TV speakers on or muted.** By default both the TV and the AirPods play. `--mute-tv` silences the TV while the AirPods keep playing; its previous mute state returns when the bridge stops.
- **Recovers a degrading TV Wi-Fi link** by refreshing the association while streaming.

Verified on an **LG 49UK6200PUA** (2018, MediaTek/MStar SoC, webOS 4.x) with AirPods Pro 2 on an Apple-silicon Mac. Other MStar-based LG TVs may work, but their capture channel or source number may differ. See [Porting](#porting).

## Requirements

- **A rooted LG TV with SSH as root**, for example via [RootMyTV](https://rootmy.tv/) or the webOS Homebrew Channel. Root is what lets the helper reach the audio DSP.
- **A Mac on the same network**, staying awake while you listen.
- **[Zig](https://ziglang.org/)** to cross-compile the TV helpers, and the Xcode Command Line Tools for `clang`.
- **Optional:** full Xcode, for `gamepolicyctl`. Without it the bridge cannot switch Game Mode on and runs unchanged.

## Setup

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Triston0130/lgtv-airpods-bridge
cd lgtv-airpods-bridge
sh build.sh                      # ZIG=/path/to/zig sh build.sh if zig is not on PATH
cp config.example.json config.json
```

Edit `config.json` with your TV's address, SSH user and private key. Host keys are checked strictly, so connect once with plain `ssh` first to record the TV's key.

## Use

Connect the AirPods to the Mac and select them as the sound output, then run:

```sh
./control start                  # TV and AirPods both play
./control start --mute-tv        # AirPods only; the TV unmutes when you stop
./control status
./control stop
```

The first time, macOS may ask whether Python can accept incoming network connections. Allow it, or no audio arrives.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--volume N` | last remote level, initially 35 | Player volume, 0–100 |
| `--buffer-ms N` | 70 | Jitter-buffer target, 20–200. Lower is closer to lip sync; too low drops out during Wi-Fi stalls. |
| `--mute-tv` | off | Mute the TV's own output while streaming |
| `--no-game-mode` | off | Leave macOS Game Mode alone. By default it is forced on while streaming, because Apple says it lowers AirPods latency, and set back to automatic on stop. |
| `--recover-ms N` | 50 | How long a missing packet is re-requested before it is concealed |
| `--transport ssh` | `udp` | The older PCM-inside-SSH transport. It stalls up to about 300 ms behind TCP. |

`relay-state.json` reports these:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `recovered` | Missing packets that were re-requested and arrived |
| `concealed` | Missing packets given up on and filled in |
| `rtt_p50_ms` | Median Mac-to-TV round trip |
| `reassociations` | TV Wi-Fi refreshes the bridge triggered |
| `peak_last_second` | Loudest sample in the last second; 0 means silence |

## How it works

### Capture (`capture.c`, runs on the TV)

LG's audio DSP sits behind MStar's "Utopia" driver layer, exposed by `/usr/lib/libkadaptor.so`.
- The helper `dlopen`s that library and initializes `MsOS`, `Utopia`, MMIO and the audio register mapping. A plain `MApi_AUDIO_PCMCapture_*` call faults without that setup.
- It then captures PCM channel 1 from source 8. On the 49UK6200 that is the TV's final mixed output: HDMI, apps and tuner alike.
- The capture taps the audio before the TV's volume and mute, so muting the TV does not silence the AirPods.
- The helper is uploaded to TV RAM (`/tmp`) on each start. Nothing is installed on the TV.

### Transport (`capture.c` and `relay.py`)

Each 10 ms chunk is one UDP datagram: sequence number, the TV's send time, then PCM.
- The TV keeps the last 1.28 s of packets.
- The Mac reorders by sequence number and `NACK`s gaps immediately, repeating every 20 ms. It conceals a chunk only once its deadline passes: repeat for short gaps, silence for long ones.
- SSH only launches the helper and owns its lifetime. The helper exits when its session goes away.

### TV menus and remote volume

The optional Mac agent lets the TV's full Settings and Quick Settings menus start the bridge. Connect and select the AirPods as the Mac's output, then run:

```sh
python3 agent.py install
python3 tv/install_settings.py --check   # before the menus have been installed
python3 tv/install_settings.py
```

The menu installer copies the stock Settings and Quick Settings files, patches the copies, and bind-mounts them at boot. It checks the stock file hashes before mounting, so a changed firmware leaves the stock menu in place. Quick Settings may need a TV restart to load the patched QML. Run `/var/lib/webosbrew/airpods-bridge/uninstall-settings.sh` on the TV to remove the menu changes.

Selecting AirPods or AirPods + TV starts streaming; choosing a TV output stops it. The agent remembers the last AirPods choice and reconnects when they become the Mac's output again. The TV must be able to reach the Mac on TCP port 47801.

On this TV, remote volume keys are handled by an existing Python 2 remote remapper (`/var/lib/webosbrew/remote-remap.py`). `python3 tv/install_remote_keys.py` installs the tested AirPods extension only when that remapper's fingerprint matches. The original is saved as `remote-remap.py.before-airpods`. While AirPods-only is active, volume and mute control the AirPods without unmuting the TV. In AirPods + TV mode the keys also keep their normal TV action. The Ma

Browser open-world pirate RPG (Three.js + TypeScript + Vite). First island: Bellwether Isle.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # play at http://localhost:5173
npm test           # game-rule tests (headless, ~2 s)
node scripts/e2e.cjs out/ --shots   # browser smoke test (needs dev server running)
npm run build      # static build in dist/ for GitHub Pages
```

See `PROJECT_LOG.md` for status, systems, controls and known issues, and `docs/ART_DIRECTION.md` for the look.

# DoublePixel - studio site

Privacy policies, terms and `app-ads.txt` for DoublePixel's games, served by GitHub Pages at
<https://doublepixel-studio.github.io/>.

This repository is **public on purpose**: Google Play and the App Store need a privacy policy at
a URL anyone can open, and free GitHub Pages serves only public repositories. Nothing here but
static HTML - no game code, no keys.

The rules for these pages (format, both languages, what a policy must say) are in the private
studio handbook, `doublepixel-studio/mobile-games/CLAUDE.md`, section "Legal pages".

## Adding a game

One folder per game, one page per document:

    <game-slug>/privacy-policy.html
    <game-slug>/terms.html            (if the game has terms)
    <game-slug>/delete-account.html   (if the game has accounts)

then add a card to `index.html` and a row below. The URL a store has been given must never
change afterwards, so pick the folder name once and leave it alone.

## app-ads.txt

`app-ads.txt` at the root is what AdMob reads for every game whose store listing names
`https://doublepixel-studio.github.io` as its website. It must contain exactly:

    google.com, pub-8111779805371074, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0

## Live URLs

| Game | Privacy policy | Terms |
|---|---|---|
| (none yet) | | |

Games published before 2026-10-23 keep their pages at <https://barsagivv.github.io/arclogic-studio/>.

# CapyPS5

**English** · [Español](README.es.md)

The first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android, built on KytyPS5 and the FEX x86-64 JIT.

**Website:** <https://capyps5.org> · **Discord:** <https://discord.com/invite/PEE7Q5TVM5>

> **Alpha (v0.0.1).** Few games work and many don't run at full speed. This release is for testing
> and reporting problems. The app tells you when a new version is out.

Source code: <https://git.capyps5.org/CapyPS5/CapyPS5> (mirror: <https://github.com/Ghael-V/CapyPS5>).
Every release has a tag (`v0.0.1`, …) with the exact code it was built from.

## Requirements

- Android 12 or later, arm64.
- A GPU with Vulkan 1.3. **Only tested on Qualcomm Adreno 830 (AYN Odin 3)** with the system driver.
  On other Adreno GPUs (for example the 750 in the Galaxy S24 Ultra) use a Turnip driver, and on Mali
  try PanVK: the app downloads them in **Settings → Graphics → Download drivers**.
- 12 GB of RAM or more recommended.
- Your own PS5 game dumps (a folder with `eboot.bin` and `sce_sys/`).

**CapyPS5 includes no games, BIOS, firmware or Sony keys, and needs none of them.** Only use games
you dumped from your own console. CapyPS5 is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment;
PlayStation and PS5 are trademarks of their respective owners.

## Usage

1. Install the APK and grant all-files access (the app asks for it on first start).
2. Copy each game as a folder into `CapyPS5/` on internal storage, or add your folders in
   **Settings → Game folders**.
3. Pick a game and press **Play**. **Ⓨ** or **⋯** opens that game's own options.
4. In game, swipe from the left edge, press the back button, the controller's home button or
   Select + Start to open the menu.

If a game closes because of an error, the library shows why when you return and can save the log
(to `CapyPS5/logs/`). Attach it when you report the problem.

## Compatibility (v0.0.2)

fix(3rdparty): restore xxHash build/cmake lost to the build/ gitignore rule

The top-level 'build/' ignore rule also matched the vendored xxHash's
build/cmake directory, so core/3rdparty/CMakeLists.txt:138
(add_subdirectory(xxHash/build/cmake)) failed on any fresh clone. Re-add the
files from the matching xxHash snapshot and re-include the path explicitly.

fix(tiler): include the no8bit SPIR-V headers referenced by GetPipeline

The fallback variant array entries reference GPU_TILER_*_NO8BIT_SPV, but the
corresponding generated headers were never included, breaking the build on
any configuration (spotted by a local compile of the modified objects).

fix(vulkan): make storageBuffer8BitAccess optional with 32-bit fallback

Adreno 6xx + Turnip (e.g. Adreno 660, Turnip v26.3.0-R5) reports
VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features::storageBuffer8BitAccess = false, so the
device selector rejected the only GPU (vulkanWindow.cpp) and the emulator
closed with DbgExit status 321.

The SPIR-V subword emitters already implement 32-bit fallbacks for both
directions (shift/mask loads in LoadSubwordInBounds, atomic read-modify-write
stores in StoreSubwordInBounds), and the BDA path never used 8-bit types.
This change gates the requirement instead of failing:

- vulkanWindow.cpp: treat storageBuffer8BitAccess as an optional feature in
  device selection (same policy as Mali/old-Adreno optional features), and
  only request it at vkCreateDevice when the driver exposes it. The state is
  logged as storageBuffer8Bit=... and can be forced off on Android with
  'setprop debug.capy.no_buffer_u8 1' for bisection.
- HostFeatures.h/Program.cpp: new g_host_features.buffer_u8 flag; when the
  device lacks the feature, StorageBufferElementBits clamps 8-bit buffer
  accesses to the 32-bit alias, so recompiled shaders never emit
  SPV_KHR_8bit_storage.
- gpu_tiler_common.inc + CMakeLists.txt + tiler.cpp: the embedded tiler
  compute shaders also required VK_KHR_8bit_storage. They now build a second
  SPIR-V variant (-DCAPY_NO_8BIT_STORAGE) that reads bytes through the 32-bit
  alias and writes them with an atomic compare-and-swap loop, selected at
  runtime when storage_buffer_8bit_enabled is false.

Devices that do expose the feature keep using the native 8-bit paths, so
behavior on working GPUs is unchanged.

Keep the d-pad and left stick apart, allow multitouch on the virtual pad, save trophies on Android

- SubmitPad mirrored the left stick into d-pad buttons (and the d-pad into the stick), so
  moving the stick fired the d-pad in games that use both.
- On-screen buttons only handled ACTION_DOWN, so a second finger was ignored; buttons now
  track their own pointers and sticks follow the finger that grabbed them.
- Trophy unlocks were written relative to the working directory, which is / on Android.

and third-party code (core/3rdparty, SDL's Java glue, font8x8) is untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Share loop budgets per dispatch, suballocate BDA buffers and rescale images that become targets

- Compute invocations start with DispatchLoopBudget() (debug.capy.loop_budget, 2^26)
  divided among all invocations of the dispatch, between 32 and loop_cap, so a
  full-screen pass where every invocation loops ends within the driver timeout.
- Device-address buffers are suballocated (upstream d58aefd): one dedicated
  allocation each exhausted the Adreno driver's address space.
- An unscaled image that later becomes a render or depth target is recreated at
  the target scale, so passes no longer mix scaled and unscaled attachments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bound shader loops, report hung GPU scopes and stop late downloads clobbering CPU writes

- Every guest loop spends a per-invocation iteration budget (debug.capy.loop_cap,
  65536 by default) and the invocation returns once it is spent, so a loop that
  never ends cannot hang the host GPU.
- With gpu_profile on, a watchdog logs the pass or dispatch that started and did
  not finish (CapyPS5-GpuHang).
- CPU write faults on pages with GPU data wait for the download: the asynchronous
  path left the page writable and the late download overwrote newer CPU writes
  (shader code decoded as code for 0x100 bytes and vertex data after).
- Shader code is synchronised with pending GPU writes before it is read and its
  hash refreshed.
- Shader text dumps decode stages that end in S_SETPC_B64 as front programs.
- debug.capy.bvh_miss makes every BVH node miss (diagnostic).

# Casino FP Gran Sur

Texas Hold'em y Ruleta de Tiza con fichas de mentira para la última fila de clase.
Abre el enlace, pon tu nombre y a jugar. Sin cuentas y sin sonido.

- **Hold'em**: abre una mesa y di en voz alta el código de 4 letras, o practica contra bots.
  Hasta 6 jugadores, 1000 fichas cada uno, ciegas de 10 y 20.
- **Ruleta de Tiza**: una sola ruleta para todos los que están en la web. Justo al cerrarse
  las apuestas, la tiza marca de 1 a 3 números que pagan de 50 a 300 veces en vez de 30.
  También se puede jugar en solitario.

## Cómo funciona

- `index.html`: el juego completo. Cada mesa funciona en el dispositivo del jugador que
  reparte. Si se va, otro jugador toma el relevo.
- `bridge.js`: la conexión multijugador. Hace long-polling a `/api/sync`.
- `api/sync.js`: una función de Vercel que reparte las actualizaciones de cada jugador al
  resto de su sala. Guarda las salas en memoria y las reconstruye un segundo después de
  un reinicio.

Las cartas de cada jugador viajan cifradas entre el dispositivo que reparte y ese jugador
(ECDH + AES-GCM), así que nadie puede ver tu mano mirando el tráfico de red.

## Despliegue

Importa este repositorio en https://vercel.com/new y pulsa Deploy. No hace falta
configurar nada. Cada push a `main` se despliega solo.

Cada jugador hace más o menos una petición por segundo mientras juega. El plan gratuito
Hobby de Vercel tiene límites de uso mensuales; puedes consultarlos en la pestaña Usage
del proyecto.

realangelodev/ValdoriaOT.readme:
# Valdoria OTS

A complete Open Tibia server for **client 10.98**:

- **The Forgotten Server 1.4.2**: the official TFS release for 10.98. The datapack, config and C++ source are in [`server/`](server).
- **MariaDB** for accounts, characters, houses and guilds.
- **MyAAC 1.9.5**: the website where players create accounts and characters, with highscores, who's online and an admin panel.

It runs on Windows with the official TFS Windows build. [XAMPP](https://www.apachefriends.org) supplies the database and web server programs, and `start.bat` starts and stops them for you, so you never have to open XAMPP. When you're ready to host for real, the same server folder moves to an Ubuntu machine. See [Moving to an Ubuntu server](#moving-to-an-ubuntu-server).

## Run it on Windows

### What you need

- **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.**
- **[XAMPP](https://www.apachefriends.org)**, the PHP **8.2** version, installed in `C:\xampp` (the default).
- **This repo**: [download the ZIP](https://github.com/realangelodev/valdoria-ots/archive/refs/heads/main.zip) and unzip it, or `git clone` it.
- **A Tibia 10.98 client.** See [Connecting with a client](#connecting-with-a-client).

### Set it up (once)

Double-click **`setup.bat`** in this folder. The first time, Notepad opens `.env`. Set your admin account name, password (8–29 characters, with a letter and a number), email and Game Master character name, then save and close Notepad.

`setup.bat` then does the rest:

- Installs the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime if your PC doesn't have it.
- Downloads the official TFS 1.4.2 Windows build (`theforgottenserver-x64.exe` and its DLLs) from GitHub, checks it against a known checksum, and puts it in `server\`.
- Starts XAMPP's MySQL, creates the `forgottenserver` database and user, and loads the game tables.
- Starts XAMPP's Apache, installs MyAAC into `C:\xampp\htdocs`, and runs its installer with your `.env` details.
- Applies the custom **Valdoria website design** (from `website/valdoria/`) and replaces MyAAC's sample news with a welcome post.
- Stops MySQL and Apache again when it's done. XAMPP's own start page is moved to `C:\xampp\htdocs-xampp-original`.

It's safe to run again: each step skips itself once it's done. If XAMPP is somewhere else, run `setup.bat -XamppPath D:\xampp`. If you gave MySQL's root user a password, add `-RootPassword yourpassword`.

### Every time you play

Double-click **`start.bat`**. It starts the database and the website in the background, then the game server in its window. When the window says **`>> Valdoria Server Online!`**, log in with your client. Players sign up at **http://localhost**.

To stop, press **Ctrl+C** in the server window. The server saves every player first, then `start.bat` shuts the website and database down too.

If you close the window instead, the server still saves, but MySQL and Apache keep running in the background. That's harmless: the next `start.bat` reuses them.

| Script | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `setup.bat` | One-time setup, described above |
| `start.bat` | Starts the database, website and game server; stops them all when the server stops |
| `backup.bat` | Saves the whole database to `backups\valdoria_<date>.sql`, whether or not the server is running |

After you edit `server\config.lua` or anything in `server\data`, stop the server and run `start.bat` again. Many changes can also be reloaded in-game with `/reload`.

## Updating

The project lives on GitHub at https://github.com/realangelodev/ValdoriaOT. To get the latest version, double-click **`update.bat`**: it downloads the changes and runs `setup.bat` to apply them. It needs [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) (the default install options are fine).

The first time, it links your existing folder to GitHub and replaces the project files with the latest ones. Your `.env`, the server program, logs and backups are kept. After that, your own edits (for example to `server\config.lua`) are kept too; if one clashes with an update, Git stops and tells you which file, and you can keep yours or take the new one.

## Connecting with a client

The game client isn't included: it belongs to CipSoft and isn't open source. You need the **10.98** client, the same version this server speaks.

**Login details:** host `127.0.0.1` (or your public IP for friends), port **7171**, plus the account name and password you made on the website.

The regular Tibia client is locked to CipSoft's servers, so use one of these:

- **An IP changer** for 10.98 that also replaces the RSA key. Most OT IP changers do. Point it at `127.0.0.1`, port `7171`.
- **[OTClientV8](https://github.com/OTCv8/otclientv8)** (recommended):
  1. The client is included in the [`client`](client) folder, already set up for Valdoria: a simple login (account name and password only), no server list, and OTClientV8's online services switched off. `update.bat` keeps it up to date.
  2. It needs the 10.98 `Tibia.dat` and `Tibia.spr` in `client\data\things\1098\`. They belong to CipSoft, so they are not in the repository; `setup.bat` copies them there from `otclientv8-master` on your Desktop if it finds them.
  3. Start `client\otclient_gl.exe` (or `otclient_dx.exe`) and log in with your account name and password.
- **[OTClient](https://github.com/edubart/otclient)** (the original): put the same two files in `data/things/1098/`, choose client version **1098** on the login screen, and use the details above.

This server uses the standard Open Tibia RSA key (`server/key.pem`), which is the one those tools expect.

### Offering the client on the website

The **Download our client** button on the website's Downloads page serves `C:\xampp\htdocs\files\Valdoria-Client.zip`. `setup.bat` makes that zip for you from the `client` folder (or whatever folder you put in `CLIENT_FOLDER` in `.env`), once the `.dat`/`.spr` files are in place. After changing the client, delete the zip and run `setup.bat` again to repack it.

## Playing with friends

By de

imthegoodboy/alice-in-botherland.readme:
# Alice in Botherland: The Last Island

A multiplayer survival-trial game for Windows, built in **Unreal Engine 5.8** (C++ and Slate).

The world burned. The survivors took to the sea as five floating communities, the Nomads. When a beacon rises
from the last habitable island, each community sends one champion. Three trials decide who reaches the Guardian,
and at the end of it all a single choice remains: **become the King, or save your people.**

## The game

Five champions (human players, with AI filling any empty seats) play one match:

| Phase | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Room** | The host creates a room and shares its **room code**; friends join by typing it. When all five seats are filled (AI test mode fills empty seats with AI) and everyone is ready, the host presses **Start**. |
| **The story** | A narrated picture story (skippable): the fall of Earth, the search for survival, the last island, the Guardian's trials. |
| **Arrival** | A short cinematic (skippable): the fleets sail through the channel into the cove and the champions land. |
| **The island** | 30 seconds to explore. Five old marker stones (follow the green light pillars) each tell part of the island's past. |
| **Stage 1: the Number Game** | Everyone secretly picks 0-100. Target = average × 0.8. The champion **farthest** from the target is eliminated. Ties go to sudden death. |
| **Stage 2: the Hidden Symbol** | Everyone sees every symbol except their own. Talk in chat, trust, lie, then name your own symbol. 3 rounds; the top two advance. |
| **Stage 3: the race** | The two finalists drive offroad buggies to the Guardian's beam and hold the switch for 3 s. Winning only earns the **first choice**. |
| **The Guardian's choice** | **Become the King** (you win; your people are lost) or **Save your people** (you die; they live, and the choice passes to the other finalist). No choice in time means King. |
| **Ending** | Three main endings (*The Crowned Exile*, *The Gift and the Crown*, *The Double Sacrifice*) plus two for when a finalist forfeits. A leaderboard records champions, sacrifices and eliminations. |

Alice, the narrator, welcomes the champions and explains every trial's rules in plain words, with captions and a
picture card, while everyone can still walk around.

The full design document is [`game.md`](game.md).

### Playing

- **First launch**: enter your champion name and pick your date of birth on the scroll wheels (kept on your PC only).
- **Main menu**: pick a mode (Play vs AI, Create room, Join room) and press **START**; Rules, Hall, Settings, Credits and Quit are the icons at the top right.
- **Play vs AI**: you and four AI champions.
- **Create room / join room**: the room shows a short code such as `6C2M-9QZ`. Friends on the same network type it in **Join room**. For internet play, the host switches to the **internet code** and forwards UDP port 7777 on their router. Rooms on your network are also listed, and you can still connect by IP address.
- **Voice chat**: hold **V** to talk (or set the microphone to *always on* / *off* in Settings). A microphone icon shows who is talking.
- **In a match**: press **Esc** or the gear at the top right for the game menu (resume, settings, how to play, leave) with quick sliders for mouse sensitivity, field of view and volume.
- **Settings**: audio, voice and captions, controls (sensitivity, invert, field of view, key list) and graphics (quality, resolution, brightness, frame-rate limit, motion blur, FPS counter, fullscreen, VSync).
- Reconnects: a disconnected player's seat is held by an AI "ghost" for 30 s in the lobby and 20 s during a match.

| Action | Keyboard / mouse | Gamepad |
|---|---|---|
| Move / look | WASD / mouse | Left / right stick |
| Sprint, jump | Left Shift, Space | Left stick click, A |
| Interact (read a marker stone, hold the switch) | E | X |
| Voice chat (push to talk) | V | D-pad up |
| Chat | Enter or T | |
| Scoreboard, menu | Tab, Esc | View, Menu |
| Drive (Stage 3) | W/S, A/D, Space handbrake, R reset | Triggers, left stick, B, Y |
| Spectate next / previous | Left / right mouse button | Shoulder buttons |

A packaged game ships with a `HOW TO PLAY.txt` for players.

## Building from source

### Requirements

- **Unreal Engine 5.8** (Epic Games Launcher).
- **Visual Studio 2022** (or Build Tools) with the *Desktop development with C++* workload and a Windows SDK.
- **.NET Framework 4.8 SDK** (UnrealBuildTool needs it on this setup).
- **[Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com/)**: all `.uasset`/`.umap` files, textures, models and audio are stored in LFS.

### 1. Clone

```bash
git lfs install
git clone https://github.com/imthegoodboy/alice-in-botherland.git
```

acannnz/monopoly-3D.readme:
# Monopoli Nusantara 3D

Monopoli klasik versi web 3D dengan kota-kota Indonesia, dibuat untuk nostalgia main berdua.

## Fitur

- Papan 3D (Three.js) dengan 22 kota Nusantara, stasiun/pelabuhan/bandara, kartu Kesempatan & Dana Umum
- Dadu ala Let's Get Rich: pilih Ganjil/Genap (pasti dituruti), tahan tombol, lepas saat jarum di posisi yang diinginkan (besar-kecil angka tetap untung-untungan)
- Angka langkah 1–12 di pinggir papan di depan pion
- Bangunan Rumah → Vila → Hotel (boleh sekaligus), lalu Landmark khas daerah (Monas, Gedung Sate, Rumah Gadang, Jembatan Ampera, dll.)
- Kamera mengikuti pion yang berjalan, aura kuning pada pion yang sedang giliran
- Aturan klasik: penjara, dadu kembar, gaji START, kas Bebas Parkir, bangkrut

## Menjalankan

Semua ada di satu file `index.html`, tanpa proses build. Buka langsung di browser, atau jalankan server statis:

```bash
python -m http.server 8080
```

lalu buka http://localhost:8080.

## Mode bermain

- **Satu HP (hot-seat):** berjalan di mana saja, progres tersimpan di browser.
- **Online (HP masing-masing):** di domain sendiri memakai server WebSocket di `server/` (alamat `/ws` pada domain yang sama). Saat dibuka sebagai artifact di claude.ai, game memakai penyimpanan bersama artifact.

## Server online (`server/`)

Node.js + [`ws`](https://github.com/websockets/ws). Satu room = satu dokumen state (kode 4 huruf), disimpan ke `rooms.json` dan disiarkan ke semua perangkat di room itu.

```bash
cd server
npm install
STATIC_FILE=../index.html PORT=3077 node server.js   # dev lokal: buka http://localhost:3077
```

## Deploy (VPS dengan HestiaCP)

| Bagian | Lokasi di VPS |
|---|---|
| Halaman | `/home/arcandapp/web/monopoli.arcand.my.id/public_html/index.html` |
| Server Node | `/home/arcandapp/monopoli-server/` (layanan systemd `monopoli`, port 127.0.0.1:3077) |
| Proxy `/ws` | `deploy/nginx.conf_ws` → `/home/arcandapp/conf/web/monopoli.arcand.my.id/nginx.conf_ws` dan `nginx.ssl.conf_ws` |
| Layanan | `deploy/monopoli.service` → `/etc/systemd/system/monopoli.service` |
| Header keamanan | `deploy/nginx.ssl.conf_security` → `/home/arcandapp/conf/web/monopoli.arcand.my.id/nginx.ssl.conf_security` |

Template Hestia domain ini `no-php` (web & backend), HSTS lewat `v-add-web-domain-ssl-hsts`.

Perintah berguna: `systemctl status monopoli`, `journalctl -u monopoli -f`.

## Batas pengaman server

| Batas | Nilai |
|---|---|
| Jumlah room | 300 (saat penuh, room tak tersentuh 7 hari diganti; room tak tersentuh 30 hari dihapus) |
| Room baru per IP | 15 per jam |
| Koneksi per IP | 6 |
| Kecepatan pesan | ±8 per detik per koneksi (lonjakan sampai 20) |
| Ukuran state | 64KB |

## Struktur kode (di dalam `index.html`)

| Bagian | Isi |
|---|---|
| Data papan | `T` (petak), `CH`/`CC` (kartu), `GROUPS` (warna & biaya bangun) |
| Mesin aturan | `actRoll`, `actBuy`, `actBuild`, `pay`, `resolve` — state lama → state baru + daftar efek |
| 3D | papan dari kanvas, pion, dadu, bangunan & `LANDMARKS` |
| Animasi | `playFx` memutar daftar efek (dadu, jalan, koin, kartu, bangun) |
| Online | satu dokumen state per room, semua perangkat mendengarkan perubahan |

Bar dadu hanya tampil di HP pemain yang sedang giliran

  maks 64KB, dan endpoint HTTP tidak lagi membocorkan jumlah room

  nginx.ssl.conf_security; HSTS lewat Hestia

# Kitten Summon Arena

A 3D browser card game inspired by Exploding Kittens, built with Three.js. Every card you play is summoned as a hologram in the middle of the table for all players to see.

The whole game is a single file, `index.html`. Open it in a browser to play.

## Features

- Two decks: **Classic** (13 card types, 2 to 5 players) and **Party** (49 card types, 2 to 15 players), including Targeted Attack, Reverse, Alter the Future, Undead Kitten, Collapsing Kitten, Sun Cat and many more.
- Full rules: Attack stacking, Nope chains, play-any-time cards, cat-card pairs and triples with wild Feral Cats.
- 3D table with an animated hologram for every card, card flights, and explosion effects.
- Computer opponents that remember what they have seen and react to the table.
- Cat customization: fur, eyes, pattern and headwear, in a cozy loaf-cat style with a live 3D preview.
- Seven arenas: outer space, beach, living room, bar, pyramids, neon rooftop, and volcano.
- Synthesized sound effects and music, with a sound menu for sound, music and the announcer.
- MC Whiskers, a roasting announcer with over 400 lines.
- Table chat with quick replies and speech bubbles over players, plus open-mic voice chat on the website (each player can turn their mic on and mute others for themselves).
- An in-game card guide that explains every card and combo.
- Works on phones: compact top bar, adaptive camera and seat layout, labels that stay on screen.

## Multiplayer

Play online at **https://kitten-summon-arena.vercel.app**.

1. Create a lobby. You get a 5-letter code and an invite link.
2. Friends open the invite link, or enter the code under "Join a lobby".
3. Fill empty seats with bots, then start the game.

The host's browser runs the game, and other players connect to it directly with PeerJS (WebRTC). There is no game server. Keep the host's tab open: if the host leaves, the lobby closes. Some strict networks, such as certain office or school Wi-Fi, block direct connections.

When the same file runs as a claude.ai Artifact, it uses the Artifact's shared database instead, with a public lobby list.

## Card art

All card art and characters are original. The card names follow the game's mechanics, but no official Exploding Kittens art or branding is used.

Blockheads-Club/mod-sdk.desc: Make mods for The Blockheads — in Lua, Rust, C, Go, Java and more.
Blockheads-Club/mod-sdk.readme:
Blockheads Mod SDK

Make mods for The Blockheads: new commands, chat tools, minigames and more, in Lua or Rust. 🧩

--- ## 🚀 Project Status **Current Status:** Server mods in Lua and WASM (milestones M1 and M2). This repo holds the mod API, the file formats, the network protocol, the `bhmod` tool, the shared mod host and the Rust SDK; the [Blockheads Server](https://github.com/Blockheads-Club/blockheads-server) runs Lua and WASM mods with it. Things may still change before 1.0. Mods can run on the server, on the client, or both. Players who join a modded server see the list of mods, accept, and the client part downloads straight from the server. --- ## 📦 Other Blockheads Club Repositories - [**blockheads-server**](https://github.com/Blockheads-Club/blockheads-server) - Host your own Blockheads server - [**blockheads-pc**](https://github.com/Blockheads-Club/blockheads-pc) - Play The Blockheads on your computer - [**blockheads-patcher**](https://github.com/Blockheads-Club/blockheads-patcher) - Fix crashes and add small improvements to the game on your phone - [**website**](https://github.com/Blockheads-Club/website) - The [Blockheads Club website](https://blockheads.club): downloads, guides and docs --- ## ⚡ Your first mod Install the tool (needs [Rust](https://rustup.rs)): ```bash cargo install --git https://github.com/Blockheads-Club/mod-sdk bhmod ``` **Lua (easiest):** ```bash bhmod new my-mod # creates my-mod/ with mod.toml and server/main.luau cd my-mod bhmod check . # finds mistakes in mod.toml and the files bhmod pack . # builds my-mod-0.1.0.bhmod ``` **Rust (WASM):** ```bash rustup target add wasm32-wasip2 bhmod new my-mod --lang rust cd my-mod && ./build.sh && bhmod pack . ``` Copy the `.bhmod` (or the unpacked mod folder) into the server's mods folder (`/mods/`, or `BLOCKHEADS_MODS_DIR`) and grant the permissions it asks for in `mods.toml` there: ```toml [hello-lua] grant = ["players:chat"] ``` Lua mods run on the server since milestone M1, WASM mods since M2. Every example comes as a Lua and a Rust twin that behave exactly the same (a test checks it): [`hello-lua`](examples/hello-lua) / [`hello-rust`](examples/hello-rust) (`/hello`), [`chat-filter`](examples/chat-filter) / [`chat-filter-rust`](examples/chat-filter-rust) (cancel and rewrite chat), [`scheduler-lua`](examples/scheduler-lua) / [`scheduler-rust`](examples/scheduler-rust) (`/countdown`, `/remind`). Rust, C, Zig and Go: [`docs/wasm.md`](docs/wasm.md). A client mod can call a service of a server mod over the network (API 0.3.1, asynchronous): [`prices-lua`](examples/prices-lua) is a price check with a server half that provides `prices` (`remote = true`) and a client half (`/price `), [`prices-rust`](examples/prices-rust) is the Rust twin of the client half. Content mods (API 0.3) declare textures in `[content]`: [`cosmetics-hats`](examples/cosmetics-hats) is a hat and hair set worn with `/hat` and `/hair` (see [`docs/content.md`](docs/content.md)). Java and Kotlin (milestone M9) are unsandboxed, so they need the `native` permission and a host with JVM support turned on: `bhmod new my-mod --lang java`, the examples ending in `-java` (`shop-java` calls the Lua `economy` service) and [`docs/jvm.md`](docs/jvm.md). Native mods (milestone M10) hook the game itself through a small C ABI (`libbhmod`: Objective-C swizzles, inline hooks on exported functions or addresses, import redirects) and are loaded only from the reviewed index, after the player confirmed a red warning: [`docs/native.md`](docs/native.md), example [`sdk/native/hello-c`](sdk/native/hello-c). --- ## 📚 What's inside | Path | What | | --- | --- | | [`wit/blockheads-api/`](wit/blockheads-api/) | The mod API (`blockheads:api@0.3.1`, WIT): events (incl. gameplay), commands, scheduler, storage, players, services (also across the network, client <-> server), channels, client UI (HUD, toasts, dialogs), mod content (items, blocks, cosmetics); the frozen 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3.0 copies are in [`wit/compat/`](wit/compat/) | | [`docs/luau-api.md`](docs/luau-api.md) | How the API looks from Lua | | [`docs/wasm.md`](docs/wasm.md) | WASM mods: Rust SDK, C/Zig/TinyGo, how the host runs them, the conformance suite | | [`docs/jvm.md`](docs/jvm.md) | JVM mods: Java/Kotlin SDK (generated from the WIT), how the host runs them, Android (ART) | | [`sdk/rust/blockheads-mod`](sdk/rust/blockheads-mod) | The Rust SDK (bindings + closures for events, commands, tasks) | | [`docs/native.md`](docs/native.md) | Native mods: the `libbhmod` C ABI and header, hook kinds, who may load native code, weapon skins | | [`docs/package.md`](docs/package.md) | The `.bhmod` package and its rules | | [`schema/`](schema/) | JSON Schemas for `mod.toml`, index entries and the published `index.json` | | [`docs/protocol-0xbc.md`](docs/protocol-0xbc.md), [`vectors/`](vectors/) | Client ⇄ server mod protocol and its byte-exact test vectors | | `crates/bhmod-manifest` | Reads and checks `mod.toml` and packages | | `crates/bhmod-proto` | Encodes and decodes the 0xBC protocol | | `crates/bhmod-cli` | The `bhmod` tool (`check`, `pack`, `new`, `index`) | | `crates/bhmod-native` | The `libbhmod` ABI, the armv7 inline-hook relocator and the hook engine both clients share | | `crates/bhmod-index` | Checks, builds and signs the public mod index ([`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md)) | | `crates/bhmod-core` | The shared

feat(core): JVM runtime behind the jvm feature

bhmod-core loads libjvm from the user's JRE at run time (JNI), keeps one JVM per process and gives each mod its own
class loader. Canonical CBOR crosses two functions (Glue.invoke into the mod, Glue.host into the Rust host API), so
the Java side is the generated WIT bindings. A watchdog interrupts calls past the hard deadline plus a grace period;
exceptions are faults, Errors are traps, a deliberate on-enable or service error is a failure. attach_existing adopts a
JVM that already runs in the process (ART on Android). The numeric locale is restored to C after the JVM starts: the
JVM's setlocale made Luau read 0.2 as 0 in Turkish. Conformance scenarios move to tests/common so the JVM suite
shares them with the WASM one; fixtures, unit and integration tests keep jvm.rs at 100 % line coverage.

fix(android): take network callbacks from other game threads

On a real phone (Galaxy Z Fold4, Android 14) the game receives some
packets on a second thread while a world loads. The receive hook used
thread-local loader state, so such a packet built a second, empty
loader on that thread and the 0xBC packet was dropped: the m7-echo
reply never reached the client mod.

The loader thread is now the one that runs drawFrame. Contact, 0xBC
packets and disconnects from other threads are queued (inbox) and
handled at the next frame in order; the connection pointer is shared
behind a mutex; a 0x1f sent from another thread joins without mods.

mindattic/Unity.Chain.readme:
# Unity.Chain

A mouse-steered angel swings a spiked mace on a spring chain, knocking down, grabbing and throwing a flock of
enemies. A Unity 6 rebuild of the 2005 VB.NET / DirectX 9 *Chain Game*, which was itself built on Philip Winston's
2000 *Elastic Trail* script, a mouse-follow chain of spring-linked dots.

[![Unity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity-6000.4.3f1-222222)](ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt)
[![C#](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-C%23-512BD4)](Assets/Unity.Chain)
[![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-in%20development-orange)](docs/BIBLE.md)

There is no public build yet. Build it from source with the steps below.

## The game

Move the mouse and the angel flies; behind it hangs a chain ending in a mace, simulated link by link as springs
with drag and gravity, so it lags, swings and whips. Circle the mouse and the mace winds up like a flail. A hit
knocks an enemy back and scores; hold the left button and the mace grabs instead, and letting go throws the enemy
into the others. Fourteen enemies home in on you, each touch costs one of your 30 HP, a heart drifts down for +10,
and at zero the light fades and the round starts again by itself.

## Status

In development, rebuilding the original to full parity. On main and tested:

- the spring chain (`ChainSimulation`, `ChainController`), the mace with `[` / `]` chain length and the overhead
  boost (`MaceController`)
- the angel's flight: mouse steering, hover bob, facing, flap frames, bounds (`AngelFlight`, `AngelController`)
- one `GameWorld` in Core that only `GameSession` steps: players send commands carrying their player id, and the
  enemies, audio and HUD play the events it produces (`Core/World/`, docs/BIBLE.md §5.3)
- grapple and throw (`Core/Grapple/`), enemies with seek, knockback, grab, throw and flocking, hit by a swept circle so
  fast swings never tunnel (`Enemies/`), the enemy spawner and the heart pickup (`Items/`)
- HP, score, pause, and the original's game-over fade and automatic reset (`GameState`, `GameSession`), with an
  interim IMGUI HUD (`GameHud`)
- the original's lighting: the ambient fade times the r/g/b tint the Day, Dusk, Night, Morning cycle walks (now on a
  24-minute day; the original's never moved), on a URP 2D global light, L toggling it (`LightingState`, `SceneLight`)
  under the URP 2D pipeline (`Rendering/ChainURP`, `Editor/RenderPipelineBuilder`)
- level bounds and a camera that fits or follows (`Level/`), sound and music players (`Audio/`, no clips yet)
- every input from one Input System action asset built in code, with keyboard, mouse and gamepad bindings; a
  gamepad's left stick steers like the mouse and J switches it off and on (`Input/ChainControls`, `Input/SeatInput`,
  `Core/Input/SteerInput`, `input.json`)
- the scene and the Windows player generated in code (`Editor/SceneBuilder`, `Editor/PlayerBuilder`)

Every tuning figure is data: the original's own figures in `Assets/StreamingAssets/Settings/*.json`, validated
on load and mapped to world units in one place (`Core/Settings`, see [BIBLE §6](docs/BIBLE.md)).

Still to come, in build order:
Unity.Shared settings, a UI Toolkit HUD, the original's art and sound,
and the remaining keys and screens. The full list, one ticket per step, is
[docs/RECONSTRUCTION.md §6](docs/RECONSTRUCTION.md); open tickets are in the MindAttic ticket database
(`tickets ticket list --repo Unity.Chain`).

## Build and test

Prerequisites: Unity 6000.4.3f1. Close the Editor before any batchmode run.

In the Editor, open the project and use the **MindAttic > Chain** menu:

- **Build Main Scene** regenerates `Assets/Scenes/Main.unity` and the build settings from code.
- **Build Windows Player** writes `Builds/Windows/Unity.Chain.exe`.

Play `Assets/Scenes/Main.unity`, or run the built player. Run the tests from **Window > General > Test Runner**
(EditMode and PlayMode).

From the command line (PowerShell, from the repo root):

```powershell
$unity = "C:\Program Files\Unity\Hub\Editor\6000.4.3f1\Editor\Unity.exe"

# regenerate the scene, then build the Windows player
& $unity -batchmode -quit -projectPath . -executeMethod MindAttic.Chain.EditorTools.SceneBuilder.BuildMainScene -logFile -
& $unity -batchmode -quit -projectPath . -executeMethod MindAttic.Chain.EditorTools.PlayerBuilder.BuildWindows -logFile -

# edit-mode and play-mode tests
& $unity -batchmode -projectPath . -runTests -testPlatform EditMode -testResults TestResults-EditMode.xml -logFile -
& $unity -batchmode -projectPath . -runTests -testPlatform PlayMode -testResults TestResults-PlayMode.xml -logFile -
```

`build.bat`, `test.bat` and `deploy.bat` like the reference repos' are planned (UNI-T39). The engine-free rules are
tested by `Tests/Core.Tests` (`dotnet test Tests/Core.Tests`, or `./run-core-tests.ps1`).

## Controls

| Keyboard and mouse | Gamepad | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse | left stick | fly |
| Left button (hold, release) | right trigger or A (hold, release) | arm the grapple, throw what it holds |
| `[` / `]` | left / right shoulder | shorten / lengthen the chain |
| F | Y | chain follows the hand / hangs slack |
| Pause, P or Escape | Start | pause |
| R | Back (Select) | start over |
| J | | gamepad stick steering on / off |
| L | | lighting on / off |

The bindings live in one `InputActionAsset` built in code (`Runtime/Input/ChainControls`); the stick's speed and
dead zone are in `input.json`.

The original's other keys (live spring, drag and gravity tuning, game speed, gem skins, backgrounds,
shake, debug views, the script console) are listed with their tickets in
[docs/RECONSTRUCTION.md §3.5](docs/RECONSTRUCTION.md).

## Project layout

```
Assets/
  Scenes/Main.unity                generated by SceneBuilder; do not edit by hand
  StreamingAssets/Settings/*.json  every tuning figure, the original's own (BIBLE §6)
  Unity.Chain/
    Core/                          Unity.Chain.Core asmdef (no engine): the GameWorld and every rule
      World/  Chain/  Player

thesigns/HotAir.readme:
# Hot Air

Fly a hot-air balloon as far as the propane allows – and land softly.
Low-poly 3D, a mobile-first browser game. Design: [docs/HotAir-GDD.md](docs/HotAir-GDD.md).

**Play: https://thesigns.github.io/HotAir/**

Status: **M2** – three countries, every world procedural:

- **The Netherlands** (easy): the polder with ditches, canals, roads, farms, windmills, cows, villages
  with a church, greenhouses, power lines and – in most worlds – the North Sea coast with dunes and a beach.
- **Italy – Tuscany** (medium): rolling hills, a patchwork of fields, vineyards and olive groves (no place
  to land), cypress drives to stone farmhouses, towns on the hilltops.
- **Switzerland** (hard): deep valleys with rivers, lakes, villages and chalets, pine woods, rock and snow
  on the ridges, cable cars, winds that follow the valleys low down, and thin air.

Other balloons with their own pilots. The flight model with burner lag, winds that change with height
and time, the pilot balloon, the wind ladder, three propane presets with records per country, landing
ratings, settings, help, synthesized sound with a soundscape below.

## Running locally

ES modules need an HTTP server (it won't work from `file://`):

```
python tools/serve.py 8766
```

(a plain `python -m http.server 8766` works too, but Chrome then caches the modules), then open
`http://localhost:8766/`. Add `?debug` for a state readout, `?seed=123` to fly the same world again.

On a phone in the same network, open `http://<computer-IP>:8766/`.

## Controls

| Touch | Keyboard / mouse | |
|---|---|---|
| BURN (right thumb), held | W / ↑ / Space | the burner – heat, lift |
| VENT (left thumb), held | S / ↓ | spill hot air – sink; on the ground: deflate |
| drag | mouse drag | look around the balloon |
| pinch | wheel | zoom |
| double-tap | double-click | reset the view |
| II | P / Esc | pause |

Settings: sound, vibration, the burner as tap-on / tap-off instead of held, a left-handed layout.

The balloon answers late: burn, then wait. You only go up and down – every height has its own wind.
The red pilot balloon at the launch draws the winds in the sky; the ladder on the right remembers them,
drawn so that an arrow pointing up takes you further from the launch (green). Flying high is faster,
but the thin air costs more propane.

Other balloons drift with the same winds: one at your own height stays where it is, so the danger is
climbing or sinking through somebody else's height – the HUD warns of a balloon above or below on a
collision course. Power lines along some roads carry orange balls; the HUD warns when your track and
sink rate lead into the wires. The coast is usually somewhere downwind: the beach is a fine place to
land, the sea is not.

When the propane bar reaches the reserve, look for a field. Land on dry, flat ground: a touchdown at
up to 0.3 m/s is EXCEPTIONAL (×1.5), up to 1 m/s GOOD (×1), harder or in the trees ROUGH (×0.5);
water, a house or more than 3 m/s is a CRASH. Hold VENT right after the touchdown, before the basket
is dragged into a ditch. With the propane gone, holding BURN still gives the last vapour – enough to
come down ROUGH instead of crashing.

## Models

All models are built in Blender from code: `tools/blender/models.py`. Rebuild them (and their previews) with

```
"E:\Programy\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.2\blender.exe" --background --factory-startup --python tools/blender/build.py -- previews
```

which writes `assets/models/models.glb`, `assets/models/models.blend` and `js/models/dims.js`.

## Tuning checks

```
node tools/feel.mjs        # the flight model against the GDD §5.1 table
node tools/fly.mjs 60 150 italy  # 60 whole flights with a scripted pilot at ~150 m (netherlands | italy | switzerland)
node tools/traffic.mjs 30  # the other balloons around scripted flights
```

# Fish Loop

A colour-sorting fish puzzle on a looping pipe, built with Phaser 4

A Phaser 4 + TypeScript prototype. Play it at https://huykc1.github.io/fish-loop-phaser-demo/demo/ · docs and Game Design Document at https://huykc1.github.io/fish-loop-phaser-demo/docs/.

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:8080
npm run build
```

## Releases

The live site is built locally and pushed to the `gh-pages` branch. There is no CI deploy.

```bash
npm run release:latest                  # after pushing main: update https://huykc1.github.io/fish-loop-phaser-demo/
npm version minor && npm run release    # publish a frozen copy at /fish-loop-phaser-demo/vX.Y.0/
```

The landing page lists every version. See `docs/guide/deployment.md` for details.

dacoowork/free-rein.readme:
# Free Rein

Small interactive things Claude built when it was told to build anything it liked.
Each build is a single self-contained HTML page that runs in the browser.

## Layout

- `index.html`: the hub gallery
- `play.html?b=<slug>`: shows a build with a thin bar to get back to the hub or move to the next build
- `builds/<slug>/index.html`: each build, also openable on its own
- `builds.js`: the list of builds, newest first

## Adding a build

1. Save the build's page as `builds/<slug>/index.html`.
2. Add an entry to the top of `builds.js` with its title, date, a one-line blurb and its colours and font.
3. Bump the `?v=` date on the `builds.js` script tag in `index.html` and `play.html`, so browsers don't keep a cached list.
4. Commit and push. GitHub Pages republishes within a minute or two.

## Hosting

Served free by GitHub Pages from the `main` branch root.

skyvaint/skyvaint-game-launcher.readme:
# SKYVAINT Game Launcher

A console-style game launcher for Windows: one fullscreen HOME for your Steam, Epic, Roblox and PC games, with account switching, clips, quests and a desktop dock.

## Install

1. Open **[Releases](../../releases/latest)** and download `SkyvaintGameLauncher-win-x64.zip`.
2. Unzip it anywhere (for example `Documents\SkyvaintGameLauncher`).
3. Run **`SkyvaintGameLauncher.exe`**.
   - If Windows SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info → Run anyway**. The app isn't code-signed, which is why that appears.

**Needs:** Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which Windows 11 already has. On an older PC without it, get it from [Microsoft](https://developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/#download-section) (Evergreen Bootstrapper).

Your settings and accounts are saved in `%APPDATA%\SkyvaintGameLauncher` on your own PC. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

## What it does

- **Games:** finds your whole Steam library, Epic games, Roblox and Roblox Studio, and you can add any .exe. Banners and icons are fetched automatically, and your own pictures always take priority.
- **Accounts:**
  - Pick which Epic account plays Fortnite or Rocket League, and switch smoothly between them.
  - Steam account switching.
  - A Roblox account manager: multiple accounts, places, private-server links, several instances at once.
- **Roblox list:** picking Roblox opens a shelf of your saved places. Roblox Studio opens your recent and cloud projects.
- **Clips:** your Medal library on HOME and in CLIPS, with favorites, your own categories and copy-Medal-link.
- **Quests:**
  - Daily and weekly quests that track themselves from your playtime and clips.
  - In-game challenges, lifetime milestones, and quests you write yourself.
  - XP and ranks.
- **Discover:** free Epic games, Steam top sellers and deals, trending Roblox games.
- **Rows under HOME:** scroll down for your Roblox games, Studio projects, upcoming releases, Roblox Studio news and Discord commission requests (needs your own bot).
- **NEXUS bar:** a see-through desktop dock with just the logos of the apps, games and sites you pick.
- **Discord Rich Presence:** you write the text and buttons yourself.
- **Looks:**
  - Themes, textures and an animated backdrop that runs on its own thread, so it keeps your monitor's full frame rate.
  - Sound packs, a custom app icon, the mini widget, and a fade-out when hiding to the tray.
- **Controls:** keyboard, mouse and controller. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Home</kbd> summons it from anywhere.

## Build from source

Needs the [.NET 9 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/9.0).

```bash
dotnet build -c Release
```

The app is in `bin\Release\net9.0-windows\`. To make the same self-contained zip as the release:

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true -o publish
```

The shell is WinForms + WebView2 (C#). The whole interface is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in `wwwroot/`.

### Command-line switches

| Switch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--background` | Start hidden in the tray |
| `--debug-port 9333` | Open the page to Edge/Chrome dev tools |
| `--dump <folder>` | Write what the game and clip scanners find, then exit |

markahman/ascii-craft.readme:
# ASCIICRAFT

A small Minecraft-like game that runs in the browser and draws everything as coloured
ASCII text: terrain, sky, water, mobs, explosions and the gun in your hand. It's plain
HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no build step, dependencies or framework.

## Running it

Open `index.html` in a browser. The scripts are classic `<script>` tags, so it works
straight from `file://`.

You can also serve the folder over HTTP:

```bash
python -m http.server 8137
```

Then open <http://localhost:8137>. Click the title screen to start playing. Clicking
captures the mouse and goes fullscreen.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| W A S D | Move |
| Mouse | Look |
| Space | Jump, swim up, fly up |
| Ctrl | Fly down |
| Shift, or double-tap W | Sprint |
| Left click | Break a block, hit a mob, or fire the gun |
| Right click | Place a block, or aim the gun |
| Middle click | Copy the block (or water) you're looking at into the hotbar |
| 1–0, mouse wheel | Choose a hotbar slot |
| G | Switch between survival and creative |
| F | Toggle flying (creative only) |
| R, or click | Respawn after dying |
| T | Skip ahead six hours |
| + / − | More or less detail (smaller or larger characters) |
| Esc | Pause |
| N (while paused) | Start a new world |

Symbol keys are matched on the typed character, so `+` and `-` work on any keyboard
layout. While playing, the game goes fullscreen and uses Keyboard Lock (Chrome and Edge),
so Ctrl shortcuts like Ctrl+W can't close the tab while you fly down.

The default hotbar is grass, dirt, stone, cobblestone, planks, sand, bricks, torch, TNT
and the gun (slot 0).

## Features

### World

- A 192 × 64 × 192 block world generated from a seed: rolling hills, mountains with snow,
  lakes and a sea, sandy beaches, winding caves, coal and iron ore, and forests.
- A day and night cycle (eight minutes per day) with a square sun and moon, stars and
  drifting clouds. Nights are darker than day but still readable, under a slightly blue
  moonlight.
- Your world saves itself in the browser (localStorage) every few seconds, when you pause
  and when you leave. Only your changes are stored; the world is rebuilt from its seed.

### Blocks

- **Torches** stand on floors or hang on walls, and light up their surroundings with warm,
  flickering light.
- **Sand** falls when there's nothing under it. A whole column drops together under
  gravity, like in Minecraft.
- **Water** flows by Minecraft's rules. It spreads up to seven blocks from a source,
  heads for the nearest drop, pours down waterfalls, and dries up when its source is cut
  off. Two sources side by side make a new one. Flowing water has a lower surface.
  Middle-click water to pick it up like a bucket, then place it anywhere.
- **TNT** is lit by placing a torch next to it. It hops, flashes and swells, then explodes
  after three seconds. Blasts light nearby TNT and fling it, so chains go off. Explosions
  blow white puffs of smoke, shake the screen, knock you back and leave craters that
  water flows into.

### Survival and creative

New worlds start in **survival**. Press **G** to switch to **creative**.

- **Survival:** you have ten hearts (shown as `<3` above the hotbar). Zombies bite,
  creepers explode, TNT hurts, and falls of more than three blocks hurt unless you land
  in water. A hit flashes the screen edges red. Health comes back slowly once you've been
  left alone for a few seconds. When you die, a "YOU DIED" screen appears, and you
  respawn at the world spawn in the same world, with everything you built still there.
- **Creative:** you can fly (F) and can't be hurt, and hostile mobs ignore you.

Blocks are unlimited and break instantly in both modes. There's no hunger, drowning or
inventory.

### Mobs

- **Pigs, cows and sheep** wander the grass in small herds and run away when hit.
- **Zombies** come out at night and in dark caves. In survival they chase you and bite.
  Caught in daylight under open sky, they catch fire and burn.
- **Creepers** also come out at night. In survival they walk up to you, hiss, flash
  white and swell, then explode. Get seven blocks away in time and they calm down.

Mobs are hurt by your hits, by gunshots and by explosions, and vanish in a puff of smoke
when they die.

### The gun

Slot 0 holds a pistol, drawn in your hand as a shaded 3D model.

- Left click fires; hold it down to keep firing. Shots reach 64 blocks, hurt the first
  mob in line (a pig takes two shots, a zombie four), light TNT, and kick up dust where
  they hit a block. Blocks aren't damaged.
- Right click aims down the sights: the view zooms in and the mouse slows down.
- Each shot has recoil, a muzzle flash and a bang. There's no ammo.

## How it works

Every frame, the renderer casts one ray per character cell through the voxel grid (an
Amanatides & Woo grid walk), up to 64 blocks away. Whatever the ray hits picks the
character and colour from an 8 × 8 ASCII texture. That colour is then lit by sun or
moonlight (a surface counts as sunlit if nothing is above it), torch light from a
flood-filled light map, and face shading, and then fogged towards the horizon. Mobs are
small box models; each ray is rotated into the mob's space and tested against its boxes.
Lit TNT and falling sand are drawn as moving cubes, and flowing water as boxes that only
fill a cell up to its surface.

The frame is drawn on a canvas. A one-pixel-per-cell background image (sky, fog, glow)
is scaled up in a single draw, and then each row of text is drawn as runs of
same-coloured characters, one `fillText` per run. Colours are quantised to 15 bits so
neighbouring cells share colours and runs stay long. A frame of about 30,000 cells takes
around 15 ms.

On top of that come effects drawn in screen space: explosion puffs, flames on burning
zombies (hidden behind blocks using a per-cell depth buffer), the gun, the hurt and death
screens, and the HUD. The gun is its own small ray tracer: a box model in front of the
camera with diffuse and s

# Machi Koro 2 Online (ภาษาไทย)

เว็บเกม Machi Koro 2 เล่นออนไลน์กับเพื่อน 2–5 คน แบบ realtime — ไม่ต้องสมัครสมาชิก ใช้แค่ชื่อเล่น + รหัสห้อง/ลิงก์เชิญ

> ⚠️ ชุดการ์ดตอนนี้เป็น **DEMO / UNVERIFIED DECK** — จำนวนสำเนาการ์ดยังไม่ได้ยืนยันจาก Rulebook (ดู `docs/RULE_ISSUES.md`)

## โครงสร้าง
```
packages/game-engine   Pure TS engine (deterministic, seeded RNG) + ข้อมูลการ์ด + protocol types + Vitest
apps/worker            Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object `GameRoom` (SQLite, WebSocket Hibernation)
apps/web               React + Vite + Tailwind v4 (UI ภาษาไทย, responsive)
data/                  JSON ที่ export จาก engine (cards_localized, establishments_th, landmarks_th, manifests)
translations/          Thai Translation Reference (แหล่งข้อความการ์ด)
docs/                  Audit, RULE_ISSUES, DEPLOY
```

## รันในเครื่อง
```bash
npm install
npm test                      # unit tests ของ engine
npm run dev:worker            # http://127.0.0.1:8787
npm run dev:web               # http://localhost:5173
```
เปิด 2 แท็บขึ้นไป → แท็บแรก "สร้างห้อง" → คัดลอกลิงก์เชิญไปเปิดในแท็บอื่น (แต่ละแท็บเป็นผู้เล่นคนละคน)

ทดสอบหลาย client ผ่าน server จริง (ต้องเปิด worker ไว้):
```bash
node apps/worker/scripts/smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8787 5
node apps/worker/scripts/fullgame.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8787 4
```

## เล่นออนไลน์
https://mropoom-tech.github.io/machi-koro-2-online/

## Deploy
ดู `docs/DEPLOY.md`
